pages.title: What is the difference between the JDK, JVM and runtime?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Java foundations and execution
Q001  What is the difference between the JDK, JVM
and runtime?
20-SECOND ANSWER
The JDK develops and runs Java programs; the runtime supplies libraries and the JVM;
the JVM executes bytecode.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
javac is a development tool supplied by the JDK. The java launcher starts the JVM, which uses the
runtime libraries. Traditionally, JDK contains JRE, and JRE contains JVM. Modern runtime packaging
can differ.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
javac Hello.java  // Compile source to Hello.class
   java Hello        // Launch the JVM and run bytecode
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Bytecode portability still depends on a compatible Java version, libraries and native
dependencies.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you package a smaller runtime for one application?
Use jdeps to identify required modules, then jlink to build a runtime image with only those
modules. Test the image with the real application and its native dependencies.

pages.title: Why can Java run on different operating systems?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Java foundations and execution
Q002  Why can Java run on different operating
systems?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Java runs on different operating systems because compatible JVMs execute the same
platform-independent bytecode.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Compile ordinary Java code once. Each operating system supplies its own JVM, which executes the
bytecode using instructions for that machine. The bytecode is portable; the JVM executable is platform-
specific.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Hello.java -> javac -> Hello.class
   Windows JVM -> executes Hello.class
   Linux JVM   -> executes Hello.class
   macOS JVM   -> executes Hello.class
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Java portability does not mean the JVM executable itself is portable.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What does javac --release 8 check?
It checks Java 8 language syntax, available standard APIs, and the generated class-file version
together. It helps prevent accidental calls to newer JDK APIs.
Original source: Core Java Zero to Hero, page 12 · Q002 · Interview study edition
START / CASE
Hello.java -> javac -> Hello.class ›
JAVA RULE
Java runs on different operating
systems because…
›
RESULT
Compile ordinary Java code once.

pages.title: Is Java pass by value or pass by reference?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Java foundations and execution
Q003  Is Java pass by value or pass by reference?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Java is always pass by value. For an object, the copied value is its reference.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
p and names initially refer to the same list, so add changes that list. Assigning a new list to p changes
only the method's local reference. It does not replace names. The same rule means a primitive
argument's reassignment cannot change the caller's variable.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
static void change(List<String> p) {
       p.add("Kiran");           // Change shared object
       p = new ArrayList<>();   // Change local reference
   }
   List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
   change(names);
   System.out.println(names);   // [Kiran]
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Seeing a mutation in the caller does not imply pass by reference.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why can a method not swap two caller variables of type Integer?
The method receives copies of the two Integer references. Swapping those local copies cannot
reassign the caller's variables; Integer values are also immutable.

pages.title: How do fields and local variables get initial values?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Java foundations and execution
Q004  How do fields and local variables get initial
values?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Fields and array elements receive defaults automatically. Local variables must be
assigned before reading.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Numeric fields default to zero, boolean to false, char to '\u0000', and references to null. These defaults
apply to static fields too. A local int[] a = new int[3] has assigned its reference; its three elements still
default to zero.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
class Example {
       int count;           // Default: 0
       boolean active;      // Default: false
       String name;         // Default: null
       void show() {
           int x;
           // System.out.println(x); // Compile-time error
           x = 10;
           System.out.println(x);   // 10
       }
   }
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A null field is initialized, but dereferencing it can still fail.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What are the default values of char and boolean?
A char field or array element defaults to the null character ('\\u0000'); a boolean defaults to
false. Unassigned local variables have no usable default.
Original source: Core Java Zero to Hero, page 13 · Q004 · Interview study edition

pages.title: What happens when an integer calculation overflows?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Java foundations and execution
Q005  What happens when an integer calculation
overflows?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Ordinary integer overflow wraps around; assigning the result to long afterward does not
repair it.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The first multiplication uses int operands, so it overflows before assignment. The L suffix makes the
second multiplication use long. multiplyExact checks overflow and rejects it instead of silently wrapping.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
long wrong = 50_000 * 50_000;
   long right = 50_000L * 50_000;
   System.out.println(wrong); // -1794967296
   System.out.println(right); // 2500000000
   Math.multiplyExact(50_000, 50_000); // ArithmeticException
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Assigning the result to long cannot undo an earlier int overflow.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you safely compare two integers without subtraction?
Use Integer.compare(a, b), or compare with a < b and a > b. Subtraction can overflow and
reverse the intended order.

pages.title: What is autoboxing and where can it fail?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Java foundations and execution
Q006  What is autoboxing and where can it fail?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Boxing converts primitives to wrappers; unboxing converts wrappers to primitives and
fails for null.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Unboxing behaves like calling intValue on an Integer, so null cannot be unboxed. equals compares
wrapper values. Comparing wrapper references with == is unreliable for value equality because identity
can depend on caching.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Integer boxed = 10;           // Boxing
   int value = boxed;            // Unboxing
   Integer missing = null;
   // int x = missing;           // NullPointerException
   Integer a = 1000, b = 1000;
   System.out.println(a.equals(b)); // true
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Integer == Integer usually compares references, unless an operand causes unboxing.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why might IntStream be preferable to Stream<Integer>?
IntStream operates on primitive int values, avoiding much boxing/unboxing overhead and
supporting primitive operations such as sum() and average(). Measure before claiming a speedup.
Original source: Core Java Zero to Hero, page 14 · Q006 · Interview study edition

pages.title: How do widening, narrowing and numeric promotion differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Java foundations and execution
Q007  How do widening, narrowing and numeric
promotion differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Widening usually needs no cast; narrowing needs a cast and can lose information;
arithmetic promotes small integers to int.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
A byte cannot hold 130, so narrowing retains only the byte-sized representation. b + 1 has type int.
Compound assignment includes a conversion back to byte, which explains why += compiles.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
int n = 130;
   byte small = (byte) n;
   System.out.println(small); // -126
   byte b = 1;
   b += 1;                   // Compiles: implicit cast
   // b = b + 1;             // Compile-time error
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A compound assignment includes an implicit conversion back to the left-hand type.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why is a char a UTF-16 code unit rather than every possible Unicode character?
Java's char stores one 16-bit UTF-16 code unit. Supplementary code points require surrogate
pairs, so one Unicode code point may occupy two chars.

pages.title: How do short-circuit operators and evaluation order work?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Java foundations and execution
Q008  How do short-circuit operators and evaluation
order work?
20-SECOND ANSWER
&& and || short-circuit; boolean & and | always evaluate both operands. Java evaluates
operands left to right.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
With &&, the false null check prevents isEmpty from running. With &, both sides run, so the call
dereferences null. Similarly, true || expensiveCall skips the call.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
String name = null;
   boolean ok = name != null && !name.isEmpty();
   System.out.println(ok); // false
   // name != null & !name.isEmpty(); // NullPointerException
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Replacing && with & can introduce a null dereference.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What does false && expensiveCall() evaluate?
Only false is evaluated; expensiveCall() is not called because && short-circuits once the left
operand is false.
Original source: Core Java Zero to Hero, page 15 · Q008 · Interview study edition

pages.title: Why do abstract classes still matter after Java 8 default methods?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Object-oriented design
Q009  Why do abstract classes still matter after Java
8 default methods?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Abstract classes share instance state and construction rules; interfaces define
capabilities and can supply default behavior.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Each Exporter object has its own destination, initialized through the constructor. Printable supplies a
reusable method but cannot own per-object instance fields or a constructor. Java 8 default methods
therefore do not replace abstract classes.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
abstract class Exporter {
       protected final String destination;
       Exporter(String d) { destination = d; }
       abstract void export();
   }
   interface Printable {
       default void print() { System.out.println("Ready"); }
   }
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: An interface default method does not replace every use of shared state.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
When would composition be safer than extending AbstractExporter?
Composition is safer when an object needs an exporter without really being an exporter, or when
you want to swap implementations, mock dependencies, and avoid inherited state coupling.

pages.title: Can you instantiate an abstract class?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Object-oriented design
Q010  Can you instantiate an abstract class?
20-SECOND ANSWER
You cannot instantiate an abstract class directly. You can instantiate a concrete or
anonymous subclass.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The anonymous class provides the missing implementation. The created object's class is that concrete
anonymous subclass. Task is just the reference type. The abstract superclass constructor still
participates in construction.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
abstract class Task {
       abstract void run();
   }
   // Task t = new Task(); // Compile-time error
   Task t = new Task() {
       @Override void run() { System.out.println("Done"); }
   };
   t.run(); // Done
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: An abstract class may have constructors and may contain no abstract methods.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Can an abstract class have a final concrete method?
Yes. An abstract class may define a final concrete method. Subclasses inherit that method but
cannot override it.
Original source: Core Java Zero to Hero, page 17 · Q010 · Interview study edition

pages.title: How are overloading and overriding resolved?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Object-oriented design
Q011  How are overloading and overriding resolved?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Overloading selects a signature at compile time; overriding selects an instance
implementation at runtime.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
a is declared Animal, so show(Animal) is selected. The receiver object is a Dog, so the overridden speak
runs. The two decisions happen at different stages.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
class Animal { String speak() { return "Animal"; } }
   class Dog extends Animal {
       @Override String speak() { return "Dog"; }
   }
   static void show(Animal a) { System.out.println("Animal overload"); }
   static void show(Dog d) { System.out.println("Dog overload"); }
   Animal a = new Dog();
   show(a);                       // Animal overload
   System.out.println(a.speak());  // Dog
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A private method is not overridden by a same-named subclass method.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How does overload resolution treat a null argument?
The compiler chooses the most specific applicable overload; null matches reference types, not
primitives. If unrelated overloads are equally specific, the call is ambiguous.

pages.title: Can static methods and fields be polymorphic?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Object-oriented design
Q012  Can static methods and fields be polymorphic?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Static methods are hidden, and fields are selected by the reference's declared type.
Neither uses instance-method dispatch.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The declared Parent type selects the field and static method even though the object is Child. Use class
names for static calls to make this selection explicit.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
class Parent {
       int value = 1;
       static String who() { return "Parent"; }
   }
   class Child extends Parent {
       int value = 2;
       static String who() { return "Child"; }
   }
   Parent p = new Child();
   System.out.println(p.value); // 1
   System.out.println(p.who()); // Parent; prefer Parent.who()
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Calling a static method through an instance can misleadingly resemble virtual dispatch.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Can a subclass change an instance method into a static method?
No. A subclass cannot hide an inherited instance method with a static method having the same
overriding signature; the compiler rejects it.

pages.title: What is the order of construction and initialization?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Object-oriented design
Q013  What is the order of construction and
initialization?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Fields first receive defaults. In the Java 8-21 construction model, superclass
construction precedes subclass initializers and constructor body.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Base's constructor dispatches to Child.show before Child's name initializer runs. The field still contains
its default null. Avoid calling overridable methods from constructors. Class-level static initialization is a
separate stage.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
class Base {
       Base() { show(); }
       void show() {}
   }
   class Child extends Base {
       String name = "ready";
       @Override void show() { System.out.println(name); }
   }
   new Child(); // Prints null
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Avoid publishing this or invoking overridable behavior during construction.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED

Reading a static final compile-time constant such as a literal int or String may use an inlined
value, without triggering initialization of its declaring class.

pages.title: How are conflicting interface default methods resolved?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Object-oriented design
Q014  How are conflicting interface default methods
resolved?
20-SECOND ANSWER
An implementing class must resolve matching defaults inherited from unrelated
interfaces.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Without Report's override, the compiler cannot choose between A and B. A.super.label explicitly
delegates to A's default. A concrete inherited class implementation normally wins over an interface
default.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
interface A { default String label() { return "A"; } }
   interface B { default String label() { return "B"; } }
   class Report implements A, B {
       @Override public String label() {
           return A.super.label();
       }
   }
   System.out.println(new Report().label()); // A
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Interfaces do not inherit static methods as instance behavior.

No. An interface default method cannot override a public method of Object such as
equals(Object), hashCode(), or toString(). Implement it in a class instead.

pages.title: When should composition replace inheritance?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Object-oriented design
Q015  When should composition replace inheritance?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Use inheritance for a valid is-a relationship; use composition to reuse or replace
behavior through a collaborator.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
RetryService has a Sender instead of claiming to be a particular HTTP sender. A test can supply a fake
Sender. Retry logic can evolve independently of the transport implementation.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
interface Sender { void send(String text); }
   class RetryService {
       private final Sender sender;
       RetryService(Sender s) { sender = s; }
       void send(String text) { sender.send(text); }
   }
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Sharing a few methods is insufficient evidence of a valid subtype relationship.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What parent guarantee would a subclass that rejects add() violate?
It violates the Liskov Substitution Principle if the parent contract promises add() support. A caller
relying on that promise cannot safely substitute the subclass.

pages.title: How do SOLID principles translate into Java interview answers?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Object-oriented design
Q016  How do SOLID principles translate into Java
interview answers?
20-SECOND ANSWER
SOLID keeps responsibilities focused, extensions isolated, subtypes substitutable,
interfaces small, and policy dependent on abstractions.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Checkout owns checkout policy; the gateway owns payment behavior (SRP). Add a UPI implementation
without rewriting Checkout (OCP). Every gateway must honor pay's contract (LSP). The interface
exposes only needed operations (ISP). Checkout depends on the interface (DIP).
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
interface PaymentGateway { void pay(int rupees); }
   class Checkout {
       private final PaymentGateway gateway;
       Checkout(PaymentGateway g) { gateway = g; }
       void complete() { gateway.pay(500); }
   }
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: More interfaces and more classes do not automatically improve the design.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Which principle fails if a gateway sometimes silently discards payments?
Primarily Liskov Substitution: the implementation breaks the PaymentGateway contract. It can
also violate the application's expected error-reporting policy.

pages.title: What are the equals and hashCode contracts?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Equality, copying and immutability
Q017  What are the equals and hashCode contracts?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Equal objects must have equal hash codes. Equal hash codes do not guarantee equal
objects.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Both methods use the same stable value field. A HashMap can therefore find a mapping with an
equivalent new Id. equals must also be reflexive, symmetric, transitive, consistent, and false for null.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
final class Id {
       private final int value;
       Id(int v) { value = v; }
       @Override public boolean equals(Object o) {
           return o instanceof Id && value == ((Id) o).value;
       }
       @Override public int hashCode() { return Integer.hashCode(value); }
   }
   System.out.println(new Id(7).equals(new Id(7))); // true
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A different hash code proves inequality; an equal hash code does not prove equality.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What breaks if you override equals but inherit Object.hashCode()?
Two objects that compare equal could have different identity-based hash codes. HashMap and
HashSet may then fail to treat them as the same key, violating the contract.

pages.title: Why are mutable keys dangerous in a HashMap?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Equality, copying and immutability
Q018  Why are mutable keys dangerous in a
HashMap?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Changing a map key's equality or hash fields after insertion can make its entry
unreachable through normal lookup.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Insertion uses the old hash. Lookup uses the new hash, which may search a different bucket or fail the
stored-hash check. A final reference would still allow key.id to change. Use an immutable identity key.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
// MutableKey uses id in equals and hashCode.
   MutableKey key = new MutableKey(1);
   Map<MutableKey, String> map = new HashMap<>();
   map.put(key, "Sai");
   key.id = 2;
   System.out.println(map.get(key)); // Can be null
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: final Customer key prevents reassignment, not mutation of key.id.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Would a TreeMap key mutation also cause problems?
Yes. Changing a comparison field after insertion can corrupt the tree's expected ordering;
lookups, removal and uniqueness checks may behave incorrectly. Use stable keys.

pages.title: How do you make a Java class immutable?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Equality, copying and immutability
Q019  How do you make a Java class immutable?
20-SECOND ANSWER
An immutable class prevents observable state changes and controls mutable inputs,
outputs, and subclassing.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Changing input after construction does not change values because the constructor copied the
structure. Callers cannot modify the returned list. String elements are immutable; mutable elements
would need their own copy policy.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
final class Names {
       private final List<String> values;
       Names(List<String> input) {
           values = Collections.unmodifiableList(new ArrayList<>(input));
       }
       List<String> values() { return values; }
   }
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: An unmodifiable list of mutable elements does not make the entire object graph immutable.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What would you do when an immutable object contains Date?
Make defensive copies on input and output, such as new Date(input.getTime()). Prefer immutable
java.time types when the API permits.

pages.title: How do final, finally and finalize differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Equality, copying and immutability
Q020  How do final, finally and finalize differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER
final restricts changes; finally runs cleanup control flow; finalize is an obsolete,
unreliable cleanup mechanism.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
final prevents reassigning names, not changing its list. finally prints cleanup when normal try control
flow exits. Use try-with-resources for owned closeable resources rather than relying on finalize.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
final List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
   names.add("Sai");         // Allowed: object is mutable
   // names = new ArrayList<>(); // Compile-time error
   try {
       System.out.println("work");
   } finally {
       System.out.println("cleanup");
   }
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: finally is not guaranteed during forced process termination.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Does a final field make every operation on its object thread safe?
No. final prevents reassignment of that field; it does not synchronize mutations of the referenced
object or make its methods atomic.

pages.fullText:

Q021  What is the difference between shallow and
deep copying?
20-SECOND ANSWER
A shallow copy duplicates the outer container; a deep copy duplicates the mutable
elements that must be independently owned.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The lists differ, but their first elements reference the same StringBuilder. To isolate this element, create
a new StringBuilder from its text while copying. Immutable elements can safely be shared.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<StringBuilder> original = new ArrayList<>();
   original.add(new StringBuilder("A"));
   List<StringBuilder> copy = new ArrayList<>(original);
   copy.get(0).append("B");
   System.out.println(original.get(0)); // AB
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A recursive deep copy must account for cycles and shared identity if they matter.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED

Copy the outer collection and each mutable element, including nested mutable fields where
ownership requires it. Define how shared references and cycles should be treated.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Equality, copying and immutability
Q023  How are identity, value equality and ordering
different?
20-SECOND ANSWER
== compares reference identity, equals compares domain values, and comparison zero
means equivalence in an ordering.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The objects differ in identity. BigDecimal.equals includes scale, so they differ as values under that
contract. compareTo compares numeric magnitude, so they occupy the same natural-order position in
a TreeSet.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
BigDecimal a = new BigDecimal("1.0");
   BigDecimal b = new BigDecimal("1.00");
   System.out.println(a == b);           // false
   System.out.println(a.equals(b));      // false
   System.out.println(a.compareTo(b));   // 0
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Objects.compare(a,b,cmp) and Objects.equals(a,b) answer different questions.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What happens if a TreeSet comparator compares employees only by salary?
Employees with equal salaries compare as zero and TreeSet keeps only one of them. Add a
unique tie-breaker, such as employee ID, when distinct employees must remain.

pages.title: When are immutable objects useful in concurrent code?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Equality, copying and immutability
Q024  When are immutable objects useful in
concurrent code?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Immutable snapshots simplify concurrent reads; publishing or replacing them still needs
a clear coordination policy.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Readers obtain a complete snapshot through the volatile reference. Config's value never changes
afterward. Two writers doing read-modify-write replacement can still lose updates unless a lock or
atomic update coordinates them.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
final class Config {
       final int timeout;
       Config(int t) { timeout = t; }
   }
   volatile Config current = new Config(1000);
   // Writer:
   current = new Config(2000);
   // Reader:
   Config snapshot = current;
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Immutability of a snapshot does not make a read-modify-write replacement atomic.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you prevent two config writers from losing each other's updates?
Use one immutable Config value in AtomicReference and update it with compareAndSet/
updateAndGet, or guard the full read-modify-write with one lock. Retry functions should be side-
effect-free.

pages.title: How does the string pool affect == and equals?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Strings, numbers and arrays
Q025  How does the string pool affect == and equals?
20-SECOND ANSWER
String literals are interned, but use equals for text comparison regardless of pooling.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
a and the compile-time constant b use the pooled string. c is a distinct object with identical text.
Pooling explains identity; equals expresses the application's text comparison.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
String a = "java";
   String b = "ja" + "va";
   String c = new String("java");
   System.out.println(a == b);      // true
   System.out.println(a == c);      // false
   System.out.println(a.equals(c)); // true
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Do not infer business equality from incidental string interning.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What changes if one operand of concatenation is a non-final variable?
Concatenation may happen at runtime, producing a different String object rather than the same
interned compile-time constant. Compare text with equals(), not ==.

pages.title: Why is String immutable?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Strings, numbers and arrays
Q026  Why is String immutable?
20-SECOND ANSWER
String is immutable: its methods produce a result rather than modifying its existing
value.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The first call's returned value is ignored. The second assignment changes the local reference to the
uppercase result. The original string remains unchanged, so its hash and value stay stable when shared.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
String s = "java";
   s.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
   System.out.println(s); // java
   s = s.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
   System.out.println(s); // JAVA
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Immutability does not mean that every string operation creates a fresh object.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why is a char[] sometimes preferred for a password?
A char[] can be overwritten after use; an immutable String cannot be cleared in place. This
reduces some exposure, but copies, logging and runtime memory still need care.

pages.title: When should you use StringBuilder or StringBuffer?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Strings, numbers and arrays
Q027  When should you use StringBuilder or
StringBuffer?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Use StringBuilder for mutable text built within one thread. StringBuffer synchronizes
methods but not every multi-step workflow.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
One builder accumulates characters before producing a String. Repeatedly replacing a growing String
in a loop can cause extra copying. A thread-local builder needs no StringBuffer synchronization.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder();
   for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
       out.append(i).append(' ');
   }
   System.out.println(out.toString()); // 1 2 3 (trailing space)
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Synchronization on individual StringBuffer calls does not make every multi-call algorithm
atomic.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Can a shared StringBuilder be safe if all access uses one external lock?
Yes, if every read and write uses the same lock and the builder does not escape that policy.
Individual uncoordinated accesses remain unsafe.

pages.title: What is the difference between a char and a Unicode code point?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Strings, numbers and arrays
Q028  What is the difference between a char and a
Unicode code point?
20-SECOND ANSWER
A char is a UTF-16 code unit. Some Unicode code points need two chars, and a
displayed character can contain several code points.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The supplementary emoji uses a surrogate pair, so length counts two code units. codePointCount counts
one code point. Combining marks and joined emoji require grapheme-aware handling for displayed-
character operations.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
String emoji = new String(Character.toChars(0x1F600));
   System.out.println(emoji.length()); // 2
   System.out.println(emoji.codePointCount(0, emoji.length())); // 1
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A char-based frequency map can split a supplementary character.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Would reversing code points preserve every user-visible grapheme?
No. A grapheme can contain several code points (combining marks or joined emoji). Use
Unicode grapheme segmentation, for example BreakIterator with its documented limitations.

pages.title: Why should money usually avoid double?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Strings, numbers and arrays
Q029  Why should money usually avoid double?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Use decimal arithmetic with an explicit rounding policy for money; binary double
cannot represent many decimal fractions exactly.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The double result reflects binary approximation. Decimal string construction preserves the intended
decimal amount. Choose currency scale and rounding at the business-defined boundary.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
System.out.println(0.1 + 0.2); // 0.30000000000000004
   BigDecimal total = new BigDecimal("0.10")
           .add(new BigDecimal("0.20"));
   System.out.println(total); // 0.30
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: BigDecimal operations return new values; add does not mutate the receiver.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why can divide throw ArithmeticException even when the divisor is nonzero?
Some exact decimal quotients never terminate, such as 1 / 3. Supply an explicit scale and
RoundingMode, or a MathContext, for the domain.

pages.title: Why do BigDecimal.equals and compareTo give different results?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Strings, numbers and arrays
Q030  Why do BigDecimal.equals and compareTo give
different results?
20-SECOND ANSWER
BigDecimal.equals includes scale; compareTo compares numeric value only.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
HashSet uses equals, so scale makes these values distinct. TreeSet uses natural comparison, so
numeric equality collapses them. Normalize decimals according to your domain before using them as
identity keys.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
BigDecimal a = new BigDecimal("2.0");
   BigDecimal b = new BigDecimal("2.00");
   Set<BigDecimal> hash = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList(a, b));
   Set<BigDecimal> tree = new TreeSet<>(Arrays.asList(a, b));
   System.out.println(hash.size()); // 2
   System.out.println(tree.size()); // 1
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: stripTrailingZeros can produce a negative scale, so do not assume scale is always
nonnegative.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you store a price key consistently?
Choose one canonical representation, such as fixed currency scale and currency code, before
storing the key. Avoid treating 2.0 and 2.00 as different product prices accidentally.

CHAPTER 04 / Strings, numbers and arrays
Q031  Why can array covariance throw
ArrayStoreException?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Reference arrays allow covariance but check stores at runtime; an incompatible element
causes ArrayStoreException.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The variable type accepts Object, but the actual array accepts only String. Generics reject the
analogous unsafe List assignment at compile time through invariance.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Object[] values = new String[1];
   values[0] = "Java"; // Allowed
   // values[0] = 42; // ArrayStoreException
   // List<Object> xs = new ArrayList<String>(); // Compile error
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: List<String> cannot be assigned to List<Object>.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why can new List<String>[10] not be created directly?
Generic component types are erased and not reifiable, so Java cannot check array stores for
List<String> at runtime. Prefer List<List<String>> or a carefully managed List<?>[].

pages.title: How do arrays and lists differ in copying and conversion?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Strings, numbers and arrays
Q032  How do arrays and lists differ in copying and
conversion?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Arrays.asList creates a fixed-size view over a reference array; copying it into ArrayList
creates independently resizable structure.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
set changes the backing array. add would change its fixed length and is rejected. The ArrayList copy
has its own structure. Arrays.asList(new int[]{1,2}) creates one list element containing the primitive
array.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
String[] a = {"A", "B"};
   List<String> view = Arrays.asList(a);
   view.set(0, "X");
   System.out.println(a[0]); // X
   // view.add("C");        // UnsupportedOperationException
   List<String> copy = new ArrayList<>(view);
   copy.add("C");           // Allowed
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Fixed size and unmodifiable describe different properties.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you get a mutable list from an int[]?
Use Arrays.stream(intArray).boxed().collect(Collectors.toCollection(ArrayList::new));
Arrays.asList(intArray) gives a single element containing the whole primitive array.

CHAPTER 05 / Exceptions and resource ownership
Q033  How do checked and unchecked exceptions
differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Checked exceptions must be caught or declared; unchecked exceptions have no such
compile-time obligation.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Calling read requires handling or declaring IOException. Calling validate does not require a catch
declaration. Exception category describes compiler obligations, not whether recovery is possible.

   static void validate(int age) {

Translate it at the repository boundary to a stable domain/data-access exception with the original

pages.title: What are the disadvantages of checked exceptions?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Exceptions and resource ownership
Q034  What are the disadvantages of checked
exceptions?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Checked exceptions make failures explicit, but can spread implementation coupling and
add wrapping boilerplate.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
A service contract exposing SQLException ties callers to a database detail. Translation can preserve the
cause while exposing a stable domain contract. Keep checked exceptions when callers have a
meaningful recovery responsibility.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
// JDBC detail leaks into every caller's signature:
   User loadUser(int id) throws SQLException;
   // An alternative boundary can translate to a domain failure:
   // throw new UserLoadException("Cannot load " + id, cause);
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Checked exceptions are not inherently bad; the recovery contract determines their value.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you handle IOException inside a stream mapping operation?
Catch IOException inside the mapping function and wrap it in an unchecked exception with its
cause, or move the I/O outside the stream. Translate it back at a suitable boundary.

Q035  What is the difference between throw and
throws?
20-SECOND ANSWER
throw raises an exception object; throws declares failures a method can propagate.

The throws clause alone performs no action. The throw statement changes control flow immediately. An
overriding method cannot broaden checked failures beyond the parent's permitted contract.

static void load() throws IOException { // Declaration
       throw new IOException("Missing file"); // Action
   }
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A method can declare an unchecked exception for documentation without forcing callers to
catch it.

Can an override narrow a checked exception from Exception to IOException?
Yes. An override may declare the same, a narrower checked exception such as IOException, or
none, as long as the superclass declares a compatible checked type.

pages.title: What happens when both try and finally return or throw?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Exceptions and resource ownership
Q036  What happens when both try and finally return
or throw?
20-SECOND ANSWER
An abrupt return or throw in finally replaces the pending return or exception from try.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The try prepares a return value of 1, then finally runs before returning. Its return replaces the pending
result. Avoid returns in finally because they can also hide failures.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
static int result() {
       try { return 1; }
       finally { return 2; }
   }
   System.out.println(result()); // 2
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Avoid control-flow-changing finally blocks.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What if try throws IOException and finally throws IllegalStateException?
IllegalStateException from finally replaces the pending IOException, which is normally lost unless
explicitly preserved. Avoid throwing from finally; use try-with-resources for suppression.

pages.title: How does try-with-resources close multiple resources?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Exceptions and resource ownership
Q037  How does try-with-resources close multiple
resources?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Try-with-resources closes owned resources in reverse declaration order and preserves
body failures through suppression.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The later-created output closes first. If the body fails and close also fails, the body exception remains
primary and close exceptions are available through getSuppressed. Resources must implement
AutoCloseable.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
try (InputStream in = Files.newInputStream(source);
        OutputStream out = Files.newOutputStream(target)) {
       // Read and write bytes.
   }
   // Close order: out, then in
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Check getSuppressed() when diagnosing a body failure followed by failed cleanup.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What happens if creating the second resource fails?
Already-created first resource is closed even if construction of the second resource throws. The
original construction failure stays primary and closing failures are suppressed.

pages.title: How should you wrap an exception without losing useful information?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Exceptions and resource ownership
Q038  How should you wrap an exception without
losing useful information?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Wrap with meaningful context and keep the original cause so diagnosis remains
possible.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The outer message identifies the operation. The cause retains the lower-level stack trace and failure
reason. This sketch assumes ImportException has a constructor accepting a message and cause.

try {
       importBatch(batchId);
   } catch (IOException cause) {
       throw new ImportException("Failed batch " + batchId, cause);
   }
DRAW THE IDEA

Avoid blindly catching fatal JVM errors (such as OutOfMemoryError), cancellation, and stable
validation or business errors. Retry only documented transient failures with bounded attempts.

pages.title: Why should catch blocks be ordered from specific to general?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Exceptions and resource ownership
Q039  Why should catch blocks be ordered from
specific to general?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Order catch blocks from specific to general; otherwise a broader catch makes the
narrower one unreachable.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
A missing file matches the first catch. Other I/O failures match the second. Reversing these catches is a
compile-time error because IOException already covers FileNotFoundException.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
try {
       readFile(); // Declares IOException
   } catch (FileNotFoundException e) {
       System.out.println("Missing file");
   } catch (IOException e) {
       System.out.println("Other I/O failure");
   }
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: catch (IOException | FileNotFoundException e) is invalid because one is a subtype of the
other.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why can a multi-catch parameter not be reassigned?
A multi-catch variable has an implicitly final binding because its type represents several
alternatives. Reassignment would undermine type safety in that combined catch.

pages.title: What should you do with InterruptedException?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Exceptions and resource ownership
Q040  What should you do with InterruptedException?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Propagate interruption or restore the interrupt flag and stop the current operation
when propagation is unsuitable.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Blocking take reacts to interruption by throwing InterruptedException and clearing the status. Restoring
the flag preserves cancellation information for outer code. Returning stops this operation instead of
silently continuing.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
try {
       queue.take();
   } catch (InterruptedException e) {
       Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
       return;
   }
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Restoring the flag and immediately continuing the same blocking loop can create a busy
failure loop.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why does Future.cancel(true) not guarantee that a task stops?
cancel(true) requests interruption if running, but code may ignore it or be blocked in
uninterruptible work. Check task termination and resource cleanup separately.

pages.title: Why are generic collections invariant?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Generics, nested classes and annotations
Q041  Why are generic collections invariant?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Generics are invariant: List<Dog> is not a List<Animal>, even when Dog extends Animal.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
If unrestricted assignment were allowed, a Cat could enter a list promised to contain Dogs. The extends
wildcard permits reading Animal values, but blocks adding arbitrary Animal instances.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<Dog> dogs = new ArrayList<>();
   dogs.add(new Dog());
   // List<Animal> animals = dogs; // Compile-time error
   List<? extends Animal> animals = dogs;
   Animal first = animals.get(0); // Assumes a non-empty list
   // animals.add(new Cat());     // Compile-time error
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Inheritance between element types does not imply inheritance between their generic
containers.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Which value can you always add to a List<? extends Animal>?
You may add null to a List<? extends Animal> when null is supported. You cannot safely add a
particular Animal because its actual element subtype is unknown.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Generics, nested classes and annotations
Q042  What does PECS mean and when do you use
it?
20-SECOND ANSWER
PECS means producer extends, consumer super: use wildcards according to whether
you read or write values.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
src produces values that can be read as T. dst accepts T values even if it is a list of a supertype. This
allows integers to be copied safely into a Number list.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
static <T> void copy(List<? super T> dst,
                        List<? extends T> src) {
       for (T value : src) dst.add(value);
   }
   List<Integer> src = Arrays.asList(1, 2);
   List<Number> dst = new ArrayList<>();
   copy(dst, src);
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Reading from ? super T yields Object because the actual list may hold a wider type.

List<?> retains generic type checking: reading gives Object, and arbitrary additions are blocked.
Raw List suppresses checks and can introduce heap pollution.

pages.title: What is type erasure?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Generics, nested classes and annotations
Q043  What is type erasure?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Type erasure removes most generic type arguments from runtime object types while
the compiler inserts checks and casts.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Both objects have runtime class ArrayList. Their generic arguments enforce source-level safety, not
different runtime classes. Some generic signatures remain available as metadata; erasure does not
mean every type detail disappears.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<String> a = new ArrayList<>();
   List<Integer> b = new ArrayList<>();
   System.out.println(a.getClass() == b.getClass()); // true
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Erasure does not mean all generic declaration metadata disappears.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why can overloads f(List<String>) and f(List<Integer>) clash?
Both erase to the same JVM parameter type List, causing a name clash. Use different method
names or distinct parameter types.

CHAPTER 06 / Generics, nested classes and annotations
Q044  Why can you not use new T() or instanceof
List<String>?
20-SECOND ANSWER
An erased type parameter does not provide a concrete constructor or a runtime test for
parameterized element types.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The Supplier supplies the construction decision that new T cannot make. List<?> can test the runtime
list type, but the erased list object cannot prove that all elements are String.

       return factory.get();
   }
   StringBuilder b = create(StringBuilder::new);
   Object value = new ArrayList<String>();
   System.out.println(value instanceof List<?>); // true
   // value instanceof List<String> // Not permitted here
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: An unchecked cast does not validate every element of a collection.

A Class<T> token lets you validate, cast or construct types at runtime despite generic erasure, for
example T value = type.cast(raw).

pages.title: What causes heap pollution?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Generics, nested classes and annotations
Q045  What causes heap pollution?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Heap pollution occurs when a parameterized reference reaches an object containing
incompatible values, often through raw types.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The raw reference bypasses the generic add check. Reading through List<String> inserts a String cast,
which fails for Integer. Treat unchecked warnings as points requiring review.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
   List raw = names; // Unchecked/raw-type warning
   raw.add(42);     // Pollutes the list
   // String name = names.get(0); // ClassCastException
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: @SuppressWarnings and @SafeVarargs are promises about safety, not runtime enforcement.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why should a generic varargs method avoid writing incompatible elements into its
parameter array?
Generic varargs expose an array whose runtime component type may be less specific than the
generic promise. Storing the wrong element can cause heap pollution and later
ClassCastException.

enclosing object.

state. This enclosing relationship can unintentionally retain an outer object.

       class Inner {}

   Outer outer = new Outer();
   Outer.Inner i = outer.new Inner();

Watch out: An unnecessary enclosing reference can extend an object's lifetime.

A static nested node has no implicit reference to the enclosing instance, reducing accidental
retention and unnecessary per-node state.

Q047  What does effectively final mean for a lambda
capture?
20-SECOND ANSWER
A captured local variable must be final or effectively final; the referenced object's
contents can still change.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The reference out stays assigned to the same object, so capture is legal. The lambda changes that
object's contents. Effective finality does not make the list immutable or thread safe.

   Runnable r = () -> out.add("A");
   r.run();
   System.out.println(out); // [A]
   // out = new ArrayList<>(); // Would invalidate the capture
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Compiling a capture does not make the referenced mutable object thread safe.

Captured local variables must be final or effectively final. Use an AtomicInteger for genuine
shared mutation or compute a new stream result rather than incrementing a local.

pages.title: How do annotation retention and targets work?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Generics, nested classes and annotations
Q048  How do annotation retention and targets work?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Retention controls how long annotation metadata survives; target controls where the
annotation can appear.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
METHOD limits placement to methods. RUNTIME keeps the annotation available to reflection. SOURCE
would discard it during compilation; CLASS retains it in the class file without ordinary runtime reflection
access.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
   @Target(ElementType.METHOD)
   @interface Audited {}
   class Service { @Audited public void save() {} }
   boolean marked = Service.class.getMethod("save")
           .isAnnotationPresent(Audited.class); // true

pages.title: How do ArrayList and LinkedList compare?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Lists, sets, queues and ordering
Q049  How do ArrayList and LinkedList compare?
20-SECOND ANSWER
ArrayList is usually the default list; LinkedList helps specific iterator-local operations but
has costly indexed access and extra nodes.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
ArrayList uses a resizable array, giving fast indexed reads and good locality. LinkedList must walk to an
index. Repeated get(i) over all LinkedList positions can turn a traversal into quadratic work.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<Integer> values = new ArrayList<>();
   values.add(10);
   values.add(20);
   System.out.println(values.get(1)); // 20: constant-time access
   // On LinkedList, get(i) must traverse nodes.
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: LinkedList middle insertion is not constant time when you first locate the index.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why is ArrayDeque usually a better queue than LinkedList?
ArrayDeque is usually faster and has less node allocation for stack/queue operations. It disallows
null and is not thread-safe.

pages.title: How do HashSet, LinkedHashSet and TreeSet differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Lists, sets, queues and ordering
Q050  How do HashSet, LinkedHashSet and TreeSet
differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER
HashSet has no encounter-order guarantee, LinkedHashSet preserves insertion order,
and TreeSet uses sorted comparator order.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Both remove duplicates. LinkedHashSet retains each value's first insertion position. TreeSet sorts values
and uses comparison zero to decide whether an element is already present.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<Integer> input = Arrays.asList(3, 1, 3, 2);
   System.out.println(new LinkedHashSet<>(input)); // [3, 1, 2]
   System.out.println(new TreeSet<>(input));       // [1, 2, 3]
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: TreeSet uniqueness depends on comparison zero, not a separate equals check.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What happens when a key's ordering field changes after insertion?
TreeSet/TreeMap maintain search structure using the original ordering. Mutation may make
contains(), remove() and navigation inconsistent; use immutable sort keys.

pages.title: How do Comparable and Comparator differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Lists, sets, queues and ordering
Q051  How do Comparable and Comparator differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Comparable defines a type's natural order; Comparator supplies an external ordering
that can vary by use case.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
String's natural order is lexical, but this comparator first orders by length. A lexical tie breaker makes
equal-length ordering explicit without changing String's own implementation.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<String> names = new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList("Sai", "A", "Bo"));
   names.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(String::length)
                        .thenComparing(Comparator.naturalOrder()));
   System.out.println(names); // [A, Bo, Sai]
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Reversing an entire chained comparator also reverses its tie breakers.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you sort salary descending and name ascending?
Use Comparator.comparing(Employee::salary).reversed().thenComparing(Employee::name), adding
a final unique key if deterministic total ordering is required.

pages.title: What is a fail-fast iterator?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Lists, sets, queues and ordering
Q052  What is a fail-fast iterator?
20-SECOND ANSWER
A fail-fast iterator may detect unsupported structural changes; it is a bug detector, not
a thread-safety guarantee.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
iterator.remove coordinates with that iterator's expected modification state. Calling xs.remove directly
during traversal can invalidate it and cause ConcurrentModificationException, even in one thread.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<Integer> xs = new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3));
   Iterator<Integer> it = xs.iterator();
   while (it.hasNext()) {
       if (it.next() % 2 == 0) it.remove();
   }
   System.out.println(xs); // [1, 3]
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Absence of ConcurrentModificationException does not prove concurrent access is safe.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How does a ConcurrentHashMap iterator differ?
ConcurrentHashMap iterators are weakly consistent: they do not throw ordinary fail-fast
ConcurrentModificationException and may reflect some updates, but not a full snapshot.

pages.title: How do immutable collections differ from unmodifiable views?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Lists, sets, queues and ordering
Q053  How do immutable collections differ from
unmodifiable views?
20-SECOND ANSWER
An unmodifiable view blocks changes through the view; a structural immutable snapshot
also isolates later backing-list changes.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The wrapper reads the live source. List.copyOf preserves the accepted structure as a snapshot. Neither
approach deep-copies mutable elements; here String values are immutable.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<String> source = new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList("A"));
   List<String> view = Collections.unmodifiableList(source);
   List<String> snapshot = List.copyOf(source); // Java 10+
   source.add("B");
   System.out.println(view);     // [A, B]
   System.out.println(snapshot); // [A]
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: List.copyOf does not recursively copy mutable element objects.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you expose a safe snapshot when elements themselves are mutable?
Copy the collection and defensively copy each mutable element, or expose immutable DTO
snapshots. A shallow copy alone leaves mutable objects shared.

pages.title: What is the difference between a queue, a deque and a priority queue?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Lists, sets, queues and ordering
Q054  What is the difference between a queue, a
deque and a priority queue?
20-SECOND ANSWER
A queue usually models FIFO, a deque supports both ends, and a priority queue
removes the highest-priority element by its ordering.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
FIFO returns the oldest inserted value. The min-priority queue returns the smallest value. Its iterator is
not guaranteed to visit all values in sorted order.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Deque<Integer> fifo = new ArrayDeque<>();
   fifo.offer(3); fifo.offer(1);
   System.out.println(fifo.poll()); // 3
   Queue<Integer> priority = new PriorityQueue<>();
   priority.offer(3); priority.offer(1);
   System.out.println(priority.poll()); // 1
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: PriorityQueue iteration order is not a sorted result.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would a bounded BlockingQueue change producer behavior?
A bounded BlockingQueue blocks, times out or rejects when full, depending on put/offer policy.
That creates backpressure instead of unlimited memory growth.

pages.title: What risks come with subList and other collection views?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Lists, sets, queues and ordering
Q055  What risks come with subList and other
collection views?
20-SECOND ANSWER
subList is a backed view, so changes can affect its parent and parent structural
changes can invalidate the view.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The view shares the parent's storage and ownership. The copy has independent list structure. Do not
keep a view while making unsupported structural changes to its parent.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
List<String> all = new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList("A", "B", "C"));
   List<String> view = all.subList(1, 3);
   view.set(0, "X");
   System.out.println(all); // [A, X, C]
   List<String> copy = new ArrayList<>(view);
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A copy of a view still shares its mutable element objects.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Would you return a live view from a public API without documenting it?
Only if the API explicitly promises a live view and defines mutation, concurrency and lifecycle
behavior. Otherwise return a snapshot to prevent surprising changes.

pages.title: How do you choose a collection under interview constraints?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Lists, sets, queues and ordering
Q056  How do you choose a collection under interview
constraints?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Choose a collection from required ordering, access, duplicates, mutation, concurrency,
and memory limits.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The bounded min-heap keeps the two largest values, 7 and 9. It uses O(k) space and O(n log k) time.
Sorting all inputs would use more work when k is small; duplicate policy must also be stated.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
int k = 2;
   PriorityQueue<Integer> top = new PriorityQueue<>();
   for (int n : new int[]{7, 2, 9, 4}) {
       top.offer(n);
       if (top.size() > k) top.poll();
   }
   System.out.println(top.peek()); // 7: second-largest value
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: One collection does not optimize every workload.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What collection would support floor/ceiling queries on timestamps?
Use NavigableMap, commonly TreeMap<Instant,Value>, with floorEntry(), ceilingEntry() and range
views. Use a concurrent alternative when needed.

pages.title: How does HashMap put and get work?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 / HashMap and map design
Q057  How does HashMap put and get work?
20-SECOND ANSWER
HashMap uses a hash to select a bucket and equals to identify the matching key within
candidates.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
These strings collide in hashCode but are not equal. The map keeps separate entries and distinguishes
them through equality. A collision is normal; an inconsistent equals/hashCode contract is a defect.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
   System.out.println("Aa".hashCode() == "BB".hashCode()); // true
   map.put("Aa", 1);
   map.put("BB", 2);
   System.out.println(map.get("Aa")); // 1
   System.out.println(map.size());    // 2
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A hash collision does not mean the map overwrites an unequal key.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why are capacity values powers of two in the implementation?
Power-of-two capacity lets HashMap choose a bucket with (capacity - 1) & hash and supports
efficient resizing. This is an implementation detail, not an API guarantee.

pages.title: What changed in HashMap collision handling in Java 8?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 / HashMap and map design
Q058  What changed in HashMap collision handling in
Java 8?
20-SECOND ANSWER
Java 8 HashMap can treeify heavily collided buckets, but resizing and implementation
thresholds affect when it does so.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
These are implementation constants, not configurable API guarantees or legal variable declarations
here. A threshold of 8 should not be memorized as an unconditional 'the eighth put creates a tree' rule.
Table size and insertion path matter.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
// OpenJDK HashMap implementation constants:
   TREEIFY_THRESHOLD = 8
   UNTREEIFY_THRESHOLD = 6
   MIN_TREEIFY_CAPACITY = 64
   // A small table generally resizes instead of treeifying.
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Avoid promising that every put at exactly eight entries always creates a tree.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Is every adversarial equal-hash lookup guaranteed logarithmic for arbitrary key types?
No. Tree bins have thresholds and comparable-key behaviors; arbitrary hostile collisions do not
guarantee logarithmic behavior in every case.

pages.title: How do load factor and capacity affect resizing?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 / HashMap and map design
Q059  How do load factor and capacity affect
resizing?
20-SECOND ANSWER
A HashMap resizes when its size exceeds the threshold determined by capacity and load
factor.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
A lower load factor spends more space to reduce average bucket occupancy. Pre-sizing for expected
entries can avoid repeated growth. OpenJDK rounds capacity to a power of two; constructor allocation
is normally lazy.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Map<Integer, String> map = new HashMap<>(16, 0.75f);
   // Once allocated, capacity 16 usually has threshold 12.
   for (int i = 0; i < 13; i++) map.put(i, "v");
   // The thirteenth mapping exceeds 12 and triggers growth.
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: new HashMap<>(100) does not mean exactly 100 buckets or a maximum of 100 entries.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why can iteration cost depend on both size and capacity?
HashMap iteration walks its internal capacity table and entries, so excess capacity can increase
iteration work even when few mappings are stored.

pages.title: Can HashMap contain null keys and values?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 / HashMap and map design
Q060  Can HashMap contain null keys and values?
20-SECOND ANSWER
HashMap permits one null key and null values; get alone cannot distinguish a missing
key from a null mapping.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Both lookups return null, but containsKey identifies the stored mapping. A null key is permitted once
because keys are unique. This differs from ConcurrentHashMap's no-null contract.

   System.out.println(map.get("missing"));   // null
   System.out.println(map.containsKey("x")); // true
   map.put(null, "default");
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: ConcurrentHashMap disallows null keys and null values.

It invokes the function when the key is absent or currently maps to null. A non-null existing value

pages.title: How do HashMap, LinkedHashMap and TreeMap differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 / HashMap and map design
Q061  How do HashMap, LinkedHashMap and
TreeMap differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER
HashMap supports general lookup, LinkedHashMap adds encounter order, and TreeMap
provides sorted keys and range operations.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
floorEntry finds the greatest key not above 15. LinkedHashMap preserves insertion order by default and
can optionally track access order. HashMap supplies neither guarantee.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
NavigableMap<Integer, String> prices = new TreeMap<>();
   prices.put(10, "old"); prices.put(20, "new");
   System.out.println(prices.floorEntry(15)); // 10=old
   Map<String, Integer> ordered = new LinkedHashMap<>();
   ordered.put("B", 2); ordered.put("A", 1);
   System.out.println(ordered.keySet()); // [B, A]
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: TreeMap comparison determines key equivalence.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What changes when accessOrder is true in LinkedHashMap?
An access (such as get) moves an entry to the end of access order, enabling LRU eviction.
Iteration order now reflects use, not only insertion.

pages.title: How do putIfAbsent, computeIfAbsent and merge differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 / HashMap and map design
Q062  How do putIfAbsent, computeIfAbsent and
merge differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER
putIfAbsent supplies a value, computeIfAbsent derives a missing value, and merge
combines an incoming value with an existing one.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
merge sums 1 with the existing 1. computeIfAbsent calls its function because kafka has no non-null
mapping. Atomicity depends on the implementation; HashMap does not make these concurrent
operations safe.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Map<String, Integer> counts = new HashMap<>();
   counts.putIfAbsent("java", 1);
   counts.merge("java", 1, Integer::sum);
   counts.computeIfAbsent("kafka", k -> k.length());
   System.out.println(counts.get("java"));  // 2
   System.out.println(counts.get("kafka")); // 5
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Do not perform recursive updates on the same map inside a remapping function.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Why should a concurrent remapping function be short and side-effect conscious?
It can execute under map coordination or be retried depending on API. Keep it short and avoid
external side effects, blocking calls and recursive updates.

pages.title: Why is HashMap unsafe for concurrent updates?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 / HashMap and map design
Q063  Why is HashMap unsafe for concurrent
updates?
20-SECOND ANSWER
HashMap has no concurrent-update safety; visibility and compound operations need
external coordination or a concurrent alternative.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Using get followed by put allows two threads to read the same old value and overwrite one increment.
ConcurrentHashMap.compute coordinates one key's update, unlike the same sequence on a plain map.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
ConcurrentHashMap<String, Integer> counts = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
   counts.put("java", 0);
   counts.compute("java", (k, v) -> v + 1);
   // Atomic per-key update; repeating from two tasks preserves both updates.
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Safe concurrent reading requires a properly published map that is not being unsafely
mutated.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Would Collections.synchronizedMap make an entire iteration safe automatically?
No. Synchronize on the map around the complete traversal and use its documented iterator
discipline, or take a safe snapshot first.

pages.title: How would you implement a bounded LRU cache in core Java?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 / HashMap and map design
Q064  How would you implement a bounded LRU
cache in core Java?
20-SECOND ANSWER
An access-order LinkedHashMap can implement size-bounded LRU eviction; concurrent
use needs synchronization.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
get(1) makes key 1 recently accessed. Inserting 3 exceeds the limit, so the least recently used key 2 is
removed. Reads can modify access order and must be included in any locking policy.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Map<Integer, String> cache = new LinkedHashMap<Integer, String>(16, 0.75f, true) {
       @Override protected boolean removeEldestEntry(Map.Entry<Integer, String> e) {
           return size() > 2;
       }
   };
   cache.put(1, "A"); cache.put(2, "B"); cache.get(1);
   cache.put(3, "C");
   System.out.println(cache.keySet()); // [1, 3]
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: A basic LRU exercise does not implement TTL, request coalescing or concurrent cache
guarantees.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you stop several threads from loading the same missing key?
Use atomic per-key loading, such as ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent when appropriate, or
cache a shared Future per key. Define failure, expiry and duplicate-load policy.

pages.title: How does ConcurrentHashMap differ from synchronizedMap?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 / Concurrent collections
Q065  How does ConcurrentHashMap differ from
synchronizedMap?
20-SECOND ANSWER
ConcurrentHashMap provides coordinated concurrent operations; synchronizedMap
serializes operations through its wrapper's lock.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Each compute is an atomic update for x. With synchronizedMap, multi-call check-then-update logic still
needs an outer synchronized block on the wrapper. Its iteration also requires documented external
synchronization.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
ConcurrentHashMap<String, Integer> counts = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
   counts.compute("x", (k, v) -> v == null ? 1 : v + 1);
   counts.compute("x", (k, v) -> v == null ? 1 : v + 1);
   System.out.println(counts.get("x")); // 2
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Java 8+ ConcurrentHashMap should not be explained as a fixed array of the old Java 7
segments.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Which option is simplest for a small map with one compound invariant?
A single synchronized block or lock around the whole map operation is often simplest. It protects
the compound invariant without complex per-entry coordination.

pages.title: What does a weakly consistent iterator guarantee?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 / Concurrent collections
Q066  What does a weakly consistent iterator
guarantee?
20-SECOND ANSWER
A weakly consistent iterator tolerates concurrent changes without promising a whole-
collection snapshot.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Concurrent updates do not cause the ordinary fail-fast behavior of a HashMap iterator. Traversal can
observe some changes without presenting every entry from one single instant.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
ConcurrentHashMap<Integer, String> map = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
   map.put(1, "A");
   Iterator<Integer> it = map.keySet().iterator();
   map.put(2, "B");
   while (it.hasNext()) System.out.println(it.next());
   // Do not promise whether this iteration observes key 2.
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Weak consistency does not mean arbitrary memory corruption or a stable snapshot.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you obtain a transactionally consistent total across entries?
Use one lock/transaction covering the entries or an immutable snapshot published atomically.
Iterating a concurrent map alone is not a transactional snapshot.

pages.title: Why does ConcurrentHashMap reject null?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 / Concurrent collections
Q067  Why does ConcurrentHashMap reject null?
20-SECOND ANSWER
ConcurrentHashMap forbids null keys and values so null retrieval has an unambiguous
absence meaning.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
In a changing map, a separate containsKey check could observe a different state from get. Rejecting
null values makes the individual get result easier to interpret.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
ConcurrentHashMap<String, String> map = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
   System.out.println(map.get("x")); // null: no observed mapping
   // map.put("x", null);           // NullPointerException
   // map.put(null, "A");           // NullPointerException
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: An absent observation can become outdated immediately after the operation.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Does a non-null get result imply the entire map is in one consistent snapshot?
No. The returned mapping is safely obtained, but other keys may change before or after it. A
global consistent snapshot needs another mechanism.

pages.title: When is CopyOnWriteArrayList appropriate?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 / Concurrent collections
Q068  When is CopyOnWriteArrayList appropriate?
20-SECOND ANSWER
CopyOnWriteArrayList suits frequent reads and rare writes; each iterator traverses a
structural snapshot.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The iterator retains the old array. The write creates a new array containing A and B for later readers.
Copying every write is expensive, and mutable element state is not frozen.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
CopyOnWriteArrayList<String> xs = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
   xs.add("A");
   Iterator<String> it = xs.iterator();
   xs.add("B");
   while (it.hasNext()) System.out.println(it.next()); // A only
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: It is a poor default for a large list with frequent writes.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Can mutating a listener object still require synchronization?
Yes. CopyOnWriteArrayList protects its array structure, not the mutable listener object's fields.
Synchronize those fields or make the listener immutable.

pages.title: How does BlockingQueue help producer- consumer code?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 / Concurrent collections
Q069  How does BlockingQueue help producer-
consumer code?
20-SECOND ANSWER
A bounded BlockingQueue coordinates producer-consumer handoff and applies
backpressure when full.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
put waits for capacity; take waits for an item. offer without a timeout returns immediately. A real worker
loop must also define interruption and termination rather than wait forever after producers finish.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
BlockingQueue<String> queue = new ArrayBlockingQueue<>(1);
   queue.put("A");
   System.out.println(queue.offer("B")); // false: full
   System.out.println(queue.take());     // A
   queue.put("B");                       // Now space exists
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: An unbounded queue can hide overload until memory is exhausted.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How does a poison-pill protocol change with several consumers?
Use one poison marker per consumer or a documented shutdown/coordinator protocol; one
marker may stop only one consumer and leave others waiting.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 / Concurrent collections
Q070  Should you use AtomicLong or LongAdder for
counters?
20-SECOND ANSWER
AtomicLong fits exact atomic counter operations; LongAdder fits highly contended
statistics whose concurrent sum may be approximate.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
AtomicLong exposes a single atomic current value and compare-and-set. LongAdder spreads
contention across internal cells. Its sum is not an atomic snapshot of updates occurring concurrently.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
AtomicLong exact = new AtomicLong();
   System.out.println(exact.incrementAndGet()); // 1
   LongAdder metric = new LongAdder();
   metric.increment(); metric.increment();
   System.out.println(metric.sum()); // 2 when no updates overlap
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: LongAdder is unsuitable for reserving unique sequential identifiers with sum().
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
How would you enforce a strict maximum number of admitted requests?
Acquire a semaphore permit or an atomic admission token before accepting, release it exactly
once on terminal completion, and define rejection behavior.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 / Concurrent collections
Q071  What are the limits of computeIfAbsent for
cache loading?
20-SECOND ANSWER
computeIfAbsent is useful for short atomic initialization, but slow loading needs explicit
execution, failure, and cache-lifecycle policies.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
Creating a LongAdder is short and local. A remote call can hold up competing map updates and
should not be hidden inside a long mapping computation. Failed loads and eviction require separate
decisions.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> counts = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
   counts.computeIfAbsent("java", k -> new LongAdder()).increment();
   // For slow I/O, reserve an in-flight future atomically,
   // then perform the load outside the map computation.
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Do not equate one atomic insertion with an end-to-end exactly-once external call.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
What happens when the loader throws and the next request retries?
A failed computeIfAbsent does not establish a value; a later caller may invoke the loader again.
Ensure loaders are idempotent and handle repeated failure appropriately.

CHAPTER 09 / Concurrent collections
Q072  Can a concurrent collection protect mutable
values?

A concurrent map protects its mappings, not arbitrary mutable objects stored as values.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The map safely publishes the list reference. ArrayList's internal array and size are still mutable without
synchronization. Replacing values with immutable snapshots is another possible design.

ConcurrentHashMap<String, List<String>> map = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
   map.put("team", new ArrayList<>());
   // Concurrent map.get("team").add(...) is still unsafe.
   // Choose a concurrent value collection or protect every access.

Watch out: Replacing one map value atomically differs from mutating a value in place.

No. compute coordinates the map entry update, but readers later mutating or reading a shared
ArrayList require their own thread-safe protocol.

pages.title: What makes an interface functional?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 10 / Lambdas, functional interfaces and Optional
Q073  What makes an interface functional?
20-SECOND ANSWER
A functional interface has one abstract method contract; default and static methods do
not count toward that total.
WHY IT WORKS · EASY EXPLANATION
The lambda implements apply. The default method already has an implementation, so it creates no
additional abstract obligation. @FunctionalInterface asks the compiler to check the intended contract.
JAVA EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
@FunctionalInterface
   interface Calculator {
       int apply(int a, int b);
       default String name() { return "calculator"; }
   }
   Calculator add = (a, b) -> a + b;
   System.out.println(add.apply(2, 3)); // 5
DRAW THE IDEA
Watch out: Two separately named abstract methods normally prevent lambda targeting.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP - ANSWERED
Can a functional interface have several default methods?
Yes. Only one abstract method counts toward the functional-interface requirement; it may also
contain multiple default and static methods.
