pages.title: What does newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor do?
pages.fullText:
Q073 · JAVA 21: VIRTUAL-THREAD FUNDAMENTALS · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q073 What does newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor do?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
It starts a new virtual thread for each submitted task; it is not a fixed
reusable pool of virtual workers.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · What does newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor do
Request / task → Virtual thread → Carrier / result
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
try (var executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
Future<Integer> result = executor.submit(() -> 42);
System.out.println(result.get());
}
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
ExecutorService implements AutoCloseable from Java 19, so this permanent Java 21 form closes the
executor and waits for termination. Define task lifetime and failure handling. Do not pool virtual
threads merely to reuse cheap thread instances.
COMMON MISTAKE
Unbounded thread creation still needs bounded resource admission.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How do you cap database work without pooling virtual threads?
CLEAR ANSWER
Use a semaphore, database pool or a bounded admission queue around scarce resources; do
not turn virtual threads themselves into a fixed worker pool.

pages.fullText:
Q074 · JAVA 21: VIRTUAL-THREAD FUNDAMENTALS · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q074 Are virtual threads daemon threads and why does
that matter?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
They are daemon threads; their presence alone does not keep the JVM
alive when no non-daemon thread remains.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · Are virtual threads daemon threads and why does that matter
Request / task → Virtual thread → Carrier / result
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
Thread worker = Thread.startVirtualThread(() -> doWork());
worker.join(); // explicit lifecycle owner waits
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
A fire-and-forget virtual thread can be abandoned when the process exits. Joining, executor
ownership or a structured scope keeps responsibility visible. A virtual thread's priority is fixed, and
thread-group assumptions differ from platform-thread tuning.
COMMON MISTAKE
Starting a thread is not a completion or delivery guarantee.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Who owns work during application shutdown?
CLEAR ANSWER
Virtual threads are daemon threads, so process exit does not wait for them alone. The owning
service must join/cancel outstanding tasks during orderly shutdown.
Source chapter 15 · Java version and feature status should be checked for the stated release.

Q076 How does synchronized pinning differ between Java
21 and 25?

In Java 21, blocking inside a held monitor can pin a virtual thread; Java

strategy may help. On 25, do not repeat the old blanket recommendation to replace every
synchronized block. Native/foreign interactions still require review.

Reduced pinning does not remove serialization caused by holding the lock.

Compare JFR virtual-thread pinning events and carrier utilization with thread dumps and
monitor-blocked time; Java 25 changed monitor pinning behavior relative to 21.

pages.fullText:
Q077 · JAVA 21: RESOURCES, PINNING AND CANCELLATION · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q077 How should ThreadLocal be used with virtual
threads?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
Use it for genuinely thread-local state, but avoid per-thread expensive
resource caches across very large numbers of short-lived threads.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How should ThreadLocal be used with virtual threads
Many tasks → Limits + cancellation → Safe cleanup
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
ThreadLocal<RequestContext> context = new ThreadLocal<>();
try { context.set(value); handle(); }
finally { context.remove(); }
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Virtual threads support thread-local variables, yet millions of threads can multiply stored resources.
A thread-local JDBC connection is not automatically a good design. ScopedValue, final in 25, fits
some bounded read-only context flows.
COMMON MISTAKE
Virtual threads do not automatically propagate arbitrary request context.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Which resources should be shared or pooled independently?

Q078 · JAVA 21: RESOURCES, PINNING AND CANCELLATION · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q078 How do you bound scarce work when threads are
cheap?

Use resource-level limits such as connection-pool capacity, semaphores
and bounded admission, independent of virtual-thread creation.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How do you bound scarce work when threads are cheap
Many tasks → Limits + cancellation → Safe cleanup
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
Semaphore permits = new Semaphore(20);
permits.acquire();
try { callDownstream(); }
finally { permits.release(); }

The semaphore limits concurrent use, not total queued requests. Add a queue/admission and
deadline policy to bound memory and waiting. Acquiring before entering try ensures release is
paired with a successful acquisition.

A semaphore alone can leave an unlimited backlog.

When should a request be rejected rather than wait?

capacity; return an explicit overload outcome such as HTTP 429/503.

pages.title: Why must interrupt handling remain cooperative?
pages.fullText:
Q079 · JAVA 21: RESOURCES, PINNING AND CANCELLATION · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q079 Why must interrupt handling remain cooperative?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
An interrupt is a cancellation signal that APIs/tasks must honor; it is not
forced rollback or immediate thread termination.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · Why must interrupt handling remain cooperative
Many tasks → Limits + cancellation → Safe cleanup
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
try { Thread.sleep(1000); }
catch (InterruptedException e) {
Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
return;
}
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
sleep clears interrupt status when throwing, so restoring it is useful when the boundary returns
rather than rethrows. Other APIs have different interruption behavior. Ensure cleanup and an
appropriate return/propagation strategy.
COMMON MISTAKE
Swallowing interruption can delay shutdown or scope close.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What if a blocking native call cannot be interrupted?
CLEAR ANSWER
Use an operation-level timeout and close/cancel external resources when supported. A blocked
native call may require process or driver-specific recovery.
Source chapter 16 · Java version and feature status should be checked for the stated release.

pages.title: How should a deadline cover several parallel downstream calls?
pages.fullText:
Q080 · JAVA 21: RESOURCES, PINNING AND CANCELLATION · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q080 How should a deadline cover several parallel
downstream calls?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
Give the overall operation an explicit time budget and cancellation/
cleanup ownership, instead of independent unlimited child work.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How should a deadline cover several parallel downstream calls
Many tasks → Limits + cancellation → Safe cleanup
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
Request budget: 500 ms
Reserve response/cleanup time; children share the remaining deadline.
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
CompletableFuture composition alone does not cancel every sibling when one fails. Executor close
or structured scope close can wait for uncooperative tasks, so operation-level timeouts also matter.
Known remote rejection and unknown side-effect outcome are distinct.
COMMON MISTAKE
Completing a timeout future does not prove children stopped.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How would you prevent leaked work after the caller leaves?
CLEAR ANSWER
Pass a shared absolute deadline/cancellation signal to children, cancel unfinished work on
departure and wait for structured cleanup where possible.

pages.title: How do record patterns differ from ordinary instanceof patterns?
pages.fullText:
Q081 · JAVA 21: RECORD PATTERNS AND PATTERN SWITCH · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q081 How do record patterns differ from ordinary
instanceof patterns?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
They deconstruct record components into nested patterns rather than only
bind the entire matched object.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How do record patterns differ from ordinary instanceof patterns
Record / selector → Pattern / guard → Matched action
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
record Point(int x, int y) {}
if (value instanceof Point(int x, int y)) {
System.out.println(x + y);
}
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
The pattern follows the record's declared components and their types. A null record does not match.
Deconstruction is a matching feature, not a mutable destructuring assignment or arbitrary getter
convention for every class.
COMMON MISTAKE
A record pattern does not match any class with similar field names.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How would a nested record be matched?
CLEAR ANSWER
A nested record can be matched with nested components, e.g. case Box(Point(int
x,int y) p) -> ... using the appropriate record component structure.

pages.title: What does pattern matching for switch add?
pages.fullText:
Q082 · JAVA 21: RECORD PATTERNS AND PATTERN SWITCH · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q082 What does pattern matching for switch add?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
It lets switch match suitable type/record patterns and express guarded
alternatives, with exhaustiveness and dominance rules.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · What does pattern matching for switch add
Record / selector → Pattern / guard → Matched action
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
String label = switch (value) {
case null -> "missing";
case String s -> "text:" + s;
case Integer n -> "number:" + n;
default -> "other";
};
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
This Object-oriented switch is permanent Java 21 syntax. Each pattern variable belongs to its
matching arm. The explicit null arm chooses missing-value behavior rather than relying on a default
that does not itself match null.
COMMON MISTAKE
default is not a substitute for case null.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What happens when the null case is omitted?
CLEAR ANSWER
For a switch selector of reference type, omitting case null means a null value typically
causes a NullPointerException, rather than matching default.

pages.title: What is dominance in a pattern switch?
pages.fullText:
Q083 · JAVA 21: RECORD PATTERNS AND PATTERN SWITCH · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q083 What is dominance in a pattern switch?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
An earlier case that covers every value a later case can match makes the
later case unreachable under the language rules.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · What is dominance in a pattern switch
Record / selector → Pattern / guard → Matched action
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
// Invalid order:
case CharSequence c -> "sequence";
case String s -> "text";
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Every String is a CharSequence, so the later String arm is dominated. Put more-specific alternatives
first when appropriate. Guard analysis follows defined language rules; the compiler does not prove
every arbitrary business predicate.
COMMON MISTAKE
Case ordering is part of semantics, not only presentation.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Why can two differently guarded cases need deliberate order?
CLEAR ANSWER
A general case can dominate a narrower one. Put narrower or guarded cases first and confirm
that each later case is reachable.

pages.title: How do when guards work?
pages.fullText:
Q084 · JAVA 21: RECORD PATTERNS AND PATTERN SWITCH · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q084 How do when guards work?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
A guard adds a Boolean condition after a pattern match, letting one type
have several behavior cases.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How do when guards work
Record / selector → Pattern / guard → Matched action
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
case String s when s.isBlank() -> "blank";
case String s -> "text";
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
The blank case only succeeds after String matching and its guard are true; the next String case
handles the remaining strings. Guard expressions should have clear failure/side-effect behavior.
They do not replace null handling.
COMMON MISTAKE
The Java 21 guard keyword is when, not the older preview syntax.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Where should the unguarded String case go?
CLEAR ANSWER
Place the unguarded case String s after the specific guarded case String s
when ..., otherwise it dominates the guarded one.

pages.title: How does exhaustiveness help with sealed models?
pages.fullText:
Q085 · JAVA 21: RECORD PATTERNS AND PATTERN SWITCH · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q085 How does exhaustiveness help with sealed models?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
A switch covering all permitted alternatives can omit a general default and
force source updates when the modeled alternatives change.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How does exhaustiveness help with sealed models
Record / selector → Pattern / guard → Matched action
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
String describe(Outcome outcome) {
return switch (outcome) {
case Accepted a -> "id=" + a.id();
case Rejected r -> r.reason();
};
}
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
This example assumes the two-type sealed model and a non-null input contract. Separate
compilation/version skew can still produce an unanticipated runtime alternative and a
MatchException. Recompilation catches a newly permitted alternative.
COMMON MISTAKE
Compile-time exhaustiveness is not immunity to incompatible binary evolution.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Should a domain error be encoded as null or as a subtype?
CLEAR ANSWER
Use a sealed subtype for a domain error rather than using null. Exhaustive switching can then
force callers to handle every defined outcome.

pages.title: What is a sequenced collection?
pages.fullText:
Q086 · JAVA 21: SEQUENCED COLLECTIONS · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q086 What is a sequenced collection?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
It is a collection with a defined encounter order and common first/last/
reversed operations under its supported mutation contract.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · What is a sequenced collection
Ordered collection → Sequenced view → Front / back
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
List<String> names = new ArrayList<>(List.of("A","B"));
System.out.println(names.getFirst()); // A
System.out.println(names.getLast()); // B
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
List gains these operations through the new hierarchy in 21. An ordered collection is not necessarily
sorted; its order can come from insertion or a comparator. Empty endpoint access throws
NoSuchElementException.
COMMON MISTAKE
HashSet does not gain a meaningful encounter-order guarantee.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What is the difference between sorted and insertion order?
CLEAR ANSWER
Sorted order follows a comparator; insertion order follows when elements entered a sequence.
A SequencedCollection specifies encounter order, not necessarily sorting.

pages.title: Is List.reversed a copied list?
pages.fullText:
Q087 · JAVA 21: SEQUENCED COLLECTIONS · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q087 Is List.reversed a copied list?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
No. It provides a reverse-ordered view whose backing relationship and
mutation support follow the original list.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · Is List.reversed a copied list
Ordered collection → Sequenced view → Front / back
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
List<String> source = new ArrayList<>(List.of("A","B"));
List<String> reversed = source.reversed();
source.add("C"); // reversed now observes [C, B, A]
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Do not assume a snapshot. Supported writes through a view can affect the backing collection, while
unmodifiable sources restrict mutation. Use an explicit copy if later changes must be isolated.
COMMON MISTAKE
Reversed order is not structural immutability.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How would you produce a reverse-ordered snapshot?
CLEAR ANSWER
Copy the reversed view using List.copyOf(source.reversed()) if you want a stable
structural snapshot rather than a backed view.

sets?

They can explicitly position elements in supporting implementations, while

insertion.

contract instead of assuming all sequenced collections are deques.

A common interface does not mean every mutator is supported.

CLEAR ANSWER
TreeSet follows comparator ordering, so it cannot arbitrarily move a value to the first or last
encounter position; positional modifications are unsupported.

pages.title: How does an unmodifiable sequenced view differ from a stable result?
pages.fullText:
Q090 · JAVA 21: SEQUENCED COLLECTIONS · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q090 How does an unmodifiable sequenced view differ
from a stable result?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
It blocks supported mutation through that reference but can still reflect
changes in the underlying collection and mutable elements.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How does an unmodifiable sequenced view differ from a stable result
Ordered collection → Sequenced view → Front / back
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
SequencedCollection<String> source = new ArrayList<>(List.of("A"));
var view = Collections.unmodifiableSequencedCollection(source);
source.add("B"); // view observes the new element
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Read-only access, snapshot structure and deep immutability are three separate guarantees. Choose
the one the caller needs and document alias ownership. Endpoint methods do not alter this
distinction.
COMMON MISTAKE
Naming a result immutable cannot strengthen its backing contract.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Which guarantee does List.copyOf add?
CLEAR ANSWER

pages.title: Does binding a mutable object make it immutable?
pages.fullText:
Q103 · JAVA 25: SCOPED CONTEXT AND STABLE VALUES · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q103 Does binding a mutable object make it immutable?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
No. The binding is stable for its scope, but shared contents need
immutability or proper synchronization.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · Does binding a mutable object make it immutable
Trusted request → Scoped context → Bound lifetime
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
ScopedValue<List<String>> DATA = ScopedValue.newInstance();
ScopedValue.where(DATA,new ArrayList<>()).run(() -> {
DATA.get().add("A"); // mutates the bound object
});
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Nested rebinding can temporarily select another value without mutating the outer binding. Prefer
small immutable context records where the use case permits. Shared structured children must not
race on a mutable payload.

Bounded lifetime and thread-safe contents are different guarantees.

What should a request-context record contain?
CLEAR ANSWER
Use an immutable record of request ID, tenant ID and safe tracing metadata; do not hide
mutable sessions, secrets or shared state inside it.

pages.title: How does StableValue differ from a final field?
pages.fullText:
Q104 · JAVA 25: SCOPED CONTEXT AND STABLE VALUES · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q104 How does StableValue differ from a final field?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
A final field is assigned during construction/initialization; a StableValue
holder can acquire its contents later and then keep that association fixed.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How does StableValue differ from a final field
Trusted request → Scoped context → Bound lifetime
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
// Java 25 PREVIEW:
private final StableValue<String> label = StableValue.of();
String value = label.orElseSet(() -> "created");
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
The holder provides an initialization contract rather than making referenced contents deeply
immutable. It can fit deferred expensive state, but lifetime/resource ownership still needs design.
Permanent API code must not use it without preview opt-in.
COMMON MISTAKE
StableValue is not a refreshable cache.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How would you represent changing configuration instead?
CLEAR ANSWER
Use a reloadable config holder with explicit versioning or an atomic reference for changing
values; StableValue models once-initialized state, not live reconfiguration.

pages.title: · JAVA 25: SCOPED CONTEXT AND STABLE VALUES · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Q105 How should StableValue initialization failures be
pages.fullText:
Q105 · JAVA 25: SCOPED CONTEXT AND STABLE VALUES · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q105 How should StableValue initialization failures be
interpreted?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
If the supplier throws, the exception propagates and the holder remains
unset; a later call can retry. After successful initialization, the established
value is stable.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How should StableValue initialization failures be interpreted
Trusted request → Scoped context → Bound lifetime
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
// Java 25 PREVIEW:
String value = holder.orElseSet(() -> createValue());
// If creation throws, the holder remains unset; a later call may retry.
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
orElseSet coordinates successful initialization under races, while a precompute-then-trySet pattern
can create several discarded objects. Supplier effects should be safe for the documented retry/
failure behavior. Stable association does not deduplicate an external side effect.
COMMON MISTAKE
'Exactly one business effect ever' is not this holder's guarantee.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Who closes a successfully initialized resource?
CLEAR ANSWER
Failed initialization may be retried and may already have side effects. The owning component
must explicitly close any resource produced by a successful initializer.

pages.title: How do Stream Gatherers differ from Collectors?
pages.fullText:
Q106 · JAVA 25: INHERITED APIS AND NEW SECURITY APIS · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q106 How do Stream Gatherers differ from Collectors?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
A gatherer defines an intermediate stream transformation; a collector
performs a terminal mutable reduction.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How do Stream Gatherers differ from Collectors
API / runtime → Platform feature → Compatibility
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
// Permanent from Java 24, available in 25:
var windows = Stream.of(1,2,3,4,5)
.gather(Gatherers.windowFixed(2)).toList();
// [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]]
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Gatherers support transformations beyond ordinary one-to-one map, including stateful operations.
Collector and gatherer state/combination contracts are different. The API is not available in Java 21
without a different library/design.
COMMON MISTAKE
Gatherers are not newly finalized in 25.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Why is windowing an intermediate operation?
CLEAR ANSWER
A gatherer can process a stream into intermediate windows/results before downstream
operations; a collector is terminal and produces a final result.

pages.title: How do windowFixed and windowSliding differ?
pages.fullText:
Q107 · JAVA 25: INHERITED APIS AND NEW SECURITY APIS · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q107 How do windowFixed and windowSliding differ?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
Fixed windows partition the sequence into batches; sliding windows overlap
by moving across adjacent elements.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How do windowFixed and windowSliding differ
API / runtime → Platform feature → Compatibility
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
Stream.of(1,2,3,4,5).gather(Gatherers.windowFixed(3)).toList();
// [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]]
Stream.of(1,2,3,4,5).gather(Gatherers.windowSliding(3)).toList();
// [[1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4], [3, 4, 5]]
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
These permanent 24+ methods make batch and rolling-window semantics explicit. Empty input emits
no window. Nonempty input shorter than a sliding window emits one partial window containing all
input values. Windowing alone does not apply a remote concurrency limit.
COMMON MISTAKE
Batch size and maximum in-flight work are separate controls.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Which form fits a three-reading moving average?
CLEAR ANSWER
A sliding three-reading moving average uses windowSliding(3); fixed windows would skip
overlapping triples.
Source chapter 22 · Java version and feature status should be checked for the stated release.
JAVA 8 / 11 / 17 / 21 / 25 • PREMIUM STUDY NOTES 136

pages.fullText:

Q108 What does the Class-File API provide?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
The permanent Java 24 API, inherited by 25, supports reading, generating
and transforming Java class files with a standard model.

concurrency and agent-tool tests after instrumentation.

pages.title: What does an Arena control in the final FFM API?
pages.fullText:
Q109 · JAVA 25: INHERITED APIS AND NEW SECURITY APIS · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q109 What does an Arena control in the final FFM API?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
It controls lifetime and access rules for allocated foreign memory;
segments cannot be used freely after their arena is closed.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · What does an Arena control in the final FFM API
API / runtime → Platform feature → Compatibility
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
try (Arena arena = Arena.ofConfined()) {
MemorySegment segment = arena.allocate(8);
segment.set(ValueLayout.JAVA_LONG,0,42L);
}
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
This is permanent 22+ code, not permanent Java 21. A confined arena imposes thread-access rules;
shared arenas have a different concurrency contract. Native pointer/function misuse can still violate
assumptions outside the managed checks.
COMMON MISTAKE
An arena is not a garbage-collected Java byte array.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What fails if another thread uses a confined segment?
CLEAR ANSWER
Using a confined segment from a different thread violates its ownership rules and fails; choose
an arena with appropriate sharing/lifetime where required.

HotSpot's compact-header mode reduces header size on supported 64-bit
configurations and becomes a product feature in 25, after experimental
status in 24.

collector interactions matter. Product status does not mean universally enabled or universally
beneficial.

Q117 Why use --release instead of only -source and
-target?

--release aligns supported source syntax, bytecode target and documented

Q118 · MIGRATION: BUILD TARGETS AND RELEASE DISCIPLINE · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q118 How do you compile and run preview code correctly?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
Use the matching JDK and release-specific --enable-preview at
compilation and runtime; preview class files are tied to that release.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How do you compile and run preview code correctly
Build artifact → Release target → Compatibility tests
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
javac --release 25 --enable-preview Lab19.java
java --enable-preview Lab19
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
JDK 25 preview code must be built/run as the supported 25 preview, not treated as a portable 21
feature. Incubator modules need their own module flags. Pin release-specific examples so changing
API shapes do not silently mix.
COMMON MISTAKE
A newer JVM does not generally accept another release's preview class files.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How would CI keep permanent and preview examples separate?
CLEAR ANSWER
Build preview examples in a separate target-JDK profile and run with --enable-preview on
the matching release; keep shipping code on permanent features unless approved.

pages.fullText:
Q119 · MIGRATION: BUILD TARGETS AND RELEASE DISCIPLINE · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q119 What are source, binary and behavioral compatibility?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
Source compatibility concerns compilation; binary compatibility concerns
linkage/loading; behavioral compatibility concerns the application's
observed contract.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · What are source, binary and behavioral compatibility
Build artifact → Release target → Compatibility tests
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
Source compiles; binary loads; timezone/encoding output still changes
Each layer needs evidence, not just a green compile.
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Removed APIs, reflective access, serialization, default charset and thread/GC behavior can affect
different layers. Mixed versions also affect instrumentation and preview support. Compatibility
decisions need your real dependency/workload inventory.
COMMON MISTAKE
Class-file compatibility is only one part of an upgrade.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Which tests exercise defaults your application relies on?
CLEAR ANSWER
Test API behavior, serialization, charset/time-zone defaults, reflection, dynamic agents and
performance; same bytecode compatibility does not prove same runtime behavior.

pages.title: How would you migrate a production service from Java 8 to 25?
pages.fullText:
Q120 · MIGRATION: BUILD TARGETS AND RELEASE DISCIPLINE · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q120 How would you migrate a production service from
Java 8 to 25?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
Inventory dependencies/tooling and implicit behavior, verify on staged
targets as useful, then deploy a measured compatible build with a rollback
plan.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How would you migrate a production service from Java 8 to 25
Build artifact → Release target → Compatibility tests
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
Compile/tests -> packaged startup -> integration/load/soak
Canary -> compare SLOs and memory -> broaden -> monitor
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Update unsupported libraries and agents before replacing every loop with new syntax. Retest I/O
encodings, TLS, reflection, time zones, resources and cancellation. Rollback must include artifact/
runtime/configuration compatibility.
COMMON MISTAKE
A version upgrade is not a reason to rewrite all concurrency at once.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What evidence would block promotion of the canary?
CLEAR ANSWER
Block the canary for correctness failures, unsafe concurrency/GC regressions, dependency
incompatibility or SLO breaches; require a tested rollback path.

pages.title: · SENIOR INTERVIEWS: CHOOSE FEATURES FROM GUARANTEES · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Q121 How do virtual threads compare with reactive
pages.fullText:
Q121 · SENIOR INTERVIEWS: CHOOSE FEATURES FROM GUARANTEES · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q121 How do virtual threads compare with reactive
programming?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
Virtual threads preserve a blocking thread-per-task style; reactive designs
model asynchronous signals and backpressure through their own
contracts.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How do virtual threads compare with reactive programming
Business constraint → Choose API / model → Guarantee + test
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
Blocking JDBC + virtual threads: connection pool still bounds database work
Reactive pipeline: actual nonblocking dependencies and demand matter
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Neither style automatically fixes bottlenecks or business correctness. Existing framework/
dependency support, cancellation and team complexity influence the choice. Calling blocking work
inside a nonblocking event loop can still be harmful.
COMMON MISTAKE
Virtual threads are not a drop-in promise of reactive backpressure.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Which boundary should limit incoming demand?
CLEAR ANSWER
Use admission control, concurrency limits and backpressure where demand enters the system,
rather than unlimited request submission to cheap virtual threads.
Source chapter 25 · Java version and feature status should be checked for the stated release.

pages.title: How do CompletableFuture, virtual threads and structured concurrency differ?
pages.fullText:
Q122 · SENIOR INTERVIEWS: CHOOSE FEATURES FROM GUARANTEES · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q122 How do CompletableFuture, virtual threads and
structured concurrency differ?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
They model completion composition, cheap thread execution and related-
task lifetime/policy respectively; they can cooperate but are not synonyms.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How do CompletableFuture, virtual threads and structured concurrency differ
Business constraint → Choose API / model → Guarantee + test
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
Future chain: combine completions
Virtual thread: execute sequential task code
Structured scope: own child lifetime and failure policy
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
Choose how to run work separately from how to aggregate results and stop siblings.
StructuredTaskScope is still preview in 25. Cancellation and external effect identity remain
application concerns in all three approaches.
COMMON MISTAKE
An async return type is not proof of nonblocking work.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Which model helps prove children finish before request context closes?
CLEAR ANSWER
Structured concurrency ties child tasks to the lexical parent scope, making it easier to ensure
children finish or are cancelled before context/resources close.

pages.title: How do you modernize a Java 8 stream solution across versions?
pages.fullText:
Q124 · SENIOR INTERVIEWS: CHOOSE FEATURES FROM GUARANTEES · ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED
Q124 How do you modernize a Java 8 stream solution
across versions?
INTERVIEW-READY ANSWER
Preserve ordering, duplicates, nulls, mutability and error behavior, then
choose a newer API whose contract fits the requirement.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP · How do you modernize a Java 8 stream solution across versions
Business constraint → Choose API / model → Guarantee + test
JAVA EXAMPLE / QUICK TRACE
Java 8: collect(toCollection(ArrayList::new)) for a mutable list
Java 17: Stream.toList() only if unmodifiable output is acceptable
Java 25: gather windowFixed(...) for true batching semantics
IN SIMPLE WORDS · WHAT HAPPENS
A shorter pipeline can change the caller's ability to mutate or the meaning of prefix selection. Keep
a small counterexample test and state the minimum release. New operators must earn their place
through clearer semantics.
COMMON MISTAKE
Syntax modernization is not always behavior-preserving.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Which test catches replacing filter with takeWhile?
CLEAR ANSWER
Use a non-monotonic input such as [1, 4, 2] with predicate n < 3: filter keeps 1 and
2, while takeWhile stops at 4.

AT A GLANCE
Quick interview checklist
1. What release first finalized this feature?
2. Which return type, side effect or exception changes?
3. Which statement is a guarantee versus an OpenJDK implementation detail?
4. What happens under null, concurrency, cancellation or partial failure?
5. Can I show a five-line reproducible example?
Testing scope
Runnable labs were compiled and checked only where matching JDK support was available.

pages.title: What is a thread, and how is it different from a process?
pages.fullText:
CH 01 · Q001/080
original illustration
 THREADS / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES 
Thread foundations & task design
Q001. What is a thread, and how is it different from a
process?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A thread is one path of work inside a running program. Threads in the same Java
process share objects, but each has its own call stack. Separate processes have
their own memory space.
Why it matters: Two requests can reach the same mutable state concurrently.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
EXAMPLE FROM THE GUIDE 
One JVM process
Request thread A -> shared service object
Request thread B -> the same service object
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which data would you keep immutable in a shared service?
Answer → Keep request DTOs, configuration snapshots and shared lookup values immutable
where possible. Build a new value when changes are needed.
! COMMON TRAP A separate stack does not make every object referenced from it private.

pages.title: Thread foundations & task design What is concurrency versus parallelism?
pages.fullText:
CH 01 · Q002/080
original illustration
 THREADS / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES 
Thread foundations & task design
Q002. What is concurrency versus parallelism?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Concurrency means tasks make progress during overlapping time periods.
Parallelism means tasks actually run at the same moment on different CPU
capacity. One CPU core can switch between concurrent tasks.
Why it matters: Concurrency can improve utilization when work waits, without increasing CPU
capacity.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
EXAMPLE FROM THE GUIDE 
Concurrent: A waits while B makes progress
Parallel: A and B compute on different cores
More tasks != more available CPU
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Why can adding threads slow a CPU-bound workload?
Answer → Extra runnable workers fight for the same CPU, creating context switches and cache
pressure. If all cores are busy, throughput may fall.
! COMMON TRAP Thread count is not a measure of useful parallel throughput.

pages.title: Should you extend Thread or implement Runnable?
pages.fullText:
CH 01 · Q003/080
original illustration
 THREADS / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES 
Thread foundations & task design
Q003. Should you extend Thread or implement
Runnable?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Put the task in a Runnable or Callable, then decide separately where it runs. This
keeps business work reusable and avoids tying it to a particular Thread object.
Why it matters: The same task abstraction can later be submitted to an executor.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
JAVA / PSEUDOCODE EXAMPLE 
Runnable work = () -> processOrder();
Thread thread = new Thread(work, "order-worker");
thread.start();
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How does Callable change the task contract?
Answer → Callable<V> returns a typed result and can throw checked exceptions. An executor
normally exposes this through Future<V>.
! COMMON TRAP Reusing a task object is safe only if its mutable state supports that reuse.

pages.title: Thread foundations & task design How do Runnable and Callable differ?
pages.fullText:
CH 01 · Q004/080
original illustration
 THREADS / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES 
Thread foundations & task design
Q004. How do Runnable and Callable differ?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Runnable performs work without returning a value. Callable returns a value and
may declare checked exceptions. An executor runs either task and can give you a
Future for its result.
Why it matters: The Future represents the submitted execution and its result or failure.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
JAVA / PSEUDOCODE EXAMPLE 
Callable<Integer> work = () -> 42;
Future<Integer> result = pool.submit(work);
int value = result.get();
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
What does submit(Runnable) return on successful completion?
Answer → submit(Runnable) returns Future<?>. After successful completion, its get() returns
null; failures appear through ExecutionException.
! COMMON TRAP A Runnable can still fail with an unchecked exception.

CH 01 · Q005/080
original illustration
 THREADS / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES 
Thread foundations & task design
Q005. When is a thread-per-request design appropriate?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
One thread per request is easy to understand when load and downstream resources
are limited. Platform threads are relatively costly; virtual threads can make blocking
waits cheaper, but database connections still need limits.
Why it matters: The bottleneck may be the dependency rather than the number of runnable tasks.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
EXAMPLE FROM THE GUIDE 
Request -> execution resource -> database connection
Thread choice and connection budget are separate decisions.
Bound admission when the dependency cannot keep up.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
When would asynchronous I/O fit better than blocking calls?
Answer → Use async I/O when there are many long waits, a small controlled thread budget
and good asynchronous client support. Measure its complexity.
! COMMON TRAP Cheap threads do not make queues, connections or payload memory unlimited.

pages.title: Lifecycle, start, run & join What is the difference between start and run?
pages.fullText:
CH 02 · Q006/080
original illustration
 THREADS / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES 
Lifecycle, start, run & join
Q006. What is the difference between start and run?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Calling start() launches a new thread that runs the task. Calling run() directly on a
conventional platform Thread executes an ordinary method call on the current
thread.
Why it matters: The direct call and the started execution are two task invocations in this example.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
JAVA / PSEUDOCODE EXAMPLE 
Thread t = new Thread(() -> use(Thread.currentThread()));
t.run();   // conventional platform task: caller executes
t.start(); // new thread executes its task
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which thread would an exception from the direct call reach?
Answer → It reaches the caller of run(), because no new thread boundary was created by that
direct call.
! COMMON TRAP Java 25 Thread.run documentation has special behavior for virtual threads; start them
normally.

01
Current thread executes
02
t.start() launches worker

pages.title: Can a Thread be started twice or restarted after termination?
pages.fullText:
CH 02 · Q007/080
original illustration
 THREADS / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES 
Lifecycle, start, run & join
Q007. Can a Thread be started twice or restarted after
termination?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A Thread object can start only once. After it ends, create another Thread or submit
another task to an executor. You may reuse task code only when its state is safe.
Why it matters: Completion does not reset the Thread object's start eligibility.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
JAVA / PSEUDOCODE EXAMPLE 
Thread t = new Thread(work);
t.start(); t.join();
t.start(); // IllegalThreadStateException
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
What state makes a Runnable unsafe to submit twice concurrently?
Answer → Shared mutable fields such as counters or iteration indexes can race between
submissions. Use stateless tasks or coordinate changes.
! COMMON TRAP A reusable Runnable and a reusable Thread are different things.

02
second start throws

pages.fullText:
CH 02 · Q008/080
original illustration

Lifecycle, start, run & join
Q008. What are the six Java thread states?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Java reports NEW, RUNNABLE, BLOCKED, WAITING, TIMED_WAITING and
TERMINATED. These are snapshots of the JVM's view, not a promise about which
thread will execute next.
Why it matters: A state snapshot is evidence about a moment, not a whole causal history.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
EXAMPLE FROM THE GUIDE 
NEW -> start -> RUNNABLE
Monitor contention -> BLOCKED
Completion of run -> TERMINATED
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Why might RUNNABLE not mean that a thread is consuming CPU?
Answer → RUNNABLE also covers eligible threads waiting for CPU time or some OS
operations. It is not an observed CPU-usage metric.
! COMMON TRAP RUNNING is not a separate Thread.State enum constant.

Q009. How do BLOCKED, WAITING and

BLOCKED usually means waiting to enter a synchronized monitor. WAITING means
an untimed wait or park; TIMED_WAITING has a timeout. Read the stack trace to
find the real cause.

monitor.

Thread.sleep: TIMED_WAITING

Answer → Queue wait often shows LockSupport.park in ThreadPoolExecutor.getTask; a monitor
wait shows BLOCKED and an owned monitor in the dump.

pages.title: What does join guarantee, and does it order two workers?
pages.fullText:
CH 02 · Q010/080
original illustration
 THREADS / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES 
Lifecycle, start, run & join
Q010. What does join guarantee, and does it order two
workers?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
join() lets one thread wait until another finishes, and then safely observe that
worker's completed actions. Calling join on A before join on B does not force A and
B to run in that order.
Why it matters: The observer can process completed results without asserting worker print order.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
JAVA / PSEUDOCODE EXAMPLE 
a.start(); b.start();
a.join(); b.join();
// Both finished; no promise that a ran before b.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How would you require B to start only after A completes?
Answer → Start B only after A.join() succeeds, or have A signal a latch/future that starts the
dependent B task.
! COMMON TRAP Joining A before B is not equivalent to starting B after A finishes.

pages.fullText:
CH 03 · Q011/080
original illustration
 THREADS / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES 
Scheduling, sleep & metadata
Q011. Does sleep release a lock?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
sleep() pauses execution but keeps every lock the thread owns. Object.wait()
releases its associated monitor while waiting and takes it again before returning.
Why it matters: Other threads needing this monitor must wait through the sleep.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✦
➜ ➜
JAVA / PSEUDOCODE EXAMPLE 
synchronized (lock) {
Thread.sleep(100); // still owns lock
}
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Why might a timed Condition await be a better design here?
Answer → Condition.await releases its associated ReentrantLock while waiting and can return
on timeout. It avoids holding a lock during idle time.
! COMMON TRAP sleep and wait are not interchangeable delay methods.

pages.fullText:

original illustration

Q013. What are daemon threads?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A daemon thread does not keep the JVM alive by itself. The JVM may shut down
while daemon work remains, so important writes must have a controlled shutdown
path.
Why it matters: The application must explicitly coordinate completion when background work must
finish.

Q018. What should you do with InterruptedException?

interrupt flag if your method cannot pass it along. Then follow your task's
cancellation policy.

Q023. What does reentrant locking mean?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Reentrant means a thread may take a lock it already owns. Each lock acquisition
must have a matching release. Reentrancy does not prevent deadlocks between
different locks.

normally in finally, until the count reaches zero.

Deadlock means no participant can move because of a cycle. Livelock means
everyone keeps reacting but never finishes. Starvation means one participant keeps
missing its turn.

release locks in a true deadlock by itself.

ExecutorService separates task code from the policy that runs it. It manages

stop, not each request or task.

original illustration

Q045. What is thread-pool starvation deadlock?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Starvation deadlock happens when all pool workers wait for child tasks that are
queued to that same full pool. Avoid blocking within the pool on work that needs
that pool.
Why it matters: No monitor cycle is needed to produce this progress failure.

➜ ➜

Answer → Express child work through nonblocking stages (thenCompose/thenCombine),
execute it directly if safe, or use separate appropriately sized execution resources.
! COMMON TRAP Lock deadlock detection may not report a Future/queue dependency cycle.

Semaphore holds a limited number of permits. Acquire before using a limited

release its permit exactly once through a coordinated completion/cancel path.

Q071. How do you print odd and even numbers in order

pages.title: QUICK REVISION · THREAD CORRECTNESS
pages.fullText:
QUICK REVISION · THREAD CORRECTNESS
Pick the right tool.
Need an exact shared count? AtomicInteger.incrementAndGet or an appropriate lock.
Need to guard multiple fields? One shared lock or one immutable snapshot updated
atomically.
Need one-way state publication? A correct volatile/release-acquire handoff.
Need to wait for a predicate? Condition/Object.wait in a loop, with a bound if needed.
Need N workers to finish? CountDownLatch or Futures, with failure handling.
Need a hard downstream concurrency
cap?
Semaphore with acquire/release ownership.
Need a producer-consumer handoff? Bounded BlockingQueue and clear shutdown protocol.
Need several independent results? CompletableFuture thenCombine/allOf plus cleanup.
Need high-volume blocking tasks? Virtual threads plus admission and dependency limits.
Need no duplicate remote side effect? Durable idempotency state; threads alone cannot provide
it.
Architect habit: Start from an invariant, not an API name. Say what must never happen, what can time out, and
what proves completion.
88

pages.title: QUICK REVISION · FAILURE SIGNATURES
pages.fullText:
QUICK REVISION · FAILURE SIGNATURES
Observe before tuning.
BLOCKED threads Who owns the monitor? How long has it been held?
WAITING pool workers Are they idle or waiting for work that cannot start?
Long queue age Are arrivals exceeding successful completions?
Executor maxPoolSize ignored Is an unbounded queue accepting all tasks first?
Frequent request timeouts Do remote tasks keep running after responses finish?
Lost counter increments Is the update split into read / compute / write?
Stale ThreadLocal values Was remove() called in finally on reused workers?
Deadlock with no monitor cycle Look for Future/queue dependency cycles.
Increasing threads but flat throughput Check CPU, DB pool and upstream/downstream
saturation.
Virtual-thread slowdowns Measure pinning or blocking on the deployed Java
release.
Record before/after: p95/p99, goodput, CPU, queue depth, in-flight tasks, DB pool wait, errors, cancellation
completion.
89

pages.title: What is the Java Memory Model?
pages.fullText:
Q001 · Foundations: what the JMM guarantees INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q001. What is the Java Memory Model?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
The JMM is Java's rulebook for how threads see shared data and in what
order.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
The JMM defines which reads and writes may be observed across threads and the ordering
constraints imposed by synchronization. It lets implementations optimize execution while
preserving specified behavior. It is a concurrency contract, distinct from a diagram of heap, stacks
and metaspace.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
Question: can thread B observe thread A's update?
JMM answer: inspect actions and synchronization edges.
Memory-area answer: where are objects and frames managed?
What happens: Visibility and legal observations need a synchronization argument.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
Why do two machines sometimes show different outcomes for the same racy
code?
Answer: Different CPU instructions, compiler optimizations and scheduling can expose
different outcomes because a data race lacks a guaranteed ordering. Correctly
synchronized code must not rely on one machine's behavior.
Interview trap: Explaining only heap versus stack does not answer a JMM question.
Original source p. 6 · References M01, M21-M23

pages.title: How do visibility, atomicity and ordering differ?
pages.fullText:
Q002 · Foundations: what the JMM guarantees INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q002. How do visibility, atomicity and ordering
differ?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Visibility is seeing changes, atomicity is doing one indivisible step, and
ordering says what may happen first.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
Visibility concerns whether a read can observe another thread's writes. Atomicity concerns whether
an operation is indivisible at the required level. Ordering constrains which observations and action
sequences are permitted. One mechanism can provide some guarantees without providing every
business invariant.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
volatile int count;
count++; // read, compute and write: not one atomic increment
What happens: Volatile access does not combine multiple actions into one transaction.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
Which mechanism would you choose for an exact concurrent counter?
Answer: Use AtomicInteger.incrementAndGet() for a single exact counter, or a lock if the
count must change together with other state.
Interview trap: 'Thread-safe' without naming the operation or invariant is imprecise.
Original source p. 6 · References M01, M21-M23
Read / write Atomic operation Correct counter
JAVA / MEMORY MODEL
LEARN · DRAW · PROVE · PRACTICE 6

pages.title: What is a data race?
pages.fullText:
Q003 · Foundations: what the JMM guarantees INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q003. What is a data race?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
A data race happens when threads access the same data without an ordering
rule and at least one writes.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
Conflicting accesses to the same variable form a data race when at least one is a write and they
are not ordered by happens-before. Data-race freedom is a property of the program's
synchronization, not of whether a failure happened during a test.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
int balance; // shared ordinary field
A: balance = 100;
B: int seen = balance; // no connecting synchronization
What happens: The accesses lack the required ordering even if the hardware usually shows 100.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
Can a program using only atomic accesses still violate a business rule?
Answer: Yes. Two separate atomic reads or updates can be individually safe while the
combined check and business decision is wrong; protect the whole rule.
Interview trap: A data race and a broader business race condition are related but not
identical terms.
Original source p. 7 · References M01, M21-M23
Unsynchronized read Competing write Data race
JAVA / MEMORY MODEL

pages.title: What is sequential consistency?
pages.fullText:
Q004 · Foundations: what the JMM guarantees INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q004. What is sequential consistency?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Sequential consistency means actions look like one shared timeline that keeps
each thread's own order.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
Sequential consistency means observations can be explained by one interleaving that respects
each thread's program order. Correctly synchronized, data-race-free Java programs receive this
guarantee under the JMM's conditions. Racy ordinary code is not generally entitled to that simple
interleaving model.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
A: write x; read y
B: write y; read x
Ask whether one order can explain all observations.
What happens: Synchronization makes reasoning closer to interleaving source-level actions.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
Why can a data-race-free check-then-act workflow still be wrong?
Answer: Because another thread can change the state after a safe read but before a safe
action. The check and action must form one atomic step.
Interview trap: Sequential consistency does not make two separately synchronized fields one
atomic snapshot.
Original source p. 7 · References M01, M21-M23
Thread A sequence One legal interleaving Thread B sequence

LEARN · DRAW · PROVE · PRACTICE 8

pages.title: Does happens-before mean an action happened earlier by the clock?
pages.fullText:
Q005 · Foundations: what the JMM guarantees INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q005. Does happens-before mean an action
happened earlier by the clock?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Happens-before is a Java ordering promise, not simply one event occurring
earlier on a clock.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
No. Happens-before is a specified ordering relation used to constrain observations. Clock time
alone does not create it. Nor does an edge necessarily mean every later read sees that exact write
if other allowed writes intervene.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
A writes data at 10:00:00
B reads data at 10:00:01
Elapsed time alone supplies no publication guarantee.
What happens: Prove an edge through synchronization rather than through timing.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
What would establish a reliable edge between those actions?
Answer: Use a matching volatile write/read, unlock/lock on the same monitor, a queue
handoff or another documented synchronizing action.
Interview trap: Sleeps, logs and elapsed delays are not substitutes for the required memory
contract.

Write data Synchronization edge Safe read
JAVA / MEMORY MODEL

Q006 · Happens-before rules and proof INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q006. What are the most useful happens-before
rules?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Useful rules include program order, volatile handoff, lock release/acquisition
and thread start or completion.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
Program order supplies within-thread edges. Monitor unlock precedes a subsequent lock of the
same monitor. Volatile write precedes subsequent read of that variable in synchronization order.
Thread start, termination detection and documented concurrent APIs supply additional edges.
Transitivity connects them.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
Write data -> publish -> acquire -> read data
Every arrow needs a rule or documented API contract.
What happens: A proof names the exact variable, monitor or handoff operation.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
Which edge is missing in an unsynchronized getter?
Answer: The ordinary getter has no matching acquire action, so it lacks an edge
connecting the writer's updates to its read.
Interview trap: 'There is a lock somewhere' does not prove an edge for this reader.

pages.title: How does transitivity make publication work?
pages.fullText:
Q007 · Happens-before rules and proof INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q007. How does transitivity make publication work?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
If A happens-before B and B happens-before C, then A happens-before C too.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
If A happens-before B and B happens-before C, A happens-before C. Ordinary writes before a
publication action can therefore become ordered before reads after a corresponding acquiring
action. The handoff must actually participate in the protocol.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
Writer: payload = 42; ready = true; // ready is volatile
Reader: if (ready) use(payload);
Chain: payload write -> ready write -> read -> payload read
What happens: The ordinary payload access is protected by the publication chain in this one-
shot protocol.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
How would you design a reusable message channel?
Answer: Use BlockingQueue, another documented channel or a versioned immutable
message with an atomic publication step; define ownership and reuse.
Interview trap: Resetting the flag and reusing payload introduces lifecycle questions that this
example does not solve.

Write payload Publish ready Reader sees payload

pages.title: What does the thread-start rule guarantee?
pages.fullText:
Q008 · Happens-before rules and proof INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q008. What does the thread-start rule guarantee?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Writes made before Thread.start() are visible to the new thread through that
start handoff.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
Actions in the thread that precede starting another thread are ordered before actions in the
started thread. Construct and configure the task before start. The rule does not publish arbitrary
later mutations back and forth automatically.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO

pages.title: What does join guarantee?

Q009 · Happens-before rules and proof INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q009. What does join guarantee?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
After a successful join detects completion, the parent may safely read the
worker's completed writes.

→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION

ordered before the joining thread continues with dependent reads. A timed join that returns while
the target is still alive does not establish completion.

worker.join(); // completes after target termination

What happens: The completion boundary permits reading results written by that worker.

Answer: After a timed join, check worker.isAlive(); if still alive, do not treat results as
complete. Wait or use a Future with a clear completion contract.
Interview trap: A timeout return is not proof that the worker's result is ready.

pages.title: What does volatile provide?

Q011 · Volatile: power and limitations INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q011. What does volatile provide?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Volatile lets threads see a variable through Java's ordering and visibility rules,
but does not lock a multi-step operation.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
Volatile reads and writes are atomic accesses with specified ordering and visibility semantics. They
participate in synchronization order and can publish earlier ordinary writes through a correct
protocol. They do not supply mutual exclusion for a sequence of operations.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
volatile boolean stopped;
void requestStop() { stopped = true; }
boolean stopRequested() { return stopped; }
What happens: An eventual worker observation of the flag can coordinate a simple stop request.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
How would a blocked worker be woken promptly?
Answer: Call interrupt for interruptible waits, notify a guarded condition, or complete an
explicit signaling primitive; a flag alone cannot wake blocked I/O.
Interview trap: Visibility is not a fairness or bounded-scheduling guarantee.

Q012 · Volatile: power and limitations INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q012. Why is volatile count++ unsafe for exact
counting?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
count++ is read, add and write: two threads can both read 0 and both write 1.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION

overwrite with the same next value. Each volatile access can be valid while the combined increment
loses one logical update.

A reads 0; B reads 0
A writes 1; B writes 1
Final count can be 1, not 2
What happens: Protect the compound operation with a suitable atomic update or lock.

Answer: incrementAndGet() uses an atomic read-modify-write operation, so concurrent
increments on that counter are not lost.

pages.title: Does a volatile reference make the referenced object thread-safe?
pages.fullText:
Q013 · Volatile: power and limitations INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q013. Does a volatile reference make the referenced
object thread-safe?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Volatile safely publishes a reference but cannot protect changes made inside
a mutable object.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION

need their own discipline unless the object is immutable or safely confined. Replacing a complete
immutable snapshot is a common appropriate pattern.

volatile List<String> names;
names = new ArrayList<>();
names.add("A"); // mutation is not made safe by reference volatility
What happens: Reference publication and collection mutation are different actions.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
How would you publish a read-only replacement list?
Answer: Create a defensive List.copyOf version and publish it through a volatile reference
or AtomicReference; readers keep that immutable snapshot.
Interview trap: A volatile array reference does not turn every element into a volatile variable.

pages.title: What is safe one-shot publication with a volatile flag?
pages.fullText:
Q014 · Volatile: power and limitations INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q014. What is safe one-shot publication with a
volatile flag?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Write the data first, then set a volatile ready flag; the reader checks ready
before reading data.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
Write all required payload state before writing the volatile ready flag, then read payload only after
the reader observes readiness. For a one-shot, single-publication protocol, the chain orders the
payload initialization before those reads.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
int payload;
volatile boolean ready;
Writer: payload = 42; ready = true;
Reader: if (ready) assert payload == 42;
What happens: The payload can remain ordinary because the protocol supplies ordering.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
Which outcomes are permitted when the reader sees ready as false?
Answer: If ready is false, it may skip reading and report not-ready, such as -1. It cannot
claim that publication was observed.
Interview trap: Reading payload before testing ready, or mutating it later without
synchronization, breaks the stated argument.

Write payload Volatile ready=true Read payload

pages.fullText:
Q015 · Volatile: power and limitations INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q015. Is volatile literally a flush to main RAM on
every access?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Volatile promises ordering and visibility, not a literal RAM flush on every
access.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
That is an unreliable implementation explanation. The portable contract is about legal observations
and ordering. Compilers and CPUs use architecture-specific instructions, barriers and coherent
caches to implement it; Java code should rely on the contract.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
Portable argument: volatile write/read synchronization
Implementation question: inspect generated code and ISA
Neither requires a universal RAM transaction story.
What happens: Correctness must not depend on a particular cache layout.

Why can the same volatile operation compile differently on x86 and ARM?
Answer: Different processors have different memory-ordering instructions. The JVM uses
instructions needed on each platform to implement the same JMM rule.
Interview trap: A CPU-cache metaphor can hide the difference between a reference write and
a compound invariant.

pages.title: What does synchronized guarantee?
pages.fullText:
Q016 · Locks, monitors and conditions INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q016. What does synchronized guarantee?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Synchronized allows only one thread at a time to hold the same monitor and
connects state changes across lock boundaries.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
It provides mutual exclusion on one monitor and release/acquire-style memory ordering through
its specified unlock/lock relationship. Every relevant access must follow the same policy.
Reentrancy lets the owning thread acquire the same monitor again.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
synchronized (lock) {
 balance -= amount;
 ledger.add(entry);
}
What happens: A reader using the same lock can observe a consistent guarded invariant.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
How would you return a safe balance-and-ledger summary?
Answer: Read the balance and ledger inside one synchronized block and return an
immutable summary made while holding the lock.
Interview trap: An unsynchronized reader is not protected merely because the writer uses
synchronized.

pages.title: When should you use ReentrantLock instead of synchronized?
pages.fullText:
Q017 · Locks, monitors and conditions INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q017. When should you use ReentrantLock instead of
synchronized?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Use ReentrantLock when timed or interruptible acquisition, conditions or
other explicit-lock features are needed.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
Use an explicit lock when its supported features, such as interruptible acquisition, timed attempts,
fairness options or multiple Conditions, fit the design. The memory contract of successful locking/
unlocking parallels monitor guarantees, while lifecycle management requires explicit finally
cleanup.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
lock.lock();
try { updateState(); }
finally { lock.unlock(); }
What happens: The lock must be released on exceptional control paths.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
When would lockInterruptibly be preferable?
Answer: Use lockInterruptibly() when cancellation should stop a thread waiting to acquire
a lock, such as a request with a deadline.
Interview trap: Fairness options do not promise a global scheduler or a maximum wait time.
Original source p. 14 · References M08, M09, M24, M34
Acquire lock try/finally Always unlock
JAVA / MEMORY MODEL

pages.title: Why must wait or await be used in a loop?
pages.fullText:
Q018 · Locks, monitors and conditions INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q018. Why must wait or await be used in a loop?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Always recheck a waiting condition in a loop because a wakeup is not proof
the condition became true.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
A wait can return for reasons that do not make the predicate true, including spurious wakeups and
another thread consuming the state first. Test the guarded predicate while holding its associated
lock, wait, then recheck after reacquisition.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
synchronized (lock) {
 while (!ready) lock.wait();
 consume();
}
What happens: Rechecking ties progress to state rather than to the mere occurrence of a
notification.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
How would a timeout change the loop's result contract?
Answer: Compute a deadline and return a distinct timeout result if the predicate is still
false after the remaining wait budget is exhausted.
Interview trap: An if check can proceed with a false predicate after waking.
Original source p. 14 · References M08, M09, M24, M34
Check predicate Wait Recheck predicate
JAVA / MEMORY MODEL
LEARN · DRAW · PROVE · PRACTICE 25

pages.title: Does notify release the monitor immediately?
pages.fullText:
Q019 · Locks, monitors and conditions INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q019. Does notify release the monitor immediately?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Notify wakes a waiter, but the notifying thread still holds the monitor until it
exits the synchronized block.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
No. A notified waiter cannot resume the guarded operation until it can reacquire the monitor.
Publication is explained through monitor release and reacquisition, with the condition predicate
rechecked. Notifications are not durable queued messages by themselves.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
synchronized (lock) {
 ready = true;
 lock.notifyAll();
 // This thread still owns the monitor here.
}
What happens: The notifier's later unlock is part of the handoff.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
Why is the predicate more important than the notification count?
Answer: The boolean/state predicate records the truth; notifications can be missed or
spurious. Wait until the predicate is true, not until a signal count matches.
Interview trap: A notification sent before a thread waits can be missed unless the predicate
preserves the relevant state.

Q020. Why is locking each getter insufficient for a

Answer: Expose one synchronized getSnapshot() that copies all fields under one lock, or
return a published immutable record.

pages.title: Why is double-checked locking correct with a volatile reference?
pages.fullText:
Q023 · Safe publication and singleton patterns INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q023. Why is double-checked locking correct with a
volatile reference?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Double-checked locking works when the instance reference is volatile and
construction is protected by a synchronized slow path.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
The synchronized slow path serializes construction, and the volatile publication orders initialized
state before a fast-path reader that acquires the reference. The second null check handles another
thread's completed construction. A local variable reduces repeated volatile reads.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
Service s = instance; // instance is volatile
if (s == null) synchronized (Service.class) {
 s = instance;
 if (s == null) instance = s = new Service();
}
return s;
What happens: Both publication and singleton construction are covered by distinct mechanisms.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
What if the constructor throws before assignment?
Answer: The assignment never runs if construction throws; other callers can retry later.
Handle failures explicitly rather than exposing a partial singleton.
Interview trap: Removing volatile leaves the unsynchronized fast path without the required
ordinary-state publication guarantee.

Q024 · Safe publication and singleton patterns INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q024. Why does the initialization-on-demand holder
idiom work?

The holder pattern is safe because Java class initialization publishes the static
value correctly.

→ →

Class initialization has synchronization and completion rules that safely initialize the static holder
state before its valid use. A nested holder defers creation until the holder is initialized. Constructor
work and initialization failures still need appropriate handling.

}
Service get() { return Holder.INSTANCE; }
What happens: The class-initialization contract supplies the publication boundary.

How does this differ from an eagerly initialized static field?

holder delays construction until the nested holder is first used.

across every class loader.

Q025. How do you safely publish configuration
updates?

Publish one complete immutable configuration rather than updating several
fields separately.

→ →

mechanism. Each reader captures that reference once and uses one version throughout the
operation. Coordinate concurrent writers if update composition matters.

use(c.timeout(), c.retries());

the current version and must not silently overwrite a concurrent update.

logical modifications.

pages.title: What special guarantee do final fields provide?
pages.fullText:
Q026 · Final fields and genuine immutability INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q026. What special guarantee do final fields
provide?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Final fields of a correctly constructed object get special initialization
guarantees, even without a full ordinary publication handoff.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
A correctly constructed object that does not escape during construction receives final-field
initialization guarantees. When a reader obtains the object, it can observe the properly initialized
final values under the specified rules. This special protection is not a general happens-before edge
for every ordinary field.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
class Pair {
 final int x;
 int y;
 Pair() { x = 1; y = 2; }
}
What happens: Final x and ordinary y have different guarantees under otherwise unsafe
publication.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
If a reader sees a non-null Pair, what can it rely on about x versus y?
Answer: For a correctly constructed non-escaping Pair, final x is guaranteed to be
initialized as specified; ordinary y is not given the same broad promise by final-field
rules.
Interview trap: Do not claim final publishes every field in an arbitrary mutable object.

pages.title: Does a final reference make its object deeply immutable?
pages.fullText:
Q027 · Final fields and genuine immutability INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q027. Does a final reference make its object deeply
immutable?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Final stops reassignment of the reference; it does not freeze the referenced
list or object.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
No. The final variable cannot be reassigned through ordinary assignment after construction, but
the referenced object can still change. Special constructor-time final-field guarantees can include
referenced initialization state under the rules; later mutations require separate synchronization.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
final List<String> values = new ArrayList<>();
values.add("A"); // reference remains unchanged
What happens: Finality constrains the reference binding, not every reachable object.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
How would defensive copying change the guarantee?
Answer: Copy mutable inputs and avoid exposing a modifiable original, so external callers
cannot mutate the snapshot behind your back.
Interview trap: A record component referencing a mutable list is not automatically deeply
immutable.

Q028 · Final fields and genuine immutability INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q028. Why is this-escape during construction
dangerous?

Letting this escape during construction lets another thread call the object
before setup is finished.

→ →

assumptions behind final-field initialization safety. Callback registration, starting work or inserting

// Prefer a separate post-construction registration step.

register/publish it afterward.

constructor refactor.

Q029. What makes an object safely shareable as
immutable?

An immutable object never changes observable state, including the objects it
exposes.

→ →

components. Complete construction, defensive copies and appropriate APIs establish that property.

initialization safety.

considered.

What if each list element is itself mutable?

elements or use immutable element types too.

immutable copy.

Q030. Can final-field rules replace all
synchronization?

Q031. What is compare-and-set?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
CAS changes one value only when it still equals the expected old value.

→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION

comparison matches. The boolean result reports success. Java atomic/VarHandle methods define
the applicable access-mode memory effects; not every similarly named weak operation has
identical ordering.

pages.title: Why should retrying atomic update functions avoid side effects?
pages.fullText:
Q032 · Atomics, CAS and compound state INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q032. Why should retrying atomic update functions
avoid side effects?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
An atomic update function may run more than once, so doing side effects
inside it can duplicate them.
THREAD / MEMORY FLOW DIAGRAM
→ →
PRECISE TECHNICAL EXPLANATION
An update function may be invoked repeatedly when contention forces retry. Keep it pure with
respect to externally visible effects, and perform separately coordinated side effects after a
successful transition where the design allows it.
JAVA / CONCURRENCY SCENARIO
state.updateAndGet(old -> computeNext(old));
// Avoid charging a customer inside this retry function.
What happens: The successful state update does not imply the computation ran once.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
How would you coordinate a durable event with an in-memory CAS result?
Answer: A local CAS cannot atomically commit an external event; use a durable database
transaction and outbox or a coordinated idempotent workflow.
Interview trap: Counting each function invocation as a committed business event can
overcount.

effects CAS retries Commit once

Q033. How do AtomicInteger and LongAdder differ?

AtomicInteger gives exact updates to one counter; LongAdder scales statistics

→ →

Concurrent sum -> aggregate observation, not exact snapshot

Answer: Once all writers have finished and their completion is established (for example
by join), the final sum may be read as the exact completed total.

another invariant.

Q034. What is the ABA problem?

ABA means a value changed from A to B and back to A, fooling a CAS that
checks only the value.

→ →

relevant transition follows the protocol and wraparound/lifecycle are considered.

Other actor: A -> B -> A
CAS expects A: value matches despite intervening history
What happens: Value equality does not necessarily encode state history.

Answer: AtomicStampedReference checks the expected reference and stamp together,
detecting intervening transitions if every writer updates the stamp.

eliminate every logical ABA case.

expectations are handled rather than splitting related fields into separate atomics.

against the latest range; never update low and high independently.

Q036. What is a VarHandle?

VarHandle gives explicit ways to read, write and atomically change a field with
different memory-ordering strengths.

→ →

including ordinary, opaque, acquire/release, volatile and atomic operations. It is an API for explicit
memory semantics; use simpler abstractions when they fit the design.

Q037 · VarHandles, access modes and fences INTERVIEW ANSWER CARD
Q037. How do plain, opaque, acquire/release and
volatile modes differ?
SHORT ANSWER · SAY THIS FIRST
Plain, opaque, acquire/release and volatile are increasingly different ordering
contracts, not interchangeable performance switches.

add coherence for that location with weaker ordering than acquire/release. Acquire/release can
constrain surrounding operations in a handoff; volatile provides stronger synchronization-order
semantics. Exact method contracts matter.

Plain: ordinary access discipline
Opaque: coherent location, weak surrounding order
Release/acquire: directed handoff ordering
Volatile: stronger ordering among volatile actions
What happens: Choose the weakest mode only when its proof is understood and worth the
complexity.
ANSWERED FOLLOW-UP · PRACTICE ALOUD
Which mode is sufficient for your one-shot payload handoff?
Answer: A release write paired with an acquire read that sees it is sufficient for the
described one-shot data handoff; volatile is simpler when unsure.
Interview trap: Opaque is not a drop-in replacement for a volatile publication flag.
