pages.title: What is the Single Responsibility Principle?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
SOLID AND DESIGN JUDGMENT
16
Q007
FOUNDATION
What is the Single Responsibility Principle?
THE SHORT ANSWER
A module should group behavior that changes for the same reason and separate
behavior driven by different responsibilities.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Business contract
Clear
responsibility
Verified behavior
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Invoice calculation != PDF rendering != payment persistence
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Separate pricing rules from presentation and storage so one policy change need not disturb the others.
SRP is not one method per class; related operations can share one coherent responsibility.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A class named Manager can still hide unrelated reasons to change.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Who owns each change in this example?
Answer: Pricing owns amounts and discounts, rendering owns PDF layout, and persistence owns
database writes. Each responsibility should change for its own business reason.

pages.title: What is the Open/Closed Principle?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
SOLID AND DESIGN JUDGMENT
17
Q008
FOUNDATION
What is the Open/Closed Principle?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Keep stable policy intact while allowing a required axis of variation through
extension.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Business contract
Clear
responsibility
Verified behavior
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Checkout uses DiscountPolicy
   Add SeasonalDiscount without editing checkout algorithm
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The composition/configuration point may still change to select the new implementation. OCP does not
mean source files are never edited. Preserve a verified stable contract and avoid extensibility for every
imagined future need.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Moving a switch into a factory does not remove all change points.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which variation should remain closed?
Answer: Keep the checkout calculation and its invariants stable. Allow discount implementations to
vary behind a validated DiscountPolicy contract.

pages.title: What is the Liskov Substitution Principle?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
SOLID AND DESIGN JUDGMENT
18
Q009
FOUNDATION
What is the Liskov Substitution Principle?
THE SHORT ANSWER
A replacement implementation must preserve the behavioral contract clients rely
on, including valid inputs and promised outcomes.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Business contract
Clear
responsibility
Verified behavior
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
ReadableStore contract accepts all supported IDs
   CachedStore must not reject IDs merely because they are uncached
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Avoid stronger preconditions, weaker guarantees and broken invariants. Java type compatibility is not
sufficient. Exception and side-effect expectations matter, especially when an adapter fronts a remote
service.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A subclass that throws UnsupportedOperationException for promised behavior can violate substitution.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How would a contract test detect the violation?
Answer: Run the same contract suite against every ReadableStore implementation, including
missing IDs, failures, ordering, and accepted inputs; a subtype must not silently narrow the
contract.

pages.title: What is the Interface Segregation Principle?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
SOLID AND DESIGN JUDGMENT
19
Q010
FOUNDATION
What is the Interface Segregation Principle?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Clients should depend on contracts containing the operations they need rather
than a broad unrelated interface.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Business contract
Clear
responsibility
Verified behavior
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
ReadableStore.find(id)
   WritableStore.save(value)
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Split read-only and mutation capabilities when clients genuinely differ. Keep cohesive methods
together instead of fragmenting every operation. This prevents read-only implementations from faking
unsupported writes.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Many tiny interfaces can also obscure an understandable contract.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which client benefits from the split?
Answer: Read-only clients, such as reporting screens, depend only on ReadableStore, so they
cannot accidentally call writes or implement meaningless save methods.

SOLID AND DESIGN JUDGMENT
20
Q011
FOUNDATION
What is the Dependency Inversion Principle?
THE SHORT ANSWER
High-level policy and low-level implementation should depend on suitable
abstractions rather than high-level code depending directly on low-level details.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Business contract
Clear
responsibility
Verified behavior
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Domain PaymentPort <- HttpPaymentAdapter
   OrderService depends on PaymentPort
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The business layer can own the port, and infrastructure implements it. Dependency injection supplies
an implementation; DIP is about dependency direction and contracts. A container can inject tightly
coupled concrete classes without achieving DIP.
INTERVIEW TRAP
DI and DIP are related but not identical.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which package should own the interface?
Answer: Put PaymentPort in the domain or application-core module that needs it. Keep
HttpPaymentAdapter in infrastructure so dependencies point inward.

How should SOLID be balanced with simplicity?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Apply it to real sources of change and verify the design remains understandable
and efficient.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Business contract
Clear
responsibility
Verified behavior
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
One payment provider today, several required next quarter
   A small PaymentPort boundary is justified
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Explain a tradeoff: extra interfaces help replace external infrastructure, while excessive abstractions
slow navigation. Patterns should preserve business invariants and make tests meaningful. Prefer
explicit contracts over slogan-based redesign.

SOLID is not a score calculated from interface counts.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What evidence shows the abstraction paid off?
Answer: Compare change size, number of impacted classes, test isolation, and defect rate before
and after. An abstraction earns its cost when real changes become safer.

pages.fullText:

23
Q013
CREATIONAL
What is Singleton and when is it useful?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Singleton controls access to one instance within a defined runtime scope.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Client
Access point
Defined scope
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
enum AppSettings {
     INSTANCE;
     public String region() { return "local"; }
   }
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
An enum is a concise Java singleton with well-defined construction/serialization behavior. Define the
scope: class-loader identity matters, and multiple processes still have multiple instances.
Dependency-injected lifecycle control often avoids static global access.
INTERVIEW TRAP
One instance does not imply safe mutable state.

pages.title: CREATIONAL How do you implement lazy initialization safely?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
SINGLETON
24
Q014
CREATIONAL
How do you implement lazy initialization safely?
THE SHORT ANSWER
The initialization-on-demand holder idiom uses Java class initialization to
publish a lazy instance safely.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Access point
Defined scope
Single instance
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
final class Registry {
     private Registry() {}
     private static class Holder { static final Registry R = new Registry(); }
     static Registry instance() { return Holder.R; }
   }
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Initialization occurs when the holder is first used. For double-checked locking, the instance reference
must be volatile and the algorithm must be correct. The holder controls construction but not thread
safety of later mutations.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Lazy construction cannot repair unsafe shared maps inside the instance.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
When would you choose eager creation instead?
Answer: Choose eager creation if the object is cheap, always required, or startup should detect
initialization problems immediately; lazy creation is useful for costly optional work.

Why can Singleton make testing and design harder?

or consumers.

Client

   Better boundary: constructor accepts PaymentPort

pages.title: CREATIONAL What is Factory Method?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
FACTORY METHOD
27
Q016
CREATIONAL
What is Factory Method?
THE SHORT ANSWER
A creator exposes an overridable creation method so subclasses can supply the
concrete product used by its workflow.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Creator workflow
Product contract
Concrete creator
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
abstract class Job {
     abstract Parser createParser();
     Result run(String input) { return createParser().parse(input); }
   }
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The workflow depends on Parser while specialized Jobs choose the parser. This is different from any
static method named of or create. The extension point should serve a stable workflow rather than add
inheritance for one constructor.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A static switch factory is not automatically the GoF Factory Method.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which method does the subclass override?
Answer: The subclass overrides createParser(), not run(). The base run() retains the workflow and
calls the chosen Parser.

When is Factory Method worth using?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Use it when an existing creator workflow needs a creation variation point aligned
with its subclasses.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Product contract
Concrete creator
Concrete product
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA

   JsonImportJob creates JsonParser
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Each job can retain the shared run algorithm while choosing a product. If parser choice varies
independently from job type, injecting a Parser or Supplier may be simpler. Avoid multiplying
subclasses for unrelated combinations.
INTERVIEW TRAP
An inheritance hierarchy can become the wrong axis of variation.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How would constructor injection change this design?
Answer: Inject Parser into Job's constructor and remove the subclasses if parser choice is the only
variation; the shared run algorithm stays in one class.

How can a Factory Method preserve substitutability?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Every returned product must satisfy the product contract the creator's workflow
uses.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Creator workflow
Product contract
Concrete product
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA

   Both CsvParser and JsonParser preserve this contract

The caller should not require downcasts to concrete parsers. Specify ownership and reuse: a factory
may create a new object or provide a suitable existing one. Tests should exercise the shared workflow
for every product.

Which product contract would you test?

thread-safety expectations using the same cases for every Parser.

pages.title: CREATIONAL What is Abstract Factory?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
ABSTRACT FACTORY
31
Q019
CREATIONAL
What is Abstract Factory?
THE SHORT ANSWER
It supplies related products through one family-level creation contract while
hiding concrete family classes.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Client
Family factory
Concrete family
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
interface UiFactory {
     Button button();
     Menu menu();
   }
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A DesktopFactory and TouchFactory can provide compatible button/menu pairs. The client chooses a
family once and uses its abstractions. Compatibility constraints, not the word Factory in the name,
justify the pattern.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Independently mixing family products may violate assumptions.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What makes two products belong to one family?
Answer: Products form a family if they must share compatible versions, configuration, style,
credentials, or protocols and should be selected together.

ABSTRACT FACTORY
32
Q020
CREATIONAL
What is the main extension tradeoff?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Adding a family is easy, while adding a new product kind can require changing the
abstract factory and every family implementation.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Family factory
Concrete family
Compatible

SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
New family: HighContrastFactory
   New product kind: Tooltip -> update all UiFactory implementations
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
This tradeoff differs from Factory Method's single-product variation. If product kinds grow constantly,
consider a simpler composition model or a carefully designed registry. Avoid weakening types merely
to avoid every interface change.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A string-to-Object factory sacrifices useful compile-time checks.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which dimension grows more often here?
Answer: If you add more deployment families often, Abstract Factory helps. If you continually add
product types, every family must be updated; consider simpler ports.

How would you use Abstract Factory in backend code?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Group mutually compatible infrastructure products when a real compatibility
requirement exists.

Client

Compatible

StorageFamily -> BlobWriter + SignedUrlProvider
   CloudAFamily keeps endpoint and credential policy aligned

A Spring configuration can assemble the family through DI, but a collection of unrelated bean methods

family choice or cross-product compatibility guarantee.

pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
BUILDER
35
Q022
CREATIONAL
What is Builder?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Builder separates stepwise construction from the final representation so complex
objects can be assembled clearly.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Builder steps
Build validation
Immutable product
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Request r = new Request.Builder("/orders")
       .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(2)).header("Accept", "json").build();
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Fluent Java builders often replace telescoping constructors; the GoF form can also use a director to
control steps for different representations. Clearly distinguish required fields from optional settings
and reject invalid combinations.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A fluent setter chain alone does not guarantee a valid object.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Where should cross-field validation run?
Answer: Run validation in build() or the constructed type's constructor, after all fields are
available. Reject inconsistent combinations before returning an object.

pages.title: CREATIONAL How do you make a built object immutable?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
BUILDER
36
Q023
CREATIONAL
How do you make a built object immutable?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Validate and copy mutable inputs into the result rather than sharing the
builder's internal containers.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Build validation
Immutable product
Safe caller
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
this.headers = Map.copyOf(builder.headers);
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Final fields prevent reference reassignment, but not mutation of referenced objects. Deep immutability
needs immutable elements or defensive copies at the necessary depth. Decide whether builders are
reusable; they are usually not shared across threads.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Unmodifiable view can still reflect changes in its backing collection.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What if a header value is itself mutable?
Answer: Copy that value too, or use an immutable representation. Map.copyOf only copies the map
structure; it does not deep-copy mutable values.

When should you avoid a builder?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Avoid it for a tiny value whose constructor or record clearly expresses all valid
required inputs.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP

Safe caller
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
record Coordinates(double latitude, double longitude) {}
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A builder improves readability when options grow or construction involves constraints. It costs code

increase generic/interface complexity.

A builder for every two-field DTO is often needless ceremony.

explain meaning better than a builder.

New instance

clearer.

How do shallow and deep copying differ?

A shallow copy duplicates the outer object but shares nested references; a deep
copy duplicates the required mutable graph.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Copy policy
New instance
New identity
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Original and shallowCopy share the same mutable List<Section>
   Deep policy copies sections and their mutable state as needed
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Copy only the state that must be independent. Cycles, shared subgraphs, resources and immutable
objects require explicit policy. Blind recursive duplication can lose intended sharing or fail on cycles.
INTERVIEW TRAP

FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How would you test aliasing?
Answer: Copy, then mutate the original nested object; the deep copy must remain unchanged. Also
mutate the copy to prove independence in both directions.

new object and define which object owns closing it.

pages.title: STRUCTURAL What is Adapter?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
ADAPTER
43
Q028
STRUCTURAL
What is Adapter?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Adapter presents the interface a client needs while translating calls to a
different existing interface.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Client contract
Adapter
Vendor API
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
final class PaymentAdapter implements PaymentPort {
     private final VendorClient client;
     public Receipt pay(Money m) { return map(client.charge(toRequest(m))); }
   }
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The adapter isolates vendor request/response types and error mapping. Its purpose is compatibility
rather than simply adding features. Contract conversion includes units, identity and failure semantics,
not only method names.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Mapping vendor timeout to definite failure can trigger unsafe repeated charges.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which outcomes are uncertain?
Answer: Vendor timeout or connection loss after submission may leave the payment outcome
unknown. Query by stable idempotency ID before retrying the charge.

pages.title: STRUCTURAL What is Bridge?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
BRIDGE
47
Q031
STRUCTURAL
What is Bridge?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Bridge separates an abstraction from its implementation hierarchy so both can
evolve independently.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Abstraction
Implementor
Refined type
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
abstract class Notification {
     protected final Channel channel;
   }
   // Alert/Receipt notifications x Email/Sms channels
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The notification abstraction delegates delivery to Channel implementations. New notification behavior
and new delivery channels need not create a subclass for every combination. Both sides still need a
coherent contract.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Ordinary composition alone is not enough to establish Bridge intent.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which two dimensions vary independently?
Answer: Notification type (Alert/Receipt) and transport (Email/SMS) vary independently. Compose
one of each rather than creating every combined subclass.

It composes two varying dimensions instead of encoding their Cartesian product
in one inheritance hierarchy.

Implementor

Concrete channel

   With bridge: Alert, Receipt + EmailChannel, SmsChannel

pages.title: STRUCTURAL What is Composite?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
COMPOSITE
51
Q034
STRUCTURAL
What is Composite?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Composite represents a part-whole tree where leaves and groups support a
common operation.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Component
Leaf
Composite
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
interface CostItem { int cents(); }
   // Product is a leaf; Bundle sums child CostItems.
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Clients can price a Product or Bundle through CostItem. Use a tree or explicitly define shared-node
graph semantics. A group recursively delegates the operation to its children.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Recursion is unsafe if cycles are allowed accidentally.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How would you prevent a bundle containing itself?
Answer: Reject insertion if a child is this bundle or already reaches it through descendants. An
immutable tree and visited-node checks can enforce acyclicity.

pages.title: STRUCTURAL Should leaf objects expose add/remove operations?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
COMPOSITE
52
Q035
STRUCTURAL
Should leaf objects expose add/remove operations?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Choose between a uniform but partly unsupported interface and a safer split
where only composites expose child management.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Leaf
Composite
Child components
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
CostItem -> cents()
   Bundle -> add(CostItem), remove(CostItem)
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Keeping add/remove out of leaves avoids unsupported operations and can better preserve
substitution. Uniform management APIs can simplify some clients but need a deliberate contract.
Immutable trees are another useful choice.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Returning fake success from leaf.add breaks expectations.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which clients actually need tree editing?
Answer: Only editors, builders, and admin tools that change bundle structure need add/remove
operations; ordinary pricing clients need cents() only.

COMPOSITE
53
Q036
STRUCTURAL
How do you handle performance and ownership in
Composite?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Bound depth, define child ownership and cache derived totals only with a valid
invalidation policy.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Component
Leaf
Child components
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Bundle(List<CostItem> children) uses List.copyOf(children)
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Immutable children make aggregate computation easier to reason about. Large/deep trees may
require iterative traversal or incremental summaries. Shared mutable children can change several
parents unexpectedly.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A cached total becomes stale if a child changes without notification.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How do you test a shared child update?
Answer: Update one shared child and assert each parent reflects the agreed ownership model; if
parents are immutable, confirm shared mutable children are rejected.

pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
DECORATOR
55
Q037
STRUCTURAL
What is Decorator?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Decorator adds behavior by wrapping an object behind the same component
contract.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Client
Wrapper
Component
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
interface Sender { void send(Message m); }
   // LoggingSender wraps Sender; CompressionSender wraps Sender.
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Decorators can be stacked at assembly time without multiplying subclasses for every feature
combination. The wrapper must preserve required semantics and deliberately choose behavior
before/after delegation.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A wrapper that changes the expected interface is more likely an Adapter.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which order should the wrappers use?
Answer: Choose order from the required behavior: authorize before send, log appropriate data,
then compress before encryption. Test the actual nested call path.

DECORATOR
56
Q038
STRUCTURAL
Why does decorator order matter?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Each wrapper sees the call and data at its position, so changing nesting can
change effects, timing and errors.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Wrapper
Component
Extra behavior
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Retry(Tracing(Sender)) -> each retry can get a trace
   Tracing(Retry(Sender)) -> one outer logical operation span
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Choose the intended observability, authorization and failure boundary. Compression then encryption
differs from encryption then compression. Tests should assert operation order and failure behavior,
not only final success.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Retry wrappers can duplicate nonidempotent effects.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What should happen when logging itself fails?
Answer: A noncritical logging failure should usually be isolated and reported without changing
successful delivery. Never silently ignore an audit failure when audit is mandatory.

Q040
STRUCTURAL
What is Facade?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Facade supplies a simpler cohesive interface over a set of subsystem operations.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Client
Facade
Subsystem A
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
CheckoutFacade.placeOrder(request)
   // Coordinates pricing, stock and payment collaborators.
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The client need not know every subsystem step. A facade should delegate rather than absorb all
domain policy into a giant service. Its purpose is usability and coupling reduction.
INTERVIEW TRAP
One method call does not mean one atomic distributed operation.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What happens if payment succeeds and shipment fails?
Answer: Do not call the whole operation atomic. Track order state and use a compensating or
recovery workflow to retry shipment or refund when business policy requires.

   Mediator: form controls communicate through a coordinator

through the mediator. One component can play both roles, but explaining separate responsibilities
keeps the design clear.

Answer: The client knows the Facade, but subsystems need not. In Mediator, collaborating controls
know or communicate through the coordinator.

STRUCTURAL
What is Flyweight?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Flyweight shares common intrinsic state across many logical objects while callers
supply differing extrinsic context.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Caller context
Flyweight pool
Shared immutable
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
GlyphStyle(font, size, color) shared
   Glyph position supplied when drawing

intrinsic state from per-use position, owner or request identity. The shared value should normally be
immutable.

ID, tenant context, and mutable state outside the flyweight.

pages.title: STRUCTURAL How is Flyweight different from a normal cache?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
FLYWEIGHT
64
Q044
STRUCTURAL
How is Flyweight different from a normal cache?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Flyweight models shared identity/state for many logical instances; a cache
broadly retains previously computed or loaded results.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Flyweight pool
Shared immutable
Per-call context
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
StylePool returns one immutable style for equivalent StyleKey
   Product cache stores a source result with expiry
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A flyweight pool may be implemented with a map/cache, but the design intent is state factoring.
Lifetime and eviction depend on equality/identity assumptions and actual memory savings. Measure
retained memory.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A map named pool is not automatically a Flyweight.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Does the client require reference identity?
Answer: Not necessarily. If clients only care about equivalent immutable values, equality is enough;
reference identity should be part of the contract only when required.

65
Q045
STRUCTURAL
What can go wrong with a Flyweight pool?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Unbounded unique keys can consume more memory than sharing saves, and
mutable keys/state can corrupt reuse.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Caller context
Flyweight pool
Per-call context
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
ConcurrentHashMap<StyleKey, GlyphStyle> with stable value keys
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use bounded domains or reviewed retention policies. computeIfAbsent can coordinate construction
within the map's contract, but loaders should avoid inappropriate recursion/blocking. Correct equality
and hash codes define which styles are shared.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Including unique requestId in StyleKey defeats sharing.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How would you prove memory savings?
Answer: Benchmark allocated objects and retained heap for realistic cardinality, plus hit ratio and
pool overhead. An unbounded map may cost more than sharing saves.

pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
PROXY
67
Q046
STRUCTURAL
What is Proxy?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Proxy stands in for a subject and controls access, such as authorization, lazy
creation or remote invocation.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Client
Proxy
Subject contract
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
interface Report { Data load(); }
   // AuthorizedReportProxy checks permission then delegates.
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The client uses the subject contract while the proxy manages an access concern. This differs from
Decorator's primary intent of composable responsibility addition, although structures can look similar.
Preserve documented exceptions and results.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A remote proxy cannot make a network call behave like a guaranteed local call.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What timeout semantics should it expose?
Answer: Expose deadlines and timeout exceptions clearly. A timeout says the remote result may be
unknown, not that the action was never performed.

68
Q047
STRUCTURAL
How do JDK dynamic proxies and subclass proxies
differ?
THE SHORT ANSWER
JDK dynamic proxies implement interfaces; subclass proxies derive from a
concrete class and inherit its overridability constraints.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Proxy
Subject contract
Real subject
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Proxy.newProxyInstance(loader, interfaces, invocationHandler)
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
JDK proxy invocation routes through an InvocationHandler. A subclass cannot override final methods;
private methods are not normal override join points. Framework defaults depend on configuration.
Handle Object methods and exception translation appropriately.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Never assume every Spring bean uses the same proxy type.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Why can a final method escape advice?
Answer: Subclass proxies cannot override final methods, so proxy interception cannot apply advice
to that call. JDK dynamic proxies advise interface methods through their proxy.

Why does a self-call bypass common Spring proxy
advice?

proxy interception boundary.

CHAIN OF RESPONSIBILITY
71
Q049
BEHAVIORAL
What is Chain of Responsibility?
THE SHORT ANSWER
It gives multiple handlers a chance to process a request, reducing sender
coupling to a specific receiver.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Request
Handler A
Handler B
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Request -> authentication handler -> quota handler -> endpoint
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Classical chains may stop at a suitable handler; validation/filter variants can execute multiple steps
before continuing. Specify what handled, rejected and passed-on mean. Order must be visible and
testable.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A request should not silently vanish at the end.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What is the default terminal behavior?
Answer: Specify fail-closed terminal behavior, such as reject or explicit unhandled result. Never
silently authorize a request when no handler accepts it.

pages.title: BEHAVIORAL How do you design a safe chain contract?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
CHAIN OF RESPONSIBILITY
72
Q050
BEHAVIORAL
How do you design a safe chain contract?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Represent continuation and rejection explicitly, and define who owns progression
through the chain.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Handler A
Handler B
Terminal result
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Decision = Continue | Reject(reason) | Handled(result)
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A linked handler or coordinator-owned list can work. Prevent double continuation, unexpected cycles
and exceptions interpreted as success. Security chains should deny unsupported paths deliberately
rather than accidentally permit them.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Logging a rejection then continuing may undo the policy.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which handler can terminate processing?
Answer: The first handler that returns a handled/terminal result may stop the chain. Define errors
and fallback behavior explicitly rather than relying on null.

How does a chain differ from a fixed pipeline?

generally applies a defined sequence of transformations.

   Pipeline stage transforms input for the next stage

pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
COMMAND
75
Q052
BEHAVIORAL
What is Command?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Command encapsulates a request, its receiver/context and execution behavior as
an object.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Invoker
Command object
Receiver
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
interface Command { void execute(); }
   record RenameCommand(Document doc, String title) implements Command {
     public void execute() { doc.setTitle(title); }
   }
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
It enables deferred invocation, queues, histories or audit metadata. A command object need not be
remotely serializable or durable. Separate in-memory behavior from a persisted command envelope.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Capturing a live entity reference does not make a safe durable message.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What must be stored for execution after restart?
Answer: Persist a durable command ID, validated payload, type/version, execution state, and retry
policy. In-memory Runnable objects cannot survive a restart.

pages.fullText:

COMMAND
76
Q053
BEHAVIORAL
How can Command support undo?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Store the information needed to reverse a local action or provide an explicit
compensating operation.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Command object
Receiver
Outcome
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Rename records previousTitle before changing it
   undo restores that title under reviewed ordering rules
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Not every action is reversible. Undo after another edit may overwrite valid work unless version/history
ownership is defined. A payment refund is a new business action, not erasure of the original payment.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Undo is not a generic rollback of external side effects.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What happens if compensation fails?
Answer: Escalate to reconciliation or a human recovery queue with the original operation ID. An
undo command is not a guaranteed transaction rollback.

How do commands need to change for distributed
delivery?

Use a stable command identity, serializable intent and a durable idempotent
handling/recovery policy.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Invoker
Command object
Outcome

IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A queued command may execute more than once. Deduplicate at the durable effect boundary or use a
provider-supported idempotency key. Record accepted, executing and completed states if the
workflow needs them.

as pending until confirmed or reconciled, not as a definite failure.

Q055

What is Interpreter?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Interpreter represents grammar rules as objects that evaluate sentences in a
supplied context.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Input grammar
AST nodes
Context
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Expr = Number | Add(Expr,Expr)
   Add(Number(2),Number(3)).eval() -> 5
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Terminal nodes represent basic values; nonterminals combine expressions. It suits a small stable
language or expression grammar. Parsing the text into the structure is a separate concern from
evaluation.
INTERVIEW TRAP
An if statement is not automatically an Interpreter.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which part owns syntax errors?

When should you choose a parser/library instead?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Choose a mature parser/evaluator when grammar, diagnostics, security or
performance exceeds a small object-tree model.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
AST nodes
Context
Evaluated result
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Complex expression language -> grammar tool/library + controlled evaluation
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The classical pattern can create many rule classes and expensive traversals. Do not expose arbitrary
scripting capabilities merely to make business rules configurable. Bound nesting and evaluation cost
for untrusted input.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A user expression can cause resource exhaustion even without code execution.

How do you validate and limit rule complexity?
Answer: Restrict allowed operators, recursion depth, input length, evaluation time, and data
access. Prefer a proven parser when grammar and error handling grow.

Q058
BEHAVIORAL
What is Iterator?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Iterator exposes sequential traversal while hiding the underlying aggregate
representation.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Collection
Iterator
hasNext()
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Iterator<Order> it = orders.iterator();
   while (it.hasNext()) { process(it.next()); }
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The traversal contract defines exhaustion and supported mutation. Java Iterable allows obtaining an
iterator; Iterator carries traversal state. A tree or paged data source can provide a suitable traversal
abstraction.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Iteration does not automatically mean all data is loaded or stable.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What happens after exhaustion?
Answer: hasNext() becomes false; calling next() after exhaustion normally throws
NoSuchElementException. Do not infer automatic restart.

Q059
BEHAVIORAL
Are fail-fast iterators a concurrency guarantee?
THE SHORT ANSWER
No. Fail-fast detection is generally best effort and must not be used as a
correctness mechanism for concurrent access.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Iterator
hasNext()
next()
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Concurrent modification may throw ConcurrentModificationException
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Choose synchronization, immutable snapshots or a collection with documented concurrent iteration
semantics. Weakly consistent and snapshot iterators behave differently. Do not catch the exception
and assume the traversal became complete.
INTERVIEW TRAP
No exception does not prove no concurrent modification occurred.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which semantics does CopyOnWriteArrayList provide?
Answer: CopyOnWriteArrayList iterators traverse a snapshot from iterator creation and do not
reflect later writes; writes copy the array, making it suited to read-heavy cases.

Q060

How do Iterator and Stream differ?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Iterator gives explicit pull traversal; Stream describes a pipeline with its own
consumption, laziness and resource semantics.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Collection
Iterator
next()
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
orders.stream().filter(Order::paid).map(Order::id).toList();
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A stream can be backed by a collection, iterator-like source or I/O resource. Streams are generally
single-use and can require closing when resource-backed. Parallel execution adds ordering and
thread-safety considerations.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Using Stream does not automatically make mutable work thread-safe.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
When is explicit iteration clearer?
Answer: Use an explicit loop when traversal needs early return, checked resource handling,
mutation through Iterator.remove(), or step-by-step debugging.

Q061
BEHAVIORAL
What is Mediator?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Mediator coordinates interactions among colleagues so they need not depend
directly on every peer.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Peer A
Mediator
Peer B
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
FormMediator coordinates country, city and submit controls
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A control reports a change to the mediator, which applies the agreed interaction rules. Domain work
should remain with appropriate collaborators. This can reduce a dense dependency graph while making
coordination more explicit.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A mediator that performs every task becomes a god object.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which rules should stay inside the controls?

navigation, and dependency decisions in the Mediator.

Q062

How does Mediator differ from Observer?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Mediator coordinates a specific interaction workflow; Observer distributes
change notifications to subscribers.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Mediator
Peer B
Coordinated effect
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Observer: country changed -> subscribers notified
   Mediator: country changed -> reload cities + reset selection + revalidate
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A mediator can receive observer-style events. The distinction is the responsibility for coordination, not
whether callbacks exist. Avoid circular event flows and define reentrancy/order where state changes
trigger more notifications.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Event notification alone does not define workflow consistency.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How would you prevent repeated update loops?
Answer: Use change detection, deduplication, or bounded propagation; do not let callbacks blindly
publish the same update forever.

What are Mediator's main tradeoffs?
THE SHORT ANSWER
It reduces peer coupling but can concentrate complex coordination and become a
bottleneck for changes.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Peer A
Mediator
Coordinated effect
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Split checkout workflow and form workflow into coherent coordinators
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Keep interaction rules cohesive, test transitions and outcomes, and avoid exposing every peer's
internals. A mediator usually executes in-process; a distributed orchestrator needs durable state and
recovery beyond this pattern.

An in-memory mediator cannot survive process failure by itself.

Which state needs persistence in a long-running workflow?

durable storage. An in-memory mediator cannot resume after crash.

Q064
BEHAVIORAL
What is Memento?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Memento lets an originator capture and restore its state through an opaque
snapshot managed by a caretaker.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Editor state
Snapshot
Caretaker
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Editor -> snapshot -> UndoHistory
   UndoHistory returns snapshot -> Editor restores
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The originator understands the snapshot's internals; the caretaker stores it without rewriting state.
Java access control and immutable snapshot types can support the boundary. Choose the required
state depth.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Exposing a mutable live list is not a safe snapshot.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which fields belong in the snapshot?
Answer: Save only state needed to restore the defined editor behavior: content, cursor, and
selected options. Avoid copying unrelated services or credentials.

a separate configured object by copying.

Snapshot

Restore

   Prototype: create a new document from a template

usually makes a new object with a new identity.

How do you manage snapshot cost and compatibility?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Bound history, use immutable/shared data safely, and version snapshots when
restoring across deployments.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Editor state
Snapshot
Restore
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Keep last 50 editor states; discard older history
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Large graphs make full snapshots expensive. Deltas reduce size but complicate replay and dependency
ordering. Do not serialize secrets or resource handles casually. Domain restoration must still enforce
valid current invariants.

When would an event log be more suitable?

only point-in-time editor undo. Replay and versioning must be designed.

consumers, and permit replay/retry. In-process Observer has none of those guarantees.

What is State?
THE SHORT ANSWER
State delegates behavior to an object representing the context's current state,
allowing behavior to change with transitions.

Context
Current State
Legal transition
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
OrderState current = PendingState;
   current.cancel(order); // allowed only by its state contract

transition ownership explicitly. State is useful when many operations have substantial state-specific
behavior.

Answer: An explicit transition policy or current State implementation decides the next state;
persisted workflows should validate and atomically store that transition.

PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
STATE
101
Q072
BEHAVIORAL
How do you implement State safely for persisted
workflows?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Enforce transitions against durable version/current-state constraints and
handle duplicate or out-of-order events.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Context
Current State
Next State
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
UPDATE orders SET status='PAID', version=version+1
   WHERE id=:id AND status='PENDING' AND version=:expected;
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
State objects can express policy, while the database enforces the actual transition under concurrency.
Record event identity when duplicate delivery matters. A transition that emits an event needs reliable
publication such as an outbox.
INTERVIEW TRAP
An in-memory state change cannot guarantee the database committed.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What if payment succeeds before persistence fails?
Answer: Record payment intent/outcome with an idempotency key and reconcile after a crash.
Never assume a failed DB commit undoes an external payment.

pages.fullText:

PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
STRATEGY
103
Q073
BEHAVIORAL
What is Strategy?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Strategy encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind a contract used by a
context.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Context
Strategy contract
Algorithm A
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
interface Discount { long apply(long cents); }
   Discount tenPercent = cents -> cents - cents / 10;
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The context delegates without encoding every algorithm's rules. Lambdas fit single-method policies,
while classes fit richer state/configuration. Define precision, valid inputs and output guarantees so
strategies remain interchangeable.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Algorithm interchangeability does not excuse different business units or semantics.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How would you validate a new strategy?
Answer: Run shared contract tests, boundary values, invalid identifiers, and golden examples;
confirm it obeys the same return and error policy as other strategies.

How should strategy selection be implemented?

Choose through an explicit policy/registry and reject unsupported identifiers
deliberately.

Strategy contract

Algorithm B
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Discount d = strategies.get(code);
   if (d == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown discount");
IN PLAIN ENGLISH

be perfectly reasonable. In Spring, injected strategies can be assembled into a validated map without
reflection.

configuration should select the single intended strategy.

Q075

How do you test Strategies for substitutability?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Run shared contract tests across implementations, then test each algorithm's
specific examples and boundaries.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Context
Strategy contract
Algorithm B
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
For valid cents: result >= 0 and result <= original
   Then verify agreed rounding for each discount
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The contract should reflect real business rules, not invented constraints that every policy cannot
satisfy. Stateful strategies need lifecycle and concurrency review. Compare outputs using exact units
appropriate to the domain.

A shared interface does not prove behavioral compatibility.

Which extreme inputs reveal overflow?

amounts, nulls, and unsupported policies.

pages.title: BEHAVIORAL What is Template Method?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
TEMPLATE METHOD
107
Q076
BEHAVIORAL
What is Template Method?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Template Method fixes an algorithm's sequence in a superclass and lets
subclasses specialize selected steps.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Base workflow
Stable steps
Variation hooks
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
abstract class ImportJob {
     final void run() { read(); validate(); save(); }
     abstract void read(); abstract void validate(); abstract void save();
   }
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The template owns ordering, while steps provide variation. Making the template final can protect
sequencing. This is suited to a stable shared workflow, not arbitrary independently combinable
behaviors.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Subclasses can still violate step contracts even when run is final.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which invariant depends on the step order?
Answer: The order may ensure validate before charge and cleanup after resources are opened.
Tests must show reordered steps would violate a stated invariant.

pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
TEMPLATE METHOD

Q077
BEHAVIORAL
How do hooks differ from abstract steps?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Abstract steps require implementation; hooks provide optional extension points
with defined defaults.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Stable steps
Variation hooks
Complete result
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
protected void beforeSave() { } // optional no-op hook
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Hooks should be few and have precise timing/side-effect contracts. Too many hooks create an implicit
framework that is difficult to reason about. Template execution must define cleanup if a step fails.
INTERVIEW TRAP
A finally block should not hide an earlier failure with cleanup errors.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
What resources must be released after read fails?
Answer: Close streams, files, and locks in finally or try-with-resources even when reading fails.
Avoid leaving the resource alive after a subclass hook throws.

composition?

inheritance causes many combinations.

pages.title: BEHAVIORAL What is Visitor?
pages.fullText:
JAVA DESIGN PATTERNS
PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
VISITOR
111
Q079
BEHAVIORAL
What is Visitor?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Visitor separates operations from elements by letting elements dispatch to
type-specific visitor methods.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Element
accept(visitor)
visit(Type)
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
interface Expr { <R> R accept(Visitor<R> v); }
   // NumberExpr.accept -> v.visitNumber(this)
   // AddExpr.accept -> v.visitAdd(this)
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The element call and overloaded visit method establish the classic double-dispatch structure.
Evaluation, printing or analysis can be separate visitors over the same tree. The tree structure stays
with elements.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Overloading alone does not dynamically select by runtime parameter type.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Why is accept needed?
Answer: accept(this) allows a node's runtime class to select the correct visit(NodeType) method,
achieving double dispatch without repeated instanceof chains.

VISITOR

Q080

What is Visitor's extension tradeoff?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Adding an operation is relatively easy; adding an element type can require
updating every visitor.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
accept(visitor)
visit(Type)
Operation
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
New operation: PrettyPrinter visitor
   New element: MultiplyExpr -> update Visitor and implementations
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Visitor fits a stable hierarchy with frequently added operations. If element kinds grow often,
polymorphic methods or a version-appropriate sealed-type dispatch may be simpler. Avoid default
handlers that silently skip unsupported elements.
INTERVIEW TRAP
The visitor can become brittle as the element set expands.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
Which dimension changes more often here?
Answer: If operations change frequently but node types stay stable, Visitor fits; if new node types
arrive often, adding methods to each visitor becomes expensive.

Q088

Is Spring singleton scope the GoF Singleton?
THE SHORT ANSWER
No. Spring singleton scope is normally one bean instance per bean definition per
container, rather than a globally enforced unique Java instance.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Two application
 contexts
two singleton-
scoped instances
another instance
 outside the co
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Two application contexts -> two singleton-scoped instances
   Manual new -> another instance outside the container
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A stateless singleton-scoped service is a useful lifecycle choice. Mutable fields still need concurrency
design. The container makes dependency replacement easier than static global lookup.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Singleton scope does not make request-specific fields safe.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How would you store per-request data instead?
Answer: Store per-request data in local variables, request-scoped beans, or explicit immutable
request context; never put mutable user data on a shared singleton service.

advised service

   DispatcherServlet -> HandlerAdapter -> supported handler

Are Spring application events durable Observer
delivery?
THE SHORT ANSWER
No. Application events integrate publishers/listeners inside the application
context; execution and transaction timing depend on configuration.
VISUAL MEMORY MAP
Spring client
Framework boundary
Application result
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
publisher.publishEvent(new OrderPlaced("42"));
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A default event multicaster commonly invokes synchronously, while asynchronous setup changes
propagation and failure behavior. A transactional event listener can align handling with a transaction
phase, but is not a durable cross-service outbox.
INTERVIEW TRAP
Process failure can lose work held only in memory.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How would you publish the order outcome reliably?
Answer: Persist an outbox row in the same DB transaction as the order, then publish
asynchronously with retries and idempotent consumers. Plain in-process events are not durable.

How do repository and hexagonal ports complement
GoF patterns?

They isolate domain access and dependency direction at architectural
boundaries; adapters and strategies can implement those boundaries.

Spring client
Framework boundary
Application result

Domain OrderRepository port <- JpaOrderAdapter
   Domain PaymentPort <- VendorPaymentAdapter

concrete Spring Data repositories and HTTP adapters outside.

Requirement

pages.title: ADVANCED How would you design a loan approval workflow?
pages.fullText:

PREMIUM STUDY NOTES
SENIOR INTERVIEW SCENARIOS AND ANTI-PATTERNS
131
Q096
ADVANCED
How would you design a loan approval workflow?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Make durable states and allowed transitions explicit, then use replaceable
policies for eligibility and handlers for ordered checks when justified.

Application state:
 RECEIVED
VERIFIED
APPROVED or
 REJECTED
SOURCE EXAMPLE / JAVA IDEA
Application state: RECEIVED -> VERIFIED -> APPROVED or REJECTED
   EligibilityPolicy selected by product
IN PLAIN ENGLISH
State governs workflow lifecycle; Strategy governs decision algorithm variation. Persist versioned
transitions and record decisions for audit. An in-memory mediator or command object alone cannot
recover a long-running process.

A design pattern does not replace durable orchestration requirements.
FOLLOW-UP EXPLAINED
How do you recover after a provider callback arrives twice?
Answer: Store callback/event IDs and a versioned loan state transition in durable storage. On
duplicate callback, return the prior result without approving twice.

How should patterns handle concurrency and resource
ownership?

Define immutability, thread-safety and close/lifecycle rules explicitly; the

Singletons, pools, observers and mutable commands need especially careful review. Prefer immutable
values and per-operation state where feasible. Test realistic concurrent use and failure cleanup rather

pages.title: Check whether an integer is prime.
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · NUMBER FOUNDATIONS QUESTION 001 / 120
Q001. Check whether an integer is prime.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Reject values below two; check divisors only through the square root. Use division in the loop
condition to avoid overflow in d*d.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
Check whether an integer is
prime. ➜
KEY LOGIC
Reject values below two; check
divisors only through the square
root.
➜
RESULT
true; 1 -> false
💡 If n has a nontrivial divisor, one factor is at most sqrt(n).
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(sqrt(n)); auxiliary space O(1).
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Negative values, zero and one are not prime.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would a sieve answer many prime queries?
Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes once up to the largest query number. Mark multiples of each prime starting
at p*p; then each query is a constant-time array lookup. Preprocessing takes about O(N log log N) time and
O(N) space.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q001 · 5 lines
static boolean isPrime(int n) {
  if (n < 2) return false;
  for (int d = 2; d <= n / d; d++) if (n % d == 0) return false;
  return true;
}

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · NUMBER FOUNDATIONS QUESTION 002 / 120
Q002. Find the greatest common divisor.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
For nonnegative longs, repeatedly replace the pair by the divisor and remainder. Euclid preserves
the gcd and stops when the remainder becomes zero.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
gcd(48,18) ➜
KEY LOGIC
For nonnegative longs, repeatedly
replace the pair by the divisor and
remainder.
➜
RESULT
6; gcd(0,0) -> 0
💡 (48,18) -> (18,12) -> (12,6) -> (6,0).
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(log(min(a,b))) for positive operands; space O(1).
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
The nonnegative contract avoids abs(Long.MIN_VALUE).
Zero is handled explicitly by the loop.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would you compute lcm without overflowing?
Compute gcd first, then calculate (a / gcd(a,b)) * b. Dividing before multiplying reduces overflow risk. For
guaranteed exact large results, use BigInteger; Math.multiplyExact can detect long overflow.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q002 · 5 lines
static long gcd(long a, long b) {
  if (a < 0 || b < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException();
  while (b != 0) { long r = a % b; a = b; b = r; }
  return a;
}

Q003. Compute factorial without primitive overflow.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER

When could a long implementation use Math.multiplyExact?
Use a long result while each factorial step fits in signed 64-bit range. Math.multiplyExact(result, i) throws

not.

  BigInteger result = BigInteger.ONE;
  for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++) result = result.multiply(BigInteger.valueOf(i));
  return result;
}

pages.title: Compute the nth Fibonacci number.
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · NUMBER FOUNDATIONS QUESTION 004 / 120
Q004. Compute the nth Fibonacci number.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Maintain two adjacent values and advance them iteratively. BigInteger gives exact results beyond
primitive limits without exponential recursive recomputation.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
F(10) ➜
KEY LOGIC
Maintain two adjacent values and
advance them iteratively.
➜
RESULT
55; F(0) -> 0
💡 At loop entry i, a=F(i) and b=F(i+1).
⏱ TIME & SPACE
n additions; O(n) bits of live numeric storage, with
growing addition bit cost.
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Reject negative index; define the zero-index convention
before coding.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would fast doubling reduce the number of arithmetic steps?
Fast doubling calculates F(2k)=F(k)*(2*F(k+1)-F(k)) and F(2k+1)=F(k)^2+F(k+1)^2. Halve the index
recursively or use its bits, taking O(log n) big-integer arithmetic steps instead of O(n).
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q004 · 8 lines
static BigInteger fibonacci(int n) {
  if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException();
  BigInteger a = BigInteger.ZERO, b = BigInteger.ONE;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    BigInteger next = a.add(b); a = b; b = next;
  }
  return a;
}

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · NUMBER FOUNDATIONS QUESTION 005 / 120
Q005. Check whether a nonnegative integer is a
decimal palindrome.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Reverse the digits into a long and compare with the original. The wider accumulator safely holds
the reversed decimal representation of any nonnegative int.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
1221 ➜
KEY LOGIC
Reverse the digits into a long and
compare with the original.
➜
RESULT
true; -121 -> false
💡 Reversing 1221 reconstructs the same value; trailing zeros change the representation.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(decimal digits); space O(1).
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Zero is a palindrome; leading zeros are not part of an
integer value.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would reversing only half the digits work?
Build only the reversed last half. Stop when the remaining half is no larger than the reversed half. Compare
them directly for even digit counts, or drop the reversed half's middle digit for odd counts. Numbers ending
in zero need special handling.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q005 · 8 lines
static boolean numberPalindrome(int n) {
  if (n < 0) return false;
  long reversed = 0; int remaining = n;
  while (remaining != 0) {
    reversed = reversed * 10 + remaining % 10; remaining /= 10;
  }
  return reversed == n;
}

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · DIGITS, BITS AND ARITHMETIC QUESTION 007 / 120
Q007. Check an Armstrong number.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Count decimal digits, raise each digit to that count using integer multiplication, and compare the
sum with the number. For an int input the accumulated powers fit in a long.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
153
➜
KEY LOGIC
Count decimal digits, raise each
digit to that count using integer
multiplication, and compare the
sum with the number.
➜
RESULT
true because 1^3+5^3+3^3=153
💡 Use integer powers rather than floating-point equality.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(digits squared); auxiliary space O(digits) for the
digit-count string.
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Zero has one decimal digit and passes; negative inputs
fail.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would you avoid the digit-count string allocation?
Count digits with a division loop: start at one and repeatedly divide by ten until the remaining number is
below ten. Then perform the power sum. This avoids Integer.toString and its allocation.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q007 · 10 lines
static boolean armstrong(int value) {
  if (value < 0) return false;
  int digits = Integer.toString(value).length(), n = value; long sum = 0;
  do {
    int d = n % 10; long power = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < digits; i++) power *= d;
    sum += power; n /= 10;
  } while (n > 0);
  return sum == value;
}

Q009. Implement exponentiation by squaring.

  while (n > 0) {
    if ((n & 1) != 0) result *= base;
    base *= base; n >>= 1;

  return result;
}

  int[] counts = new int[26];

}

  StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();

}

}

Q029. Find a majority element, if one exists.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER

greater than n/2 because existence is not assumed here.

empty input returns absent.

  int count=0; for(int x:a) if(x==candidate) count++;
  return count>a.length/2 ? OptionalInt.of(candidate) : OptionalInt.empty();
}

Q041. Implement stable merge sort.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER

O(log n) recursion.

with equal keys.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
When does iterative bottom-up merge sort help?
Bottom-up merge sort avoids recursive stack frames and merges runs of width 1, 2, 4, 8, and so on. It is
useful for predictable iterative control while retaining O(n log n) time and O(n) merge storage.

static void mergeSortRange(int[] a,int[] temp,int l,int r) {
  if(r-l<2) return; int m=l+(r-l)/2;
  mergeSortRange(a,temp,l,m); mergeSortRange(a,temp,m,r);
  int i=l,j=m,k=l;
  while(i<m && j<r) temp[k++]=a[i]<=a[j] ? a[i++] : a[j++];
  while(i<m) temp[k++]=a[i++]; while(j<r) temp[k++]=a[j++];
  System.arraycopy(temp,l,a,l,r-l);
}

CHAPTER 09 · SORTING, SELECTION AND INTERVALS QUESTION 042 / 120
Q042. Implement in-place quicksort.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Partition around a selected pivot using two inward scans, then recurse on remaining partitions.
This middle-pivot version is simple but does not guarantee balanced partitions or logarithmic
stack depth.
SKETCH THE PATTERN

using two inward scans, then
recurse on remaining partitions.
➜

💡 The pivot value stops each scan; exchanges place values on appropriate sides.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Average O(n log n) under suitable partitions; worst O(n
squared). Stack worst O(n).
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
In-place is not constant total space when recursion is
included; stability is not preserved.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How do randomized pivots or introsort improve robustness?
Randomized pivots reduce the chance of repeatedly choosing a bad pivot on patterned input. Introsort
switches to heapsort when recursion becomes too deep, preserving O(n log n) worst-case time while
keeping fast average quicksort behavior.

static void quickSort(int[] a) { quickSortRange(a,0,a.length-1); }
static void quickSortRange(int[] a,int l,int r) {
  if(l>=r) return; int i=l,j=r,pivot=a[l+(r-l)/2];
  while(i<=j) {
    while(a[i]<pivot) i++; while(a[j]>pivot) j--;
    if(i<=j) { int t=a[i]; a[i++]=a[j]; a[j--]=t; }
  }
  if(l<j) quickSortRange(a,l,j); if(i<r) quickSortRange(a,i,r);
}

static List<Integer> spiral(int[][] a) {
  int cols=columns(a),top=0,bottom=a.length-1,left=0,right=cols-1;
  List<Integer> out=new ArrayList<>();
  while(top<=bottom && left<=right) {
    for(int c=left;c<=right;c++) out.add(a[top][c]); top++;
    for(int r=top;r<=bottom;r++) out.add(a[r][right]); right--;
    if(top<=bottom) { for(int c=right;c>=left;c--) out.add(a[bottom][c]); bottom--; }
    if(left<=right) { for(int r=bottom;r>=top;r--) out.add(a[r][left]); left++; }
  }
  return out;
}

Q051. Validate balanced brackets.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Push opening brackets and match each closing bracket with the most recent unmatched opening
bracket. This version rejects all characters outside the six bracket symbols.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT

each closing bracket with the

stack.

Empty input passes; unmatched leftover openings fail.

How would you allow ordinary characters while checking delimiters?

match recognized closings. State whether text inside quotes or escaped delimiters should be ignored
separately.

  Deque<Character> stack=new ArrayDeque<>();
  for(char c:text.toCharArray()) {
    if(c=='(' || c=='[' || c=='{') stack.push(c);
    else {
      char expected=c==')' ? '(' : c==']' ? '[' : c=='}' ? '{' : 0;
      if(expected==0 || stack.isEmpty() || stack.pop()!=expected) return false;
    }
  }
  return stack.isEmpty();
}

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 11 · STACKS AND MONOTONIC STACKS QUESTION 052 / 120
Q052. Find the next greater value to the right.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Scan from right to left, removing candidates no larger than the current value. The stack then
exposes the nearest surviving greater value.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
[2,1,2,4,3] ➜
KEY LOGIC
Scan from right to left, removing
candidates no larger than the
current value.
➜
RESULT
[4,2,4,absent,absent]
💡 Smaller/equal candidates are blocked by the current closer value for earlier positions.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(n), each value pushed/popped once; space
O(n).
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
The relation is strictly greater, not greater-or-equal.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would circular next-greater search use a doubled scan?
Process indices from 2n-1 down to zero, using i % n to map into the original array. Maintain a decreasing
stack; fill answers only in the final n relevant visits, so each value can see items across the wraparound.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q052 · 9 lines
static OptionalInt[] nextGreater(int[] a) {
  OptionalInt[] out=new OptionalInt[a.length]; Deque<Integer> stack=new ArrayDeque<>();
  for(int i=a.length-1;i>=0;i--) {
    while(!stack.isEmpty() && stack.peek()<=a[i]) stack.pop();
    out[i]=stack.isEmpty() ? OptionalInt.empty() : OptionalInt.of(stack.peek());
    stack.push(a[i]);
  }
  return out;
}

CHAPTER 11 · STACKS AND MONOTONIC STACKS QUESTION 053 / 120
Q053. Find days until a warmer temperature.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Maintain indices whose next warmer day is unresolved. When a warmer reading arrives, pop
colder indices and record their distance to the current index.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
[73,74,75,71,69,72,76,73] ➜
KEY LOGIC
Maintain indices whose next
warmer day is unresolved.
➜
RESULT

💡 Each popped day receives its first strictly warmer day.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(n); space O(n), excluding output.
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Equal temperatures do not resolve a wait; no warmer
day yields zero.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
Could a bounded temperature alphabet support another approach?
If temperatures belong to a small fixed integer range, keep the most recent future index for each possible
temperature while scanning backward; find the closest warmer recorded temperature. Cost depends on
alphabet size rather than stack operations.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q053 · 10 lines
static int[] warmerDays(int[] temperatures) {
  int[] days=new int[temperatures.length]; Deque<Integer> stack=new ArrayDeque<>();
  for(int i=0;i<temperatures.length;i++) {
    while(!stack.isEmpty() && temperatures[i]>temperatures[stack.peek()]) {
      int previous=stack.pop(); days[previous]=i-previous;
    }
    stack.push(i);
  }
  return days;
}

CHAPTER 11 · STACKS AND MONOTONIC STACKS QUESTION 054 / 120
Q054. Design a stack with constant-time minimum.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Maintain a value stack and a minimum stack. Push a minimum whenever the new value is no
larger than the current minimum; pop that minimum when its matching value is removed.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
push 2,1,1; pop ➜
KEY LOGIC
Maintain a value stack and a
minimum stack.
➜
RESULT
minimum still 1
💡 Equal minima need one marker per pushed occurrence.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Each operation O(1); total storage O(n).
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Empty pop/min throws NoSuchElementException; this
class is not thread-safe.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How could storing a minimum with each entry simplify the invariant?
Store each stack entry as (value, minimumSoFar). push computes min(value, previousMin), pop removes
both, and getMin reads the top's saved minimum. All operations are O(1), with O(n) storage.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q054 · 6 lines
static class MinStack {
  private final Deque<Integer> values=new ArrayDeque<>(), minima=new ArrayDeque<>();
  void push(int x) { values.push(x); if(minima.isEmpty() || x<=minima.peek()) minima.push(x); }
  int pop() { int x=values.pop(); if(x==minima.peek()) minima.pop(); return x; }
  int min() { return minima.element(); }
}

pages.title: Find the k most frequent integers with deterministic ties.
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 · HEAPS, WINDOWS AND CACHE DESIGN QUESTION 056 / 120
Q056. Find the k most frequent integers with
deterministic ties.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Count frequencies, then retain the best k keys with a worst-first heap. Rank higher frequency first
and lower numeric value first on ties.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
[1,1,2,2,3], k=2 ➜
KEY LOGIC
Count frequencies, then retain the
best k keys with a worst-first heap.
➜
RESULT
[1,2]
💡 The heap discards the lowest frequency, breaking a tie against the larger value.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Expected O(n+u log(k+1)+k log(k+1)); space O(u+k), with
k capped by u in output.
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
k=0 returns empty; k above distinct count returns every
key.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would buckets trade heap work for frequency-indexed storage?
Build a frequency map, then buckets indexed by count (0..n). Walk counts from largest to smallest and
collect k values, sorting values within equal-frequency buckets if deterministic tie order is required.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q056 · 9 lines
static List<Integer> topFrequent(int[] a,int k) {
  if(k<0) throw new IllegalArgumentException();
  Map<Integer,Integer> freq=new HashMap<>(); for(int x:a) freq.merge(x,1,Integer::sum);
  Comparator<Integer> best=Comparator.comparingInt((Integer x)->freq.get(x))
      .reversed().thenComparingInt(x->x);
  PriorityQueue<Integer> heap=new PriorityQueue<>(best.reversed());
  for(int x:freq.keySet()) { heap.offer(x); if(heap.size()>k) heap.poll(); }
  List<Integer> out=new ArrayList<>(heap); out.sort(best); return out;
}

CHAPTER 12 · HEAPS, WINDOWS AND CACHE DESIGN QUESTION 058 / 120
Q058. Maintain the kth largest value in a stream.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Keep a min-heap of at most k values. After each insertion, its minimum is the kth largest once at
least k values have arrived.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
k=2; add 5 ➜
KEY LOGIC
Keep a min-heap of at most k
values.
➜
RESULT
absent; add 1 -> 1; add 8 -> 5
💡 Old values below the retained top k can never affect a future kth-largest answer.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Each add O(log(k+1)); space O(k).

Duplicates count as separate values; concurrent calls
require a separate policy.

How would a changing k affect discarded history?
A fixed-size heap throws away values below the current kth threshold. If k later increases, those discarded
values may be needed, so either retain full history or define a new stream/rebuild contract.

  private final int k; private final PriorityQueue<Integer> heap=new PriorityQueue<>();
  KthStream(int k) { if(k<1) throw new IllegalArgumentException(); this.k=k; }
  OptionalInt add(int value) {
    heap.offer(value); if(heap.size()>k) heap.poll();
    return heap.size()<k ? OptionalInt.empty() : OptionalInt.of(heap.element());
  }
}

CHAPTER 12 · HEAPS, WINDOWS AND CACHE DESIGN QUESTION 059 / 120
Q059. Design a bounded LRU cache.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Use access-order LinkedHashMap and evict the eldest entry after insertion exceeds capacity. A
successful get refreshes recency under this implementation.

and evict the eldest entry after

are part of its public surface.

How would composition give tighter API and null policies?

stated null policy. Encapsulation prevents callers from bypassing the invariants of access order and
maximum size.

  private final int capacity;

  }
  @Override protected boolean removeEldestEntry(Map.Entry<K,V> entry) {
    return size()>capacity;
  }
}

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 · HEAPS, WINDOWS AND CACHE DESIGN QUESTION 060 / 120
Q060. Find the maximum in every sliding window.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Maintain a deque of candidate indices with decreasing values. Remove expired indices from the
front and dominated values from the back.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
[1,3,-1,-3,5,3,6,7], k=3 ➜
KEY LOGIC
Maintain a deque of candidate
indices with decreasing values.
➜
RESULT
[3,3,5,5,6,7]
💡 A newer no-smaller value dominates an older candidate and expires later.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(n); auxiliary space O(k), excluding output.
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Require 1<=k<=n; storing indices is necessary for expiry.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would a heap compare in time and stale-entry management?
Store pairs (value,index) in a max-heap. Before returning the top, remove entries whose index is outside the
current window. This costs O(n log n) with stale-entry bookkeeping, versus O(n) amortized time for a
monotonic deque.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q060 · 11 lines
static int[] windowMax(int[] a,int k) {
  if(k<1 || k>a.length) throw new IllegalArgumentException();
  int[] out=new int[a.length-k+1]; Deque<Integer> deque=new ArrayDeque<>();
  for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++) {
    while(!deque.isEmpty() && deque.peekFirst()<=i-k) deque.removeFirst();
    while(!deque.isEmpty() && a[deque.peekLast()]<=a[i]) deque.removeLast();
    deque.addLast(i);
    if(i>=k-1) out[i-k+1]=a[deque.peekFirst()];
  }
  return out;
}

  while(a!=null && b!=null) {
    if(a.value<=b.value) { tail.next=a; a=a.next; }
    else { tail.next=b; b=b.next; }
    tail=tail.next;
  }
  tail.next=a!=null ? a : b; return dummy.next;
}

✎  SIMPLE ANSWER

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 · ADVANCED LINKED-LIST PROBLEMS QUESTION 068 / 120
Q068. Add numbers stored in reverse-order digit
lists.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Read one digit from each list plus carry, emit sum modulo ten and carry the quotient. Allocate a
fresh result.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
[2,4,3] + [5,6,4] ➜
KEY LOGIC
Read one digit from each list plus
carry, emit sum modulo ten and
carry the quotient.
➜
RESULT
[7,0,8]
💡 [2,4,3] represents 342; 342+465=807, output [7,0,8].
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(max(n,m)); auxiliary space O(1), excluding result
nodes.
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Null plus null returns null under this empty-input
convention; acyclic lists required.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
What changes for most-significant-digit-first lists?
For most-significant-digit-first lists, push digits onto two stacks, pop from least significant to most significant
with carry, and prepend output nodes. Alternatively reverse copied lists, add, and reverse the result.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q068 · 10 lines
static ListNode addDigits(ListNode a,ListNode b) {
  ListNode dummy=new ListNode(0),tail=dummy; int carry=0;
  while(a!=null || b!=null || carry!=0) {
    int x=a==null ? 0 : a.value,y=b==null ? 0 : b.value;
    if(x<0 || x>9 || y<0 || y>9) throw new IllegalArgumentException();
    int sum=x+y+carry; tail.next=new ListNode(sum%10); tail=tail.next; carry=sum/10;
    if(a!=null) a=a.next; if(b!=null) b=b.next;
  }
  return dummy.next;
}

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 · ADVANCED LINKED-LIST PROBLEMS QUESTION 070 / 120
Q070. Check a list palindrome and restore its links.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Find the first-half end, reverse the second half, compare corresponding values, and reverse the
second half back before returning. Restoration matters to callers holding aliases to the original list.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
Check a list palindrome and
restore its links. ➜
KEY LOGIC
Find the first-half end, reverse the
second half, compare
corresponding values, and reverse
the second half back before
returning.
➜
RESULT
2 -> 2 -> 1 -> true, original order
retained
💡 The shorter half excludes a center node when the length is odd.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(n); auxiliary space O(1).
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Acyclic list; it is temporarily mutated, so concurrent
observers are outside the contract.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would an immutable/nonmutating alternative change space?
Copy values into an array/list and use two pointers, which costs O(n) extra memory but does not change
links. A stack for half the values is another O(n) nonmutating option.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q070 · 8 lines
static boolean listPalindrome(ListNode head) {
  if(head==null || head.next==null) return true;
  ListNode slow=head,fast=head;
  while(fast.next!=null && fast.next.next!=null) { slow=slow.next; fast=fast.next.next; }
  ListNode reversed=reverseList(slow.next),a=head,b=reversed; boolean same=true;
  while(b!=null) { if(a.value!=b.value) same=false; a=a.next; b=b.next; }
  slow.next=reverseList(reversed); return same;
}

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 15 · BINARY-TREE TRAVERSAL AND STRUCTURE QUESTION 071 / 120
Q071. Traverse a binary tree in preorder iteratively.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Push the root, then pop and visit it. Push right before left so the stack visits left next.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
Root 1, left 2, right 3 ➜
KEY LOGIC
Push the root, then pop and visit
it.
➜
RESULT
[1,2,3]
💡 The stack contains roots of unvisited subtrees in next-visit order.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(n); auxiliary space O(height), excluding output.
⚠ INTERVIEW PITFALL
Do not push null into ArrayDeque.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION · ANSWERED
How would inorder change the traversal invariant?
For inorder, walk left repeatedly while pushing nodes, then pop/visit and move to the right child. Unlike
preorder, visiting happens after exhausting the left subtree; the stack stores unfinished ancestors.
JAVA 17 · SOLUTION Source Q071 · 9 lines
static List<Integer> preorder(TreeNode root) {
  List<Integer> out=new ArrayList<>(); Deque<TreeNode> stack=new ArrayDeque<>();
  if(root!=null) stack.push(root);
  while(!stack.isEmpty()) {
    TreeNode n=stack.pop(); out.add(n.value);
    if(n.right!=null) stack.push(n.right); if(n.left!=null) stack.push(n.left);
  }
  return out;
}

✎  SIMPLE ANSWER

avoiding separate repeated height calculations for every node.

Why can a naive per-node depth check become quadratic?

How could subtree-size metadata support frequent rank queries?

adjusting k. Balanced tree queries are O(log n), but inserts/deletes must maintain sizes.

static int kthSmallest(TreeNode root,int k) {
  if(k<1) throw new IllegalArgumentException();
  Deque<TreeNode> stack=new ArrayDeque<>(); TreeNode current=root;
  while(current!=null || !stack.isEmpty()) {
    while(current!=null) { stack.push(current); current=current.left; }
    current=stack.pop(); if(--k==0) return current.value; current=current.right;
  }
  throw new IllegalArgumentException("k exceeds node count");
}

Q079. Serialize a binary tree with structure
preserved.
✎  SIMPLE ANSWER
Write preorder values and an explicit marker for every null child. Values alone do not encode an
arbitrary tree's shape.
SKETCH THE PATTERN
EXAMPLE / INPUT
Tree 2 with children 1,3 ➜
KEY LOGIC
Write preorder values and an
explicit marker for every null child.
➜
RESULT
"2,1,#,#,3,#,#,"
💡 Each node and null boundary appears once in preorder.
⏱ TIME & SPACE
Time O(n + encoded characters); space O(height)
recursion plus output.

No cycles or shared-subtree graph semantics; deep
recursion can overflow.

What versioning and validation would a durable wire format need?
Use an explicit format version, a defined character encoding, safe delimiters/escaping and limits on depth/
node count. Validate integer ranges, token count and malformed streams before constructing a durable
tree.

  StringBuilder out=new StringBuilder(); serializeNode(root,out); return out.toString();
}
static void serializeNode(TreeNode n,StringBuilder out) {
  if(n==null) { out.append("#,"); return; }
  out.append(n.value).append(','); serializeNode(n.left,out); serializeNode(n.right,out);
}
