pages.title: What does transaction isolation control?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 11 • TRANSACTIONS AND CONSISTENCY
What does transaction isolation control?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It controls permitted interactions with concurrent database transactions, according to
the database's supported semantics.
DRAW THE IDEA — transaction isolation control
BEFORE
Service invocation ➜
FOCUS
Transaction boundary ➜
AFTER
Commit / rollback
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Transactional(isolation = Isolation.READ_COMMITTED)
public BalanceDto readBalance(long id) { return loadBalance(id); }
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
READ_COMMITTED generally prevents dirty reads but does not universally guarantee repeatable reads or eliminate
every anomaly. Database implementation and query shape matter. Isolation on a joining method may not replace
the already-running transaction's isolation.
04 / WATCH OUT
A label alone is not a proof of business correctness.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which anomaly threatens a check-then-update invariant?
Answer: A check-then-update can suffer non-repeatable reads, lost updates or write skew depending on
constraints and isolation. Use a conditional write or locking to enforce the actual invariant.
Source guide p. 49 • Intermediate • References: D03, D04

pages.title: Does readOnly=true prevent every write?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 11 • TRANSACTIONS AND CONSISTENCY
Does readOnly=true prevent every write?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It is a transaction hint that may affect optimizations and connection behavior; it is not
a universal write-prohibition guarantee.
DRAW THE IDEA — readOnly true prevent every
BEFORE
Service invocation ➜
FOCUS
Transaction boundary ➜
AFTER
Commit / rollback
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Transactional(readOnly = true)
public List<CustomerDto> list() {
  return repository.findAll().stream().map(this::toDto).toList();
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Use the hint for genuinely read-only work. Behavior depends on the manager, provider, and database. Do not rely
on this annotation as a security or data-integrity constraint.
04 / WATCH OUT
An ordinary collection mutation is not blocked by a database read-only hint.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you enforce database-level write restrictions?
Answer: Use a database read-only account, transaction-level read-only mode where supported, or explicit
permissions. Spring's readOnly hint alone is not a security boundary.

pages.title: Do transactions propagate automatically to @Async tasks?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 11 • TRANSACTIONS AND CONSISTENCY
Do transactions propagate automatically to @Async tasks?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Ordinary imperative transactions are thread-bound, so a new async thread does not
inherit the caller's transaction.
DRAW THE IDEA — transactions propagate automatically @A
BEFORE
Service invocation ➜
FOCUS
Transaction boundary ➜
AFTER
Commit / rollback
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Transactional
public void submit() {
  repository.save(order);
  asyncNotifier.send(order.getId()); // Another thread
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
The task can run before the transaction commits and may not see the row. Use after-commit dispatch when best-
effort is acceptable or a durable outbox for recoverable delivery. Reactive transactions use Reactor context instead
of this thread model.
04 / WATCH OUT
Passing a managed entity between threads introduces another ownership problem.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you handle task submission followed by rollback?
Answer: A new asynchronous task has a separate transaction context. Publishing a task before commit
can expose rolled-back data; enqueue durable intent in an outbox instead.
Source guide p. 50 • Intermediate • References: D03, D04

pages.title: What is the N+1 query problem?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 • DATABASE PERFORMANCE AND CONCURRENCY
What is the N+1 query problem?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
One query loads parents and later access triggers additional child queries, often one
per parent.
DRAW THE IDEA — N+1 query problem
BEFORE
Query + pool ➜
FOCUS
DB execution ➜
AFTER
Measured result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
// Load 20 orders in one query.
orders.forEach(o -> o.getLines().size());
// With lazy associations, this can trigger many more queries.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
The extra round trips can dominate latency. A suitable fetch join, entity graph, projection, or batch-fetch policy can
help. Measure the generated SQL for the actual access pattern rather than assuming one repository call equals one
query.
04 / WATCH OUT
EAGER does not guarantee one efficient query.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why is collection fetch-join pagination risky?
Answer: Joining a to-many collection multiplies rows and can make SQL limit/offset paginate joined rows
rather than distinct root entities. Page IDs first or use targeted batch fetching.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 • DATABASE PERFORMANCE AND CONCURRENCY
What is LazyInitializationException telling you?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Code tried to initialize lazy state without an appropriate open persistence context or
session.
DRAW THE IDEA — LazyInitializationException telling
BEFORE
Query + pool ➜
FOCUS
DB execution ➜
AFTER
Measured result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Order detached = service.loadOrder(id);
// Outside its persistence boundary:
detached.getLines().size(); // May fail when not already loaded
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Choose the required result shape inside a deliberate boundary. DTO projection or explicit fetch planning is
preferable to making every relationship eager. Open-in-view can mask the boundary while allowing queries during
response serialization.
04 / WATCH OUT
Lazy failure is often an ownership design issue.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you count lines without loading all of them?
Answer: Use a count query such as SELECT COUNT(line) at the database instead of loading every child
entity or initializing its collection.

pages.title: How do Page, Slice and keyset pagination differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 • DATABASE PERFORMANCE AND CONCURRENCY
How do Page, Slice and keyset pagination differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Page includes total-count information, Slice focuses on another-page existence, and
keyset uses a stable last-seen key.
DRAW THE IDEA — Page Slice keyset pagination
BEFORE
Query + pool ➜
FOCUS
DB execution ➜
AFTER
Measured result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
SELECT ... FROM orders
WHERE (created_at, id) < (:lastTime, :lastId)
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT :pageSize
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
This SQL is a conceptual keyset pattern; syntax and index design depend on the database. It avoids scanning an
ever-growing offset, but needs cursor semantics and matching deterministic order.
04 / WATCH OUT
A count query can be more expensive than fetching the page.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would filters affect cursor validity?
Answer: A cursor must bind to the same tenant, filters and sort definition. If any changes, reject or restart
pagination; always add a unique tie-breaker.

pages.title: How should HikariCP pool size be chosen?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 • DATABASE PERFORMANCE AND CONCURRENCY
How should HikariCP pool size be chosen?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Align pool capacity with measured database capacity, application concurrency, and the
number of service replicas.
DRAW THE IDEA — HikariCP pool size chosen
BEFORE
Query + pool ➜
FOCUS
DB execution ➜
AFTER
Measured result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=20
spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=2000
# Ten replicas can allow up to 200 connections in aggregate.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
These values illustrate units and capacity, not a recommendation. A larger pool may increase database contention.
Separate connection acquisition wait from query execution and socket deadlines.
04 / WATCH OUT
Hikari connection-timeout is not a query timeout.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How does a rolling deployment change peak connection count?
Answer: Rolling deployments may run old and new pods together, with maxSurge adding temporary
replicas. Multiply each replica's max pool size by peak concurrent pods, plus other database clients.

pages.title: How do optimistic and pessimistic locking differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 • DATABASE PERFORMANCE AND CONCURRENCY
How do optimistic and pessimistic locking differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Optimistic locking detects conflicting updates through a version; pessimistic locking
obtains database locks during the operation.
DRAW THE IDEA — optimistic pessimistic locking
BEFORE
Query + pool ➜
FOCUS
DB execution ➜
AFTER
Measured result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Entity
class Inventory {
  @Id Long id;
  @Version long version;
  int available;
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A version-checked update fails if another writer changed the version. Retrying needs fresh state and business
revalidation. Pessimistic locking can serialize updates but creates waits and deadlock risks.
04 / WATCH OUT
Versioning does not protect unrelated rows automatically.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which approach fits a highly contended stock counter?
Answer: For very high contention, an atomic conditional SQL update may outperform repeated optimistic
retries. Pessimistic locking is useful when a short critical section must serialize conflicts.

CHAPTER 12 • DATABASE PERFORMANCE AND CONCURRENCY
Why can bulk updates leave managed entities stale?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
JPQL or SQL bulk updates operate on rows without applying ordinary per-entity
managed-state synchronization.
DRAW THE IDEA — bulk updates leave managed
BEFORE

FOCUS
DB execution ➜
AFTER

02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE

@Query("update Customer c set c.active=false where c.lastSeen < :cutoff")
int deactivate(@Param("cutoff") Instant cutoff);
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Run this in an appropriate transaction. Flushing and clearing can reduce stale-state problems, but clearing detaches
managed objects and changes ownership. Check version handling and callbacks separately.
04 / WATCH OUT
Bulk update semantics differ from editing each entity.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What happens to existing entity references after clear?
Answer: clear() detaches managed instances; existing references still exist in Java but no longer receive
persistence-context updates. Re-read needed entities after a bulk operation.

pages.title: How do authentication and authorization differ?

CHAPTER 13 • SPRING SECURITY FUNDAMENTALS
How do authentication and authorization differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Authentication verifies who the caller is; authorization decides which operation that
caller may perform.

Authenticated user -> still needs permission for /admin
// Login success does not imply administrator rights.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A valid identity can still receive an access-denied response. URL rules are one layer; business-object ownership may
need method or service checks. Keep failure contracts distinct.
04 / WATCH OUT
A valid token alone does not authorize every resource.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you check tenant ownership?
Answer: Derive tenant identity from an authenticated trusted principal/claim and check both tenant and
resource ownership at the service or data access boundary.

pages.title: How is security configured in modern Boot applications?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 • SPRING SECURITY FUNDAMENTALS
How is security configured in modern Boot applications?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Declare SecurityFilterChain beans using the supported HttpSecurity DSL; do not base
new examples on the removed adapter.
DRAW THE IDEA — security configured modern applications
BEFORE
Client identity ➜
FOCUS
Security checks ➜
AFTER
Authorized access
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Bean
SecurityFilterChain chain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
  http.authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a.requestMatchers("/public/**").permitAll()
      .anyRequest().authenticated());
  return http.build();
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
This defines authorization but must be paired with the authentication mechanism you intend, such as resource-
server JWT or login. Supplying custom chains means owning their rules, including management endpoints.
04 / WATCH OUT
Matcher order and which chain matches matter.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you define a separate actuator chain?
Answer: Use distinct SecurityFilterChain beans with request matchers/order; give actuator routes a
restrictive, separately tested rule instead of accidentally inheriting public API access.

pages.title: When should CSRF protection be retained?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 • SPRING SECURITY FUNDAMENTALS
When should CSRF protection be retained?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Retain it for requests whose credentials are automatically attached by browsers, such as
cookie sessions; choose a separate policy for truly bearer-only APIs.
DRAW THE IDEA — CSRF protection retained
BEFORE
Client identity ➜
FOCUS
Security checks ➜
AFTER
Authorized access
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Cookie/session application -> CSRF token required for unsafe methods
Bearer token explicitly sent in Authorization header ->
  assess credential behavior and client architecture
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Stateless does not automatically mean CSRF-safe if browser credentials are still auto-sent. A blanket disable copied
from a tutorial can weaken a cookie-based app. CORS addresses a different browser concern.
04 / WATCH OUT
JWT stored in a cookie can still create CSRF exposure.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What does SameSite mitigate and what remains?
Answer: SameSite cookies reduce some cross-site sending, but do not replace CSRF tokens for every
supported browser flow, and they do not solve XSS or incorrect authorization.

pages.title: How does CORS differ from authentication?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 • SPRING SECURITY FUNDAMENTALS
How does CORS differ from authentication?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
CORS controls browser cross-origin access rules; it does not establish caller identity or
authorize non-browser clients.
DRAW THE IDEA — CORS authentication
BEFORE
Client identity ➜
FOCUS
Security checks ➜
AFTER
Authorized access
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Allowed origin: https://app.example
Allowed method: GET
Allowed header: Authorization
Preflight OPTIONS -> handled before ordinary bearer authentication
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Configure a precise CORS policy and integrate it with security. Browser preflight generally carries no bearer access
token. A curl request is not stopped merely because its Origin is outside a CORS allowlist.
04 / WATCH OUT
Wildcard origins and credentialed responses have restrictions.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why can a preflight receive 401 while the endpoint works in Postman?
Answer: Browsers send an unauthenticated OPTIONS preflight. Permit the intended CORS handling before
authorization; Postman does not enforce browser CORS rules.

pages.title: How should passwords be stored?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 • SPRING SECURITY FUNDAMENTALS
How should passwords be stored?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Store a salted adaptive password hash using a supported PasswordEncoder; never
plaintext or reversible application encryption for login verification.
DRAW THE IDEA — passwords stored
BEFORE
Client identity ➜
FOCUS
Security checks ➜
AFTER
Authorized access
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
PasswordEncoder encoder = PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder();
String stored = encoder.encode("example-password");
System.out.println(encoder.matches("example-password", stored)); // true
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
The stored format identifies the encoder, enabling policy evolution. Compare by matches rather than hashing twice
and comparing strings because salts vary. Set cost using deployment measurements.
04 / WATCH OUT
Logs and fixture files can still leak raw credentials.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you upgrade stored hashes on successful login?
Answer: On successful login, detect an outdated password-hash encoding and rehash with the current
PasswordEncoder policy; never convert to plaintext or skip verification.
Source guide p. 56 • Intermediate • References: S01, S02, S03

pages.title: CHAPTER 13 • SPRING SECURITY FUNDAMENTALS
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 • SPRING SECURITY FUNDAMENTALS
How do method authorization and URL rules complement
each other?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
URL rules protect routes; method checks enforce business permissions even through
other entry points.
DRAW THE IDEA — method authorization URL rules
BEFORE
Client identity ➜
FOCUS
Security checks ➜
AFTER
Authorized access
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@EnableMethodSecurity
@Configuration
class MethodSecurityConfig {}
@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('orders:approve')")
public void approve(long id) { /* also enforce ownership */ }
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
The method call must cross the advised boundary. A messaging consumer or another controller can reuse
protected service logic. Authorities alone may not prove the caller owns this particular order.
04 / WATCH OUT
Self-invocation can bypass method advice.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you test an object-level permission denial?
Answer: Use a test identity allowed at the URL but denied by service-level ownership checks. Assert 403
and that the protected record was not changed.

pages.title: What is the difference between JWT, OAuth and OIDC?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 • JWT, OAUTH 2.0 AND OPENID CONNECT
What is the difference between JWT, OAuth and OIDC?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
JWT is a token format; OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework; OIDC adds identity
authentication on top of OAuth.
DRAW THE IDEA — difference JWT OAuth OIDC
BEFORE
Token / flow ➜
FOCUS
Verify claims + roles ➜
AFTER
Protected API
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
JWT: encoded claims, often signed
OAuth: obtain scoped access to resources
OIDC: identity protocol with an ID token
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
An OAuth access token can be opaque rather than JWT. A JWT can exist outside OAuth. OIDC ID tokens are meant
for the client identity flow, not automatically for authorization at your API.
04 / WATCH OUT
These terms do not name interchangeable login mechanisms.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which token should an API accept?
Answer: APIs accept access tokens intended for that resource server, not ID tokens intended for the client
application. Validate issuer, audience, expiry and scopes.

pages.title: What must a resource server validate in a JWT?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 • JWT, OAUTH 2.0 AND OPENID CONNECT
What must a resource server validate in a JWT?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Validate the signature and allowed algorithms, time claims, trusted issuer, intended
audience, and required application claims.
DRAW THE IDEA — must resource server validate
BEFORE
Token / flow ➜
FOCUS
Verify claims + roles ➜
AFTER
Protected API
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri=https://id.example/issuer
# Add an audience validator for this API as required.
# A configured JWT decoder and resource-server chain validate tokens.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
issuer-uri supports trusted discovery and issuer validation. Audience policy must match the API and configuration;
do not assume every setup checks your custom audience automatically. Never trust claims just because Base64
decoding succeeded.
04 / WATCH OUT
Signature validity alone is insufficient.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How do you handle clock skew safely?
Answer: Allow only a small policy-defined clock-skew tolerance for nbf/exp checks. Large leeway makes
expired tokens usable for longer and should not mask clock drift.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 • JWT, OAUTH 2.0 AND OPENID CONNECT
What does a JWT resource-server SecurityFilterChain look
like?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Enable bearer-token authentication with the resource-server JWT DSL and explicit
authorization rules.
DRAW THE IDEA — JWT resource-server SecurityFilterChain
BEFORE
Token / flow ➜
FOCUS
Verify claims + roles ➜
AFTER
Protected API
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
http.sessionManagement(s -> s.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS))
    .authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a.anyRequest().authenticated())
    .oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(Customizer.withDefaults()));
// Apply inside a SecurityFilterChain @Bean and configure a decoder.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Bearer authentication delegates validation to JwtDecoder. This sketch keeps CSRF policy separate so cookie-based
authentication is not accidentally weakened. Issuer, audience, and authority mapping must match your identity
provider.
04 / WATCH OUT
The resource server does not mint tokens merely by enabling this DSL.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How are scopes mapped to authorities by default?
Answer: Scopes commonly become SCOPE_<name> GrantedAuthority values. Customize a
JwtAuthenticationConverter only when your token claim and prefix contract requires it.

pages.title: What is authorization code with PKCE used for?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 • JWT, OAUTH 2.0 AND OPENID CONNECT
What is authorization code with PKCE used for?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It lets a client exchange a redirected authorization code with proof of possession of its
original verifier, reducing intercepted-code misuse.
DRAW THE IDEA — authorization code PKCE used
BEFORE
Token / flow ➜
FOCUS
Verify claims + roles ➜
AFTER
Protected API
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Client -> authorization request with code challenge + state
Browser -> authorization server -> callback with code
Client -> token endpoint with code + verifier
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Verify redirect URIs and state, and use OIDC nonce validation where required. PKCE is useful for public clients and
modern authorization-code flows; it does not replace all client or redirect controls.
04 / WATCH OUT
Do not recommend the password grant for new client designs.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How is a public client different from a confidential client?
Answer: A public client cannot keep a client secret confidential; PKCE protects its authorization-code
exchange. A confidential client can authenticate itself securely to the token endpoint.

pages.title: How do access tokens and refresh tokens differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 • JWT, OAUTH 2.0 AND OPENID CONNECT
How do access tokens and refresh tokens differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Access tokens authorize resource requests; refresh tokens obtain new access tokens
from the authorization server.
DRAW THE IDEA — access tokens refresh tokens
BEFORE
Token / flow ➜
FOCUS
Verify claims + roles ➜
AFTER
Protected API
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
API request -> access token
Access expires -> client uses refresh token at token endpoint
API should not accept a refresh token as its bearer credential.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Refresh tokens generally need stronger storage and rotation/reuse policy. Not every flow issues one. Resource
servers normally validate the access token; token issuance and refresh belong to the authorization server.
04 / WATCH OUT
Longer access-token lifetime delays revocation effects.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would rotation detect stolen refresh-token reuse?
Answer: Store refresh-token family state; each rotation invalidates its predecessor. Reuse of an old token
signals theft or concurrency misuse and should revoke or quarantine the family.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 • JWT, OAUTH 2.0 AND OPENID CONNECT
Can a signed JWT be revoked immediately without server
state?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Local signature checks alone cannot know every early revocation; immediate revocation
needs state, introspection, or another coordinated policy.
DRAW THE IDEA — signed JWT revoked immediately
BEFORE
Token / flow ➜
FOCUS
Verify claims + roles ➜
AFTER
Protected API
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
JWT exp in 10 minutes + local verification
Logout now -> token may still validate until exp
Options -> short lifetime, denylist, introspection, key policy
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Choose a revocation requirement explicitly. Key rotation affects many tokens and is not a per-user logout
mechanism. JWT payloads are ordinarily readable unless encrypted, so do not store secrets in claims.
04 / WATCH OUT
Deleting a browser token does not invalidate a stolen copy.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When is opaque-token introspection preferable?
Answer: Introspection lets the resource server ask an authorization server whether a token is active,
supporting central revocation at the cost of a runtime dependency and caching tradeoffs.

pages.title: When should you use a plain unit test instead of @SpringBootTest?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 15 • TESTING FROM UNITS TO REAL BOUNDARIES
When should you use a plain unit test instead of
@SpringBootTest?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use plain tests for business behavior that does not require container wiring; reserve
context tests for integration questions.
DRAW THE IDEA — plain unit test instead
BEFORE
Test input ➜
FOCUS
Target boundary ➜
AFTER
Assertion evidence
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Test
void rejectsNegativeAmount() {
  Checkout checkout = new Checkout(fakeGateway);
  assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class,
      () -> checkout.pay(new BigDecimal("-1")));
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A direct test is fast and verifies a business rule without a server or database. It cannot verify component discovery,
proxy advice, or configuration binding. Pick context tests for those boundaries.
04 / WATCH OUT
Booting Spring for every arithmetic rule wastes time.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which test would expose a missing bean?
Answer: A context-loading @SpringBootTest or focused ApplicationContextRunner test detects missing
beans. Plain unit tests are best when only the algorithm and collaborators need verification.
Source guide p. 62 • Intermediate • References: T01, T02, T03

pages.title: How do @WebMvcTest and @SpringBootTest differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 15 • TESTING FROM UNITS TO REAL BOUNDARIES
How do @WebMvcTest and @SpringBootTest differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
@WebMvcTest loads an MVC-focused slice; @SpringBootTest loads the application's
broader Boot context.
DRAW THE IDEA — @WebMvcTest @SpringBootTest
BEFORE
Test input ➜
FOCUS
Target boundary ➜
AFTER
Assertion evidence
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@WebMvcTest(OrderController.class)
class OrderWebTest {
  @Autowired MockMvc mvc;
  @MockitoBean OrderService service;
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
The mocked service isolates routing, binding, serialization, and selected security behavior. @MockitoBean is available
in the modern Spring Framework used by the chosen Boot baseline. A full test is needed when real service wiring is
the subject.
04 / WATCH OUT
MVC slices can include security filters.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What would adding addFilters=false remove from coverage?
Answer: It bypasses security filters and therefore misses authentication, authorization and CORS behavior
in that test. Do not use it for endpoints whose security contract matters.

What should a MockMvc endpoint test assert?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 15 • TESTING FROM UNITS TO REAL BOUNDARIES
What does @DataJpaTest cover and what can it miss?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It focuses on JPA infrastructure and repositories, often with transactional rollback;
database substitution can hide production differences.
DRAW THE IDEA — @DataJpaTest cover miss
BEFORE
Test input ➜
FOCUS
Target boundary ➜
AFTER
Assertion evidence
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@DataJpaTest
class CustomerRepositoryTest {
  @Autowired CustomerRepository repository;
  // Persist fixtures, execute query, assert rows and ordering.
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A slice verifies mappings and query semantics in its selected database. Test dialect-specific SQL, constraints, locking,
and migrations against the actual database engine when important. A transactionally rolled-back test may not
exercise commit behavior.
04 / WATCH OUT
An in-memory database is not proof of MySQL or PostgreSQL behavior.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why explicitly flush before asserting a constraint failure?
Answer: A database constraint may be enforced only when SQL is flushed. Explicit flush makes that failure
occur inside the test, instead of after assertions.

CHAPTER 15 • TESTING FROM UNITS TO REAL BOUNDARIES
How should asynchronous and security tests be made
meaningful?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Wait for observable completion with a bound and exercise the actual authorization path,
including denied outcomes.

BEFORE
Test input ➜
FOCUS
Target boundary ➜

// Avoid an arbitrary Thread.sleep.

assertEquals("done", result.get(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS).status());
// Security cases: absent token, invalid token, wrong scope, valid scope.

policy but does not verify real signature decoding. Add token-validation integration cases where needed.

configuration, instead of mocking every Authentication or JwtDecoder.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 • HTTP CLIENTS, DEADLINES AND RESILIENCE
How do RestClient, WebClient and RestTemplate differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
RestClient is a synchronous fluent client; WebClient provides reactive composition;
RestTemplate is a legacy synchronous template style.
DRAW THE IDEA — RestClient WebClient RestTemplate
BEFORE
Outbound call ➜
FOCUS
Deadline + resilience ➜
AFTER
Known / unknown result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
String body = RestClient.create().get()
    .uri("https://service.example/status")
    .retrieve().body(String.class);
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
This is a synchronous network call, not a production timeout configuration. Choose the underlying request factory or
connector with explicit deadlines and pooling. API return style alone does not prove transport behavior.
04 / WATCH OUT
WebClient.block still blocks the caller.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which client fits a reactive chain?
Answer: WebClient fits a reactive chain where the caller can keep work non-blocking end to end. Blocking
with .block() inside an event loop defeats that benefit.

pages.title: Which timeouts should a service-to-service call consider?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 • HTTP CLIENTS, DEADLINES AND RESILIENCE
Which timeouts should a service-to-service call consider?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Consider connection acquisition, connect, TLS, read/response, and overall operation
deadlines according to the selected client.
DRAW THE IDEA — timeouts service-to-service call consid
BEFORE
Outbound call ➜
FOCUS
Deadline + resilience ➜
AFTER
Known / unknown result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Total request budget: 2 seconds
Pool/connect budget: bounded subset
Remote response + retries: must fit remaining budget
Cancellation: close or stop owned work where supported
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A single socket read timeout may not bound every stage or retry. Carry the caller's deadline across the chain and
measure pool waiting separately. Connector option names and semantics are implementation-specific.
04 / WATCH OUT
A retry budget cannot exceed the endpoint's useful lifetime.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would DNS delay be observed?
Answer: DNS resolution may happen before connection establishment and have its own timeout/caching
behavior. Measure DNS timing or instrument the resolver rather than assuming connectTimeout covers it.

pages.title: When is retry safe and when is it harmful?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 • HTTP CLIENTS, DEADLINES AND RESILIENCE
When is retry safe and when is it harmful?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Retry transient failures within a deadline only when repeated effects are safe or
deduplicated; avoid amplifying overload.
DRAW THE IDEA — retry safe harmful
BEFORE
Outbound call ➜
FOCUS
Deadline + resilience ➜
AFTER
Known / unknown result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
GET catalog -> limited transient retry may fit
POST charge -> stable idempotency identity required
Retry 401 or validation error -> usually repeats a permanent failure
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Classify the failure, use bounded attempts with backoff and jitter, and honor the downstream contract. A timeout is
an unknown outcome for side-effecting calls. Cascaded retries can multiply traffic across services.
04 / WATCH OUT
Retrying every exception is not resilience.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Where should the one owning retry layer live?
Answer: Choose one retry-owning boundary, usually the caller or designated transport policy, with a
request-wide attempt budget. Disable repeated retries elsewhere to avoid multiplication.
Source guide p. 67 • Intermediate • References: I01, R02

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 • HTTP CLIENTS, DEADLINES AND RESILIENCE
How do circuit breakers, bulkheads and rate limiters
differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A circuit breaker stops repeated calls after failure patterns; a bulkhead limits concurrent
resource use; a rate limiter controls admission over time.
DRAW THE IDEA — circuit breakers bulkheads rate
BEFORE
Outbound call ➜
FOCUS
Deadline + resilience ➜
AFTER
Known / unknown result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Breaker OPEN -> fast rejection according to policy
Bulkhead full -> reject or wait within a bound
Rate budget exceeded -> controlled throttle response
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
These solve different problems and can be combined with timeouts. None makes a slow call finish sooner by itself.
Choose a meaningful fallback or explicit failure rather than returning misleading data.
04 / WATCH OUT
A circuit breaker is not a timeout.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How do half-open probes prevent a recovery surge?
Answer: Limit concurrent half-open requests to a small probe budget, then reopen on failures or close
only after sufficient successful probes. Otherwise recovery can be flooded.
Source guide p. 67 • Intermediate • References: I01, R02

pages.title: What does an HTTP client connection pool need beyond a maximum size?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 • HTTP CLIENTS, DEADLINES AND RESILIENCE
What does an HTTP client connection pool need beyond a
maximum size?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It needs bounded pending acquisition, idle/lifetime policy, deadlines, cleanup, and
visibility into saturation.
DRAW THE IDEA — HTTP client connection pool
BEFORE
Outbound call ➜
FOCUS
Deadline + resilience ➜
AFTER
Known / unknown result
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Active connections: bounded
Pending acquisition queue: bounded
Acquire wait: bounded
Idle or expired connections: retired by policy
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
An unbounded wait queue can shift the outage from sockets to memory and latency. Observe pool wait and
downstream duration, and ensure body consumption or closing releases resources.
04 / WATCH OUT
Unlimited client concurrency does not imply unlimited useful throughput.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What can leak a connection after an error response?
Answer: Failing to consume or close a response body can keep a leased connection unavailable. Verify
response closing on success, error, timeout and cancellation paths.

pages.title: What does @Async do and what does it require?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 • ASYNC EXECUTION, SCHEDULING AND CACHING
What does @Async do and what does it require?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It submits advised method execution to an executor when async support is enabled and
the call crosses the configured proxy boundary.
DRAW THE IDEA — @Async require
BEFORE
Task / key ➜
FOCUS
Async or cache policy ➜
AFTER
Result + cleanup
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@EnableAsync
@Configuration
class AsyncConfig {}
@Async("notifications")
public CompletableFuture<Void> send(long orderId) {
  performSend(orderId); return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(null);
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Define the named executor with appropriate bounds and shutdown policy. Self-calls bypass ordinary proxy advice. A
CompletableFuture return exposes failure better than ignoring a void task's outcome.
04 / WATCH OUT
Async is not durable job delivery.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Who observes a failed notification task?
Answer: The task owner must observe Future/CompletableFuture outcomes, return status, or route errors
to monitoring. A void @Async exception handler logs failures but does not provide durable retry.
Source guide p. 69 • Intermediate • References: I02, I03

pages.title: How should an async executor be bounded?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 • ASYNC EXECUTION, SCHEDULING AND CACHING
How should an async executor be bounded?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use a deliberate worker count, finite queue, rejection behavior, and lifecycle ownership
based on the workload.
DRAW THE IDEA — async executor bounded
BEFORE
Task / key ➜
FOCUS
Async or cache policy ➜
AFTER
Result + cleanup
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
ThreadPoolTaskExecutor e = new ThreadPoolTaskExecutor();
e.setCorePoolSize(4); e.setMaxPoolSize(8);
e.setQueueCapacity(100);
// Configure rejection, thread names, shutdown; register as a bean.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
These numbers are illustrative. A full queue triggers the chosen rejection behavior, not magical elasticity. Managed
initialization and destruction must occur. Avoid silently dropping important tasks.
04 / WATCH OUT
Extra workers do not solve a constrained database.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would an event-loop caller react to CallerRunsPolicy?
Answer: CallerRunsPolicy may execute the blocking task on the submitting event-loop thread, stalling
unrelated requests. Use explicit rejection or asynchronous bounded admission instead.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 • ASYNC EXECUTION, SCHEDULING AND CACHING
How do fixedDelay, fixedRate and cron scheduling differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
fixedDelay waits after completion; fixedRate follows a time-based cadence; cron matches
a calendar schedule.
DRAW THE IDEA — fixedDelay fixedRate cron scheduling
BEFORE
Task / key ➜
FOCUS
Async or cache policy ➜
AFTER
Result + cleanup
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Scheduled(fixedDelay = 5000)
void refresh() { loadSnapshot(); }
@Scheduled(cron = "0 0 9 * * *", zone = "Asia/Kolkata")
void daily() { runDailyReport(); }
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
With scheduling enabled, refresh waits five seconds after a run completes before the next start. Cron uses Spring's
field format and the explicit zone. Scheduler capacity and overlaps need deliberate configuration.
04 / WATCH OUT
Every application replica may run the same schedule.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you ensure only one durable job instance executes?
Answer: Use a shared durable job authority, such as a database claim with unique key or scheduler
clustering, so pods cannot run the same logical job without coordination.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 • ASYNC EXECUTION, SCHEDULING AND CACHING
How do @Cacheable, @CachePut and @CacheEvict differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
@Cacheable can skip execution on a hit; @CachePut executes and updates the cache;
@CacheEvict removes entries.
DRAW THE IDEA — @Cacheable @CachePut @CacheEvict
BEFORE
Task / key ➜
FOCUS
Async or cache policy ➜
AFTER
Result + cleanup
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Cacheable(cacheNames="products", key="#id")
public ProductDto load(long id) { return repository.loadDto(id); }
@CacheEvict(cacheNames="products", key="#id")
public void update(long id, UpdateProduct request) { /* persist */ }
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Caching support and a suitable manager must be enabled. Use stable keys and immutable results. Eviction timing,
transactions, and failures determine whether readers can see stale data.
04 / WATCH OUT
Annotation-based caching also has proxy self-call limits.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What if an update commits but eviction fails?
Answer: A committed update followed by failed eviction leaves stale cache data. Use versioned keys,
durable invalidation events, bounded TTL or an appropriate write-through strategy and repair.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 • ASYNC EXECUTION, SCHEDULING AND CACHING
Does @Cacheable(sync=true) solve every cache stampede?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It requests synchronized loading supported by the cache provider, but does not
universally coordinate all replicas or all failure paths.
DRAW THE IDEA — @Cacheable sync true solve
BEFORE
Task / key ➜
FOCUS
Async or cache policy ➜
AFTER
Result + cleanup
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Cacheable(cacheNames="catalog", key="#id", sync=true)
public CatalogDto load(long id) { return remote.load(id); }
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Check provider semantics and annotation restrictions. Distributed stampede handling can require leases, shared in-
flight coordination, expiration jitter, or stale-while-refresh policy. Define failed-load cleanup.
04 / WATCH OUT
Local synchronization is not automatically a distributed lock.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would synchronized loading behave across ten pods?
Answer: The sync behavior is normally local to a cache entry/provider, not a ten-pod coordination
guarantee. Each pod may load the same item unless using suitable distributed coordination.

CHAPTER 17 • ASYNC EXECUTION, SCHEDULING AND CACHING
How should a cache key include tenant and authorization
context?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Include all input dimensions affecting the result, and enforce permission independently
rather than treating a hit as authorization.
DRAW THE IDEA — cache key include tenant
BEFORE

FOCUS

AFTER
Result + cleanup
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE

// If visibility changes by user role, address that dimension
// or cache only an authorization-independent representation.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A productId-only key can serve another tenant's data. Cache identity, freshness, and permission are separate
contracts. Prefer low-cardinality stable dimensions and bounded retention.

A cached DTO can leak data despite valid authentication.

How would permission revocation invalidate cached views?
Answer: A permission change must invalidate or version relevant cached views, or force a fresh
authorization check. Never trust a previously cached result as permanent authorization.

CHAPTER 18 • MESSAGING, KAFKA AND RELIABLE EVENTS
How does a @KafkaListener process records?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Spring creates listener containers that poll Kafka and invoke the configured handler
with conversion and error behavior.
DRAW THE IDEA — @KafkaListener process records
BEFORE
Business event ➜
FOCUS
Kafka delivery ➜
AFTER
Idempotent effect
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@KafkaListener(topics="orders", groupId="billing")
void onOrder(OrderCreated event) { billing.handle(event); }
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
The example assumes matching serialization and container configuration. Partition count limits concurrent
ownership within a group. Define acknowledgment, retries, recovery, and idempotency rather than assuming the
annotation supplies them all.
04 / WATCH OUT
A listener exception needs an explicit recovery policy.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What happens during a rebalance?
Answer: A rebalance revokes/assigns partitions and may replay uncommitted records. Make effects
idempotent and handle inflight work and offset commits carefully.

CHAPTER 18 • MESSAGING, KAFKA AND RELIABLE EVENTS
How do producer acknowledgments differ from consumer
offsets?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Producer acknowledgments concern broker acceptance; consumer offsets track
progress through a partition.
DRAW THE IDEA — producer acknowledgments consumer offse
BEFORE
Business event ➜
FOCUS
Kafka delivery ➜
AFTER
Idempotent effect
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Producer acks=all -> broker replication acknowledgment policy
Consumer commits offset -> recorded consumption position
Business transaction committed -> application side effect
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
These are separate milestones. Broker acknowledgment does not prove a billing database update occurred.
Committing an offset before durable processing can lose the effect; committing afterward can lead to redelivery.
04 / WATCH OUT
Offset numbers are partition-specific, not global record ids.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How do min.insync.replicas and acks interact?
Answer: acks=all waits for acknowledgments from the in-sync replica set under broker configuration;
min.insync.replicas enforces a minimum ISR size for such writes or rejects them.

pages.title: Why does a consumer need idempotency under at-least- once delivery?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 • MESSAGING, KAFKA AND RELIABLE EVENTS
Why does a consumer need idempotency under at-least-
once delivery?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A record can be processed again after failure or rebalance, so repeated business effects
must be prevented when required.
DRAW THE IDEA — consumer idempotency under at-least-onc
BEFORE
Business event ➜
FOCUS
Kafka delivery ➜
AFTER
Idempotent effect
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Transactional
public void handle(Event e) {
  if (processed.exists(e.id())) return;
  applyEffect(e);
  processed.insert(e.id()); // Unique constraint required
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
This is a conceptual handler: the duplicate marker and business effect must share the right atomic boundary. A
check alone races; the unique marker and conflict handling matter. External effects need their own idempotency
protocol.
04 / WATCH OUT
In-memory dedup does not survive restart.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you scope an event id by tenant or producer?
Answer: Use a stable event identity combined with trusted source/tenant scope and a unique processed-
event key in the same transaction as the effect. Cross-tenant collisions must not suppress valid events.
Source guide p. 74 • Intermediate • References: I04, I05

pages.title: What is the transactional outbox pattern?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 • MESSAGING, KAFKA AND RELIABLE EVENTS
What is the transactional outbox pattern?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Write the business update and event intent in one database transaction, then publish
the durable intent asynchronously.
DRAW THE IDEA — transactional outbox pattern
BEFORE
Business event ➜
FOCUS
Kafka delivery ➜
AFTER
Idempotent effect
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Transactional
public void place(CreateOrder command) {
  orders.insert(command);
  outbox.insert(new OrderCreated(command.operationId()));
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A publisher later sends pending outbox rows and tracks progress. Publishing can repeat if acknowledgment and
marking are interrupted, so consumers still need idempotency. Monitor backlog age and define retention.
04 / WATCH OUT
Outbox is not automatic end-to-end exactly-once effect.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you prevent losing an event after commit?
Answer: Persist an outbox row in the same transaction as the business update. A relay retries publication
after restart, so intent is not lost when the broker is unavailable.
Source guide p. 75 • Intermediate • References: I04, I05

pages.title: How should poison records and retry topics be handled?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 • MESSAGING, KAFKA AND RELIABLE EVENTS
How should poison records and retry topics be handled?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Classify transient versus permanent failures, bound attempts, and route exhausted
records with diagnostic context to a controlled recovery path.
DRAW THE IDEA — poison records retry topics
BEFORE
Business event ➜
FOCUS
Kafka delivery ➜
AFTER
Idempotent effect
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Temporary dependency outage -> bounded delayed retry
Invalid schema/business poison -> quarantine or DLT policy
Recovered message -> replay with idempotency protection
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Choose the correct container/error-handler mechanism for the project's Spring Kafka version. Non-blocking retries
can change ordering, and partition pausing affects throughput. Operators need ownership and replay tooling.
04 / WATCH OUT
A dead-letter topic without monitoring is hidden data loss.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which errors must never be retried indefinitely?
Answer: Permanent schema failures, bad authentication, unknown tenant or impossible business input
need quarantine/repair rather than infinite retries. Transient dependency errors can be retried with a
budget.

CHAPTER 18 • MESSAGING, KAFKA AND RELIABLE EVENTS
What does Kafka exactly-once not automatically
guarantee?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Kafka transaction guarantees apply to supported Kafka operations; they do not
automatically include arbitrary HTTP or database side effects.
DRAW THE IDEA — Kafka exactly-once not automatically
BEFORE
Business event ➜
FOCUS
Kafka delivery ➜
AFTER
Idempotent effect
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Read Kafka -> write Kafka in supported transaction
Read Kafka -> charge external provider -> different atomic boundary
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
State the exact scope of the guarantee. Coordinating a database with offsets can still leave a failure window unless a
supported protocol and recovery policy close it. Design idempotency for the external effect.
04 / WATCH OUT
'Exactly once' must name the observed business operation.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When would outbox plus dedup be easier to reason about?
Answer: When database updates and Kafka transactions are separate, outbox plus consumer dedup often
gives an easier end-to-end proof of business correctness.

pages.title: How do Spring MVC and WebFlux differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 • WEBFLUX, REACTOR AND VIRTUAL THREADS
How do Spring MVC and WebFlux differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
MVC uses the servlet request model; WebFlux provides reactive request handling and
composition through publishers.
DRAW THE IDEA — MVC WebFlux
BEFORE
Publisher ➜
FOCUS
Reactive operations ➜
AFTER
Subscriber signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@GetMapping("/products/{id}")
Mono<ProductDto> get(@PathVariable long id) {
  return reactiveRepository.findById(id).map(this::toDto);
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
The method returns a publisher describing the result. Benefits require suitable downstream and execution behavior;
returning Mono does not make a JDBC query non-blocking. MVC can also support some async return types.
04 / WATCH OUT
Framework choice alone does not prove higher throughput.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When is MVC simpler for a blocking stack?
Answer: MVC is often simpler when the service already uses blocking JPA/JDBC and servlet infrastructure.
Adding reactive interfaces will not make those calls non-blocking.

pages.title: What is the difference between Mono and Flux?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 • WEBFLUX, REACTOR AND VIRTUAL THREADS
What is the difference between Mono and Flux?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Mono represents zero or one item; Flux represents zero to many items, both with
completion or error signals.
DRAW THE IDEA — difference Mono Flux
BEFORE
Publisher ➜
FOCUS
Reactive operations ➜
AFTER
Subscriber signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Mono<String> one = Mono.just("A");
Flux<String> many = Flux.just("A", "B");
Mono<String> none = Mono.empty();
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
An empty publisher completes without a value; it does not emit null. A sequence can also fail. The API response
must distinguish an absent domain result from an unavailable dependency.
04 / WATCH OUT
Reactor does not permit ordinary null elements.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would switchIfEmpty implement not-found behavior?
Answer: Use switchIfEmpty(Mono.error(new NotFoundException(...))) or build an explicit 404 response. An
empty Mono is completion without a value, not automatically a not-found status.

map transforms a value synchronously; flatMap composes an asynchronous publisher
and flattens its signals.
DRAW THE IDEA — map flatMap Reactor
BEFORE
Publisher ➜
FOCUS
Reactive operations ➜
AFTER
Subscriber signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Mono<OrderDto> result = findCustomer(id)
    .flatMap(c -> findOrder(c.orderId()))
    .map(this::toDto);
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
findOrder returns another Mono, so flatMap combines the asynchronous step. Flux.flatMap can interleave
concurrent inner results; concatMap can preserve sequential processing when needed.
04 / WATCH OUT
Operator choice affects ordering and concurrency.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When would flatMapSequential fit?
Answer: flatMapSequential can run inner publishers concurrently while emitting results in source order;
use it when ordering matters but some overlap is useful.

pages.title: Why is blocking the event loop dangerous?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 • WEBFLUX, REACTOR AND VIRTUAL THREADS
Why is blocking the event loop dangerous?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A blocked event-loop thread cannot promptly process other connections and signals
assigned to it.
DRAW THE IDEA — blocking event loop dangerous
BEFORE
Publisher ➜
FOCUS
Reactive operations ➜
AFTER
Subscriber signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Mono<Result> result = Mono.fromCallable(() -> blockingClient.call())
    .subscribeOn(Schedulers.boundedElastic());
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
This isolates a known blocking call from the event loop; it does not make the call non-blocking. Bound downstream
concurrency and deadlines too. Avoid block or manual subscribe inside a request pipeline unless the ownership
design explicitly calls for it.
04 / WATCH OUT
Offloading without admission control can move the bottleneck.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you detect blocking in a load test?
Answer: Observe event-loop thread stacks, blocked-thread warnings and load-test p95/p99 latency.
BlockHound can flag some blocking calls in supported test configurations.
Source guide p. 78 • Intermediate • References: R01, R02, B02

pages.title: What are backpressure and cancellation?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 • WEBFLUX, REACTOR AND VIRTUAL THREADS
What are backpressure and cancellation?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Backpressure coordinates demand for signals; cancellation tells a publisher downstream
no longer needs the sequence.
DRAW THE IDEA — backpressure cancellation
BEFORE
Publisher ➜
FOCUS
Reactive operations ➜
AFTER
Subscriber signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Flux<Record> records = source.take(10);
// After enough items, take can cancel upstream.
// The source and transport must support meaningful cancellation.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Demand handling does not automatically limit every queue or external database query. Some hot sources cannot
slow their producer and need buffer, drop, or error policies. Cancellation also does not undo already-completed side
effects.
04 / WATCH OUT
An unbounded collectList can still exhaust memory.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you bound a streaming export?
Answer: Stream in bounded chunks with backpressure and cancellation checks, limit simultaneous exports,
and release database/file resources on cancellation and timeout.
Source guide p. 79 • Intermediate • References: R01, R02, B02

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 • WEBFLUX, REACTOR AND VIRTUAL THREADS
When might virtual threads be preferable to a reactive
rewrite?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They can support large numbers of blocking tasks with straightforward code when the
framework and dependencies support the chosen JDK configuration.
DRAW THE IDEA — might virtual threads preferable
BEFORE
Publisher ➜
FOCUS
Reactive operations ➜
AFTER
Subscriber signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true
# Boot baseline requires Java 21+ for virtual-thread support.
# Still bound database, remote-call, and admission capacity.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Check which Boot-managed execution components are affected rather than assuming every library thread is virtual.
CPU-bound work does not gain processors. Java-version-specific pinning and carrier behavior need separate
verification.
04 / WATCH OUT
A property flag is not an end-to-end capacity plan.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why can the database stay saturated after enabling it?
Answer: Virtual threads reduce platform-thread cost for waiting but do not add database connections. The
same pool, SQL and database limits still apply; bound requests to the dependency.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 • ACTUATOR, OBSERVABILITY AND OPERATIONAL HEALTH
What does Spring Boot Actuator provide?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It integrates operational endpoints and infrastructure for health, metrics, diagnostics,
and management.
DRAW THE IDEA — Actuator provide
BEFORE
Service state ➜
FOCUS
Actuator + telemetry ➜
AFTER
Operational signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
<artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
# Example routes after supported exposure:
# /actuator/health, /actuator/metrics
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Adding the dependency supplies capability, but endpoint availability depends on enablement or access, exposure,
security, and version. Select a minimal operational surface and restrict sensitive diagnostics.
04 / WATCH OUT
Presence in the context does not mean public HTTP access.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why might an enabled endpoint return 404?
Answer: An endpoint can be enabled yet not exposed on HTTP, blocked by security, moved to another
management port/base path, or unavailable due to a missing dependency.

pages.title: How do liveness and readiness differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 • ACTUATOR, OBSERVABILITY AND OPERATIONAL HEALTH
How do liveness and readiness differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Liveness asks whether the process should restart; readiness asks whether it should
receive traffic.
DRAW THE IDEA — liveness readiness
BEFORE
Service state ➜
FOCUS
Actuator + telemetry ➜
AFTER
Operational signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
/actuator/health/liveness  -> restart decision
/actuator/health/readiness -> routing decision
# Configure probe exposure and groups for the deployment.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A shared database outage should not normally make every instance fail liveness and restart together. Readiness can
consider the service's ability to serve useful requests, with a deliberate dependency policy.
04 / WATCH OUT
A healthy management port alone can hide a broken main listener.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why expose probes on the application port too?
Answer: An independent management port may report healthy while the application port is broken.
Probing the main port can verify the actual listener used by traffic.

pages.title: How should management endpoints be secured?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 • ACTUATOR, OBSERVABILITY AND OPERATIONAL HEALTH
How should management endpoints be secured?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Expose only needed endpoints and enforce explicit network and authentication/
authorization policies.
DRAW THE IDEA — management endpoints secured
BEFORE
Service state ➜
FOCUS
Actuator + telemetry ➜
AFTER
Operational signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info,prometheus
management.endpoint.health.show-details=when_authorized
# Prometheus capability also needs its registry dependency.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
HTTP exposure does not grant permission, and permission does not necessarily create exposure. When custom
security chains exist, own the management rules explicitly. Heap dumps, environment data, and configuration
diagnostics can be sensitive.
04 / WATCH OUT
include=* is rarely a good production starting point.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which monitoring identity can access metrics?
Answer: Use a dedicated least-privilege monitoring principal or service identity permitted only to required
endpoints, usually metrics/health; restrict all sensitive diagnostic endpoints.

pages.title: How do metrics, logs and traces differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 • ACTUATOR, OBSERVABILITY AND OPERATIONAL HEALTH
How do metrics, logs and traces differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Metrics summarize populations over time, logs record events, and traces connect spans
across one operation.
DRAW THE IDEA — metrics logs traces
BEFORE
Service state ➜
FOCUS
Actuator + telemetry ➜
AFTER
Operational signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Metric: p99 HTTP duration rose
Trace: database span consumed most of request time
Log: safe query failure context with matching trace id
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Use metrics to locate the symptom and traces or logs to explain examples. None replaces the others. Keep
propagation and sampling consistent across async and service boundaries.
04 / WATCH OUT
A log line without correlation can be hard to join to a failing request.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What can a low trace sampling rate miss?
Answer: Rare error traces can be unsampled at low rates. Combine traces with error counters, logs,
exemplars and focused higher-sampling rules when investigating incidents.
Source guide p. 82 • Senior • References: O01, O02

pages.title: Why is metric-tag cardinality dangerous?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 • ACTUATOR, OBSERVABILITY AND OPERATIONAL HEALTH
Why is metric-tag cardinality dangerous?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Every distinct tag combination can create another time series, increasing memory,
storage, and query cost.
DRAW THE IDEA — metric-tag cardinality dangerous
BEFORE
Service state ➜
FOCUS
Actuator + telemetry ➜
AFTER
Operational signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Good label: route=/orders/{id}, outcome=success
Bad label:  raw path=/orders/739421 or customerId=739421
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Use normalized routes and bounded categories. Put per-request ids in appropriate logs or trace fields rather than
meter tags. Even individually small label sets multiply when combined.
04 / WATCH OUT
Adding a unique request id to a metric can explode series count.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you detect runaway cardinality?
Answer: Inspect meter registry series counts and scrape sizes by metric/tag, alert on growth and forbid
unbounded IDs like userId or requestId as metric labels.

pages.title: Which signals indicate database or executor saturation?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 • ACTUATOR, OBSERVABILITY AND OPERATIONAL HEALTH
Which signals indicate database or executor saturation?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Observe active capacity, pending waits, wait duration, rejection, queue age, and useful
completion rate together.
DRAW THE IDEA — signals indicate database executor
BEFORE
Service state ➜
FOCUS
Actuator + telemetry ➜
AFTER
Operational signal
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
HTTP latency rises + Hikari pending waits rise
 -> inspect connection ownership and query latency
Queue age rises + CPU low
 -> inspect blocked workers and dependency capacity
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A high request count alone cannot identify the bottleneck. Correlate resource waits with traces and thread stacks
under the same time window. Alert on actionable capacity and service outcomes.
04 / WATCH OUT
Averages can hide tail latency.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which dashboard would separate slow SQL from pool acquisition?
Answer: Graph SQL execution time, Hikari active/pending/idle connections and acquisition wait beside
request latency. Slow SQL and waiting for a connection appear differently.

pages.title: What should a production container include?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 21 • PACKAGING, DOCKER AND KUBERNETES DEPLOYMENT
What should a production container include?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Include only the required runtime and artifact, use suitable permissions, and define
environment and resource behavior deliberately.
DRAW THE IDEA — production container include
BEFORE
Artifact / pod ➜
FOCUS
Deploy + probe ➜
AFTER
Serving traffic
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jre
WORKDIR /app
COPY app.jar /app/app.jar
USER 10001
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
This is a minimal illustrative Dockerfile, not a complete hardened image policy. Pin and maintain an appropriate
image version, ensure file permissions, and test native-memory headroom and signal handling.
04 / WATCH OUT
Container memory includes more than Java heap.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you use image layers or buildpacks?
Answer: Use layered executable jars or buildpacks to improve caching and reproducible images. Run as
non-root with a compatible JRE, health checks, limits and no embedded secrets.

pages.title: How should graceful shutdown work?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 21 • PACKAGING, DOCKER AND KUBERNETES DEPLOYMENT
How should graceful shutdown work?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Stop new useful work, allow accepted requests to drain within a bound, then close
managed resources with a recoverable policy for unfinished work.
DRAW THE IDEA — graceful shutdown work
BEFORE
Artifact / pod ➜
FOCUS
Deploy + probe ➜
AFTER
Serving traffic
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
server.shutdown=graceful
spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase=20s
# Platform termination grace must accommodate draining and cleanup.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Server behavior and defaults depend on version and implementation; the explicit setting documents intent. The
platform should remove readiness and route traffic appropriately. Long jobs need durable recovery rather than
relying solely on process life.
04 / WATCH OUT

How should Kubernetes probes be selected?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use startup for slow initialization, readiness for traffic eligibility, and liveness for
genuine restart-worthy process failure.

BEFORE
Artifact / pod ➜
FOCUS
Deploy + probe ➜
AFTER
Serving traffic
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
startupProbe -> allow expected startup budget
readinessProbe -> application readiness endpoint
livenessProbe -> application liveness endpoint
terminationGracePeriodSeconds -> include shutdown budget
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Coordinate thresholds and request timeouts. A probe against a separate management port can succeed while the
business port is unavailable; test the same relevant serving path.

Dependency outages should not cause cluster-wide restart storms.

Answer: During a rollout, deliberately make one pod unready and confirm endpoint removal and traffic
drain before termination. Inspect Service endpoints and ingress behavior.

CHAPTER 21 • PACKAGING, DOCKER AND KUBERNETES DEPLOYMENT
How should database capacity be budgeted across
replicas?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Account for maximum replicas, rollout overlap, migrations, other clients, and per-
instance connection limits.
DRAW THE IDEA — database capacity budgeted across
BEFORE
Artifact / pod ➜
FOCUS
Deploy + probe ➜
AFTER
Serving traffic
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Normal: 8 replicas x 15 connections = up to 120
Rollout overlap: 10 x 15 = up to 150
Database budget must also cover non-service clients.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Autoscaling can increase waiting database concurrency rather than throughput. Align admission, pool settings, and
database capacity before scaling. Observe the actual active connections rather than only configured maxima.
04 / WATCH OUT
A per-pod setting is not a cluster-wide limit.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What does maxSurge do to peak resource use?
Answer: maxSurge permits temporary extra pods during deployment. Count their database pools, memory
and CPU in the peak budget, not only the desired steady-state replica count.

pages.title: What makes a rollout safely reversible?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 21 • PACKAGING, DOCKER AND KUBERNETES DEPLOYMENT
What makes a rollout safely reversible?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Backward-compatible contracts and schema transitions, a validated artifact, visible
health, and a concrete rollback procedure.
DRAW THE IDEA — makes rollout safely reversible
BEFORE
Artifact / pod ➜
FOCUS
Deploy + probe ➜
AFTER
Serving traffic
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Expand schema -> deploy compatible code -> verify
Migrate consumers/data -> later remove old schema
Rollback code -> previous version still understands current schema
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Destructive schema changes can make code rollback impossible. Validate readiness and key business paths after
deployment, not just pod count. Keep configuration and secret versions part of the release record.
04 / WATCH OUT
A ready pod is not proof that transfers or authorization work.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What evidence would block a release?
Answer: Block rollout when critical authorization, payment idempotency, schema compatibility, readiness,
data recovery or rollback evidence is missing for the release risk profile.

Why does Boot 3 require changes beyond a version
number?

Boot 3 moves to the newer Spring ecosystem, Java 17+ baseline, and Jakarta
namespaces for relevant enterprise APIs.

import jakarta.validation.Valid;

pages.title: What are AOT processing and native images?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 22 • MODERN SPRING AND MIGRATION CHOICES
What are AOT processing and native images?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
AOT prepares supported application infrastructure at build time; a native image
compiles an executable with a constrained dynamic model.
DRAW THE IDEA — AOT processing native images
BEFORE
Old release ➜
FOCUS
Compatible migration ➜
AFTER
New release
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Build-time analysis -> generated infrastructure and hints
Native build -> platform-specific executable
Runtime -> validate reflection, resources, proxies, serialization
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
AOT and native packaging are related but distinct. Dynamic classpath behavior and reflection may need runtime
hints. Measure startup, memory, throughput, build time, and operational tooling rather than assuming a free
improvement.
04 / WATCH OUT
A native binary is not portable Java bytecode.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which plugin-loading behavior might be constrained?
Answer: Native-image closed-world analysis can restrict classes or plugins discovered dynamically after
build time. Declare reflection/resource hints or choose JVM deployment when dynamic loading is
essential.

pages.title: When should a modular monolith precede microservices?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 22 • MODERN SPRING AND MIGRATION CHOICES
When should a modular monolith precede microservices?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Prefer clear module boundaries within one deployment when independent distribution
does not yet justify its coordination cost.
DRAW THE IDEA — modular monolith precede microservices
BEFORE
Old release ➜
FOCUS
Compatible migration ➜
AFTER
New release
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Orders module -> published application interface
Billing module -> independent ownership and tests
One deployment -> simpler local transactions
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
A Boot application can be a well-structured monolith. Microservices add network failures, versioned contracts,
deployment complexity, and distributed consistency choices. Split when ownership, scaling, release cadence, or fault
isolation supports it.
04 / WATCH OUT
Multiple controllers do not constitute microservices.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What boundary could be extracted without sharing its tables?
Answer: Extract a bounded business capability whose APIs, data, migration and team ownership can be
separate. Stop other modules from reading its tables directly before remote extraction.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 23 • ADVANCED DESIGN AND INTERVIEW DISTINCTIONS
How do JDK proxies and class-based proxies differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
JDK proxies implement interfaces; class-based proxies subclass eligible classes, so final/
private method constraints matter.
DRAW THE IDEA — JDK proxies class-based proxies
BEFORE
Business rule ➜
FOCUS
Mechanism + proof ➜
AFTER
Safe invariant
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Interface proxy -> expose interface methods
Class proxy -> subclass target type
final method -> cannot be overridden for subclass advice
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
The actual proxy strategy depends on configuration and integration. Do not assume a method is advised merely
because it is public on an arbitrary object. Distinguish proxy type, method eligibility, and call path.
04 / WATCH OUT
A final class can constrain subclass proxy creation.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would injecting the concrete class affect an interface proxy?
Answer: An interface-based JDK proxy may not be assignable to the implementation concrete type. Inject
the interface, or deliberately choose compatible class-based proxying where required.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 23 • ADVANCED DESIGN AND INTERVIEW DISTINCTIONS
How does @Around advice differ from before and after
advice?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Around advice controls whether and how the invocation proceeds and can observe or
replace its result or failure.
DRAW THE IDEA — @Around advice before after
BEFORE
Business rule ➜
FOCUS
Mechanism + proof ➜
AFTER
Safe invariant
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Around("execution(* com.example.service.*.*(..))")
Object time(ProceedingJoinPoint p) throws Throwable {
  long start = System.nanoTime();
  try { return p.proceed(); }
  finally { recordElapsed(System.nanoTime() - start); }
}
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Calling proceed performs the target invocation. The finally observes success or failure without masking the original
outcome. This example assumes aspect registration and a safe recordElapsed implementation.
04 / WATCH OUT
Throwing from diagnostic advice can replace business failure.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why can repeated proceed duplicate a side effect?
Answer: Calling proceed more than once can rerun a payment or write method and duplicate effects.
Retry advice must enforce idempotency and bounded attempts.

pages.title: What does @TransactionalEventListener provide?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 23 • ADVANCED DESIGN AND INTERVIEW DISTINCTIONS
What does @TransactionalEventListener provide?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It binds handling to a transaction phase such as after commit, when an event is
published in an applicable transaction.
DRAW THE IDEA — @TransactionalEventListener provide
BEFORE
Business rule ➜
FOCUS
Mechanism + proof ➜
AFTER
Safe invariant
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@TransactionalEventListener(phase=TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT)
void committed(OrderPlaced e) { notifyBestEffort(e.id()); }
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
After-commit timing avoids sending a success signal before rollback, but an in-process event is not durable delivery.
New database writes at this phase need a deliberate fresh transaction policy. Without a transaction, fallback
behavior must be configured intentionally.
04 / WATCH OUT
A crash after commit can lose a non-durable notification.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When should outbox replace an in-process event?
Answer: Use outbox when the event must survive process crashes, reach another service, or be replayed.
@TransactionalEventListener is an in-process transaction-phase callback, not durable messaging.

pages.title: How do connection acquisition, transaction timeout, and query timeout differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 23 • ADVANCED DESIGN AND INTERVIEW DISTINCTIONS
How do connection acquisition, transaction timeout, and
query timeout differ?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They bound different waiting or work scopes and are enforced by different components.
DRAW THE IDEA — connection acquisition transaction time
BEFORE
Business rule ➜
FOCUS
Mechanism + proof ➜
AFTER
Safe invariant
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Hikari acquisition timeout -> wait for available connection
Transaction timeout -> manager's applicable transaction limit
Query timeout -> database statement/provider execution policy
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Do not expect a connection-wait setting to cancel a running SQL statement. Driver, manager, and database behavior
determine enforcement. Add an overall request deadline and test how failure releases resources.
04 / WATCH OUT
Timeout property names are not interchangeable across clients.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would a network stall differ from a database lock wait?
Answer: Database lock waits show blocked statements and locking sessions; a network stall shows socket/
connection wait behavior and transport timing. Correlate driver, DB and pool metrics.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 23 • ADVANCED DESIGN AND INTERVIEW DISTINCTIONS
How should multiple DataSources and transaction
managers be configured?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Define and qualify each infrastructure chain and select the intended manager for each
transaction boundary.
DRAW THE IDEA — multiple DataSources transaction manage
BEFORE
Business rule ➜
FOCUS
Mechanism + proof ➜
AFTER
Safe invariant
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@Transactional("billingTransactionManager")
public void recordCharge() { billingRepository.save(charge); }
// Configure matching DataSource, EntityManagerFactory,
// repository package and transaction manager.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
One local manager does not automatically atomically commit both databases. Decide whether distributed
coordination, outbox/saga, or a single authoritative store fits. Avoid ambiguous default bean selection.
04 / WATCH OUT
@Primary selects a default but does not unify consistency boundaries.

How would a second database failure be recovered?
Answer: Two separate local transactions cannot automatically undo each other. Use durable coordination,
idempotency and compensation or a properly supported distributed transaction protocol.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 23 • ADVANCED DESIGN AND INTERVIEW DISTINCTIONS
When are query specifications useful?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They compose typed optional predicates without building untrusted query strings, while
query and index behavior still need inspection.
DRAW THE IDEA — query specifications useful
BEFORE
Business rule ➜
FOCUS
Mechanism + proof ➜
AFTER
Safe invariant
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
Specification<Customer> active = (root, query, cb) ->
    cb.isTrue(root.get("active"));
Specification<Customer> tenant = (root, query, cb) ->
    cb.equal(root.get("tenantId"), tenantId);
repository.findAll(active.and(tenant), pageable);
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
The repository must support JpaSpecificationExecutor. Keep mandatory tenant predicates authoritative rather than
optional client filters. Inspect joins, count queries, indexes, and returned row shape.
04 / WATCH OUT
Type-safe construction is not automatic row authorization.

When would a projection-specific query be clearer?

predictable SQL. Specifications help flexible query predicates, not necessarily optimized read shapes.

pages.title: How can identifier generation affect batching?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 23 • ADVANCED DESIGN AND INTERVIEW DISTINCTIONS
How can identifier generation affect batching?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
The database/provider identifier strategy can affect when INSERTs execute and whether
efficient batching is possible.
DRAW THE IDEA — identifier generation affect batching
BEFORE
Business rule ➜
FOCUS
Mechanism + proof ➜
AFTER
Safe invariant
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
@GeneratedValue(strategy=GenerationType.IDENTITY) Long id;
// Compare with an appropriate sequence strategy where supported.
// Measure actual statement batches on the chosen engine.
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Some identity-generation paths require obtaining ids from executed inserts, constraining insert batching. Sequence
support and allocation policies vary by database. MySQL and PostgreSQL should not be assumed identical.
04 / WATCH OUT
Configuring batch_size alone does not prove batching occurred.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would generated-key requirements change an import design?
Answer: Generated identity keys may force insert round-trips and restrict batching. Consider supported
sequences, allocation strategies or staging/import operations after measuring.

pages.title: Why should indexes be chosen from workload evidence?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 23 • ADVANCED DESIGN AND INTERVIEW DISTINCTIONS
Why should indexes be chosen from workload evidence?
01 / THE SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
An index accelerates suitable lookup/order patterns but costs storage and write
maintenance, and may not match a composite predicate.
DRAW THE IDEA — indexes chosen workload evidence
BEFORE
Business rule ➜
FOCUS
Mechanism + proof ➜
AFTER
Safe invariant
02 / THE ORIGINAL EXAMPLE
WHERE tenant_id = ? AND created_at < ?
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
Candidate index -> aligned tenant, time, id columns
03 / WHY THIS WORKS
Use the database execution plan with representative data and selectivity. Verify ordering, range conditions, rows
examined, and write overhead. Exact index direction and plan behavior are engine-specific.
04 / WATCH OUT
An index on each individual column is not equivalent to a fitting composite index.
05 / INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would low selectivity change the plan?
Answer: Low selectivity means an index may read too many rows and lose to a scan. Check actual query
plans, row counts, filter order and covering possibilities.
