pages.title: Why is @ManyToMany often avoided for rich domains?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 05 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / RELATIONSHIPS AND OWNERSHIP
Q024
Why is @ManyToMany often avoided for rich
domains?
DIRECT ANSWER
The join table usually becomes a real domain relationship when it needs
timestamps, status or ownership rules. Map that join row as an entity.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
class Enrollment { Student student; Course course; LocalDate enrolledAt; }
TRACE THE IDEA
owning side → foreign key → association integrity
WATCH FOR
A bare @ManyToMany cannot carry join-row
fields naturally.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How would you store enrollment date?
ANSWER
Create an Enrollment entity with
@ManyToOne references to Student and
Course.

pages.title: What is a useful helper method for bidirectional associations?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 05 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / RELATIONSHIPS AND OWNERSHIP
Q025
What is a useful helper method for bidirectional
associations?
DIRECT ANSWER
A helper changes the owning field and the inverse collection together so the in-
memory graph stays coherent.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
void addOrder(Order o){orders.add(o);o.setCustomer(this);}
TRACE THE IDEA
owning side → foreign key → association integrity
WATCH FOR
Watch for recursive equals/toString across
both sides.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Is a helper sufficient to enforce
database integrity?
ANSWER
No. Foreign keys and uniqueness constraints
remain necessary.

pages.title: What does CascadeType.PERSIST do?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 06 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / CASCADES AND ORPHAN REMOVAL
Q026
What does CascadeType.PERSIST do?
DIRECT ANSWER
It propagates persist from a parent to related objects through a mapped
association. Only configure it when the parent controls that creation lifecycle.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
@OneToMany(cascade= CascadeType.PERSIST) List<Item> items;
TRACE THE IDEA
owner change → cascading action → child lifecycle
WATCH FOR
ALL is not a default that fits every
association.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Should you cascade from child to
shared parent?
ANSWER
Usually no. Persisting one order should not
automatically create unrelated customer
records.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.
JAVA 17 / JPA 3.1 / HIBERNATE ORM 6.6 HIBERNATE INTERVIEW LIBRARY

pages.title: How do cascade and orphanRemoval differ?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 06 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / CASCADES AND ORPHAN REMOVAL
Q027
How do cascade and orphanRemoval differ?
DIRECT ANSWER
Cascade REMOVE propagates deletion when the parent is removed.
orphanRemoval deletes a child when it is removed from its owning collection/
relationship.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
@OneToMany(mappedBy="order", orphanRemoval=true) List<Item> items;
TRACE THE IDEA
owner change → cascading action → child lifecycle
WATCH FOR
Removing a list entry can delete a database
row.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What if a child is merely moved to
another parent?
ANSWER
Handle the move explicitly and verify
ownership rules; orphan removal can
schedule deletion if modeled incorrectly.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.
JAVA 17 / JPA 3.1 / HIBERNATE ORM 6.6 HIBERNATE INTERVIEW LIBRARY

pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 06 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / CASCADES AND ORPHAN REMOVAL
Q028
Why is CascadeType.REMOVE risky on
@ManyToMany?
DIRECT ANSWER
Related entities are usually shared by many owners. Cascading delete could
remove another owner's shared entity.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
@ManyToMany Set<Tag> tags; // no REMOVE cascade
TRACE THE IDEA
owner change → cascading action → child lifecycle
WATCH FOR
Shared reference data must not be cascaded
away.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What should deletion remove in a
many-to-many relation?
ANSWER
Remove the join association, not the shared
peer entity.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.fullText:

INTERVIEW QUESTION / CASCADES AND ORPHAN REMOVAL
Q029
Why might a cascade seem to do nothing?
DIRECT ANSWER
Cascade directions only follow configured paths; the parent must be in the
relevant operation/state and associations must be synchronized.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY

Cascade is not equivalent to unlimited graph
persistence.

ANSWER
Inspect owning side, cascade configuration,
transaction, flush and SQL output.

INTERVIEW QUESTION / CASCADES AND ORPHAN REMOVAL

How should aggregate boundaries guide

choice.

pages.title: What does LAZY fetching mean?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 07 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / FETCHING, PROXIES AND LAZYINITIALIZATIONEXCEPTION
Q031
What does LAZY fetching mean?
DIRECT ANSWER
Hibernate may defer association loading until it is accessed in an open
persistence context. It is a fetch hint/contract subject to provider and mapping
rules.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
@ManyToOne(fetch=FetchType.LAZY) Customer customer;
TRACE THE IDEA
request → fetch plan → initialized fields
WATCH FOR
Never assume lazy means no database call
during serialization.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Does LAZY guarantee zero SQL at initial
load?
ANSWER
No. Mapping and instrumentation details can
affect whether an association is fetched
eagerly.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.fullText:

INTERVIEW QUESTION / FETCHING, PROXIES AND LAZYINITIALIZATIONEXCEPTION
Q032
What causes LazyInitializationException?
DIRECT ANSWER
Code accesses an uninitialized lazy association after its persistence context is
unavailable.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY

TRACE THE IDEA

EAGER.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Is Open Session in View the ideal fix?
ANSWER
Not necessarily. Prefer transaction-scoped
queries and intentional DTO fetch plans; OSIV
can hide extra SQL and extend persistence
work.

pages.fullText:

INTERVIEW QUESTION / FETCHING, PROXIES AND LAZYINITIALIZATIONEXCEPTION
Q033
What is an entity proxy?
DIRECT ANSWER
A proxy can stand in for an entity and load its state when needed. Its concrete
runtime type may differ from the mapped class.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY

context.

tricky?
ANSWER
Proxy subclasses and uninitialized identifiers
complicate entity equality; use a carefully
tested identity strategy.

When should you use an EntityGraph?
DIRECT ANSWER

duplicates.

pages.title: What is the N+1 select problem?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 08 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / N+1 QUERIES AND FETCH STRATEGIES
Q036
What is the N+1 select problem?
DIRECT ANSWER
A query loads N parents and then causes another query for each parent's
relationship, producing 1+N round trips.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
orders.forEach(o -> o.getCustomer().getName());
TRACE THE IDEA
initial SELECT → repeated child load → bounded query plan
WATCH FOR
A method that works with 3 rows can
become slow with 3,000.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How can you detect N+1?
ANSWER
Turn on SQL/statistics in tests and assert
statement counts for representative fixture
sizes.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

relationship, producing 1+N round trips.

pages.title: How can JOIN FETCH help?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 08 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / N+1 QUERIES AND FETCH STRATEGIES
Q037
How can JOIN FETCH help?
DIRECT ANSWER
It requests association data in the same query where appropriate, reducing
round trips for the selected graph.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
select o from Order o join fetch o.customer
TRACE THE IDEA
initial SELECT → repeated child load → bounded query plan
WATCH FOR
A join fetch can inflate result rows and
transferred bytes.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Why is joining multiple collections
dangerous?
ANSWER
Joining two bags can be unsupported or
multiply rows; bound collection cardinality
and consider multiple queries.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.
JAVA 17 / JPA 3.1 / HIBERNATE ORM 6.6 HIBERNATE INTERVIEW LIBRARY

pages.title: What does @BatchSize optimize?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 08 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / N+1 QUERIES AND FETCH STRATEGIES
Q038
What does @BatchSize optimize?
DIRECT ANSWER
Batch fetching gathers several uninitialized associations into fewer SELECTs,
often with an IN-list.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
@BatchSize(size=32) List<OrderItem> items;
TRACE THE IDEA
initial SELECT → repeated child load → bounded query plan
WATCH FOR
Batching reduces trips but may still load
unused data.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Is batch size 100 always better than
20?
ANSWER
No. Tune against DB parameter limits,
network cost and typical association counts.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.
JAVA 17 / JPA 3.1 / HIBERNATE ORM 6.6 HIBERNATE INTERVIEW LIBRARY

pages.title: What is subselect fetching?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 08 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / N+1 QUERIES AND FETCH STRATEGIES
Q039
What is subselect fetching?
DIRECT ANSWER
Hibernate can fetch collections for multiple loaded parents using a subquery
derived from the parent-loading scope.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
@Fetch(FetchMode.SUBSELECT) List<Item> items;
TRACE THE IDEA
initial SELECT → repeated child load → bounded query plan
WATCH FOR
Subselect fetch is not a universal N+1 fix.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
When is it a bad choice?
ANSWER
When a large parent result forces fetching
many collections not needed by the screen.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.title: How should you fetch data for a paginated list?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 08 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / N+1 QUERIES AND FETCH STRATEGIES
Q040
How should you fetch data for a paginated list?
DIRECT ANSWER
Page root IDs or DTO rows first, then fetch bounded needed details using a
second query if necessary.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
select o.id from Order o order by o.id
TRACE THE IDEA
initial SELECT → repeated child load → bounded query plan
WATCH FOR
A warning about in-memory pagination
should not be ignored.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Why avoid paging directly over a
collection fetch join?
ANSWER
SQL row multiplication can make root
pagination incorrect or force expensive in-
memory paging.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 09 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / JPQL, HQL AND DTO PROJECTIONS
Q041
What is JPQL and how is it different from SQL?
DIRECT ANSWER
JPQL queries the entity model and its fields, while SQL queries database tables
and columns. Hibernate HQL adds provider features.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
select o from Order o where o.customer.id = :id
TRACE THE IDEA
entity query → parameter binding → selected result
WATCH FOR
JPQL and SQL are not interchangeable text.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION

column names?
ANSWER
No. Use Java entity property names and
associations.

pages.title: How do you bind query parameters safely?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 09 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / JPQL, HQL AND DTO PROJECTIONS
Q042
How do you bind query parameters safely?
DIRECT ANSWER
Use typed or named parameters rather than concatenating untrusted values
into JPQL/SQL.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
query.setParameter("customerId", customerId);
TRACE THE IDEA
entity query → parameter binding → selected result
WATCH FOR
Never concatenate user-supplied filtering
values.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Does a bound parameter substitute for
a table name?
ANSWER
No. Whitelist any dynamic identifiers
separately; parameters represent values.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.fullText:

Q043
What are DTO constructor projections?
DIRECT ANSWER
A constructor projection selects only needed fields into a class with a matching
constructor instead of a managed entity.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY

TRACE THE IDEA
entity query → parameter binding → selected result
WATCH FOR
A DTO projection is not managed and won't
be dirty-checked.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Why use a DTO for a dashboard?
ANSWER
It reduces entity materialization and prevents
accidental lazy loading for read-only views.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

arbitrary match.

supported convenience API and encode
absence explicitly.

Q051
What does @Transactional do in a Spring JPA
service?

When properly intercepted, it opens or joins a transaction and manages
commit or rollback according to the transaction manager and rules.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY

WATCH FOR
A method annotation alone is not proof of a
transaction.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Does @Transactional on a private
method work by default?
ANSWER
No. Default proxy advice usually applies to
eligible calls through a Spring proxy, not
internal self-invocation.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

commit or rollback according to the transaction manager and rules.

method work by default?
ANSWER
No. Default proxy advice usually applies to
eligible calls through a Spring proxy, not
internal self-invocation.

pages.title: Why should a transaction be short?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 11 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / TRANSACTION BOUNDARIES AND SPRING INTEGRATION
Q052
Why should a transaction be short?
DIRECT ANSWER
Long transactions hold locks and database connections, increase contention
and can keep stale snapshots alive.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
reserveLocally(); // commit; then coordinate payment
TRACE THE IDEA
service command → transaction → commit or rollback
WATCH FOR
A database transaction cannot atomically
cover an unrelated remote API.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Should you make an HTTP payment call
inside a DB transaction?
ANSWER
Usually avoid it. Use a durable workflow with
explicit state and recovery across
independent systems.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.title: How do checked and unchecked exceptions affect Spring rollback?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 11 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / TRANSACTION BOUNDARIES AND SPRING INTEGRATION
Q053
How do checked and unchecked exceptions
affect Spring rollback?
DIRECT ANSWER
By default Spring rolls back on RuntimeException and Error, while checked
exceptions require explicit rules unless configured differently.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
@Transactional(rollbackFor=PaymentFailure.class)
TRACE THE IDEA
service command → transaction → commit or rollback
WATCH FOR
Catching a failure and returning normally
may commit partial work.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How do you roll back for a checked
business exception?
ANSWER
Declare rollbackFor or use a suitable domain
runtime exception after examining the
service contract.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.title: What does readOnly=true mean?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 11 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / TRANSACTION BOUNDARIES AND SPRING INTEGRATION
Q054
What does readOnly=true mean?
DIRECT ANSWER
It is a transaction hint that can reduce unnecessary work for reads, but
enforcement and optimizations depend on provider and database.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY

TRACE THE IDEA

WATCH FOR
Read-only does not replace database
privileges.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Does it guarantee write attempts are
rejected?
ANSWER
No. Do not treat it as a security or integrity
boundary.

pages.title: Why can transaction self-invocation fail?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 11 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / TRANSACTION BOUNDARIES AND SPRING INTEGRATION
Q055
Why can transaction self-invocation fail?
DIRECT ANSWER
A call from one method of a Spring bean to another on the same instance
bypasses the default proxy interception.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
service.process(); // through Spring proxy
TRACE THE IDEA

WATCH FOR
Adding annotations without testing
boundaries can silently fail.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How can you fix it?
ANSWER
Move the transactional operation to another
Spring-managed collaborator, or use a
deliberately selected interception strategy.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.title: What does optimistic locking with @Version do?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 12 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / CONCURRENCY, ISOLATION AND LOCKING
Q056
What does optimistic locking with @Version do?
DIRECT ANSWER
Hibernate includes a version condition in managed entity updates/deletes,
detecting some concurrent modifications.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
@Version long version;
TRACE THE IDEA
competing writes → conflict policy → consistent outcome
WATCH FOR
Version checks cover updates that participate
in the protocol.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How should a stale update be handled?
ANSWER
Return a conflict or retry the complete
decision using fresh state when the operation
is safely retryable.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.title: What is pessimistic locking?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 12 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / CONCURRENCY, ISOLATION AND LOCKING
Q057
What is pessimistic locking?
DIRECT ANSWER
A database lock is acquired to coordinate access before a decision, potentially
blocking competing transactions.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
em.find(Stock.class,id,LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE);
TRACE THE IDEA
competing writes → conflict policy → consistent outcome
WATCH FOR
A long remote call while holding a row lock
harms throughput.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What costs does it add?
ANSWER
Waiting, deadlocks, connection occupancy
and timeout management.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.title: Why can two updates lose one writer's changes?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 12 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / CONCURRENCY, ISOLATION AND LOCKING
Q058
Why can two updates lose one writer's
changes?
DIRECT ANSWER
Both transactions can read the same old state and write a new value without an
adequate conflict mechanism.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
update stock set qty=qty-1 where id=? and qty>0
TRACE THE IDEA
competing writes → conflict policy → consistent outcome
WATCH FOR
A Java synchronized block does not
coordinate multiple JVMs.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Can @Version fix every race?
ANSWER
No. Cross-row invariants and bulk/native
writes need their own constraints and
transaction design.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.
JAVA 17 / JPA 3.1 / HIBERNATE ORM 6.6 HIBERNATE INTERVIEW LIBRARY

pages.title: What is write skew and why is it dangerous?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 12 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / CONCURRENCY, ISOLATION AND LOCKING
Q059
What is write skew and why is it dangerous?
DIRECT ANSWER
Two transactions can each update different rows based on a shared condition
that becomes false after both commits.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
two doctors each disable own on-call row
TRACE THE IDEA
competing writes → conflict policy → consistent outcome
WATCH FOR
Row-level @Version on separate rows alone
may not prevent it.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How can you protect the invariant?
ANSWER
Use suitable serializable isolation or explicit
locking/coordination around the complete
invariant.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.title: How should deadlock retries work?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 12 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / CONCURRENCY, ISOLATION AND LOCKING
Q060
How should deadlock retries work?
DIRECT ANSWER
Retry the complete idempotent transaction with a bounded policy and fresh
reads after the database aborts one participant.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
retry with jitter and maxAttempts=3
TRACE THE IDEA
competing writes → conflict policy → consistent outcome
WATCH FOR
Blind retries can repeat external side effects.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Why is retrying only the last SQL
statement unsafe?
ANSWER
Previous reads and decisions may no longer
be valid; the entire transaction must be re-
evaluated.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.
JAVA 17 / JPA 3.1 / HIBERNATE ORM 6.6 HIBERNATE INTERVIEW LIBRARY

INTERVIEW QUESTION / FIRST-LEVEL CACHE AND PERSISTENCE CONTEXT
Q061
What is Hibernate's first-level cache?
DIRECT ANSWER
It is the identity map of the persistence context: the same entity key maps to
one managed object within that context.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY

A first-level cache is not shared across
requests.

ANSWER
Not if the entity is already managed and no
refresh semantics force a read.

pages.fullText:

Q062
Does the first-level cache guarantee fresh
database values?
DIRECT ANSWER
No. Managed state can become stale when another transaction or bulk
statement changes rows.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY

TRACE THE IDEA

WATCH FOR
A cached entity is not a substitute for
locking.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How do you reload authoritative state?
ANSWER
Use refresh, clear, or a new persistence
context as the correctness scenario requires.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.title: How can a persistence context grow too large?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 13 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / FIRST-LEVEL CACHE AND PERSISTENCE CONTEXT
Q063
How can a persistence context grow too large?
DIRECT ANSWER
Loading or persisting many entities keeps managed references and snapshots
until they are detached or cleared.

TRACE THE IDEA

WATCH FOR
Unbounded persistence contexts can exhaust
heap.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
How do you batch large imports?
ANSWER
Process bounded chunks, flush and clear
deliberately, and avoid materializing the
entire source.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

How is the second-level cache different from

managed Java object?

No. They can reuse cached state but each
manages its own entity instance.

behavior; frequently changing tables may

How should a distributed cache react to
external writers?

Design eviction/refresh when other applications update the same tables, or
avoid caching data whose updates cannot be coordinated.

Stale cross-service cache state can violate
business expectations.

write automatically?

provider cache invalidation.

pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 15 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / BATCHING, IDS AND WRITE OPTIMIZATION
Q071
What is JDBC statement batching in Hibernate?
DIRECT ANSWER
Hibernate can group compatible INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statements for
fewer database round trips when configured and supported.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
hibernate.jdbc.batch_size=32
TRACE THE IDEA
pending inserts → JDBC batches → fewer network trips
WATCH FOR
Batch size is a throughput tuning parameter,
not an invariant.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Will batching always improve
performance?
ANSWER
Not automatically. Benchmark with your
driver, generator strategy, table and batch
size.

pages.title: Why can IDENTITY IDs reduce insert batching?
pages.fullText:
HIBERNATE ORM / ZERO TO HERO 15 / 20
INTERVIEW QUESTION / BATCHING, IDS AND WRITE OPTIMIZATION
Q072
Why can IDENTITY IDs reduce insert batching?
DIRECT ANSWER
The generated identifier may require immediate insertion to retrieve its value,
limiting how Hibernate groups inserts.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
@GeneratedValue(strategy=SEQUENCE)
TRACE THE IDEA
pending inserts → JDBC batches → fewer network trips
WATCH FOR
Changing ID strategy needs migration and
ordering review.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What is a possible alternative?
ANSWER
Use a suitable sequence-based strategy on
databases supporting it, considering
allocation and identity requirements.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

Q073
What is an allocation size for sequences?
DIRECT ANSWER
It lets identifiers be reserved in blocks to reduce calls to a sequence provider,
depending on optimizer behavior.

TRACE THE IDEA
pending inserts → JDBC batches → fewer network trips

ANSWER
Gaps are normal in many generated ID
strategies; never assume sequential gap-free
business numbers.

Q074
How do ordered inserts and updates help?
DIRECT ANSWER
Grouping statements by entity and key can make JDBC batching more effective,
though it introduces ordering and processing cost.

TRACE THE IDEA

WATCH FOR
Reordered statements can expose previously
hidden constraint timing.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Should these flags always be enabled?
ANSWER
Measure realistic workloads and verify any
constraint-sensitive operations.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.fullText:

Q075
How can you process a million rows safely?
DIRECT ANSWER
Prefer chunked reads or streaming with bounded state, per-chunk transactions,
and flush/clear instead of loading all entities.

pending inserts → JDBC batches → fewer network trips

Bulk tooling changes guarantees; read the
API contract.

useful?
ANSWER
For specialized bulk operations where you
deliberately give up normal persistence-
context behavior and some event/cascade
semantics.

pages.fullText:

INTERVIEW QUESTION / BULK UPDATES, NATIVE SQL AND CONSISTENCY
Q076
How does JPQL bulk UPDATE differ from entity
dirty checking?
DIRECT ANSWER
Bulk DML acts directly on matching database rows and bypasses normal per-
entity dirty checking and lifecycle callbacks.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
update Order o set o.status=:s where o.id in :ids
TRACE THE IDEA
bulk statement → database rows → stale loaded state
WATCH FOR
Bulk DML may bypass optimistic-version
checks unless explicitly designed.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
What happens to already-managed
entities?
ANSWER
They may remain stale; clear or refresh the
context after the bulk operation.
Remember: Explain the behavior, the SQL/transaction effect, and one failure case.

pages.fullText:

Q077
When should you use a bulk delete?
DIRECT ANSWER
Use it for validated set-based removal with correct tenant, retention, FK and
audit rules, rather than loading every row.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
delete from ExpiredToken t where t.expiresAt<:now
TRACE THE IDEA
bulk statement → database rows → stale loaded state
WATCH FOR
Not all object lifecycle hooks run in bulk
SQL.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Does it invoke entity @PreRemove
callbacks?
ANSWER
Bulk DML generally bypasses entity
callbacks/cascades; validate requirements
first.

Q078
How do you combine native SQL with managed
entities safely?
DIRECT ANSWER
Flush pending relevant changes, execute bounded native SQL, and clear/refresh
affected managed state as needed.

Stale context state can overwrite SQL
changes later.

cache?
ANSWER
Do not assume complete invalidation for
arbitrary external statements.

failure where needed.

Q080
How do you avoid long retention cleanup

DIRECT ANSWER
Delete in limited batches, use indexed predicates and monitor locks, replication
lag and vacuum/purge behavior.

Usually consider reviewed bulk operations or

subtype rules.

ANSWER

constraints make the common table unwieldy.

Pool active/idle/pending, slow SQL, lock waits
and remote calls inside transactions.

Why is a cartesian product dangerous in ORM

DISTINCT doesn't undo all wasted database
work.

ANSWER
Fetch bounded relationships separately,

grain.

pages.title: How do you prevent double booking through JPA?
pages.fullText:

INTERVIEW QUESTION / SENIOR ARCHITECT SCENARIOS AND UPGRADES
Q097
How do you prevent double booking through
JPA?
DIRECT ANSWER
Use a database uniqueness/conditional update rule and an idempotency key
under a transaction, rather than read-then-insert checks.
EXAMPLE / MAPPING OR QUERY
UNIQUE(event_id, seat_id) on confirmed allocation
TRACE THE IDEA
critical invariant → ORM mechanism → recovery evidence
WATCH FOR
Two JVMs can race past a Java precheck.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION
Can optimistic locking alone enforce
seat uniqueness?
ANSWER
Only if all conflicting decisions touch the
same protected versioned state; database
uniqueness is often safer.

LAST-MINUTE REFERENCE
10 Hibernate interview traps
01 flush != commit; a flushed change can roll
back.
02 merge returns a managed instance; the
input stays detached.
03 first-level cache is per persistence
context, not globally shared.
04 LAZY does not prevent accidental queries
during serialization.
05 JOIN FETCH with collections can make
pagination unsafe.
06 N+1 should be measured with
representative entity counts.
07 @Transactional self-invocation may skip
proxy advice.
08 @Version does not protect every cross-
row invariant.
09 Bulk DML can leave managed entities
stale and bypass callbacks.
10 Cache annotations do not create durable
or linearizable storage.

pages.title: THE TOOLKIT
pages.fullText:
THE TOOLKIT
JUnit and Mockito: how they fit
JUnit runs the test and checks expectations. Mockito replaces selected
collaborators so the test can control external outcomes.
JUNIT IS RESPONSIBLE FOR
Test discovery, lifecycle, assertions, parameterized invocations, extensions, tags and
reporting.
MOCKITO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR
Creating doubles, defining collaborator responses, capturing arguments and
checking required interactions.
NEITHER LIBRARY PROVES
Database isolation, broker delivery, HTTP security or transaction durability just by
mocking those dependencies. Use a focused integration test for the real boundary.
Design rule: Mock only what is outside the unit. Keep domain calculations and result values real.

What is a unit test?
IN ONE CLEAR ANSWER
A unit test checks one small behavior with controlled inputs and clear expected
results. It should run quickly and isolate the reason for a failure; the unit may be one
class or a small cluster of related classes.

Does a unit test have to test one method?
No. Test the visible behavior of a unit, including the calls needed to reach it. Splitting
a workflow into artificial method-level tests can make refactoring harder.

What makes a test reliable and maintainable?
IN ONE CLEAR ANSWER
A reliable test has one clear purpose, deterministic setup, observable assertions and
useful failure messages. It avoids shared state, sleeps and assumptions about
execution order.

Because tests are executable requirements. A test that always passes or asserts only
a mock call can miss a broken business result.

Arrange creates inputs and collaborators; Act invokes the behavior once; Assert
verifies its result and important side effects. This readable flow reduces accidental
confusion between setup and expectations.

When should you use assertEquals instead of
assertSame?

assertEquals tests equality under equals; assertSame requires the identical object
reference. For domain values, equality is usually the intended contract.

RELATED JAVA / JUNIT EXAMPLE

INTERVIEW FOLLOW-UP
Can two different objects pass assertEquals?
Yes, if equals returns true. Their references remain different, so assertSame would
fail.

pages.title: QUICK REVISION
pages.fullText:
QUICK REVISION
Choose the correct test
USE PLAIN JUNIT + MOCKITO
For pure Java services whose dependencies can be controlled; assert return values
and required side effects.
USE A REAL DATABASE TEST
For JPQL/SQL, mapping, unique constraints, transaction isolation and optimistic
locking.
USE SPRING CONTEXT OR MVC TESTS
For component wiring, validation, filters, security rules and serialization contracts.
USE A FULL END-TO-END TEST
For a small number of critical user workflows that cross deployed services.
REVIEW THESE PITFALLS
Overmocking; no assertions; shared mutable data; Thread.sleep; unbounded futures;
unchecked Mockito defaults; verifying private call chains; assuming one mock call
proves a commit.

Q001. What is a microservice?

A microservice handles one clear business job and can be released without forcing
unrelated services to change. It owns its data and exposes a contract.

API versions work together, and no shared database migration forces a simultaneous release.

pages.title: How do a monolith, modular monolith and microservices differ?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 01 · Q002/120
Microservices foundations
Q002. How do a monolith, modular monolith
and microservices differ?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A monolith ships as one application. A modular monolith has clean modules but still ships
together. Microservices run and deploy separately over network contracts.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
A monolith is deployed as one
application ➜
A loan application can begin
with origination, underwriting
and disbursement...
➜
A monolith can be
maintainable and horizontally
scalable
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A loan application can begin with origination, underwriting and disbursement modules in one Boot 
application. Extract underwriting only when its release, ownership or scaling needs justify a remote 
boundary.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
// A modular monolith can preserve domain modules:
orders.place(order);  // same deployment
// Extract only if ownership justifies remote calls.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which module would you extract first, and why?
Answer → Extract a stable, high-change module such as underwriting only when ownership,
release pace or scaling differs. First measure call frequency and dependency coupling.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  A monolith can be maintainable and horizontally scalable.

Q003. What is a distributed monolith?

A distributed monolith has many running services but still needs joint releases or shares
internal tables. It gets network problems without independent change.

It is a collection of processes

independence

pages.title: What are the benefits and costs of microservices?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 01 · Q004/120
Microservices foundations
Q004. What are the benefits and costs of
microservices?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Microservices can give teams ownership and allow targeted scaling, but add network
errors, data coordination and monitoring work.

Useful benefits include focused
ownership, selective scaling
and...

scales separately from
checkout

freshness, event recovery, monitoring and a team that can operate it.

team effort before and after the split under comparable traffic.

driven design?

A bounded context is a place where a business word has one meaning. Billing and CRM
may describe a customer differently and should not share internal entities.

pages.title: What is an aggregate, and why does it matter?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 02 · Q007/120
Domain boundaries and ownership
Q007. What is an aggregate, and why does it
matter?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
An aggregate groups data that must follow one business rule in one local transaction. Its
root checks rules for all members.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
An aggregate is a consistency
boundary containing entities
and value...
➜
An Order root rejects a
negative quantity and owns its
line items
➜
An aggregate should not
become the entire database
graph
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
An Order root rejects a negative quantity and owns its line items. Inventory availability belongs to a 
separate owner and is represented by a reservation result, not an Order-side update of stock tables.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which rule must be atomic, and which can complete later?
Answer → Order totals and line-item quantities should agree atomically. Email notifications or
search indexing can follow later through reliable events.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  An aggregate should not become the entire database graph.

pages.fullText:

Q008. How do you decide the right service
size?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Size services by business changes, data ownership and operational needs, not file counts.
Too-small boundaries create lots of slow calls.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Group behavior that changes
together and requires closely
related invariants
➜ Returns and refund policy maybelong together initially ➜ Excessive synchronous chattercan reveal a misplacedboundary
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Returns and refund policy may belong together initially. If every return requires ten remote calls to read 
tiny fragments, reconsider the split before adding more orchestration.

Reservation result = inventory.reserve(command);
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which signals would justify merging two services?
Answer → Merge if changes repeatedly touch both services, most requests require synchronous
round trips, or ownership and data invariants cannot be separated economically.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Excessive synchronous chatter can reveal a misplaced boundary.

pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 02 · Q009/120

Q009. How should service and data ownership
work?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A service team should own its APIs, data rules, operations, monitoring and releases. Other
teams use its contract rather than editing its tables.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Assign a team accountable for
the contract, data lifecycle,
reliability and...
➜
The inventory team owns
reservation semantics and
schema migrations
➜
Ownership without operational
responsibility leaves failures
unowned
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
The inventory team owns reservation semantics and schema migrations. Checkout requests a reservation 
and handles rejection; it does not insert directly into inventory tables.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Who approves a breaking contract change?
Answer → The API owner proposes the version and migration plan; consumer owners approve or
verify compatibility through contract tests and a deprecation window.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Ownership without operational responsibility leaves failures unowned.

pages.title: What do HTTP methods and status codes mean in a service API?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 03 · Q011/120
REST contracts and API evolution
Q011. What do HTTP methods and status codes
mean in a service API?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
GET reads; POST commonly creates or commands; PUT replaces the addressed
resource; DELETE removes it. Status codes tell clients what actually happened.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Use methods according to
their semantics: GET reads,
POST performs...
➜
POST /orders returns 201 with
Location when an order is
created; 202 means work...
➜
GET-triggered charging is
unsafe even if it appears
convenient
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
POST /orders returns 201 with Location when an order is created; 202 means work was accepted for 
later processing, not that payment succeeded. A repeated DELETE can return 404 after an earlier 
success while remaining idempotent.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
POST /orders   -> 201 Created + Location
POST /jobs     -> 202 Accepted + operationId
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
When would a create operation return 202?
Answer → Return HTTP 202 when the request has been durably accepted but processing is still
pending. Supply an operation ID and status endpoint; do not imply success.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  GET-triggered charging is unsafe even if it appears convenient.

pages.title: How do you make a create or payment API idempotent?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 03 · Q012/120
REST contracts and API evolution
Q012. How do you make a create or payment
API idempotent?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Give each create or charge a stable idempotency key scoped to user/operation. Store its
request fingerprint and result durably so retries cannot repeat the effect.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Define a client-supplied
operation key scoped to the
authenticated tenant...
➜ Tenant A retries payment keyp-17 after a timeout ➜ An in-memory map does notcoordinate replicas or surviverestart
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Tenant A retries payment key p-17 after a timeout. The server returns the original payment reference. 
Tenant B's same key is a different scope; changing A's amount under p-17 produces a conflict.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
// Key identity includes tenant and operation:
record Key(String tenant, String action, String id) {}
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How do key expiry and unknown external outcomes interact?
Answer → Keep keys at least as long as the replay/recovery period. Before expiry or reuse,
resolve unknown external charges by original operation identity, not a fresh payment.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  An in-memory map does not coordinate replicas or survive restart.
MY ONE-LINE RECAP ______________________________________________________

Q013. How should a microservice return
errors?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Return a documented status and machine-readable error code. Clients need to
distinguish bad input, denied access, business rejection and temporary failure.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Provide a stable machine-
readable contract with a
documented code or...

A reservation rejection returns
a documented stock-
unavailable problem
➜
Clients should not parse
human-readable error
messages

A reservation rejection returns a documented stock-unavailable problem. A database connection failure 
returns a generic service error and trace reference, not SQL text, credentials or a stack trace.

// RFC 9457-style problem details:
{ "type":"/problems/out-of-stock", "status":409 }

Which errors may a caller safely retry?
Answer → Retry transient 429/503/network errors only within a deadline and when the operation
is safe to repeat. Do not blindly retry validation or permission failures.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Clients should not parse human-readable error messages.

pages.title: How do pagination and sorting affect API correctness?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 03 · Q014/120
REST contracts and API evolution
Q014. How do pagination and sorting affect
API correctness?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Sorting needs a unique tie-breaker. Keyset/cursor pagination avoids many offset
problems but changing records can still move between pages.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Specify a stable ordering and
a unique tie-breaker ➜
For newest orders, sort by
created_at descending and id
descending
➜ A cursor is not automatically aconsistent snapshot
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
For newest orders, sort by created_at descending and id descending. A cursor contains both values; 
using only the timestamp can skip or repeat orders created at the same instant.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
ORDER BY created_at DESC, order_id DESC
-- Cursor includes BOTH sort columns.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP

synchronously or asynchronously?

Call another service synchronously when the answer is needed now. Use a message when

failure

Q019. What coupling remains with
asynchronous events?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Messages remove immediate waiting but consumers still depend on event identity,
meaning, schema and ordering. An event is a long-lived contract.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Consumers still depend on
event meaning, schema,
identity, partition keys,...
➜ InventoryReserved means acommitted reservation exists ➜ Asynchronous does not meanloosely coupled by definition

was requested changes a business fact and breaks order progression, even if the JSON shape is 
unchanged.

How would you retire an event field?
Answer → Keep the old field during migration, add the replacement, watch real consumer
adoption and remove only after all replay and consumer compatibility windows close.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Asynchronous does not mean loosely coupled by definition.

Q020. How do you design an aggregation

THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
An aggregation endpoint combines several services. Bound parallel calls and clearly
mark missing optional sections instead of hiding failures.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Call independent
dependencies in parallel only
when the resource budget...
➜
A product page requires
product identity, but reviews
are optional

unavailable section while purchase eligibility still comes from the authoritative owner.

THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Discovery turns a service name into active endpoints. Membership can change, so a

A gateway routes and applies shared HTTP policies, but the service still owns business

A gateway provides client-

authorization

data ownership checks within the service. Never rely on gateway identity alone.

pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 06 · Q026/120

Q026. What makes a Spring Boot application a
microservice?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Spring Boot provides the application framework. It becomes a microservice because it
owns a real business capability and private state, not because of an annotation.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Boot assembles an application
with dependency injection, web
support,...
➜
An InventoryApplication has
an HTTP adapter, reservation
use case and inventory...
➜
Start with behavior and
invariants, then select
infrastructure
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
An InventoryApplication has an HTTP adapter, reservation use case and inventory repository. Adding 
@SpringBootApplication to five applications without ownership boundaries does not create five 
independent capabilities.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
@RestController class OrderController {
  private final OrderUseCase useCase;
  // Keep business rules behind a domain port.
}
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How would you structure ports and adapters inside the service?
Answer → Put HTTP controllers and repositories in adapters, use cases in the application layer,

pages.title: Are Spring singleton beans safe for concurrent requests?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 06 · Q029/120
Spring Boot implementation and configuration
Q029. Are Spring singleton beans safe for
concurrent requests?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A Spring singleton is shared by many request threads; its fields are not magically thread-
safe. Shared business writes need database-level protection across replicas.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Singleton defines sharing
scope, not thread safety ➜
A controller field
currentCustomer leaks state
between concurrent requests
➜
Stateless HTTP handlers may
still use shared stateful
dependencies
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A controller field currentCustomer leaks state between concurrent requests. A local synchronized block 
around stock updates also fails when another replica writes the same stock row.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
// One pod lock does not protect other pods.
UPDATE stock SET qty = qty - 1
 WHERE sku = :sku AND qty >= 1;
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Where should a cross-replica stock invariant be enforced?
Answer → Use one atomic conditional stock update or transaction at the Inventory owner's
database, not a synchronized Java method on one pod.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Stateless HTTP handlers may still use shared stateful dependencies.

pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 07 · Q031/120
Timeouts, deadlines and retries
Q031. Does a timeout mean the remote
operation failed?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A timeout means the answer did not arrive in time. The payment may have succeeded, so
do not charge again with a new key.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
No ➜ Payment commits charge p-17at 950 ms; order times out at
900 ms
➜
A 504 response is not proof
that no business effect
occurred
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Payment commits charge p-17 at 950 ms; order times out at 900 ms. Retrying with a new key can 
charge twice. Reuse the operation identity and ask for its recorded outcome.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
POST /payments
Idempotency-Key: pay-17
// On timeout: GET /payments/operations/pay-17
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which state should the order show while the outcome is unknown?
Answer → Show PAYMENT_PENDING or PAYMENT_UNKNOWN, save the operation ID and
reconcile with the payment owner before confirming or cancelling.

pages.title: How do connect, pool-acquisition and response timeouts differ?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 07 · Q032/120
Timeouts, deadlines and retries
Q032. How do connect, pool-acquisition and
response timeouts differ?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Connect timeout covers opening a connection; pool timeout covers waiting for one;
response timeout covers remote response behavior. Total deadline includes all waiting.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Connect timeout bounds
connection establishment ➜ An order request has a 1,000ms deadline ➜ Socket read timeouts mayreset on progress rather thancap total elapsed time
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
An order request has a 1,000 ms deadline. It spends 200 ms in a queue, leaving only 800 ms for 
application work and remote calls, even if a client's response timeout is configured as 1,000 ms.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
long remaining = deadlineNanos - System.nanoTime();
if (remaining <= 0) return expired();
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How would you propagate the remaining deadline?
Answer → Send the remaining end-to-end budget with a request header or context, recalculate
before each call and skip attempts that cannot finish in time.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Socket read timeouts may reset on progress rather than cap total elapsed time.
MY ONE-LINE RECAP ______________________________________________________

pages.title: Timeouts, deadlines and retries Q033. Which failures should be retried?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 07 · Q033/120
Timeouts, deadlines and retries
Q033. Which failures should be retried?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Retry only likely temporary failures and only when repeating the business action is safe.
Limit attempts, time and overall retry pressure.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Retry classified transient
failures only when the
operation is idempotent...
➜
A connection failure during an
idempotent inventory-status
read may be retried
➜
An exception whitelist alone
does not establish business
retry safety
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A connection failure during an idempotent inventory-status read may be retried. Insufficient stock is a 
business result. A payment timeout requires the same operation key and an outcome-recovery contract.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Who owns retries when several layers can repeat a call?
Answer → Make the application boundary responsible for its retry budget and disable other layers
or allow only explicitly coordinated low-level retries.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  An exception whitelist alone does not establish business retry safety.

pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 07 · Q034/120
Timeouts, deadlines and retries
Q034. Why use backoff and jitter, and what is
retry amplification?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Backoff waits between retries; jitter avoids many clients retrying together. Retrying at
multiple layers multiplies traffic during an outage.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Backoff spaces attempts; jitter
spreads synchronized clients ➜
Three layers making three
total attempts each can
produce up to 27 deepest
calls...
➜ Say whether an attempt countincludes the original call
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Three layers making three total attempts each can produce up to 27 deepest calls for one logical 
request, rather than three. Adding random delay changes timing but not that worst-case count.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
// Example: bounded retries with jitter
delayMs = random.nextLong(maxDelayMs + 1);
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How would you cap retries during a regional outage?
Answer → Set one small budget, cap attempts and total elapsed time, use circuit breakers and
reject overload. During regional loss, fail fast or move traffic safely.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Say whether an attempt count includes the original call.

// Use timeouts and a bulkhead separately.

pages.title: How do rate limiting and concurrency limiting differ?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 08 · Q038/120
Resilience and admission control
Q038. How do rate limiting and concurrency
limiting differ?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Rate limiting counts work over time; concurrency limiting caps work currently in progress.
Slow work can exhaust resources even at a fixed rate.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Rate limiting controls
admission over time, such as
requests per second
➜
At 100 requests per second, a
50 ms average residence time
implies roughly five in...
➜
Rate, burst size and
simultaneous work are
separate settings
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
At 100 requests per second, a 50 ms average residence time implies roughly five in flight; at two 
seconds it implies roughly 200 in flight under stable conditions.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
// Average in-flight (Little's Law):
concurrency = requestsPerSecond * avgSeconds;
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP

Resilience and admission control
Q040. What is backpressure, and how is it
different from a queue?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Backpressure prevents accepting work faster than it can be finished. A queue only holds
a bounded amount; an unlimited queue hides the overload.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Backpressure or admission
control prevents producers
from creating more...
➜
A notification worker accepts
at most a measured backlog,
and the API reports...
➜ An asynchronous method isnot automatically a durable job
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A notification worker accepts at most a measured backlog, and the API reports overload or durable 
pending work according to its contract. It does not keep adding tasks to an unlimited executor queue.

boolean accepted = queue.offer(job);

What happens when producers outpace consumers for an hour?

throttled, workers scale sustainably or old work is rejected/expired.

Q042. Why does @Transactional not create a
transaction across services?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
@Transactional controls a local managed transaction; an HTTP payment is outside that
transaction. Remote success remains even if the local order rolls back.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
A Spring transaction applies to
resources coordinated by the
configured...

Order rolls back its local insert
after payment successfully
charges through HTTP
➜
Proxy self-invocation and
rollback rules also affect local
behavior
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Order rolls back its local insert after payment successfully charges through HTTP. The charge remains 
and must be recovered or compensated through a separate business operation.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e

  repository.save(order);
  // Remote HTTP payment is NOT part of this DB txn.
}
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which durable record links a local failure to a successful remote charge?
Answer → Save the external operation ID and a durable workflow state or reconciliation/outbox
record connecting the order to that payment outcome.

pages.fullText:

Q043. What does the CAP theorem actually
say?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
During a network partition a replicated store cannot promise both strict single-copy
consistency and a response from every healthy isolated node.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
For a partitioned distributed
store under the theorem's
model, it is...
➜
If two disconnected regions
both accept conflicting writes
to the same balance,...
➜
Practical availability
percentages and CAP's formal
availability are...
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
If two disconnected regions both accept conflicting writes to the same balance, they cannot both 
guarantee one latest linearizable value. A design must restrict some operations or allow weaker 
semantics and reconcile.

Which operations would you refuse during a partition?

unreachable. Allow clearly labelled stale catalog reads if the business permits.

Q044. What does PACELC add to the

PACELC reminds us that consistency can cost latency even without a partition. A closer

PACELC highlights that
tradeoffs also exist without a
partition: if there...

can improve a read or write
guarantee while increasing...

replication, protocol and
requested operation

pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 10 · Q046/120
Concurrent writes and data invariants
Q046. What is optimistic locking?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Optimistic locking compares the version originally read with the current database version.
A losing writer sees a conflict instead of silently replacing a change.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
An optimistic update checks
the version originally read and
advances it...
➜ Two users edit order version 7 ➜ Every write path must respectthe version protocol
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Two users edit order version 7. The first update writes version 8. The second update with expected 
version 7 fails and must reload or return a conflict.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
UPDATE orders SET state=:newState, version=version+1
 WHERE id=:id AND version=:expected;
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Would you automatically retry a user-submitted price change?
Answer → Not automatically. A price update reflects a person's decision; reload and ask for
confirmation if the value changed, unless business rules explicitly permit recomputation.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Every write path must respect the version protocol.

Q047. When is pessimistic locking useful?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Pessimistic locking holds a database lock during a short local transaction. It can be right
for hot rows but increases waiting and deadlock risk.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Pessimistic locking acquires a
database lock before
modifying protected...
➜
A short transaction locks the
next available settlement row,
claims it and commits
➜
A lock inside one database
does not lock another service's
state

A short transaction locks the next available settlement row, claims it and commits. It does not hold the 
lock while calling a slow external bank API.

What evidence distinguishes deadlocks from pool exhaustion?
Answer → Database deadlock messages and lock graphs show cycles; pool exhaustion shows
connection wait/active counts without necessarily any database lock cycle.

pages.title: How do you prevent overselling inventory?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 10 · Q048/120
Concurrent writes and data invariants
Q048. How do you prevent overselling
inventory?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Reserve stock with an atomic conditional database update and a reservation ID. A
separate stock read followed by update can oversell.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Enforce the reservation
invariant in an atomic
operation at the inventory...
➜
UPDATE stock SET available =
available - 2 WHERE sku
= :sku AND available >= 2
➜
A local Java synchronized
block cannot protect multiple
inventory replicas
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
UPDATE stock SET available = available - 2 WHERE sku = :sku AND available >= 2. Exactly one affected 
row indicates a successful decrement; the reservation row and event are written in the same local 
transaction.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
UPDATE inventory SET available=available-:qty
 WHERE sku=:sku AND available>=:qty;
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How do cancellation and reservation expiry avoid double release?
Answer → Use one reservation state transition from ACTIVE to RELEASED or CONFIRMED with a
version/unique key. Only the winning transition returns stock; expiry and cancel cannot both
release.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  A local Java synchronized block cannot protect multiple inventory replicas.

pages.title: What is fencing, and why can a lease lock be insufficient?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 10 · Q050/120
Concurrent writes and data invariants
Q050. What is fencing, and why can a lease
lock be insufficient?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A lease can expire while a worker is paused. Fencing gives each new owner a higher
token that the storage system rejects if it is outdated.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
A process can pause long
enough for its lease to expire,
then resume...
➜
Worker A owns token 41,
pauses, and worker B obtains
42
➜
Token issuance and resource
enforcement require a
concrete supported design
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Worker A owns token 41, pauses, and worker B obtains 42. When A resumes, the storage operation 
rejects 41 after accepting 42 instead of allowing A to overwrite B's work.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
// Fencing token must be checked at the real sink:
UPDATE resource SET value=:v, token=:new
 WHERE id=:id AND token < :new;
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Can the external system you call actually enforce a fencing token?
Answer → Only if that system compares tokens atomically at the write boundary. If it cannot,
fencing does not protect the effect; use another authoritative conditional-write mechanism.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Token issuance and resource enforcement require a concrete supported design.
MY ONE-LINE RECAP ______________________________________________________

Q051. What is a saga?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A saga is a durable chain of local business transactions. If later work fails, new
compensation operations may be needed; it is not one big rollback.

Q053. Is compensation the same as rollback?

assumed

Sagas and workflow recovery
Q054. How should a saga handle an unknown
payment result?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A timed-out charge belongs in PAYMENT_UNKNOWN until the payment owner confirms
success or rejection. Do not guess from elapsed time.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Persist an explicit uncertain
state and the stable payment
operation...
➜ Payment times out afterinventory reservation ➜ Cancelling too early can leavea charged but unfulfillableorder
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Payment times out after inventory reservation. The order becomes PAYMENT_UNKNOWN. A later 
confirmed authorization advances it; a definitive rejection releases stock according to policy.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
// Do not turn a timeout into rejection.
state = PAYMENT_UNKNOWN;
reconcile(paymentOperationId);
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How do late callbacks interact with reservation expiry?
Answer → Accept callbacks using stable IDs and versions. If stock expired but money is
confirmed, follow a documented re-reserve/refund path; never blindly confirm stock.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Cancelling too early can leave a charged but unfulfillable order.

Q055. How does a workflow survive coordinator
crashes?

Store workflow progress and intended commands durably so another worker can resume
after a crash.

Persist state, correlation

and pending...

Q056. What is the dual-write problem?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Changing the database and publishing an event are two separate effects. A crash
between them can lose events or announce uncommitted facts.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Writing business data and
publishing a message to a
separate system can...
➜
Order commits but the broker
is unavailable, so no
OrderAccepted event reaches...
➜
A try/catch around two
independent writes is not
atomicity

Order commits but the broker is unavailable, so no OrderAccepted event reaches inventory. Reversing 
the order allows consumers to reserve stock for an order that was never committed.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
BEGIN;
INSERT INTO orders (...);
INSERT INTO outbox (...);
COMMIT;

Where could you crash the process to expose the defect?
Answer → Crash after DB commit but before broker send, and after send but before local commit.
Test whether each history leaves data and messages consistent.

Q057. How does a transactional outbox solve

background relay sends the committed event later.

an event record in the same

by magic

pages.title: Why can an outbox relay publish duplicates?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 12 · Q058/120
Transactional outbox and idempotent consumers
Q058. Why can an outbox relay publish
duplicates?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A relay can send an event, then crash before marking it sent. It sends it again after
restart, so consumers must deduplicate.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
The relay can publish
successfully and crash before
persisting that success
➜
Event e-90 reaches inventory,
but the relay dies before
marking it delivered
➜ A delivered flag is not proof ofglobally exactly-once effects
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Event e-90 reaches inventory, but the relay dies before marking it delivered. Its next run republishes 
e-90; inventory recognizes the same event identity and does not reserve stock again.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
publish(event); // succeeds
crash();        // before marking published
// Recovery can send the same event again.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How would you test the publish-before-mark crash window?
Answer → Force a crash immediately after broker acknowledgement but before delivery marking.
Restart relay and assert exactly one local business effect after duplicate delivery.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  A delivered flag is not proof of globally exactly-once effects.

Q059. How do polling and change-data-capture
outbox relays differ?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Polling reads outbox rows in batches; CDC reads committed changes from the database
log. Both must recover offsets and preserve relevant order.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Polling queries eligible outbox
records and needs indexes,
claims and...
➜ A poller claims a boundedbatch ➜ Parallel workers can changeorder unless the relay andconsumer contract...

A poller claims a bounded batch. A CDC connector observes committed outbox inserts. For either, use an 
aggregate sequence when consumers must detect missing or reordered order transitions.

Answer → If the database log was truncated past the connector offset, automatic replay may be
impossible. Rebuild safely from retained outbox/snapshot records and reconcile missing events.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Parallel workers can change order unless the relay and consumer contract preserve
it.

● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 13 · Q062/120
Events, schemas and Kafka topics
Q062. How should an event envelope be
designed?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
An event envelope carries identity, type, version, aggregate key, timestamp, trace/
correlation context and payload. Keep sensitive fields controlled.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Include a stable event ID,
event type, schema version,
aggregate identity...
➜
OrderAccepted carries eventId,
tenantId, orderId,
aggregateVersion and
accepted...
➜
A timestamp alone is a poor
unique ID or ordering
authority
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
OrderAccepted carries eventId, tenantId, orderId, aggregateVersion and accepted totals. Trace metadata 
helps diagnosis; the event ID supports deduplication and the aggregate version supports ordering 
checks.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
record Envelope(String eventId, String aggregateId,
                int version, String type) {}
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which fields belong in the partition key rather than only the payload?
Answer → Put a stable aggregate or entity ID in the Kafka record key so related records reach
the intended partition and maintain that partition's order.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  A timestamp alone is a poor unique ID or ordering authority.

pages.title: How do you evolve event schemas safely?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 13 · Q063/120
Events, schemas and Kafka topics
Q063. How do you evolve event schemas
safely?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Event consumers may replay old messages long after a producer changes. Add
compatible fields and explicitly plan schema versions.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Test compatible producer and
consumer combinations,
preserve field meaning...
➜
Add an optional
warehouseZone field with a
documented default
➜ An enum addition can failstrict readers
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Add an optional warehouseZone field with a documented default. Changing amount from major currency 
units to minor units under the same field name is a semantic break even when its numeric type stays 
valid.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which compatibility direction is required for replaying old events?
Answer → New readers must handle historical old messages during replay: backward
compatibility. Test both directions when old readers also consume new publications.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  An enum addition can fail strict readers.

pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 13 · Q064/120
Events, schemas and Kafka topics
Q064. What ordering does Kafka guarantee?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Kafka orders records within one partition, not across all partitions. Events for one
aggregate should use a stable partition key.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Kafka orders records within a
partition, not across an entire... ➜ All order o-71 transitions usethe same key and partition ➜ Increasing partition count canchange key placement forfuture records
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
All order o-71 transitions use the same key and partition. If payment results are processed concurrently 
and committed out of order, partition ordering alone has not preserved the order workflow.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
producer.send("orders", orderId, event);
// Aggregate ID becomes the Kafka record key.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How would you migrate partitions without violating aggregate ordering?
Answer → Repartition using a coordinated boundary, drain older ordered records and track
sequence versions; two live partitioning schemes can otherwise reorder one aggregate.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Increasing partition count can change key placement for future records.

pages.title: How should retry topics and dead-letter queues be used?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 13 · Q065/120
Events, schemas and Kafka topics
Q065. How should retry topics and dead-letter
queues be used?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Retry topics delay failures; DLQs isolate messages needing inspection. Both must respect
the business ordering requirement.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Classify failures, bound
attempts, and preserve enough
original identity...
➜
A malformed notification event
reaches a DLQ with its ID and
error classification
➜
A DLQ with no review or
redrive policy is delayed data
loss
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A malformed notification event reaches a DLQ with its ID and error classification. The owner repairs the 
producer or consumer and redrives it using the original identity to avoid another send.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Can later events for the same aggregate safely proceed?
Answer → Only when later events do not depend on the failed event, or a per-aggregate sequence
gate prevents applying them early. Otherwise pause or repair that key.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  A DLQ with no review or redrive policy is delayed data loss.

pages.title: How do producer acknowledgement, consumer offset and business commit differ?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 14 · Q066/120
Delivery semantics, consumer groups and replay
Q066. How do producer acknowledgement,
consumer offset and business commit differ?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Producer acks concern broker writes, committed offsets concern reading progress, and
the business database has its own commit boundary.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
A producer acknowledgement
reports the configured broker
acceptance outcome
➜
The ledger commits an update,
then crashes before
committing the Kafka offset
➜
Receiving a record is not proof
that its business effect is
durable
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
The ledger commits an update, then crashes before committing the Kafka offset. Kafka redelivers and the 
ledger deduplicates the event. Committing the offset first could instead skip an effect after a crash.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
// Commit DB effect first; then record offset progress.
// Duplicate consumption must be harmless.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which crash windows must your consumer test?
Answer → Crash before effect commit, after effect commit before offset, and after offset before
effect. Assert no lost effect or repeated business update.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Receiving a record is not proof that its business effect is durable.
MY ONE-LINE RECAP ______________________________________________________

● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 14 · Q067/120
Delivery semantics, consumer groups and replay
Q067. What does exactly-once mean with
Kafka?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Kafka exactly-once features protect supported Kafka processing/transactions, not any
arbitrary external database write.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Kafka transactions and
appropriately configured
consumers can atomically...
➜
A Kafka processor reads a
record, writes a derived Kafka
record and commits...
➜
Exactly-once is incomplete
unless the included resources
and failure model...
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A Kafka processor reads a record, writes a derived Kafka record and commits offsets in one transaction. 
A separate credit-card charge still needs a payment operation identity and reconciliation.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
UNIQUE (consumer_name, event_id)
// Same transaction as the ledger update.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How would you achieve one durable ledger effect per event?
Answer → Use a unique consumer/event ID and save it together with the ledger update in one
database transaction. Then commit the Kafka offset after success.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Exactly-once is incomplete unless the included resources and failure model are
named.

● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 14 · Q068/120
Delivery semantics, consumer groups and replay
Q068. How do consumer groups and partitions
affect parallelism?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A consumer group divides partitions among active members. More consumers than
partitions do not increase parallel reading of that topic.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Within a traditional consumer-
group assignment, each
partition is assigned...
➜
A topic with six partitions
supports up to six actively
assigned consumers in one...
➜
Newer Kafka consumption
models may differ; identify the
mode in use
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A topic with six partitions supports up to six actively assigned consumers in one such group. Two 
different groups each receive the stream for separate business purposes.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Why might adding consumers fail to reduce lag?
Answer → You may already have one consumer per partition, or be blocked by a hot key, slow
DB, rebalances or expensive messages. Measure per-partition lag and processing time.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Newer Kafka consumption models may differ; identify the mode in use.

pages.title: What is consumer lag, and how should it be interpreted?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 14 · Q069/120
Delivery semantics, consumer groups and replay
Q069. What is consumer lag, and how should it
be interpreted?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Consumer lag counts how far reading is behind writing, but does not explain why the
consumer is slow or whether events are useful.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Lag measures distance
between selected log progress
and consumer progress
➜
A consumer commits early
and hands records to an
executor
➜ Lag is a symptom, not a root-cause diagnosis
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A consumer commits early and hands records to an executor. Offset lag looks low while durable 
notification completion is hours behind. Track oldest outstanding job age and effect completion 
separately.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
// Lag alone is not enough:
monitor(partitionLag, oldestEventAge, errorRate);
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Which measurements distinguish insufficient capacity from poison messages?
Answer → Compare lag by partition, oldest-record age, failures/retries, poison-message IDs,
processing throughput, broker fetch latency and downstream saturation.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Lag is a symptom, not a root-cause diagnosis.
MY ONE-LINE RECAP ______________________________________________________

● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 14 · Q070/120
Delivery semantics, consumer groups and replay
Q070. How can you replay events safely?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
Replay is a deliberate reprocessing of retained facts. Consumers must tolerate duplicates
and control their effect destination.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Choose the replay purpose
and horizon, preserve
identities and isolate side...
➜
Rebuild an order-search
projection in a new index from
retained events
➜
Replay from a retained topic
may still be incomplete after
compaction or...
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
Rebuild an order-search projection in a new index from retained events. Do not resend every historical 
customer email merely because a new group reads the stream.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
How would you verify a rebuilt projection before cutover?
Answer → Rebuild into an isolated projection, compare counts, totals, versions and sampled
records with owner data; switch reads only after checks and a catch-up barrier.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Replay from a retained topic may still be incomplete after compaction or expiry.

pages.title: CQRS, projections and caching Q071. How do CQRS and event sourcing differ?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 15 · Q071/120
CQRS, projections and caching
Q071. How do CQRS and event sourcing differ?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
CQRS separates write and read models. Event sourcing stores events as the primary
history used to rebuild state. They are not the same pattern.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
CQRS separates command
and query models; it does not
require event sourcing...
➜
A normal order table feeds a
denormalized search
projection: CQRS without
event...
➜
An audit table beside current
state is not automatically event
sourcing
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A normal order table feeds a denormalized search projection: CQRS without event sourcing. An event-
sourced order stores accepted and cancelled events as its authoritative history.
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
When would historical state reconstruction justify the extra complexity?
Answer → Choose event sourcing when audit, temporal reconstruction or alternate models justify
storage, schema evolution and replay operations—not only because events are fashionable.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  An audit table beside current state is not automatically event sourcing.
MY ONE-LINE RECAP ______________________________________________________

pages.title: How does a projection handle duplicates and missing events?
pages.fullText:
● MICROSERVICES / HANDWRITTEN INTERVIEW NOTES CH 15 · Q072/120
CQRS, projections and caching
Q072. How does a projection handle duplicates
and missing events?
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
A projection records the last applied sequence, skips duplicates and detects missing
versions before applying dependent deltas.
CONCEPT ➜ REAL EXAMPLE ➜ RISK
Give events stable identities
and, where required, per-
aggregate versions
➜ A balance projection expectsversion 8 but receives 10 ➜ Higher version does notautomatically make a partialupdate safe
EXAMPLE FROM THE ORIGINAL GUIDE
A balance projection expects version 8 but receives 10. Applying a delta would miss version 9, so it 
requests replay or repair. A full-state snapshot may allow a different explicit policy.
IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH i l l u s t r a t i v e
if (version <= currentVersion) return; // duplicate
if (version != currentVersion + 1) repairGap();
INTERVIEWER'S FOLLOW-UP
Where do you store projection version and processed identity?
Answer → Store the projection's aggregate version and any processed event identity in the same
transaction as the projected values; repair gaps through replay.
COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP:  Higher version does not automatically make a partial update safe.
MY ONE-LINE RECAP ______________________________________________________

Q073. How do you query across service-owned
data?

Use API composition for
bounded live joins or a
maintained read model for...
➜ An order page composes oneorder with payment status ➜ Large fan-out joins can makeone slow service dominatelatency
