pages.title: TEMPLATES, SERIALIZATION AND REPOSITORIES How should cached JSON objects evolve?
pages.fullText:
Q023   •   CHAPTER 05 Foundation
TEMPLATES, SERIALIZATION AND REPOSITORIES
How should cached JSON objects evolve?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use an explicit DTO schema, tolerant reading where appropriate and a
versioned namespace for incompatible changes.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Java object → Wire serializer → Versioned key
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Avoid caching JPA entities with lazy proxies or every internal field. Class metadata can
couple values to Java implementation names; restrict accepted types. Test old stored values
against the new application during a rolling upgrade.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Deserializing successfully does not ensure semantic compatibility.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH CHANGE REQUIRES A NEW CACHE NAMESPACE?
Change namespaces when a schema breaks existing readers, changes meaning, or
changes the serialized type/codec. For compatible optional fields, tolerant readers may
allow the same namespace after tested rollouts.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
product:v1:42 -> old DTO
   product:v2:42 -> new DTO

pages.title: TEMPLATES, SERIALIZATION AND REPOSITORIES How do hash serializers differ from value serializers?

Q024   •   CHAPTER 05 Foundation
TEMPLATES, SERIALIZATION AND REPOSITORIES
How do hash serializers differ from value serializers?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A hash uses separate serializers for its field names and field values, in
addition to the key serializer.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Java object → Wire serializer → Versioned key
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Correct string values do not prove hash fields are encoded correctly. Configure the full
template consistently and validate CLI reads. Hash mapping is a separate application
concern when storing object fields.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Updating only valueSerializer does not fix a broken hash encoding.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT BYTES WOULD HGET EXPECT FOR THE FIELD NAME?
HGET sends the serializer-produced bytes for the hash field name, which must match
the bytes used by HSET. A UTF-8 string field serializer expects readable field-name
bytes; Java-serialized names will not match them.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
keySerializer; valueSerializer
   hashKeySerializer; hashValueSerializer

Q025   •   CHAPTER 05 Foundation
TEMPLATES, SERIALIZATION AND REPOSITORIES
What do Redis repositories provide?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They map supported domain objects to Redis structures and maintain
repository-specific indexes and metadata.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Java object → Wire serializer → Versioned key
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Repositories are a separate model from cache annotations. Indexes, TTL and keyspace-
event behavior require review. They do not provide relational joins or general Redis
transaction support. Select them only when their object lifecycle fits the use case.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A repository entity is not automatically a cached SQL entity.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW ARE SECONDARY INDEXES CLEANED AFTER EXPIRATION?
Redis repository index cleanup relies on its keyspace-event and shadow-copy behavior,
and expiry events are not perfectly durable. For correctness, test cleanup and use
reconciliation or explicit index maintenance rather than trusting notifications alone.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
@RedisHash("people")
   class Person { @Id String id; String name; }

pages.fullText:
Q026   •   CHAPTER 06 Foundation
SPRING CACHE ANNOTATIONS
What does @Cacheable do?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It returns a cached value for a hit and invokes the method on a miss
under the selected cache provider's behavior.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Spring proxy → Cache hit or miss → Data source
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Enable caching and select a Redis cache manager deliberately. The annotation expresses
cache behavior, not a data consistency contract. Default concurrency can allow several
callers to load the same missed key.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
@Cacheable is not a distributed mutex.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN TWO PODS MISS AT THE SAME TIME?
Both pods may see a miss and load the database at once. Ordinary @Cacheable does
not provide distributed single-flight: use bounded loader concurrency, accept some
duplication or choose a provider-specific coordination protocol.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
@Cacheable(cacheNames="products", key="#id")
   public Product find(String id) { return database.load(id); }
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 35

Q027   •   CHAPTER 06 Foundation
SPRING CACHE ANNOTATIONS
How is the default Spring cache key chosen?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
No arguments use an empty key; one argument generally uses that
argument; multiple arguments use a composite SimpleKey.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Spring proxy → Cache hit or miss → Data source
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Make important identity dimensions explicit, especially tenant, locale and representation. A
custom key or KeyGenerator can standardize identity. Redis serialization/prefixing then
produces the stored key bytes.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Omitting tenant can leak another tenant's cached result.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH ARGUMENTS TRULY INFLUENCE THE RETURNED VALUE?
Include every dimension that affects the response: tenant, product ID, locale, price tier,
representation version and permission scope when relevant. Never key a private
response only by a public entity ID.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
find("42") -> key based on "42"
   find("tenant-7", "42") -> composite identity

Q028   •   CHAPTER 06 Foundation
SPRING CACHE ANNOTATIONS
How do @CachePut and @CacheEvict differ?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
CachePut invokes the method and stores its result; CacheEvict removes
selected cached data.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Spring proxy → Cache hit or miss → Data source
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Eviction normally occurs after successful method completion unless beforeInvocation is
configured. Method completion is not necessarily outer transaction commit. Review advice
ordering and transaction-aware cache behavior for writes.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A DB rollback can leave an incorrectly updated cache.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW DO YOU ALIGN INVALIDATION WITH COMMIT?
Evict after successful DB commit via transaction-aware cache management or a
transaction synchronization/outbox event. Then test rollback and a late reader, because
post-commit eviction still allows a stale-load race.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
@CachePut(cacheNames="products", key="#result.id")
   public Product update(...) { ... }
   @CacheEvict(cacheNames="products", key="#id")
   public void delete(String id) { ... }

How do condition and unless differ?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Condition decides whether caching applies based on allowed context;
unless can veto storing the returned result after invocation.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Spring proxy → Cache hit or miss → Data source
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The result is available after invocation for supported expressions such as unless. A cache hit
does not invoke the method to recompute a result. Null policy and provider configuration
should match the annotation.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Not every annotation option combines with sync=true.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHEN WOULD SHORT-LIVED NEGATIVE CACHING BE PREFERABLE?
Cache a brief 'not found' result when repeated searches for nonexistent IDs overload
the database and the cost of short staleness is acceptable. Invalidate promptly when a
record is created.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
@Cacheable(cacheNames="products", key="#id",
       condition="#id != null", unless="#result == null")

Why does a self-call bypass @Cacheable?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Default Spring caching uses proxies, and an internal this.method() call
bypasses the proxy advice.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Spring proxy → Cache hit or miss → Data source
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Put the cached operation on a separate injected service when needed. Ensure the caller
receives the Spring-managed proxy and the method is interceptable. The same general
boundary applies to default transaction advice.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Calling new ProductService() also bypasses Spring caching.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD AN INTEGRATION TEST REVEAL PROXY BYPASS?
Inject the cached service into another Spring bean and call it twice; the source should
run once. Contrast with this.find(...) inside the bean and assert that the source runs
again, showing bypass of the proxy.

Outer bean -> cached service proxy -> interception
   this.find(id) -> direct method call -> no default cache advice

What does RedisCacheManager manage?

Cache name → TTL + codec → Reader behavior

automatically change @Cacheable serialization.

       .disableCachingNullValues();

pages.title: REDIS CACHE MANAGER CONFIGURATION Can different caches have different TTLs?
pages.fullText:
Q032   •   CHAPTER 07 Intermediate
REDIS CACHE MANAGER CONFIGURATION
Can different caches have different TTLs?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Yes. Configure named caches separately instead of treating every data
class as equally fresh.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Cache name → TTL + codec → Reader behavior
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Per-entry TTL computation is also available through version-specific cache writer APIs,
introduced in Spring Data Redis 3.2. Match TTL to tolerated staleness and load, with jitter
where the implementation permits it.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A five-minute TTL is not a promise of five-minute fresh data.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW CAN A LATE STALE WRITE EXTEND STALENESS?
A reader may load old DB content before a write, then SET it after the writer commits
and evicts. The late SET resets the key's TTL, extending the time during which an old
value remains visible.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
products: 5 minutes
   exchange-rates: 30 seconds
   feature-config: reviewed policy
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 42

pages.title: REDIS CACHE MANAGER CONFIGURATION How do TTL and time-to-idle differ?
pages.fullText:
Q033   •   CHAPTER 07 Intermediate
REDIS CACHE MANAGER CONFIGURATION
How do TTL and time-to-idle differ?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
TTL ends a fixed lifetime; time-to-idle extends a lifetime on qualifying
access.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Cache name → TTL + codec → Reader behavior
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Spring Redis cache can emulate TTI using GETEX on cache reads, requiring Redis 6.2+
support. All relevant access paths must refresh consistently; a direct GET does not follow
that policy. TTI can retain popular stale data indefinitely without invalidation.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Turning on TTI does not make every Redis client read refresh expiry.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT PREVENTS A HOT STALE VALUE LIVING FOREVER?
Use explicit invalidation/version checks or an absolute maximum age that reads cannot
extend. GETEX-based TTI alone can keep a frequently accessed stale entry alive
indefinitely.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
SET k value EX 60 -> ordinary GET does not refresh deadline
   GETEX k EX 60 -> read and set a new deadline
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 43

pages.fullText:
Q034   •   CHAPTER 07 Intermediate
REDIS CACHE MANAGER CONFIGURATION
What does @Cacheable(sync=true) guarantee?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It requests provider-supported synchronized loading, not a universal
cross-pod single-flight guarantee.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Cache name → TTL + codec → Reader behavior
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The abstraction imposes limitations, such as no unless with sync=true and a single cache.
The exact Redis loader synchronization depends on the selected writer and framework
version. Default nonlocking behavior should not be assumed to serialize misses across
instances.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Verify concurrent cold misses on two pods rather than infer distributed safety.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU MEASURE DUPLICATE LOADS?
Instrument database loader calls by cache key and run simultaneous cold requests on
two pods. Count actual loads, cache misses, duration and peak concurrent loads; do not
infer cross-pod locking from the annotation.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
@Cacheable(cacheNames="products", key="#id", sync=true)
   public Product find(String id) { ... }
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 44

pages.title: REDIS CACHE MANAGER CONFIGURATION What does a locking RedisCacheWriter lock?
pages.fullText:
Q035   •   CHAPTER 07 Intermediate
REDIS CACHE MANAGER CONFIGURATION
What does a locking RedisCacheWriter lock?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
In the 3.5 baseline, it coordinates selected multi-command cache
operations at the cache level, not simply one entry-level business lock.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Cache name → TTL + codec → Reader behavior
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Writer locking can prevent command overlap but trades throughput for coordination. Its
lifetime and scope need review. It is not proof that a database loader, cache entry or
remote payment is protected by a robust business lock.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Cache-writer locking is not a replacement for a business invariant.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT CONTENTION COULD A CACHE-WIDE LOCK CREATE?
A cache-wide writer lock can delay unrelated product keys while one operation clears
or mutates the same named cache. That raises tail latency and limits throughput
compared with narrowly scoped coordination.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Nonlocking writer -> fewer requests
   Locking writer -> extra lock checks and possible waiting
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 45

pages.title: CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION What is cache-aside?
pages.fullText:
Q036   •   CHAPTER 08 Intermediate
CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION
What is cache-aside?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
The application checks cache, loads the source on a miss, then populates
cache.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Database write → Cache invalidation → Stale-write race
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
On writes, update the authoritative store and use a documented invalidation or update
policy. Cache-aside allows miss races and temporary staleness. Define whether stale reads
are acceptable and how they are repaired.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Redis does not automatically notice a SQL update.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH WRITES BYPASS YOUR INVALIDATION PATH?
Admin scripts, batch jobs, SQL migrations, direct repository writes and other services
can bypass application invalidation. List every writer to the authoritative data and define
a shared notification or reconciliation path.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
GET product:42 -> miss -> DB read -> SET with TTL

pages.title: CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION Why prefer DB commit before cache eviction?
pages.fullText:
Q037   •   CHAPTER 08 Intermediate
CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION
Why prefer DB commit before cache eviction?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It avoids readers immediately repopulating cache from an uncommitted
old database state, but it does not remove every race.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Database write → Cache invalidation → Stale-write race
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A reader that loaded old data before commit can still write that data after eviction.
Transaction-aware eviction helps align with commit, while version checks, bounded TTL or
durable invalidation/reconciliation address remaining races.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Delete-after-commit alone is not strict consistency.
06   FOLLOW-UP: DRAW THE LATE STALE-LOADER INTERLEAVING.
Reader reads old DB value; writer updates DB and commits; writer evicts cache; reader
finally SETs the old value with a fresh TTL. A version guard, source read or invalidation
repair is needed to reject or bound it.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
DB update -> commit -> evict product:42
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 48

pages.title: •   CHAPTER 08 Intermediate CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION
pages.fullText:
Q038   •   CHAPTER 08 Intermediate
CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION
What are read-through, write-through and write-
behind?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They describe who loads values and when writes reach the authoritative
backing store.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Database write → Cache invalidation → Stale-write race
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
These are architecture patterns, not all automatic RedisCacheManager capabilities. Write-
behind needs durable buffering, ordering and failure recovery. A plain SET in Redis plus
future database work is not automatically safe.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Delayed writes can disappear if the buffer is lost.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHEN IS WRITE-BEHIND UNACCEPTABLE?
Write-behind is unacceptable when acknowledging an order, payment or ledger update
before its only durable copy is committed. A process crash can lose queued writes, so
use a durable queue/outbox or synchronous commit.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Read-through: cache layer loads miss
   Write-through: write also reaches backing store synchronously
   Write-behind: backing write delayed
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 49

pages.title: CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION What is negative caching?
pages.fullText:
Q039   •   CHAPTER 08 Intermediate
CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION
What is negative caching?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It briefly caches a known absence or rejection to avoid repeated
expensive source lookups.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Database write → Cache invalidation → Stale-write race
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Distinguish absent data from a timeout or database outage. Keep a short lifetime and evict
when the item is created. A null-caching strategy must match provider behavior and
distinguish a miss from a stored negative value.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Caching infrastructure failures as absence can hide real data.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU INVALIDATE A PREVIOUSLY ABSENT PRODUCT?
When creating a product, evict the previous negative entry for its ID or publish a
reliable invalidation. Otherwise callers may keep receiving 'not found' until the short
negative TTL expires.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
product:missing:42 -> ABSENT marker, TTL=10 seconds

pages.title: CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION Can TTL guarantee fresh reads?
pages.fullText:
Q040   •   CHAPTER 08 Intermediate
CACHE CONSISTENCY AND INVALIDATION
Can TTL guarantee fresh reads?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
No. TTL bounds the age of an entry from its expiry-setting operation, not
freshness relative to every concurrent source update.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Database write → Cache invalidation → Stale-write race
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A delayed write can start a fresh TTL for old data. Exact consistency may require bypassing
cache for critical reads or enforcing a versioned protocol with the authoritative store. Use
TTL as one recovery bound, not a universal invariant.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Adding expiry does not solve all stale-write races.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH ENDPOINT SHOULD READ DIRECTLY FROM THE SOURCE?
Read directly from the authoritative source for strict balances, authorization checks,
scarce inventory decisions and other invariants that cannot tolerate stale data. Cache
only a permitted projection or strictly versioned result.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Old DB result loaded at T0
   Written into cache at T2 with TTL 60 seconds
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 51

pages.title: STAMPEDES, PENETRATION AND HOT KEYS What is a cache stampede?
pages.fullText:
Q041   •   CHAPTER 09 Intermediate
STAMPEDES, PENETRATION AND HOT KEYS
What is a cache stampede?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Many requests miss the same key together and all load the backing
service.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Cold miss → Bounded loader → Fallback policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use bounded single-flight, carefully designed distributed loading coordination, refresh-
ahead or stale-while-revalidate where valid. Add deadlines and cap concurrent loaders.
Failure handling must not create endless waiting on a lost loader.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
An unbounded lock wait just converts DB overload into request pileup.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW DOES THE SECOND CALLER BEHAVE WHEN THE LOADER FAILS?
If the shared loader fails, the second caller should receive a controlled failure or stale
fallback after a bounded wait, not block forever. Clear an in-flight marker reliably and
allow retry under a concurrency budget.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Hot key expires -> 1000 requests -> 1000 DB loads
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 53

pages.fullText:
Q042   •   CHAPTER 09 Intermediate
STAMPEDES, PENETRATION AND HOT KEYS
What is a cache avalanche?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Many keys or an entire cache layer become unavailable together,
creating a broad source-load surge.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Cold miss → Bounded loader → Fallback policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use expiry jitter, staged warming and admission limits. A Redis outage also requires a
fallback policy that respects database capacity. Independent key failures and broad
dependency failure need different mitigation.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Blind fallback for every request can take down the database.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT IS YOUR MAXIMUM PERMITTED FALLBACK CONCURRENCY?
Size fallback concurrency from database connection capacity and measured per-query
latency, reserving headroom for normal traffic. Enforce the limit with a semaphore/
bulkhead and return overload responses once it is reached.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
All product entries written with identical 300-second expiry

pages.fullText:
Q043   •   CHAPTER 09 Intermediate
STAMPEDES, PENETRATION AND HOT KEYS
What is cache penetration?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Repeated requests for nonexistent data bypass useful cache hits and
repeatedly reach the source.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Cold miss → Bounded loader → Fallback policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Validate identifiers, rate-limit abuse and consider negative caching. A Bloom filter can reject
definite nonmembers, but false positives and update lifecycle must be managed; Bloom
support may require server features/modules.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A probabilistic filter must not falsely reject valid new items through stale updates.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW DO YOU POPULATE IT BEFORE ENABLING IT?
Warm trusted keys via a bounded batch from authoritative data, or use a Bloom filter
with a safe misses policy. Refresh the structure and handle false positives; never treat a
filter as an authorization control.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Requests for random invalid productIds -> repeated DB misses

pages.fullText:
Q044   •   CHAPTER 09 Intermediate
STAMPEDES, PENETRATION AND HOT KEYS
What is a hot key and why is Cluster not enough?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A key receiving disproportionate traffic still maps to one slot/primary, so
sharding other keys does not split its command work.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Cold miss → Bounded loader → Fallback policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Reduce requests with local caching where staleness permits, replicate read-only derived
data carefully, or redesign the aggregate. Read replicas introduce consistency tradeoffs.
Measure key distribution without generating excessive metric labels.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Adding shards does not automatically distribute one key.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT CORRECTNESS CHANGES IF A COUNTER IS SPLIT?
Splitting one logical counter can remove atomic admission and permit an overshoot
until partial counts are merged. Use sharding only when approximate totals or a
deliberate coordination protocol are acceptable.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
90% of GETs -> sale:top-product -> one shard

pages.title: STAMPEDES, PENETRATION AND HOT KEYS When is stale-while-revalidate useful?
pages.fullText:
Q045   •   CHAPTER 09 Intermediate
STAMPEDES, PENETRATION AND HOT KEYS
When is stale-while-revalidate useful?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It serves a permitted stale value temporarily while a bounded refresh
updates it asynchronously.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Cold miss → Bounded loader → Fallback policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Keep soft and hard expiry explicit and ensure refresh coordination. This is application logic,
not automatic behavior of plain @Cacheable. It fits read data with an accepted staleness
budget and is unsuitable for arbitrary authorization or money decisions.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Stale data needs an agreed maximum age.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT HAPPENS IF REFRESH KEEPS FAILING?
Serve only a bounded stale period; record refresh failures, retry with backoff and stop
using data past maximum age. For sensitive data, fail closed or read the source instead
of using stale content.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Soft deadline passed -> serve old catalog + trigger one refresh
   Hard deadline passed -> reviewed miss/failure behavior
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 57

pages.title: TRANSACTIONS, PIPELINES AND SCRIPTS What does Redis pipelining do?
pages.fullText:
Q046   •   CHAPTER 10 Intermediate
TRANSACTIONS, PIPELINES AND SCRIPTS
What does Redis pipelining do?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It batches command transmission and response handling to reduce
network round trips; it does not make commands atomic.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Command sequence → Atomic boundary → Crash outcome
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use bounded batches to avoid excessive response memory and latency. Other clients can
interleave commands. Spring executePipelined collects results; serialization and connection
usage need review. A timeout can leave uncertain command outcomes.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A pipeline is not a transaction.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU PROVE INTERLEAVING CAN STILL HAPPEN?
Run another client's SET while the pipeline issues multiple reads; the replies can reflect
different instants. Use tracing/barriers or a controlled concurrent test; pipelining
reduces round trips, not isolation.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Pipeline: GET a, GET b, GET c -> batched round trip

pages.title: TRANSACTIONS, PIPELINES AND SCRIPTS What do MULTI and EXEC guarantee?
pages.fullText:
Q047   •   CHAPTER 10 Intermediate
TRANSACTIONS, PIPELINES AND SCRIPTS
What do MULTI and EXEC guarantee?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They queue commands and execute the queued sequence without other
clients interleaving, but do not provide general rollback of runtime errors.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Command sequence → Atomic boundary → Crash outcome
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Errors detected during queuing can abort the transaction. A runtime error in one queued
command does not undo successfully executed commands. Reads inside the queue cannot
drive immediate conditional Java logic using their eventual values.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Redis transactions are not SQL rollback semantics.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU AVOID PARTIAL LOGICAL UPDATES FROM BAD TYPES?
Validate types and values before writing, preferably within a short Lua script that checks
all preconditions first. MULTI/EXEC executes queued commands in order but a runtime
command error does not roll back earlier commands.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
SET wrongType not-an-integer
   MULTI
   SET a 1
   INCR wrongType
   EXEC
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 60

pages.title: TRANSACTIONS, PIPELINES AND SCRIPTS What is WATCH used for?
pages.fullText:
Q048   •   CHAPTER 10 Intermediate
TRANSACTIONS, PIPELINES AND SCRIPTS
What is WATCH used for?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
WATCH provides optimistic conflict detection: EXEC aborts if watched
keys changed before execution.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Command sequence → Atomic boundary → Crash outcome
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use one connection for the sequence and bounded retries after conflicts. Expiration
behavior and supported commands should be checked for the server version. Avoid an
unbounded spin loop under contention.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
WATCH does not lock the key against other writers.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHEN WOULD LUA BE SIMPLER?
Lua is simpler for a small atomic check-and-update such as increment + first-expiry or
compare-token + delete. WATCH works for optimistic, client-side read/compute/update
transactions that can retry on conflicts.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
WATCH stock:42
   GET stock:42
   MULTI; SET stock:42 9; EXEC
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 61

pages.fullText:
Q049   •   CHAPTER 10 Intermediate
TRANSACTIONS, PIPELINES AND SCRIPTS
Why use Lua scripts for Redis operations?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A script can combine read/check/write logic atomically on Redis without
application round trips between steps.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Command sequence → Atomic boundary → Crash outcome
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Scripts must be short, bounded and declare accessed keys appropriately. They block
competing command execution while running and do not roll back all prior writes after a
runtime error. Validate inputs/types before mutation. In Cluster, required keys normally
share a slot.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Atomic execution is not unlimited safe computation.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A SCRIPT LOOPS FOR TOO LONG?
A long-running script blocks other server commands and increases latency. Keep
scripts bounded by data size, monitor slowlog/latency, and never scan an unbounded
keyspace inside one script.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
if GET lock equals token then DEL lock end
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 62

pages.title: TRANSACTIONS, PIPELINES AND SCRIPTS How does Spring Data support Redis transactions?
pages.fullText:
Q050   •   CHAPTER 10 Intermediate
TRANSACTIONS, PIPELINES AND SCRIPTS
How does Spring Data support Redis transactions?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use a same-connection SessionCallback for explicit MULTI/EXEC;
optional template transaction support can bind connections to Spring
transactions.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Command sequence → Atomic boundary → Crash outcome
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Ordinary template calls may not share the required connection unless coordinated.
Enabling transaction support is a configuration choice. Redis and SQL still do not become
one general atomic distributed transaction merely because Spring synchronizes them.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
@Transactional does not automatically make every template call transactional.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU RECOVER SQL COMMIT FOLLOWED BY REDIS FAILURE?
Treat the SQL commit as authoritative and use a durable outbox/change event to retry
Redis invalidation or rebuild. This is reconciliation across two systems; @Transactional
alone cannot atomically commit SQL and Redis.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
template.execute(new SessionCallback<>() { /* MULTI, queued ops, EXEC */ });
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 63

pages.title: DISTRIBUTED LOCKS AND FENCING How do you acquire a basic Redis lease safely?
pages.fullText:
Q051   •   CHAPTER 11 Intermediate
DISTRIBUTED LOCKS AND FENCING
How do you acquire a basic Redis lease safely?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use one conditional SET with a unique ownership token and an expiry.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Lease acquired → Lease expiry → Resource fencing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
NX makes acquisition conditional and PX sets the lease in the same operation. The token
distinguishes owners. This is a basic single-Redis lease with assumptions, not a proof of
mutual exclusion through every failover or pause.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
SETNX followed later by EXPIRE has a crash gap.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT IF THE HOLDER PAUSES LONGER THAN TEN SECONDS?
After the TTL expires, another worker may obtain the lease while the paused holder
resumes. The old holder must not be allowed to perform an external protected effect;
use fencing/version checks at that resource.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
SET lock:job:42 unique-token NX PX 10000
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 65

pages.fullText:
Q052   •   CHAPTER 11 Intermediate
DISTRIBUTED LOCKS AND FENCING
Why must release compare the ownership token?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A previous holder must not delete a lease now owned by a different caller.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Lease acquired → Lease expiry → Resource fencing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use an atomic compare-and-delete script or a server-version-supported equivalent. GET
followed by DEL has its own race. The token helps safe release but does not stop a paused
holder from modifying an external resource.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Token-safe unlock is not fencing.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU PROTECT THE DATABASE FROM STALE A?
Give each lease acquisition a monotonic fencing number and have the database reject
a write with an older number. Compare-and-delete protects B's Redis key; only
resource-side enforcement blocks stale A's business write.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
A's lease expires -> B acquires
   A resumes -> unconditional DEL would remove B's lease
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 66

pages.title: DISTRIBUTED LOCKS AND FENCING What is a fencing token?
pages.fullText:
Q053   •   CHAPTER 11 Intermediate
DISTRIBUTED LOCKS AND FENCING
What is a fencing token?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It is an increasing generation attached to work that the protected
resource uses to reject stale holders.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Lease acquired → Lease expiry → Resource fencing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The downstream resource must enforce token order atomically. Token allocation and
survival through failover must meet the required guarantee; an asynchronously replicated
INCR is not automatically a failover-proof fencing service.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Generating a number without checking it at the resource does nothing.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT IF THE TOKEN ALLOCATOR LOSES ITS LATEST VALUE?
If the allocator can reset to a previous value after failover, stale holders may appear
new. Allocate tokens using a durable monotonic authority or enforce an equivalent
authoritative row/version constraint.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
A token=10 pauses; B token=11 writes
   DB rejects later write carrying token=10

pages.title: DISTRIBUTED LOCKS AND FENCING Does automatic lease renewal solve every lock problem?
pages.fullText:
Q054   •   CHAPTER 11 Intermediate
DISTRIBUTED LOCKS AND FENCING
Does automatic lease renewal solve every lock problem?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
No. Renewal reduces accidental expiry during active work but cannot
eliminate long pauses, lost connectivity or stale external effects.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Lease acquired → Lease expiry → Resource fencing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Renew only if the ownership token still matches. Bound work duration and detect ownership
loss, while acknowledging a paused process may resume too late to stop safely. Robust
business invariants remain necessary.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A watchdog is not a proof of exactly-once processing.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU TEST A LONG GC PAUSE?
Pause a worker beyond its lease TTL using a test barrier, then let a second worker
acquire and write. Resume the old worker; assert the downstream resource rejects its
stale token even if auto-renew was configured.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Heartbeat renew fails -> lease can expire
   Worker must stop or have its writes fenced
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 68

Q055   •   CHAPTER 11 Intermediate
DISTRIBUTED LOCKS AND FENCING
What is the failover risk with a single replicated Redis
lock?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
An acknowledged lock may not reach the replica before failover, allowing
another client to acquire it on the new primary.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Lease acquired → Lease expiry → Resource fencing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Redis replication is normally asynchronous. Alternatives require explicit safety assumptions,
resource fencing or a stronger coordination system. Do not claim Sentinel or Redis Cluster
alone makes this lease linearizable.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
High availability and lock safety are different properties.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH INVARIANT CAN A DATABASE CONSTRAINT ENFORCE INSTEAD?
A database unique constraint or conditional row update can enforce one reservation
per item or nonnegative stock. Redis lease ownership alone cannot guarantee those
invariants across failover and pauses.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
A acquires on primary -> primary fails before replication
   Replica promoted -> B sees no lease and acquires

pages.fullText:
Q056   •   CHAPTER 12 Intermediate
RATE LIMITING AND IDEMPOTENCY
How does a fixed-window rate limiter work?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It counts requests in a time bucket and permits requests up to a
threshold.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Incoming request → Atomic admission → Duplicate control
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Counter creation and expiry should follow one atomic policy. Fixed windows allow a burst
around boundaries, such as 100 requests at the end and 100 at the start. Decide which
events count and return retry information.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Separate INCR/EXPIRE can create immortal counters.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHEN IS A BOUNDARY BURST UNACCEPTABLE?
A two-window boundary burst may admit nearly twice the nominal rate in a short real
interval. Use a sliding window or token bucket when that burst would overwhelm the
protected service or break a policy.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Key: limit:user-42:minute-123
   INCR; allow if count <= 100

How does a sliding-window limiter differ?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It evaluates recent activity across a moving interval rather than resetting
at one bucket boundary.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Incoming request → Atomic admission → Duplicate control
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Combine prune/count/admission in one script. Unique members prevent requests sharing a
timestamp from overwriting each other. Bound key growth and expiry. More precise
algorithms require more work and state than fixed windows.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Millisecond timestamp alone may not be a unique member.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU LIMIT SCRIPT COST?
Limit tracked events per identity, remove obsolete members each call, and cap Lua
work/time. For very high volume, consider a bounded-memory approximation or token
bucket instead of unbounded sorted sets.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Sorted set: requestId -> timestamp
   Remove older than window; count; conditionally add

pages.title: RATE LIMITING AND IDEMPOTENCY What is a token bucket?
pages.fullText:
Q058   •   CHAPTER 12 Intermediate
RATE LIMITING AND IDEMPOTENCY
What is a token bucket?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It refills a bounded token balance over time and consumes tokens for
admitted work, allowing a controlled burst.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Incoming request → Atomic admission → Duplicate control
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Store balance and last-refill time consistently, and define time source and precision. An
atomic script avoids concurrent overspending. Distinguish per-user limits from per-tenant
and global resource admission.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A user-supplied identity can be rotated to evade the limit.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT KEY PROTECTS A SHARED DOWNSTREAM CAPACITY?
Use a key scoped to the actual shared resource, such as provider:payment-api or
tenant+provider if isolation is required. A per-pod key does not protect aggregate
downstream capacity.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Capacity=20 tokens; refill=5 tokens/second
   Request cost=1 token

pages.title: RATE LIMITING AND IDEMPOTENCY Should a rate limiter fail open or fail closed?
pages.fullText:
Q059   •   CHAPTER 12 Intermediate
RATE LIMITING AND IDEMPOTENCY
Should a rate limiter fail open or fail closed?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Choose explicitly from abuse risk, availability and business impact; there
is no universally correct policy.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Incoming request → Atomic admission → Duplicate control
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A Redis error must not silently become a cache miss or a fresh zero counter without
analysis. Local emergency limits may preserve partial protection but differ across pods.
Monitor degraded-mode entry and exit.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Fail-open can amplify the very overload Redis was controlling.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH ENDPOINT NEEDS A DIFFERENT POLICY?
Reject or tightly limit calls when Redis fails for login attempts, payment protection or
abuse-sensitive endpoints; permit bounded fallback for noncritical browsing. Define
different policies per endpoint and measure failure impact.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Catalog reads: bounded local fallback may be acceptable
   Payment attempts: reviewed stricter admission policy
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 74

pages.title: RATE LIMITING AND IDEMPOTENCY Can SET NX with a TTL guarantee one business effect?
pages.fullText:
Q060   •   CHAPTER 12 Intermediate
RATE LIMITING AND IDEMPOTENCY
Can SET NX with a TTL guarantee one business effect?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
No. A deduplication marker and a separate business effect leave a crash
gap, and expiry permits future repeats.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Incoming request → Atomic admission → Duplicate control
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use a durable unique constraint and effect transaction for local DB work, or the external
provider's idempotency contract. Redis can assist coordination but should not promise
atomicity with an unrelated store.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A cache-only dedup flag is weak protection for payments.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW LONG MUST AN IDEMPOTENCY RECORD SURVIVE REPLAY?
Keep the request ID/result at least as long as any possible client retry, queue replay
and delayed duplicate. Make the authoritative business effect idempotent too, since
Redis TTL expiry may outlive in-flight work.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Set marker -> crash before effect: skipped work
   Effect -> crash before marker: duplicate work
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 75

pages.title: REDIS CLUSTER How does Redis Cluster distribute keys?
pages.fullText:
Q061   •   CHAPTER 13 Intermediate
REDIS CLUSTER
How does Redis Cluster distribute keys?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Redis Cluster maps keys to 16384 hash slots distributed among primaries.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Key hash slot → Primary + replica → Client routing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Cluster-aware clients discover topology and route commands. Slots are not separate
physical databases or a count of nodes. Adding nodes requires slot movement; replicas
support availability rather than independent primary write shards.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Six nodes do not automatically mean six write primaries.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD THREE PRIMARIES AND THREE REPLICAS BE ARRANGED?
Use three primary nodes covering the 16,384 hash slots and one replica per primary,
placed on different failure domains where possible. Each replica follows one primary;
plan promotion and capacity during failures.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
slot = CRC16(relevant key bytes) modulo 16384
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 77

pages.title: REDIS CLUSTER What do hash tags do?
pages.fullText:
Q062   •   CHAPTER 13 Intermediate
REDIS CLUSTER
What do hash tags do?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A valid {...} substring controls slot hashing so related keys can be
colocated.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Key hash slot → Primary + replica → Client routing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
These keys share a slot, enabling suitable multi-key operations. Key-tag syntax follows Redis
rules, so empty or multiple brace patterns need care. Putting every key under one common
tag defeats distribution.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Tenant-wide colocation can create a hot slot.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH KEYS TRULY NEED ATOMIC MULTI-KEY ACCESS?
Only keys that must be modified atomically in one multi-key command/script should
share a hash tag, such as wallet:{account42}:balance and wallet:{account42}:holds. Do
not force unrelated tenants into one hot slot.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
order:{42}:state
   order:{42}:lock
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 78

pages.fullText:
Q063   •   CHAPTER 13 Intermediate
REDIS CLUSTER
Why do CROSSSLOT errors occur?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
The operation requires keys to share a slot but the supplied keys map to
different slots.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Key hash slot → Primary + replica → Client routing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use deliberate hash tags or redesign the operation. Some client APIs decompose
operations into separate node commands, but that does not preserve server-side cross-key
atomicity. Check the chosen command and client implementation.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A client-side multiGet convenience does not imply a global transaction.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU PRESERVE A CROSS-AGGREGATE INVARIANT?
Keep cross-aggregate invariants in a transactional authoritative store or use an explicit
saga/reservation protocol. Cluster key colocation alone cannot create atomicity across
independent owners or failure domains.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
MULTI/script with order:42 and balance:7 -> possible CROSSSLOT

pages.title: REDIS CLUSTER How do MOVED and ASK differ?
pages.fullText:
Q064   •   CHAPTER 13 Intermediate
REDIS CLUSTER
How do MOVED and ASK differ?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
MOVED indicates the slot's routing owner; ASK is a temporary redirection
used during migration with special handling.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Key hash slot → Primary + replica → Client routing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A cluster-aware driver handles redirects. Topology refresh helps after resharding/failover,
but network reachability to advertised nodes remains essential. A standalone client pointed
at one cluster node is insufficient.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Retrying only against the original node can loop or fail.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT ADDRESSES MUST AN APPLICATION POD REACH?
Pods must reach every advertised Cluster node address/port returned by MOVED or
ASK, not only the initial bootstrap endpoint. Test DNS, TLS and routing during
resharding and failover.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
MOVED -> update routing knowledge
   ASK -> redirected operation with ASKING as required

pages.fullText:
Q065   •   CHAPTER 13 Intermediate
REDIS CLUSTER
How do you configure Boot for a Redis Cluster?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Configure cluster nodes and driver refresh policy appropriate to the
deployment instead of standalone-only host assumptions.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Key hash slot → Primary + replica → Client routing
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Seed nodes bootstrap discovery; the client then reaches relevant advertised nodes. Review
redirect limits, TLS names, credentials and periodic/adaptive refresh. Cluster supports
database zero rather than SELECT-based numbered DB isolation.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A reachable seed does not prove every slot owner is reachable.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU TEST A RESHARDING ROLLOUT?
Run a controlled slot migration during traffic while tracking MOVED/ASK handling, error
rates and latency. Verify that keys, scripts and client topology refresh recover without
duplicate business effects.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
spring.data.redis.cluster.nodes=node1:6379,node2:6379,node3:6379
   spring.data.redis.lettuce.cluster.refresh.adaptive=true
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 81

pages.title: REPLICATION, SENTINEL AND DURABILITY What does Redis replication provide?
pages.fullText:
Q066   •   CHAPTER 14 Advanced
REPLICATION, SENTINEL AND DURABILITY
What does Redis replication provide?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It copies a primary's data to replicas, normally asynchronously, for
availability and optional read scaling.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Primary write → Replication → Failover window
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A replica read can be stale. Failover can lose recent acknowledged writes that never
reached the promoted replica. Choose read routes and acceptable loss explicitly for
sessions, counters and authoritative state.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Replication is not automatically synchronous durability.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH DATA MUST NEVER BE SERVED FROM A STALE REPLICA?
Do not serve balances, payment status or authorization changes from a replica when
staleness is unacceptable. Replica reads are eventually consistent and need an explicit
permitted-staleness policy.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Primary acknowledges write -> replica may catch up afterward

pages.title: REPLICATION, SENTINEL AND DURABILITY What does Sentinel do?
pages.fullText:
Q067   •   CHAPTER 14 Advanced
REPLICATION, SENTINEL AND DURABILITY
What does Sentinel do?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Sentinel monitors a nonclustered primary/replica deployment and
coordinates discovery and automatic failover.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Primary write → Replication → Failover window
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Sentinel does not shard the keyspace. Configure the logical master name, Sentinel
addresses and credentials correctly. Quorum and failover authorization involve different
requirements; multiple independent failure domains matter.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
One Sentinel is not a robust high-availability design.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD CLIENTS RECOVER AFTER PROMOTION?
The Sentinel-aware client discovers the new master and reconnects/retries within
deadlines. Test writes during promotion and reconcile uncertain outcomes; in-flight
commands are not magically atomic across failover.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Sentinel quorum -> detect failure -> promote replica
   Application client -> discover current primary

pages.title: REPLICATION, SENTINEL AND DURABILITY How do Sentinel and Cluster differ?
pages.fullText:
Q068   •   CHAPTER 14 Advanced
REPLICATION, SENTINEL AND DURABILITY
How do Sentinel and Cluster differ?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Sentinel provides failover for a primary-replica topology; Cluster
combines sharding with its own failover mechanisms.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Primary write → Replication → Failover window
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The choice also depends on managed-service capabilities and consistency needs. Cluster
adds multi-key restrictions and topology-aware routing. Neither removes asynchronous
replication loss windows automatically.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Sentinel is not the coordinator Redis Cluster requires.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH APPLICATION COMMANDS COMPLICATE A CLUSTER MIGRATION?
Cross-slot Lua/MULTI operations, broad multi-key commands, key scanning, server-side
moves and connection routing need review for Cluster. Sentinel provides failover for a
nonsharded primary, not distributed hash slots.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Need more total write/memory capacity -> evaluate Cluster
   Need HA for one primary dataset -> evaluate Sentinel

Q069   •   CHAPTER 14 Advanced
REPLICATION, SENTINEL AND DURABILITY
How do RDB and AOF persistence differ?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
RDB stores snapshots; AOF records write operations for replay under its
configured persistence policy.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Primary write → Replication → Failover window
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Snapshot intervals, fsync behavior, rewrite and recovery configuration determine durability
and resource cost. An every-second setting is not an absolute no-loss guarantee under all
failures. Test backup restore, not only file creation.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Persistence on one disk is not a backup strategy.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT IS YOUR RECOVERY-POINT OBJECTIVE?
Set an RPO based on the worst business loss you can tolerate and test snapshots, AOF
policy, replication and restore time against it. State that acknowledged writes may still
be lost under some crash/failover patterns.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
RDB -> snapshot recovery point
   AOF appendfsync everysec -> typical small recent-loss window

Q070   •   CHAPTER 14 Advanced
REPLICATION, SENTINEL AND DURABILITY
Does WAIT guarantee strong consistency or no data
loss?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
No. WAIT can request acknowledgment from replicas for prior writes, but
does not turn Redis into a strongly consistent system.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Primary write → Replication → Failover window
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The returned count indicates observed replication acknowledgments, not a universal
persistence or failover guarantee. It must apply to the relevant connection/write sequence.
Review persistence acknowledgment options separately for supported server versions.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Waiting for one replica is not a proof every failure preserves the write.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT HAPPENS IF WAIT TIMES OUT AFTER THE WRITE SUCCEEDED?
The write may already exist even if WAIT times out. Do not blindly resend a non-
idempotent increment; read back state or retry with a stable operation ID and an
authoritative deduplication protocol.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Write -> WAIT 1 1000 -> inspect returned replica count
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 87
pages.shortAnswer:
No. WAIT can request acknowledgment from replicas for prior writes, but
does not turn Redis into a strongly consistent system.
pages.visualFlow:
Primary write → Replication → Failover window
04   HOW IT WORKS,
pages.explanation:
The returned count indicates observed replication acknowledgments, not a universal
persistence or failover guarantee. It must apply to the relevant connection/write sequence.
Review persistence acknowledgment options separately for supported server versions.
05
pages.pitfall: Waiting for one replica is not a proof every failure preserves the write.
pages.followup:
WHAT HAPPENS IF WAIT TIMES OUT AFTER THE WRITE SUCCEEDED?
The write may already exist even if WAIT times out. Do not blindly resend a non-
idempotent increment; read back state or retry with a stable operation ID and an
authoritative deduplication protocol.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Write -> WAIT 1 1000 -> inspect returned replica count

pages.fullText:
Q071   •   CHAPTER 15 Advanced
MEMORY, EVICTION AND PERFORMANCE
How do expiration and eviction differ?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Expiration removes logically expired keys; eviction removes keys under
configured memory pressure policy.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Memory pressure → Eviction / expiry → Application impact
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use memory policies consistent with the dataset. A cache can tolerate eviction; a lock,
session or authoritative record may not. Separate workloads when policy conflict matters.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
TTL is not a minimum guaranteed residency period.
06   FOLLOW-UP: SHOULD LOCK KEYS SHARE AN ALLKEYS-LRU CACHE?
No. Critical lease/lock state should not share a memory pool using allkeys eviction,
because the lock could disappear before TTL. Separate instances or use a policy/
capacity model that does not evict live coordination keys.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
TTL remaining=60 seconds
   maxmemory pressure -> key can still be evicted
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 89

pages.title: MEMORY, EVICTION AND PERFORMANCE How do allkeys, volatile and noeviction policies differ?
pages.fullText:
Q072   •   CHAPTER 15 Advanced
MEMORY, EVICTION AND PERFORMANCE
How do allkeys, volatile and noeviction policies differ?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Allkeys policies can choose any eligible key; volatile policies restrict
candidates to expiring keys; noeviction rejects applicable writes when
memory is exhausted.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Memory pressure → Eviction / expiry → Application impact
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
LRU/LFU selection is approximate rather than a perfect global ranking. A volatile policy
with no suitable candidates cannot simply free arbitrary permanent keys. Monitor write
errors as well as eviction counts.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
noeviction does not mean Redis has unlimited memory.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT HAPPENS TO A NEW SET AT THE LIMIT?
Under noeviction, a memory-increasing SET can fail with an OOM error; with eviction
policies, eligible keys may be removed. Test application handling and never rely on
eviction to preserve a critical invariant.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
allkeys-lru; volatile-lru; allkeys-lfu; noeviction
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 90

pages.title: MEMORY, EVICTION AND PERFORMANCE Why are big keys dangerous?
pages.fullText:
Q073   •   CHAPTER 15 Advanced
MEMORY, EVICTION AND PERFORMANCE
Why are big keys dangerous?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Large values or collections can increase network cost, command latency,
memory use and deletion/recovery work.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Memory pressure → Eviction / expiry → Application impact
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Prefer bounded access and pagination-like iteration where appropriate. Measure payload
size and collection cardinality. UNLINK can move memory freeing away from the
immediate delete path, but it does not make huge reads inexpensive.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
One key can be too large even with a low total key count.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW DO YOU IDENTIFY IT SAFELY?
Use SCAN to find candidate keys gradually and MEMORY USAGE or sampled size tools
with strict rate limits. Avoid dumping huge values or running KEYS in production;
correlate with slow commands and bandwidth.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
One hash with millions of fields -> HGETALL returns a huge response

pages.title: MEMORY, EVICTION AND PERFORMANCE Why prefer SCAN to KEYS for production inspection?
pages.fullText:
Q074   •   CHAPTER 15 Advanced
MEMORY, EVICTION AND PERFORMANCE
Why prefer SCAN to KEYS for production inspection?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
KEYS traverses the keyspace in one blocking operation; SCAN
incrementally iterates it.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Memory pressure → Eviction / expiry → Application impact
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
COUNT is a hint, not an exact result size. A live scan can return duplicates and is not a
snapshot. In Cluster, scan the required node scope with a cluster-aware strategy. Bound
cleanup batches and tolerate changing data.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
One SCAN call does not enumerate the entire database.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU MAKE CLEANUP SAFE UNDER CONCURRENT WRITES?
Use cursor-based SCAN with throttling and narrow prefixes, verify each key's expected
version before deletion, and tolerate duplicates/new writes. For business data, prefer a
versioned namespace switch over live broad deletion.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
SCAN 0 MATCH shop:prod:* COUNT 1000
   Repeat using returned cursor until cursor=0
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 92

pages.title: MEMORY, EVICTION AND PERFORMANCE How do you diagnose Redis latency?
pages.fullText:
Q075   •   CHAPTER 15 Advanced
MEMORY, EVICTION AND PERFORMANCE
How do you diagnose Redis latency?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Correlate command cost, server CPU/memory, network, payloads,
connection waits, persistence and client timeouts.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Memory pressure → Eviction / expiry → Application impact
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
SLOWLOG measures command execution time rather than all network wait. Use command
statistics and approved latency tooling alongside application metrics. A long script or large
response can affect many callers.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Increasing timeouts hides symptoms without fixing the bottleneck.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH EVIDENCE DISTINGUISHES NETWORK FROM COMMAND COST?
Compare server SLOWLOG/LATENCY data with client timers for connect, acquire,
encode, send and response. Low server execution time with high client round-trip time
points to network, queueing or client-side contention.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Slow command duration != entire client round-trip latency
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 93

Q076   •   CHAPTER 16 Advanced
SESSIONS, PUB/SUB AND STREAMS
How does Spring Session use Redis?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It can store HTTP session state centrally so multiple application instances
can access a user's session.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Publisher / worker → Redis message → Replay policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Choose the appropriate Session repository and configuration for the Boot version. Session
expiration, events, serialization and security are separate from product caching. Redis
failure can affect login continuity directly.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Shared sessions do not justify caching arbitrary sensitive objects.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW DO YOU ROTATE SESSIONS AFTER AUTHENTICATION?
After successful login, rotate the session ID through the supported session-fixation
protection and persist context correctly. Apply suitable timeout, cookie flags and logout/
revocation behavior for the actual Spring Session deployment.

   session cookie -> shared server-side session state

pages.title: SESSIONS, PUB/SUB AND STREAMS What delivery guarantee does Redis Pub/Sub provide?
pages.fullText:
Q077   •   CHAPTER 16 Advanced
SESSIONS, PUB/SUB AND STREAMS
What delivery guarantee does Redis Pub/Sub provide?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Redis Pub/Sub is at-most-once delivery to currently connected
subscribers, without retained replay history.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Publisher / worker → Redis message → Replay policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
It fits best-effort notifications when loss is acceptable or a separate repair path exists. A
listener reconnect does not recover missed messages. Do not use it as the only durable
business event transport.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Pub/Sub is not a persistent queue.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD AN L1 CACHE REPAIR A MISSED INVALIDATION?
Use short local TTLs, version checks on reads, periodic reconciliation or invalidation
fanout with recovery. Pub/Sub messages can be missed while an app is disconnected,
so a missed notice needs an independent repair path.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Subscriber disconnected during PUBLISH -> message missed
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 96

pages.title: SESSIONS, PUB/SUB AND STREAMS How do Redis Streams differ from Pub/Sub?
pages.fullText:
Q078   •   CHAPTER 16 Advanced
SESSIONS, PUB/SUB AND STREAMS
How do Redis Streams differ from Pub/Sub?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Streams retain entries and support consumer groups, progress
acknowledgment and pending-entry recovery.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Publisher / worker → Redis message → Replay policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Retention/trimming and persistence policy still matter. Consumer groups distribute work
and maintain pending entries. Business effects can repeat when unacknowledged entries
are recovered, so idempotency is required.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A stored stream is not infinite history.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN PENDING ENTRIES ARE TRIMMED AWAY?
If trimming removes pending stream entries, consumers can retain delivery metadata
without a recoverable payload. Monitor retention against processing lag, claim pending
items safely and define poison/dead-letter recovery.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
XADD orders * eventId e-42
   XREADGROUP GROUP workers c1 STREAMS orders >
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 97

pages.fullText:
Q079   •   CHAPTER 16 Advanced
SESSIONS, PUB/SUB AND STREAMS
What is the pending entries list in Streams?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It tracks entries delivered to a group consumer that have not yet been
acknowledged.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Publisher / worker → Redis message → Replay policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A failed consumer's entries need a claim/recovery policy, such as XAUTOCLAIM on
supported versions. Acknowledge after the required durable effect. Examine idle time,
delivery count and poison records during recovery.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Reading only new entries does not automatically finish all old pending work.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW DO YOU DETECT AN ABANDONED CONSUMER?
Inspect XPENDING and idle duration/delivery attempts by consumer, then use
XAUTOCLAIM on supported versions to transfer eligible abandoned work. Acknowledge
only after the durable effect succeeds.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
XPENDING orders workers
   XACK orders workers <entry-id>

Q080   •   CHAPTER 16 Advanced
SESSIONS, PUB/SUB AND STREAMS
When should you choose Kafka instead of Redis
Streams?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Choose from required retention, throughput, ecosystem, ordering,
persistence and operational isolation rather than a universal winner.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Publisher / worker → Redis message → Replay policy
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Kafka and Redis Streams have different replication, storage and consumer mechanics.
Benchmark realistic workloads and failure recovery. Shared Redis caching and stream state
can compete for memory unless isolated deliberately.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
API similarity does not imply equivalent durability.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT RECOVERY EVIDENCE WOULD DETERMINE YOUR CHOICE?
Choose by measured history retention, replay/rebuild needs, consumer scaling,
throughput and operational guarantees. Test a crash/replay and confirm the oldest
required event is still available before choosing either technology.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Large durable event platform -> evaluate Kafka
   Redis-centric bounded work stream -> evaluate Streams

Q081   •   CHAPTER 17 Advanced
REACTIVE REDIS AND ASYNCHRONOUS BOUNDARIES
What does ReactiveRedis T emplate provide?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It exposes Redis operations through Reactor types with reactive driver
support.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Reactive publisher → Nonblocking I/O → Failure signal
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Operations generally occur on subscription; compose the result into the application
response. Configure serialization in the reactive context explicitly. Reactive access is a client
execution model, not a faster Redis command algorithm.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Constructing a Mono alone does not prove a write occurred.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHO SUBSCRIBES IN A WEBFLUX CONTROLLER?
The WebFlux framework subscribes to a controller-returned Mono/Flux to drive request
processing. Application code should compose publishers rather than manually calling
subscribe inside the endpoint.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Mono<String> value = reactiveStrings.opsForValue().get("product:42");

Q082   •   CHAPTER 17 Advanced
REACTIVE REDIS AND ASYNCHRONOUS BOUNDARIES
Why avoid block() on a reactive request path?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Blocking waits can stall an event-loop thread and undermine nonblocking
throughput.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Reactive publisher → Nonblocking I/O → Failure signal
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Keep the source truly nonblocking or isolate unavoidable blocking work on a reviewed
scheduler with bounded resources. Also make loading lazy when constructing the fallback
would perform work eagerly.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A method returning Mono can still block internally.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU IDENTIFY A BLOCKING DATABASE CALL?
Use BlockHound where suitable, thread/CPU profiling, traces and bounded load tests to
find JDBC or other blocking work on event-loop threads. Replace with reactive I/O or
explicitly isolate unavoidable blocking calls.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
return redis.opsForValue().get(key)
       .switchIfEmpty(loadFromReactiveSource());

pages.title: REACTIVE REDIS AND ASYNCHRONOUS BOUNDARIES How should a reactive cache-aside miss be handled?
pages.fullText:
Q083   •   CHAPTER 17 Advanced
REACTIVE REDIS AND ASYNCHRONOUS BOUNDARIES
How should a reactive cache-aside miss be handled?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Compose a lazy source lookup, then cache only a valid returned value
under an explicit write-failure policy.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Reactive publisher → Nonblocking I/O → Failure signal
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
An empty Mono and a Redis error are different outcomes. Decide whether a cache-write
error should fail a source-backed read or return valid source data. Guard concurrent miss
load and cancellation behavior.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
onErrorResume(ignored -> empty()) can hide a real dependency failure.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH EXCEPTIONS ARE SAFE TO TREAT AS CACHE UNAVAILABLE?
Treat only classified connection/availability failures as optional for a noncritical cache.
Do not turn deserialization, authorization, programming or data-integrity failures into
silent cache misses.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
GET Mono -> switchIfEmpty(Mono.defer(loadAndCache))
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 103
pages.shortAnswer:
Compose a lazy source lookup, then cache only a valid returned value
under an explicit write-failure policy.

Reactive publisher → Nonblocking I/O → Failure signal

pages.explanation:
An empty Mono and a Redis error are different outcomes. Decide whether a cache-write
error should fail a source-backed read or return valid source data. Guard concurrent miss
load and cancellation behavior.
05
pages.pitfall: onErrorResume(ignored -> empty()) can hide a real dependency failure.

Do not turn deserialization, authorization, programming or data-integrity failures into
silent cache misses.

pages.title: REACTIVE REDIS AND ASYNCHRONOUS BOUNDARIES Are retries always safe for Redis writes?
pages.fullText:
Q084   •   CHAPTER 17 Advanced
REACTIVE REDIS AND ASYNCHRONOUS BOUNDARIES
Are retries always safe for Redis writes?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
No. A timeout can occur after the server applied the command; repeating
nonidempotent operations can duplicate effects.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Reactive publisher → Nonblocking I/O → Failure signal
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
GET is naturally repeatable; SET with the same value may still alter TTL; INCR and append
operations have effect ambiguity. Use stable request identity and an atomic dedup/effect
design when required. Bound backoff and avoid retry storms.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Transport failure is not proof the command did nothing.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU MAKE A COUNTER REQUEST IDEMPOTENT?
Deduplicate the operation ID and apply the increment in one atomic step, with enough
deduplication retention for retries. A blind retry after an uncertain response can count
the same request twice.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
INCR applied -> response lost -> retry INCR -> count increased twice
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 104

pages.title: REACTIVE REDIS AND ASYNCHRONOUS BOUNDARIES How should timeouts and cancellation be interpreted?
pages.fullText:
Q085   •   CHAPTER 17 Advanced
REACTIVE REDIS AND ASYNCHRONOUS BOUNDARIES
How should timeouts and cancellation be interpreted?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They bound caller waiting, but do not necessarily roll back or cancel a
command already accepted by Redis.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Reactive publisher → Nonblocking I/O → Failure signal
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Distinguish connection failure, enqueue delay and unknown response outcome where the
client exposes them. Maintain operation identity for correctness-critical writes. Cancellation
of a subscriber is not a general compensating operation on Redis.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Timeout does not mean absent effect.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT SHOULD AN API REPORT FOR AN UNCERTAIN WRITE?
Report that the outcome is unknown or accepted-for-reconciliation, with a stable
request ID for lookup. A timeout does not prove the write failed; avoid a false success or
unconditional repeat.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Client times out at 100 ms
   Server may finish SET at 120 ms
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 105

Q086   •   CHAPTER 18 Advanced
TESTING, OBSERVABILITY AND SECURITY
What should a Redis unit test cover?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Test key construction, policies and business decisions without pretending
mocked Redis proves server behavior.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
T est fixture → Observed behavior → Safety evidence
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Integration tests should cover serialization, expiry, Lua, transactions and the configured
cache proxy. A mocked get/set cannot validate atomicity, replication or Cluster routing.
Select a server fixture matching the tested feature.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A mock counter does not prove concurrent increments are safe.

An actual Redis integration test is needed to verify TTL, serialization bytes, Lua atomic
behavior, pipelining and Cluster routing. A mocked unit test can check key construction
and app-level fallback logic only.

Tenant included in key; TTL policy chosen; invalid input rejected

pages.fullText:
Q087   •   CHAPTER 18 Advanced
TESTING, OBSERVABILITY AND SECURITY
How do you test TTL without brittle sleeps?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use a short test expiry and bounded polling for the expected state
transition, checking the initial TTL as well.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
T est fixture → Observed behavior → Safety evidence
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Use unique keys or isolated fixtures. Test overwrite behavior and absence/no-expiry sentinel
values. Expiration timing should be asserted with reasonable tolerance rather than
millisecond equality. Cluster/failover behavior needs additional fixtures.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A passing timeout-only test may miss a key created without expiry.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT SHOULD FAILURE DIAGNOSTICS INCLUDE?
Use a short explicit TTL and poll with bounded await until the key is absent instead of
sleeping an exact number of milliseconds. On failure, include observed TTL, clock
budget, key namespace and Redis endpoint details without secrets.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Set with TTL -> assert PTTL positive
   Await until GET absent within a bounded timeout
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 108

Q088   •   CHAPTER 18 Advanced
TESTING, OBSERVABILITY AND SECURITY
Which metrics show whether caching helps?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Measure hits, misses, load latency, source load, Redis errors, evictions,
memory and end-to-end latency together.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
T est fixture → Observed behavior → Safety evidence
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Statistics can be local to a cache manager and must be enabled/configured where
supported. Add business freshness evidence. Keep metric labels bounded; individual
customer IDs belong in protected logs, not metric tag sets.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Hit ratio alone is not a success criterion.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT FRESHNESS SLO WOULD YOU TRACK?
Track an upper-bound age of cached data or percentage of reads meeting the
approved freshness budget, alongside hit rate. A 99% hit rate with stale prices can be
worse than a lower hit rate with correct values.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Hit ratio high + stale data complaints -> correctness issue
   Hit ratio low + DB saturation -> load issue

pages.fullText:
Q089   •   CHAPTER 18 Advanced
TESTING, OBSERVABILITY AND SECURITY
How should Redis access be secured?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use appropriate TLS, authentication, ACLs, network isolation and
controlled administration privileges.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
T est fixture → Observed behavior → Safety evidence
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Redis ACL users support finer privileges than one shared unrestricted credential. Store
secrets safely, test rotation and preserve hostname verification. Restrict scripts, destructive
commands and diagnostic data exposure according to the actual role.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Key prefixes do not enforce permissions without ACL policy.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH COMMANDS DOES YOUR CACHE CLIENT REALLY NEED?
Grant only the needed command categories/keys, for example GET/SET/DEL on a
namespaced cache; avoid dangerous administrative commands. Use Redis ACLs, TLS,
secret rotation and private network isolation.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Application principal -> permitted key namespace + commands
   Admin principal -> separate controlled operations

controlled administration privileges.

pages.title: TESTING, OBSERVABILITY AND SECURITY How should Redis health affect readiness and liveness?
pages.fullText:
Q090   •   CHAPTER 18 Advanced
TESTING, OBSERVABILITY AND SECURITY
How should Redis health affect readiness and liveness?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Readiness reflects the service's ability to fulfill its role; liveness should
avoid restarting a recoverable process for every remote outage.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
T est fixture → Observed behavior → Safety evidence
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Define dependency timeouts and degraded-mode capacity. Cache, lock, rate-limiter and
session roles need different policies. A restart storm can worsen reconnection pressure
without repairing Redis.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A healthy connection does not prove every slot or command is usable.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT OPERATION WOULD YOUR HEALTH EVIDENCE REPRESENT?
Liveness should test whether the process can make progress; readiness should reflect
whether it can safely serve its promised endpoints. For optional caching, Redis down
may not justify marking the entire app unready if bounded source fallback works.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Optional cache outage -> bounded source fallback
   Mandatory session store outage -> reviewed readiness failure
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 111

01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER

Incident symptom → Root cause → Safe recovery

manager is Redis rather than a local provider. A method's invocation counter across calls

and the effective RedisCacheManager. Assert the second call skips the source and
inspect the exact cache key/TTL in Redis.

Q092   •   CHAPTER 19 Senior / Architect
PRODUCTION TROUBLESHOOTING SCENARIOS
A cached update is stale after eviction. What could have
happened?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
An earlier reader may have loaded old state and populated it after the
writer evicted the key.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Incident symptom → Root cause → Safe recovery
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Reproduce this interleaving with test barriers. Consider versioned values/conditional
updates, authoritative critical reads and durable invalidation with reconciliation. Do not call
this proof Redis lost the delete.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Repeating deletion once more is not a universal race-free protocol.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW DO YOU BOUND OR REJECT A LATE STALE WRITE?
Use versioned values with compare-before-write, source version checks, or authoritative
reads for strict fields. Otherwise shorten TTL and reconcile. A delayed loader must not
overwrite an entry representing a newer DB version.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Reader DB old -> writer commits + evicts -> reader SET old

expected.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Incident symptom → Root cause → Safe recovery
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Check namespace collisions, old deployments and data migrations using TYPE and safe
inspection. Serialization mistakes can coexist with type mistakes but are distinct. Repair only
the intended keyspace and rollout contract.

incrementally. Delete only owned, verified v1 keys after rollback expires; do not flush
unrelated Redis databases.
