CROSSSLOT appears after moving to Cluster. What
changed?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A multi-key operation or script now spans different slots, even if it worked
on standalone Redis.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Incident symptom → Root cause → Safe recovery
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Audit scripts, transactions, multi-key commands and cache-clearing strategies. Hash tags
can help specific related keys, but broad tags can create skew. Client decomposition can
change atomicity, so verify semantics.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Making every key share one tag defeats sharding.

Only state that must change together in one Redis multi-key command requires key
colocation. Business invariants that cross independent aggregates should be handled at
their transactional owner, not forced into a single hash slot.

   Cluster multi-key atomic operation -> colocation required

PRODUCTION TROUBLESHOOTING SCENARIOS
Redis goes down and the database also overloads. Why?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Unbounded cache fallback or synchronized retries redirected too much
traffic to the source.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Incident symptom → Root cause → Safe recovery
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Introduce bounded admission, circuit policy, controlled retries and graceful responses.
Warm or refresh gradually after recovery. Test outage behavior under load rather than
assuming the source can absorb full cache traffic.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Fail-open is not free availability.
06   FOLLOW-UP: HOW WOULD YOU CHOOSE THE FALLBACK CONCURRENCY LIMIT?
Measure spare DB capacity and the acceptable error rate; reserve most connections
for normal traffic and enforce a semaphore/bulkhead for cache misses. Add circuit
breaking and return fast overload responses when that budget is exhausted.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Cache miss/error -> every request calls DB -> pool exhausted

pages.fullText:
Q096   •   CHAPTER 20 Senior / Architect
SENIOR ARCHITECTURE AND DESIGN CHALLENGES
How would you design a two-level product cache?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use bounded local caching plus Redis with an explicit version/invalidation
and maximum-staleness policy.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Business invariant → Redis role → Failure test
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Pub/Sub invalidation can be missed while a pod is disconnected. TTL or version validation
provides a repair bound. Ensure cold-start load and serializer changes are handled. For
strict freshness, some reads must consult the authoritative path.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
L1 can remain stale even after the Redis key was evicted.

Disable the invalidation subscription for one node or drop an event, update the product,
then check how quickly it converges. Verify L1 maximum TTL/version reads and ensure
unauthorized data is never exposed during delay.

   Invalidation event -> both layers; missed event -> expiry/repair

pages.fullText:
Q097   •   CHAPTER 20 Senior / Architect
SENIOR ARCHITECTURE AND DESIGN CHALLENGES
Can Redis locks prevent inventory overselling by
themselves?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Not reliably across every failure. Enforce the inventory invariant at the
authoritative mutation boundary.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Business invariant → Redis role → Failure test
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A conditional SQL update or appropriately designed authoritative atomic Redis operation
can enforce the actual invariant. A separate expiring lease is only coordination and may fail
during pause/failover. Define reservation expiry, release and reconciliation.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Mutual exclusion assumptions are weaker than a resource-enforced invariant.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT IF THE SAME RESERVATION REQUEST IS DELIVERED TWICE?
Use a stable reservation ID and an authoritative unique constraint or conditional
inventory update so repeated delivery returns the existing outcome. Redis lease
acquisition is an optimization, not the only oversell protection.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
UPDATE stock SET available=available-1
   WHERE item_id=:id AND available>0;

pages.title: SENIOR ARCHITECTURE AND DESIGN CHALLENGES How do you prevent cross-tenant cache leakage?
pages.fullText:
Q098   •   CHAPTER 20 Senior / Architect
SENIOR ARCHITECTURE AND DESIGN CHALLENGES
How do you prevent cross-tenant cache leakage?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Include tenant and all authorization-relevant dimensions in identity, and
authorize the source/read path correctly.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Business invariant → Redis role → Failure test
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A cached value must not bypass permissions. If access depends on changing roles or
ownership, choose invalidation, short lifetime or fresh authorization checks. Avoid caching
one user's private response under an entity-only public key.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Adding tenantId alone does not cover user-specific permissions.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN ACCESS IS REVOKED?
Recheck current authorization at the correct boundary and invalidate/version user-
specific cached responses after revocation. A previously cached response must not
grant rights that the live policy denies.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
product-summary:v1:tenant-7:user-scope:42

pages.title: SENIOR ARCHITECTURE AND DESIGN CHALLENGES How do you roll out a new cache serialization format?
pages.fullText:
Q099   •   CHAPTER 20 Senior / Architect
SENIOR ARCHITECTURE AND DESIGN CHALLENGES
How do you roll out a new cache serialization format?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use a compatible reader or versioned namespace, then deploy and warm
gradually with a rollback plan.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Business invariant → Redis role → Failure test
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Versioned keys reduce decoding conflicts but temporarily increase memory and source
load. Do not delete old state before the rollback window if it is required. Session serialization
changes can log users out or break reads and need stricter planning.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
A rolling deployment means old and new code share data concurrently.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHAT WOULD YOU MONITOR DURING THE ROLLOUT?
Monitor deserialization errors, old/new namespace hit rates, data size, latency, fallback
load and rollback-read compatibility. Keep v1 readers working until all mixed-version
instances are retired.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
v1 readers + writers -> coexist
   v2 namespace -> gradual warm -> retire v1 after safe window

Q100   •   CHAPTER 20 Senior / Architect
SENIOR ARCHITECTURE AND DESIGN CHALLENGES
What makes an architect-level Redis interview answer
strong?
01   SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
State the business invariant, selected structure/protocol, failure ambiguity,
recovery policy and verification evidence.
02   VISUAL MENTAL MODEL
Business invariant → Redis role → Failure test
04   HOW IT WORKS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Discuss memory, TTL, topology, consistency and ownership. Distinguish cache availability
from critical-state safety. Use measured load and explain the limits of locks or
asynchronous replicas rather than claiming universal exactly-once behavior.
05   COMMON INTERVIEW TRAP
Listing Redis commands without a failure model is not a design.
06   FOLLOW-UP: WHICH ASSUMPTION WOULD YOU CHALLENGE FIRST?
Challenge the claimed guarantee first: Is Redis the source of truth or only an
accelerator? Then ask what must remain correct after timeouts, failover, stale cache
writes and duplicate requests; propose tests that prove it.
03   ORIGINAL PRACTICAL EXAMPLE
Invariant: one payment effect per paymentId
   Redis: optional acceleration; DB/provider enforce identity
   Evidence: timeout, duplicate, failover and concurrent-request tests

pages.title: C01   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
C02   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
pages.fullText:
C02   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
An explicit Redis cache manager
GOAL AND SETUP
Configure named caches with string keys and a fixed JSON DTO format. Setup: Boot Redis/
cache starters; Jackson; @EnableCaching
ORIGINAL WORKED SOLUTION
@Bean
RedisCacheManager cacheManager(RedisConnectionFactory factory) {
  var base = RedisCacheConfiguration.defaultCacheConfig()
      .entryTtl(Duration.ofMinutes(5))
      .disableCachingNullValues()
      .serializeKeysWith(RedisSerializationContext.SerializationPair
          .fromSerializer(new StringRedisSerializer()))
      .serializeValuesWith(RedisSerializationContext.SerializationPair
          .fromSerializer(new Jackson2JsonRedisSerializer<>(Product.class)));
  var writer = RedisCacheWriter.nonLockingRedisCacheWriter(
      factory, BatchStrategies.scan(1000));
  return RedisCacheManager.builder(writer)
      .cacheDefaults(base)
      .withInitialCacheConfigurations(Map.of(
          "products", base,
          "shortProducts", base.entryTtl(Duration.ofSeconds(30))))
      .transactionAware().build();
}
VERIFICATION AND LIMITS
The SCAN batch strategy is supported with Lettuce in the baseline; review driver/topology
support before changing it. Product is a simple DTO supplied by the application; use this
manager only for caches storing that DTO. Provide suitable Jackson modules/ObjectMapper if
the DTO needs them. In the 3.5 baseline the default cache key prefix remains products::,
separate from template keys. transactionAware defers supported cache changes around
successful Spring-managed transactions; it does not create a SQL/Redis atomic commit. Verify
JSON bytes, TTL, cache names, rollback behavior and stored old-schema values. Do not reuse
this fixed Product serializer for arbitrary session or counter objects.
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 126

pages.title: C03   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
C04   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
C05   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
pages.fullText:
C05   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
Atomic fixed-window limiter
GOAL AND SETUP
Create/increment a per-window counter with an expiry in a short script. Setup:
StringRedisTemplate; Lua; key includes trusted identity and fixed time bucket
ORIGINAL WORKED SOLUTION
String lua = "local n=redis.call('INCR',KEYS[1]); "
    + "if n==1 then redis.call('PEXPIRE',KEYS[1],ARGV[1]); end; "
    + "return n";
RedisScript<Long> script = new DefaultRedisScript<>(lua, Long.class);
Long count = strings.execute(script,
    List.of("limit:user-42:minute-123"), "120000");
boolean allowed = count != null && count <= 100;
VERIFICATION AND LIMITS
The application computes a trusted shared time-bucket identity and supplies a validated
positive TTL longer than the bucket plus allowed clock/network margin. This script is fixed-
window counting, not exact sliding-window admission. Rejected requests also increment this
counter. Test concurrency, bucket-boundary bursts, bad types, outage policy and unknown
response outcomes. In Cluster it uses one key, so it does not require cross-slot mutation.
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 129

pages.title: C06   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
C07   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
pages.fullText:
C07   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
Cluster-compatible atomic transfer sketch
GOAL AND SETUP
Colocate required keys and validate before mutating them. Setup: StringRedisTemplate; integer
values; two keys in one hash slot
ORIGINAL WORKED SOLUTION
String lua = "local a=tonumber(redis.call('GET',KEYS[1])); "
    + "local b=tonumber(redis.call('GET',KEYS[2])); "
    + "local n=tonumber(ARGV[1]); "
    + "if not a or not b or not n or n<=0 then return -1 end; "
    + "if a<n then return 0 end; "
    + "redis.call('SET',KEYS[1],a-n); "
    + "redis.call('SET',KEYS[2],b+n); return 1";
var script = new DefaultRedisScript<Long>(lua, Long.class);
Long result = strings.execute(script,
    List.of("wallet:{tenant7}:a", "wallet:{tenant7}:b"), "10");
VERIFICATION AND LIMITS
This is a small educational integer-state exercise, not a financial ledger. Restrict input ranges
and validate exact integer representation; Lua numeric precision is unsuitable for arbitrary
large balances. SET changes TTL unless explicitly handled. Test missing/invalid values,
insufficient funds, same key rejection at the application boundary and CROSSSLOT without the
tag. Concurrent script execution is serialized, but runtime errors do not generally roll back
prior mutations, and failover durability is separate. Production money transfers need an
authoritative durable transaction design and stable operation identity.
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 131

pages.title: C08   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
pages.fullText:
C08   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
Bounded pipelining with clear semantics
GOAL AND SETUP
Send independent reads together without claiming atomicity. Setup: StringRedisTemplate; Spring
Redis callback API
ORIGINAL WORKED SOLUTION
List<Object> results = strings.executePipelined(
    (RedisCallback<Object>) connection -> {
      connection.stringCommands().get(
          "product:42".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
      connection.stringCommands().get(
          "product:43".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
      return null;
    });
VERIFICATION AND LIMITS
StringRedisTemplate applies its configured result deserialization. The callback returns null
because pipeline results are collected separately. Test ordering of replies, a missing key and
mixed result/error behavior for the selected driver. Benchmark a bounded batch against
separate calls. Other clients can mutate keys between these reads; this is not a consistent
snapshot. Cluster routing and supported commands must be tested separately before applying
the pattern there.
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 132

pages.title: C09   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
pages.fullText:
C09   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
Reactive cache-aside with an explicit failure policy
GOAL AND SETUP
Compose a lazy source read and propagate Redis errors unless a reviewed fallback is added.
Setup: ReactiveStringRedisTemplate; nonblocking source; Reactor
ORIGINAL WORKED SOLUTION
Mono<String> find(String key) {
  return redis.opsForValue().get(key)
      .switchIfEmpty(Mono.defer(() -> source.loadJson(key)
          .flatMap(value -> redis.opsForValue()
              .set(key, value, Duration.ofSeconds(30))
              .flatMap(saved -> saved
                  ? Mono.just(value)
                  : Mono.error(new IllegalStateException("Not cached"))))));
}
VERIFICATION AND LIMITS
This exercise deliberately propagates Redis get/write failures. source.loadJson returns
Mono<String> and remains nonblocking. A source-backed endpoint may choose to return valid
source data after selected cache-write failures, but implement and test that policy explicitly. Test
hit, miss, empty source, write failure, cancellation and simultaneous cold misses. The
composition does not provide cross-pod single-flight. Do not call block on the event-loop path.
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 133

pages.title: C10   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
pages.fullText:
C10   /   PRACTICAL EXERCISE
Integration and failure-test exercise
GOAL AND SETUP
Prove key lifecycle, cached invocation and failure behavior with a real Redis fixture. Setup:
Testcontainers or isolated Redis; actual Spring proxy; bounded await
ORIGINAL WORKED SOLUTION
// Fixture supplies strings and proxied ProductService.
service.find("tenant-7", "42");
service.find("tenant-7", "42");
assertThat(repositoryLoadCount()).isEqualTo(1);
assertThat(strings.getExpire("products::tenant-7:42", TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS))
    .isPositive();
await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(10)).untilAsserted(() ->
    assertThat(strings.hasKey(testExpiringKey())).isFalse());
VERIFICATION AND LIMITS
Set a short TTL for the tested cache/key and use unique fixture identities. Repository count can
be an instrumented real adapter or a controlled loader, while serialization and cache storage
use actual Redis. Awaitility/assertion imports and fixture helpers are required; this is a test
sketch. Add tests for cache-write failure, rollback, duplicate limiter requests, late lease release,
stale-loader race and serializer migration. A one-node fixture cannot prove Cluster or failover
behavior: use appropriate additional infrastructure for those tests.
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 134

pages.title: FAST REVISION
pages.fullText:
FAST REVISION
Redis commands at a glance
REMEMBER THE GUARANTEE, NOT JUST THE SYNTAX
Fast execution or one atomic Redis command does not automatically make the
downstream database effect durable.
Command / Concept Meaning Interview warning
SET key value EX 60 Write with TTL Unknown response can still mean success
TTL / PTTL Remaining lifetime -1 no expiry; -2 missing
INCR Atomic counter Retries can double-increment
SET NX PX Lease attempt Expiry does not fence stale holder
MULTI / EXEC Queued command transaction Not SQL-style rollback on runtime error
WATCH Optimistic conflict watch Must retry after conflict
SCAN Cursor key iteration Can repeat keys during changes
GETEX Get and modify expiry Not same as ordinary GET
XPENDING / XAUTOCLAIM Stream recovery Pending entry needs durable-effect handling
MOVED / ASK Cluster routing All advertised endpoints must be reachable
SPRING BOOT + REDIS | CLEAN PREMIUM EDITION 135

pages.title: If Redis disappears, can the app still reconstruct the data safely?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION CHECKLIST
The architect's Redis checklist
Source of truth
If Redis disappears, can the app still
reconstruct the data safely?
Freshness
What stale-data budget is acceptable? Can
a late writer extend it?
Identity
Do keys include tenant, permission scope
and schema version?
Failure mode
What happens after a timeout, failover, GC
pause or duplicate request?
Capacity
Are hot keys, memory, connection pools
and fallback loads bounded?
Proof
Which integration tests show the real
command, TTL, serialization and failover
behavior?
Speak this in interviews: Define the requirement → show the operation → identify the race/crash
window → choose a repair → name the test proving it.

The order below is a logical reasoning aid, not the physical plan chosen by the optimizer.
FROM / JOIN ➜ WHERE ➜ GROUP / HAVING
WINDOW ➜ SELECT ➜ ORDER / LIMIT
ALWAYS DEFINE THE GRAIN
Is one output row an employee, order, customer, joined detail row, or
aggregate group? This decides whether joins duplicate facts.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: JOIN MULTIPLICATION
Order 101 has two item rows and header amount 100. A detail join produces two copies of the header.
Summing the joined header amount gives 200 instead of 100.

pages.title: What is SQL and how is it different from procedural code?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 01   •   SQL FOUNDATIONS AND QUERY REASONING
QUESTION Q001
What is SQL and how is it different from
procedural code?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
SQL describes the required data result; the database optimizer chooses an
execution plan.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT employee_id, name FROM employees WHERE salary >= 80000;
Input rows ➜ Filter / project ➜ Result grain
WHY THIS WORKS
The query specifies columns and eligible rows rather than a loop through storage pages.
A relational result can contain duplicate rows unless the query removes them. Explain
what one result row represents before writing joins.
WATCH OUT
Declarative syntax does not guarantee an efficient plan.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What is the grain of this result?
A row represents one employee whose known salary is at least 80,000. employee_id
identifies the row.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 007

pages.title: What are DDL, DML, DQL, DCL and TCL?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 01   •   SQL FOUNDATIONS AND QUERY REASONING
QUESTION Q002
What are DDL, DML, DQL, DCL and TCL?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They are common teaching categories for defining structures, changing/
querying data, controlling privileges and managing transactions.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
DDL: CREATE, ALTER, DROP
DML: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE; DQL label: SELECT
DCL: GRANT, REVOKE; TCL: COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT
Input rows ➜ Filter / project ➜ Result grain
WHY THIS WORKS
The DQL/DML classification of SELECT varies by teaching convention. Learn command
behavior rather than treating the categories as a portable transactional specification.
DDL commit and rollback behavior differs by database.
WATCH OUT
Saying all DDL always commits is incorrect across engines.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How does MySQL DDL differ from PostgreSQL DDL?
PostgreSQL can roll back many supported DDL operations inside a transaction; MySQL
commonly performs implicit commits for DDL, including TRUNCATE. Check the exact
command before migration.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 008

pages.title: What is a relational key?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 01   •   SQL FOUNDATIONS AND QUERY REASONING
QUESTION Q003
What is a relational key?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A key identifies a row according to an invariant; candidate keys are minimal
identifiers, and one can be selected as the primary key.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
employees.employee_id is primary key
An enforced unique business identifier can be another candidate key
Input rows ➜ Filter / project ➜ Result grain
WHY THIS WORKS
A surrogate ID simplifies references but does not enforce business uniqueness by itself.
Use appropriate unique constraints for identifiers that must not repeat. Composite keys
combine columns when the identity requires them.
WATCH OUT
A generated ID does not prevent duplicate business records.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which business uniqueness constraint would you add?
For accounts, enforce UNIQUE on the immutable account number (and NOT NULL). For
tenant-scoped IDs, consider UNIQUE(tenant_id, external_id).
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 009

pages.title: What is the logical processing order of a SELECT?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 01   •   SQL FOUNDATIONS AND QUERY REASONING
QUESTION Q004
What is the logical processing order of a SELECT?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Reason roughly from FROM/JOIN to WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, window
evaluation, projection/distinct, ORDER BY and limiting, subject to SQL
semantics.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING
Window calculations -> SELECT / DISTINCT -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT
Input rows ➜ Filter / project ➜ Result grain
WHY THIS WORKS
This is a reasoning model, not a promise about the physical operator schedule. The
optimizer can reorder equivalent operations. Alias visibility and supported clauses vary by
dialect, so use a subquery when a derived result must be filtered.
WATCH OUT
Physical execution is not a literal top-to-bottom reading of SQL.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Why cannot WHERE normally use a window result?
WHERE filters rows before window values are calculated in the logical query model.
Calculate the window in a CTE or subquery, then filter outside.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 010

pages.title: Does SQL return rows in insertion order?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 01   •   SQL FOUNDATIONS AND QUERY REASONING
QUESTION Q005
Does SQL return rows in insertion order?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
No. A required order needs ORDER BY, including a deterministic tie-breaker
when pagination or ranking needs it.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT employee_id, salary FROM employees
ORDER BY salary DESC, employee_id ASC;
Input rows ➜ Filter / project ➜ Result grain
WHY THIS WORKS
Indexes and current plans can make an unordered result appear stable, but that is not a
contract. Null placement differs by database/defaults; define it explicitly when required.
Ties need additional ordering for exact row selection.
WATCH OUT
LIMIT without ORDER BY is not a reliable top-N query.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you order null salaries last portably?
ORDER BY CASE WHEN salary IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, salary DESC,
employee_id. The CASE places missing salaries last and ID breaks ties.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 011

pages.title: CHAPTER 02   •   TYPES, NULL AND THREE-VALUED LOGIC
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 02   •   TYPES, NULL AND THREE-VALUED LOGIC
QUESTION Q006
How is NULL different from zero or an empty
string?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
NULL represents an absent/unknown value; zero and an empty string are
actual values under the chosen database semantics.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT employee_id FROM employees WHERE salary IS NULL;
Known / unknown ➜ 3-valued logic ➜ Correct row
WHY THIS WORKS
A normal equality comparison to NULL produces unknown rather than true. WHERE
keeps rows where its predicate is true. Use IS NULL/IS NOT NULL and decide whether
missing data is valid in the domain.
WATCH OUT
salary = NULL does not find null salaries.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What does NOT(salary = 1000) do for NULL?
NULL = 1000 is UNKNOWN, and NOT UNKNOWN is still UNKNOWN. WHERE therefore
excludes that row.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 012

pages.title: What is SQL three-valued logic?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 02   •   TYPES, NULL AND THREE-VALUED LOGIC
QUESTION Q007
What is SQL three-valued logic?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Predicates can evaluate to true, false or unknown, and unknown affects
filtering and Boolean combinations.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
TRUE AND UNKNOWN -> UNKNOWN
FALSE AND UNKNOWN -> FALSE
TRUE OR UNKNOWN -> TRUE
Known / unknown ➜ 3-valued logic ➜ Correct row
WHY THIS WORKS
Unknown commonly comes from comparisons involving NULL. Do not assume
programming-language Boolean rules with a null simply replaced by false. A CHECK
constraint can accept unknown, so NOT NULL may be required separately.
WATCH OUT
CHECK(salary > 0) alone does not reject NULL salary.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you require a positive known salary?
Use salary DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (salary > 0). NOT NULL rejects unknown,
while CHECK rejects nonpositive values.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 013

pages.title: How do COALESCE and NULLIF help?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 02   •   TYPES, NULL AND THREE-VALUED LOGIC
QUESTION Q008
How do COALESCE and NULLIF help?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
COALESCE chooses the first non-null expression; NULLIF returns NULL when
its arguments compare equal.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT COALESCE(salary, 0) FROM employees;
SELECT 100.0 / NULLIF(denominator, 0) FROM calculation;
Known / unknown ➜ 3-valued logic ➜ Correct row
WHY THIS WORKS
Substitution is a business choice: unknown salary is not automatically zero. NULLIF can
avoid a division-by-zero failure by producing a null result. Compatible types and engine
arithmetic behavior still matter.
WATCH OUT
A null ratio and a zero ratio have different meanings.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What should the report show for an undefined denominator?
Return NULL or an explicit 'not applicable' indicator, not a made-up zero. Document the
rule for consumers.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 014

pages.title: Why use DECIMAL/NUMERIC rather than floating point for money?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 02   •   TYPES, NULL AND THREE-VALUED LOGIC
QUESTION Q009
Why use DECIMAL/NUMERIC rather than floating
point for money?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Exact decimal types avoid binary floating-point approximation for the
supported precision and scale.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
amount DECIMAL(12,2)
-- 12 total digits, 2 fractional digits
Known / unknown ➜ 3-valued logic ➜ Correct row
WHY THIS WORKS
Specify rounding, currency and permitted range. Exact storage does not decide business
rounding or stop arithmetic overflow automatically. Integer minor units are another
deliberate option; not every currency uses two decimal places.
WATCH OUT
FLOAT is not an exact currency ledger type.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you model currencies with different scales?
Store currency code and amount using a defined decimal scale or integer minor units
according to each currency. Convert and round with an explicit policy.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 015

pages.title: How do DATE and timestamp types differ?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 02   •   TYPES, NULL AND THREE-VALUED LOGIC
QUESTION Q010
How do DATE and timestamp types differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
DATE stores a calendar date; timestamp types store time-of-day, with engine-
specific time-zone semantics.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
-- PostgreSQL: timestamp without time zone vs timestamptz
-- MySQL: DATETIME vs TIMESTAMP have different conversion/range rules
Known / unknown ➜ 3-valued logic ➜ Correct row
WHY THIS WORKS
Choose whether the value is a local civil time, an instant, or a date. Session time zone
affects some displays/conversions. Keep inclusive start/exclusive end bounds for time
intervals, and define the business reporting zone.
WATCH OUT
Timestamp type names are not portable semantic guarantees.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you report one day across a daylight-saving change?
Define the business time zone; construct local midnight-to-next-midnight bounds in that
zone, convert both to instants and query a half-open interval.

CHAPTER 03   •   SCHEMA, CONSTRAINTS AND DDL
QUESTION Q011
How do PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE and NOT NULL
differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Primary key identifies each row and disallows null key parts; UNIQUE
enforces uniqueness under engine rules; NOT NULL forbids absence.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
CREATE TABLE tags (
  tag_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL UNIQUE
);
Business rule ➜ Constraint check ➜ Valid write
WHY THIS WORKS
A table can have multiple unique constraints but one primary key declaration. NULL
handling in unique constraints differs by database/options. Do not infer that UNIQUE
alone always makes a column a non-null business identifier.
WATCH OUT
Nullable unique behavior is not identical to a primary key.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you require one unique known email?
Use email VARCHAR(...) NOT NULL with a UNIQUE constraint; decide whether
normalized/case-insensitive uniqueness is needed and implement it for your engine.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 017

pages.title: What does a foreign key enforce?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 03   •   SCHEMA, CONSTRAINTS AND DDL
QUESTION Q012
What does a foreign key enforce?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It requires referenced identity to exist for applicable referencing values and
constrains related modifications through its action policy.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
FOREIGN KEY (department_id) REFERENCES departments(department_id)
Business rule ➜ Constraint check ➜ Valid write
WHY THIS WORKS
Nullable foreign keys can represent optional relationships under the configured match
semantics. Deletion actions such as RESTRICT or CASCADE have business consequences.
PostgreSQL does not automatically create a referencing-column index; MySQL InnoDB
has index requirements/creation behavior.
WATCH OUT
A foreign key does not automatically prove a query's join is one-to-one.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which side can have many rows?
The referencing/child table can contain many rows pointing to one parent. For example,
many employees can reference one department.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 018

pages.title: When should you use a CHECK constraint?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 03   •   SCHEMA, CONSTRAINTS AND DDL
QUESTION Q013
When should you use a CHECK constraint?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use it for supported row-level validity rules, along with required nullability
constraints.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0)
Business rule ➜ Constraint check ➜ Valid write
WHY THIS WORKS
A check can validate a row's values but is not a general cross-row aggregate invariant.
Expressions and enforcement differ by engine/version. A uniqueness constraint or proper
transaction protocol is needed for concurrent cross-row rules.
WATCH OUT
A positive check without NOT NULL can permit unknown values.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you enforce one active booking per slot?
Enforce a uniqueness rule on the slot identity for active bookings: in PostgreSQL a
partial unique index may work; otherwise use a modeled active-slot claim with a unique
key and transaction.

pages.title: How do DELETE, TRUNCATE and DROP differ?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 03   •   SCHEMA, CONSTRAINTS AND DDL
QUESTION Q014
How do DELETE, TRUNCATE and DROP differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
DELETE removes selected rows; TRUNCATE removes table contents through a
different engine operation; DROP removes the object definition.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
DELETE FROM demo_rows WHERE id = 1;
-- TRUNCATE demo_rows; DROP TABLE demo_rows; use only disposable fixtures.
Business rule ➜ Constraint check ➜ Valid write
WHY THIS WORKS
Do not summarize them only as slow/fast. PostgreSQL TRUNCATE can be rolled back in
a transaction, while MySQL TRUNCATE causes an implicit commit. Locking, triggers,
identity behavior and foreign-key restrictions differ.
WATCH OUT
TRUNCATE rollback behavior is not portable.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which operation preserves the table schema?
DELETE and TRUNCATE preserve the table definition; DROP TABLE removes it. Other
behavior differs by engine.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 020

pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 03   •   SCHEMA, CONSTRAINTS AND DDL
QUESTION Q015
How do you change a large production table
safely?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Plan compatibility, lock duration, backfill load, constraints and rollback
around the specific engine operation.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
Add nullable column -> deploy compatible code
Backfill in bounded batches -> validate -> enforce required constraint
Business rule ➜ Constraint check ➜ Valid write
WHY THIS WORKS
Online/concurrent options have engine-specific limitations and still consume resources.

A migration that works on ten rows can block a large live table.

Collect row counts, disk and index sizes, traffic, lock duration, rollback plan,
representative rehearsal timings and old/new app compatibility evidence.

pages.title: How do WHERE, BETWEEN, IN and LIKE differ?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 04   •   FILTERING, DATES AND DETERMINISTIC ORDERING
QUESTION Q016
How do WHERE, BETWEEN, IN and LIKE differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They express general predicates, inclusive bounds, membership and pattern
matching respectively.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
WHERE salary BETWEEN 60000 AND 90000
WHERE department_id IN (10,20)
WHERE name LIKE 'M%'
Start / end ➜ Predicate ➜ Ordered rows
WHY THIS WORKS
BETWEEN includes both ends, which can be awkward for timestamp ranges. LIKE case
sensitivity follows collation/type rules rather than one universal SQL behavior. Escape
literal wildcard characters when needed.
WATCH OUT
BETWEEN day-start and next-day-start includes the next boundary.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you filter exactly one month?
Use >= the first instant of the month and < the first instant of the next month. Bind both
boundaries with the reporting time zone.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 022

pages.title: Why use a half-open timestamp range?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 04   •   FILTERING, DATES AND DETERMINISTIC ORDERING
QUESTION Q017
Why use a half-open timestamp range?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It includes the start and excludes the next boundary without guessing the last
representable instant.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
WHERE ordered_at >= :start
  AND ordered_at < :next_start
Start / end ➜ Predicate ➜ Ordered rows
WHY THIS WORKS
Bind timestamps derived in the intended business zone. This can also be more index-
friendly than wrapping the column in a date-extraction function. Account for timestamp
precision and session conversion behavior.
WATCH OUT
'23:59:59' can miss fractional-second rows.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you build month bounds correctly?
Compute the first day of this month and the first day of the following month in the
business zone; use start inclusive and next-start exclusive.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 023

pages.title: How do CASE expressions help in reporting?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 04   •   FILTERING, DATES AND DETERMINISTIC ORDERING
QUESTION Q018
How do CASE expressions help in reporting?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
CASE maps conditions to values while keeping the rule inside a set-based
query.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT employee_id,
 CASE WHEN salary IS NULL THEN 'UNKNOWN'
      WHEN salary >= 90000 THEN 'HIGH' ELSE 'OTHER' END AS band
FROM employees;
Start / end ➜ Predicate ➜ Ordered rows
WHY THIS WORKS
Branches are considered in order and the resulting types must be compatible. Explicit
handling of NULL prevents unknown values from being mislabeled. Use CASE for
conditional aggregation as well as display values.
WATCH OUT
A label does not replace the original value's semantics.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What happens when two conditions overlap?
CASE returns the value from the first matching WHEN branch. Order overlapping
conditions from most specific to general.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 024

pages.title: How do you paginate deterministically with LIMIT?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 04   •   FILTERING, DATES AND DETERMINISTIC ORDERING
QUESTION Q019
How do you paginate deterministically with LIMIT?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Apply an explicit stable ordering with a unique tie-breaker; then choose offset
or seek behavior deliberately.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT order_id, ordered_at FROM orders
ORDER BY ordered_at DESC, order_id DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40;
Start / end ➜ Predicate ➜ Ordered rows
WHY THIS WORKS
LIMIT/OFFSET syntax works in the main PostgreSQL/MySQL examples. Other engines
use alternatives. Inserts/deletes between requests can shift offset pages; stable ordering
alone does not provide a cross-request snapshot.
WATCH OUT
Deep offsets still require work on preceding rows.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
When would seek pagination be better?
Seek/keyset pagination is better for deep sequential browsing with a stable unique sort
key; it avoids scanning large OFFSET prefixes and reduces page drift.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 025

pages.title: How do you write portable date arithmetic?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 04   •   FILTERING, DATES AND DETERMINISTIC ORDERING
QUESTION Q020
How do you write portable date arithmetic?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Do not assume interval syntax is identical; label the engine and bind
computed bounds when useful.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
-- PostgreSQL:
SELECT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '7 days';
-- MySQL:
SELECT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL 7 DAY;
Start / end ➜ Predicate ➜ Ordered rows
WHY THIS WORKS
Functions such as date truncation, date differences and formatting differ. Parameterized
start/end timestamps often keep application queries simple and consistent. Define
whether seven days means elapsed hours or calendar days.
WATCH OUT
Calendar arithmetic can differ from fixed elapsed seconds.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which time zone controls the report?
Use the business/reporting time zone selected by the product contract, not an accidental
database session default.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 026

pages.title: How do INNER and LEFT JOIN differ?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 05   •   JOINS AND RESULT CARDINALITY
QUESTION Q021
How do INNER and LEFT JOIN differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
INNER JOIN returns matching pairs; LEFT JOIN also preserves unmatched
left rows with null-extended right columns.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT d.name, e.name FROM departments d
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.department_id;
Left relation ➜ Match keys ➜ Output rows
WHY THIS WORKS
A department with no employees still appears in the left-join result. A department with
many employees appears once for every matching employee. Understand the keys and
multiplicity before aggregating.
WATCH OUT
LEFT JOIN does not guarantee one result row per left row.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How many rows does Engineering produce here?
Engineering has three matching employees: Sai, Meena and Arun. LEFT JOIN returns
one row per match.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 027

pages.title: Why can a WHERE predicate turn a LEFT JOIN into inner-like behavior?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 05   •   JOINS AND RESULT CARDINALITY
QUESTION Q022
Why can a WHERE predicate turn a LEFT JOIN
into inner-like behavior?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A predicate requiring a non-null right-side match discards null-extended rows
after the join.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id=d.department_id
WHERE e.salary > 80000
Left relation ➜ Match keys ➜ Output rows
WHY THIS WORKS
If the requirement is preserve every department while matching only high earners, place
the right-side condition in ON. If the requirement is departments with a high earner,
filtering may be intentional. Explain the requirement first.
WATCH OUT
Moving a condition between ON and WHERE can change semantics.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you preserve empty departments?
Move the right-side salary condition into JOIN ... ON and preserve each department;
count employee_id to get zero for unmatched departments.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 028

pages.title: Why do joins multiply rows?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 05   •   JOINS AND RESULT CARDINALITY
QUESTION Q023
Why do joins multiply rows?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Each matching pair produces a row; multiple one-to-many relationships can
create a multiplication of combinations.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
Order has 2 items and 3 payments
Joining both detail tables directly can create 6 rows
Left relation ➜ Match keys ➜ Output rows
WHY THIS WORKS
Declare the intended grain and aggregate each detail relation to that grain before
joining. DISTINCT on final values can hide symptoms but cannot generally repair
duplicated totals. Validate constraints rather than assuming uniqueness.
WATCH OUT
SUM(DISTINCT amount) also collapses genuinely equal amounts.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you avoid doubled order revenue?
Aggregate order-items to order_id before joining, or sum header amounts from the
orders table directly. Never fix duplicated headers with SUM(DISTINCT amount).
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 029

pages.title: What are self joins and cross joins?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 05   •   JOINS AND RESULT CARDINALITY
QUESTION Q024
What are self joins and cross joins?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A self join relates rows of one table through aliases; a cross join produces
every pair of rows from its inputs.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT e.name, m.name AS manager FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id=e.manager_id;
Left relation ➜ Match keys ➜ Output rows
WHY THIS WORKS
Use clear aliases for employee/manager roles. A cross join can intentionally generate a
calendar/product matrix, but an accidental missing join condition can explode row
counts. Multiply input cardinalities to estimate the result.
WATCH OUT
Sharing a table name does not remove the need for a relationship condition.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you find employees without a manager?
LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id=e.manager_id WHERE e.manager_id IS
NULL; this includes top-level and unassigned employees.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 030

pages.fullText:

CHAPTER 05   •   JOINS AND RESULT CARDINALITY
QUESTION Q025
Does MySQL support FULL OUTER JOIN like
PostgreSQL?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
MySQL 8.4 does not provide native FULL OUTER JOIN; PostgreSQL does.
Emulation needs careful duplicate and match handling.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
-- PostgreSQL:
SELECT * FROM a FULL OUTER JOIN b ON a.id=b.id;
-- MySQL: left branch UNION ALL right-only branch with NOT EXISTS.
Left relation ➜ Match keys ➜ Output rows
WHY THIS WORKS
Keep unmatched rows from both sides without returning matched rows twice. Use explicit
columns and a non-null key or null-safe anti-match policy. Many interview questions do
not require a full join, so verify the actual goal.
WATCH OUT
UNION can unintentionally remove legitimate duplicate rows in an emulation.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you isolate the right-only branch?
Use the left-join rows from B with no match in A, commonly WHERE a.id IS NULL when
the left key is non-null; add them with UNION ALL.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 031

pages.title: How do GROUP BY and DISTINCT differ?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 06   •   AGGREGATION AND GROUPING
QUESTION Q026
How do GROUP BY and DISTINCT differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
GROUP BY forms groups for aggregate reasoning; DISTINCT removes
duplicate projected result rows.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT DISTINCT department_id FROM employees;
SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;
Input rows ➜ Group keys ➜ Aggregate
WHY THIS WORKS
They can sometimes produce the same columns but express different intent. Choose
grouping keys representing the report grain. PostgreSQL/MySQL have specific functional-
dependency rules; avoid relying on arbitrary ungrouped columns.
WATCH OUT
Disabling strict group rules can yield misleading selected values.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which columns define one report row?
Choose grouping columns that uniquely define the report entity: for example,
customer_id for one row per customer.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 032

pages.title: How do COUNT(*), COUNT(column) and COUNT(DISTINCT column) differ?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 06   •   AGGREGATION AND GROUPING
QUESTION Q027
How do COUNT(*), COUNT(column) and
COUNT(DISTINCT column) differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They count rows, non-null column values and distinct non-null values
respectively.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(salary), COUNT(DISTINCT salary) FROM employees;
-- Fixture result: 6, 5, 4
Input rows ➜ Group keys ➜ Aggregate
WHY THIS WORKS
Null salaries contribute to row count but not salary-value counts. With a left join,
COUNT(*) also counts a preserved row for an empty department; count a non-null
employee key instead.
WATCH OUT
COUNT(*) after LEFT JOIN can report one employee for an empty group.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you count zero employees correctly?
SELECT d.department_id, COUNT(e.employee_id) FROM departments d LEFT JOIN
employees e ON e.department_id=d.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id; empty
HR returns zero.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 033

pages.title: How do WHERE and HAVING differ?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 06   •   AGGREGATION AND GROUPING
QUESTION Q028
How do WHERE and HAVING differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
WHERE filters input rows; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) FROM employees
WHERE salary IS NOT NULL GROUP BY department_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
Input rows ➜ Group keys ➜ Aggregate
WHY THIS WORKS
Row predicates reduce eligible inputs, while aggregate predicates belong at group level.
Some engines allow HAVING in additional forms, but the distinction remains useful. Do
not filter rows needed by another aggregate unintentionally.
WATCH OUT
HAVING is not merely a slower version of WHERE.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What changes if salary filtering is removed?
Removing WHERE salary IS NOT NULL allows the unknown-salary employee into their
group, changing counts if included; averages still ignore null salaries.

pages.title: How do you calculate conditional totals?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 06   •   AGGREGATION AND GROUPING
QUESTION Q029
How do you calculate conditional totals?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Aggregate CASE expressions or a supported engine-specific filtered
aggregate.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN status='PAID' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS paid_total
FROM orders;
Input rows ➜ Group keys ➜ Aggregate
WHY THIS WORKS
CASE makes this query portable across the main engines. SUM over no input rows
returns NULL, so use COALESCE when a zero total is the required contract. Keep
cancelled/pending amounts separate when the report demands them.
WATCH OUT
Returning zero is a business/reporting choice, not automatic SUM behavior.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you compute paid and pending counts together?
SUM(CASE WHEN status='PAID' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) and SUM(CASE WHEN
status='PENDING' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), together in one SELECT.

CHAPTER 06   •   AGGREGATION AND GROUPING
QUESTION Q030
Why can AVG(salary) differ from SUM(salary)/
COUNT(*)?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
AVG ignores null salary values, while COUNT(*) includes rows without a known
salary.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
Known salaries total=410000; known count=5; all rows=6
AVG(salary)=82000; total/all rows is a different measure

appropriate numeric literal.

Missing salary does not automatically mean zero compensation.

What denominator does your business metric require?
For mean known salary, divide by COUNT(salary); for payroll per headcount, choose a
documented rule for unknown salary and use the appropriate population.

pages.title: What is a scalar subquery?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 07   •   SUBQUERIES, EXISTS AND NULL-SAFE ANTI-JOINS
QUESTION Q031
What is a scalar subquery?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A scalar subquery supplies one value; no row normally yields NULL, and more
than one row is an error under PostgreSQL/MySQL semantics.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT name FROM employees
WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
Outer row ➜ Existence test ➜ Keep / discard
WHY THIS WORKS
An aggregate without grouping supplies one value even for empty input, though AVG may
return NULL. A grouped subquery can produce many rows and cannot simply act as one
scalar. Keep cardinality explicit.
WATCH OUT
SQLite's scalar-subquery behavior differs for multiple rows.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you guarantee one returned value?
Make the subquery aggregate without GROUP BY, or use a unique-key filter. Do not
arbitrarily LIMIT 1 unless that is a valid business selection.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 037

pages.title: What is a correlated subquery?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 07   •   SUBQUERIES, EXISTS AND NULL-SAFE ANTI-JOINS
QUESTION Q032
What is a correlated subquery?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It references an outer row, making its logical result depend on that row's
values.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.salary >
 (SELECT AVG(x.salary) FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id=e.department_id);
Outer row ➜ Existence test ➜ Keep / discard
WHY THIS WORKS
This finds employees above their department average. The optimizer may transform the
query rather than literally execute one independent full scan per row. Verify the plan
instead of making a universal performance claim.
WATCH OUT
Correlated does not automatically mean slow.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Can a window aggregate express the same rule?
Yes: AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) in a CTE, then filter salary >
department_avg outside the CTE.

pages.title: When should you use EXISTS?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 07   •   SUBQUERIES, EXISTS AND NULL-SAFE ANTI-JOINS
QUESTION Q033
When should you use EXISTS?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use EXISTS when the requirement is whether at least one matching row
exists, without multiplying the outer rows.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS
 (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id=c.customer_id AND o.status='PAID');
Outer row ➜ Existence test ➜ Keep / discard
WHY THIS WORKS
A customer qualifies once even with several paid orders. A join needs DISTINCT or
aggregation if the required result is one row per customer. EXISTS does not depend on
the selected literal being 1.
WATCH OUT
SELECT 1 is convention, not a special guarantee of faster execution.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you find customers with no orders?
SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM
orders o WHERE o.customer_id=c.customer_id); it naturally includes customers without
rows.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 039

pages.title: Why is NOT IN dangerous with NULLs?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 07   •   SUBQUERIES, EXISTS AND NULL-SAFE ANTI-JOINS
QUESTION Q034
Why is NOT IN dangerous with NULLs?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
If the membership set contains NULL, nonmatching comparisons can
become unknown and be filtered out.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers c WHERE c.customer_id NOT IN
 (SELECT manager_id FROM employees);
Outer row ➜ Existence test ➜ Keep / discard
WHY THIS WORKS
The fixture has NULL manager IDs, so this is a poor exclusion rule. Prefer a logically
appropriate NOT EXISTS, or prove/filter non-null values on both sides. Do not replace
one construct with another without checking outer null semantics.
WATCH OUT
NOT IN and NOT EXISTS are not universally equivalent.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What if the outer identifier is NULL?
An outer NULL requires explicit meaning. With NOT EXISTS, null-safe correlation is
necessary only if NULL is a legitimate identity; usually a NOT NULL key is preferable.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 040

pages.title: How do anti-joins find missing relationships?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 07   •   SUBQUERIES, EXISTS AND NULL-SAFE ANTI-JOINS
QUESTION Q035
How do anti-joins find missing relationships?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
NOT EXISTS can retain rows for which no qualifying related row is present.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS
 (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id=c.customer_id);
Outer row ➜ Existence test ➜ Keep / discard
WHY THIS WORKS
A left join plus IS NULL on a non-null right-side key can also express absence. Keep
additional matching filters in the appropriate place. Use the business definition of
missing: no orders differs from no paid orders.
WATCH OUT
Testing a nullable right-side field can misclassify a real match.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which key should the IS NULL test use?
Check a non-null, guaranteed right-side key such as o.order_id IS NULL after LEFT
JOIN; do not use a nullable payload column.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 041

pages.title: What is a CTE?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 08   •   CTES AND RECURSIVE QUERIES
QUESTION Q036
What is a CTE?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A common table expression names a query result within one statement using
WITH.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
WITH paid AS (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status='PAID')
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) FROM paid GROUP BY customer_id;
Anchor rows ➜ Recursive step ➜ Bounded result
WHY THIS WORKS
It improves readability and supports reuse within that statement. It is not automatically a
stored table or permanently cached result. Optimization/materialization behavior differs
by engine, version and query structure.
WATCH OUT
A CTE is not always faster than a subquery.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What would you inspect to see its physical treatment?
Check EXPLAIN or EXPLAIN ANALYZE and the engine/version rules; CTEs may be
inlined or materialized depending on plan and syntax.

pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 08   •   CTES AND RECURSIVE QUERIES
QUESTION Q037
How do a CTE, derived table and temporary table
differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
A CTE and derived table are statement-local query constructs; a temporary
table is a separate session/transaction-scoped object under engine rules.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
Derived: FROM (SELECT ...) AS q
CTE: WITH q AS (SELECT ...)
Temporary: CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE q (...)
Anchor rows ➜ Recursive step ➜ Bounded result
WHY THIS WORKS
A temporary table can support explicit staging/indexes and reuse across statements, with
creation/cleanup and transaction semantics to review. Choose from reuse, plan control
and lifecycle needs rather than style alone.
WATCH OUT
Temporary-table scope and DDL behavior vary by database.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
When is materialized staging worth the cost?
Stage results when expensive intermediate data is reused or needs indexing and stable
lifetime. Measure creation, cleanup and statistics costs.

pages.title: What does a recursive CTE contain?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 08   •   CTES AND RECURSIVE QUERIES
QUESTION Q038
What does a recursive CTE contain?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It combines an anchor term with a recursive term that consumes prior
results until no new rows are produced.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
WITH RECURSIVE org AS (
 SELECT employee_id, manager_id, 0 AS depth FROM employees WHERE employee_id=1
 UNION ALL
 SELECT e.employee_id,e.manager_id,o.depth+1 FROM employees e
 JOIN org o ON e.manager_id=o.employee_id WHERE o.depth<10)
SELECT * FROM org;
Anchor rows ➜ Recursive step ➜ Bounded result
WHY THIS WORKS
This walks Sai's reporting subtree in the fixture. Add a path/cycle policy for general
graphs; a depth cap is a bound, not proof the graph is acyclic. Output order needs
ORDER BY separately.
WATCH OUT
Recursion does not imply deterministic traversal order.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you report a detected cycle?
Carry a visited-ID path or a cycle marker and emit the offending edge; do not confuse a
shared descendant with a loop.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 044

pages.title: How do you prevent a recursive query running indefinitely?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 08   •   CTES AND RECURSIVE QUERIES
QUESTION Q039
How do you prevent a recursive query running
indefinitely?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use valid hierarchy constraints, cycle detection and a reviewed bound; do not
depend only on unlimited data being well formed.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
Track visited IDs or use supported cycle syntax
Reject revisiting a node on the current path
Anchor rows ➜ Recursive step ➜ Bounded result
WHY THIS WORKS
UNION deduplication may stop some recursions but does not generally replace path-
aware cycle logic when rows include changing depth/path values. Engine recursion limits
differ. Test cyclic, deep and shared-descendant cases.
WATCH OUT
Incrementing depth makes repeated visits distinct rows.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Is a shared child a cycle?
No. A cycle revisits a node on the current traversal path. Two independent parent paths
reaching the same child form a DAG, not necessarily a cycle.

pages.fullText:

CHAPTER 08   •   CTES AND RECURSIVE QUERIES
QUESTION Q040
What is a useful multi-stage CTE interview
pattern?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Break grain-changing operations into named stages, then join/filter their
documented outputs.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
WITH paid_totals AS (
 SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders
 WHERE status='PAID' GROUP BY customer_id)
SELECT c.name,p.total FROM customers c JOIN paid_totals p
 ON p.customer_id=c.customer_id;
Anchor rows ➜ Recursive step ➜ Bounded result
WHY THIS WORKS
The first stage creates one row per paying customer. The next joins that grain to
customers without detail multiplication. Readable stages make correctness easier to
assess, while the optimizer still chooses physical operations.
WATCH OUT
Naming a stage does not enforce uniqueness without the query/constraints.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you include zero-paying customers?
Start with customers and LEFT JOIN the per-customer payment aggregate, COALESCE
total to zero if required; preserve the empty customer.

pages.title: How do window functions differ from GROUP BY?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 09   •   WINDOW FUNCTIONS
QUESTION Q041
How do window functions differ from GROUP BY?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Window functions calculate across related rows without collapsing detail rows
into one group row.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT employee_id, department_id, salary,
 AVG(salary) OVER(PARTITION BY department_id) AS dept_avg
FROM employees;
Input rows ➜ Partition + order ➜ Window value
WHY THIS WORKS
Each employee retains an output row with its department average. A partition is a
calculation grouping, not table storage partitioning. Window ordering and final result
ordering are separate.
WATCH OUT
OVER(ORDER BY ...) does not guarantee final display order.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What is the output grain here?
The output remains one row per base order because the window annotates rows; GROUP
BY would collapse rows into groups.

pages.title: How do ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK differ?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 09   •   WINDOW FUNCTIONS
QUESTION Q042
How do ROW_NUMBER, RANK and
DENSE_RANK differ?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
ROW_NUMBER numbers rows; RANK gives peers the same rank with gaps;
DENSE_RANK gives peers the same rank without gaps.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
Salaries 100000,80000,80000,60000
ROW_NUMBER: 1,2,3,4; RANK: 1,2,2,4; DENSE_RANK: 1,2,2,3
Input rows ➜ Partition + order ➜ Window value
WHY THIS WORKS
Peer equality follows the window ORDER BY expressions. Adding employee_id to a salary-
ranking order breaks salary ties. Use a separate deterministic tie-breaker for row-
number selection when exactly N rows are required.
WATCH OUT
Top two rows and top two distinct salaries are different requirements.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which function fits second distinct salary?
DENSE_RANK on salary DESC finds the second distinct level including ties. Filter rank=2
in an outer query.

pages.fullText:

CHAPTER 09   •   WINDOW FUNCTIONS
QUESTION Q043
Why specify an explicit running-total frame?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
ROWS with a unique order makes the intended per-row accumulation explicit
instead of relying on a default peer-sensitive frame.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY ordered_at, order_id
 ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
Input rows ➜ Partition + order ➜ Window value
WHY THIS WORKS
With ordered aggregate windows, default frames can include all peers at the current
ordering value. An order_id tie-breaker plus ROWS makes row progression clear. Partition
when each customer needs a separate total.
WATCH OUT
Same-date rows can share a total under a peer-based frame.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What changes if order_id is removed?
Without order_id, equal-date rows become peers; RANGE or default frame behavior may
produce jumps. Specify ROWS and a unique tie-breaker for deterministic progression.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 049

pages.fullText:

CHAPTER 09   •   WINDOW FUNCTIONS
QUESTION Q044
How do LAG and LEAD help?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
They access values from earlier/later rows in the window's logical order
without a self join.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT order_id, amount,
 LAG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at,order_id) AS prev
FROM orders;
Input rows ➜ Partition + order ➜ Window value
WHY THIS WORKS
The first row has no preceding value unless a default is supplied. Distinguish a missing
preceding row from a preceding row whose value is NULL. Add deterministic ordering
and decide whether cancelled rows belong in the sequence.
WATCH OUT
Offset means row position, not elapsed days.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you calculate a change from the previous paid order?
Use LAG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at, order_id)
on paid orders, then subtract the prior amount.

without a self join.
pages.codeExample:
SELECT order_id, amount,
 LAG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at,order_id) AS prev
FROM orders;
Input rows ➜ Partition + order ➜ Window value
pages.explanation:
The first row has no preceding value unless a default is supplied. Distinguish a missing
preceding row from a preceding row whose value is NULL. Add deterministic ordering
and decide whether cancelled rows belong in the sequence.
WATCH OUT
Offset means row position, not elapsed days.

How would you calculate a change from the previous paid order?
Use LAG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at, order_id)

SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 09   •   WINDOW FUNCTIONS
QUESTION Q045
How do you filter a window result in PostgreSQL/
MySQL?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Compute it in a CTE/derived table, then filter in an outer query.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
WITH ranked AS (
 SELECT employee_id,salary,DENSE_RANK() OVER(ORDER BY salary DESC) AS r
 FROM employees WHERE salary IS NOT NULL)
SELECT employee_id,salary FROM ranked WHERE r=2;
Input rows ➜ Partition + order ➜ Window value
WHY THIS WORKS
WHERE in the same query level runs before the window result is available. QUALIFY
exists in some other engines but is not part of these baseline examples. Keep final
ORDER BY explicit.
WATCH OUT
A window alias in same-level WHERE is not portable SQL.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you return exactly two rows instead of ties?
Use ROW_NUMBER with unique ordering and filter row_num<=2, instead of
DENSE_RANK which may include extra tied rows.

CHAPTER 10   •   COMMON INTERVIEW QUERY CHALLENGES
QUESTION Q046
How do you find the second-highest distinct
salary?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Rank non-null distinct salary levels, or take the maximum salary below the
global maximum.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT MAX(salary) AS second_salary FROM employees
WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);
Rank / ties ➜ Select rule ➜ Expected rows
WHY THIS WORKS
This returns 90000 in the fixture and NULL if fewer than two distinct known salaries
exist. It returns a salary, not all employees earning it. Use DENSE_RANK when employee
rows at a selected level are required.
WATCH OUT
OFFSET 1 on raw employee rows can select another tied maximum.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you return all second-level employees?
Compute the second distinct amount in a CTE and filter employees whose salary equals
it; tied employees are all included.

pages.title: How do you select top N salaries per department?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 10   •   COMMON INTERVIEW QUERY CHALLENGES
QUESTION Q047
How do you select top N salaries per department?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use DENSE_RANK for salary levels or ROW_NUMBER for an exact row count,
with an explicit tie policy.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
WITH r AS (
 SELECT employee_id,department_id,salary,
 DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS pos
 FROM employees WHERE salary IS NOT NULL)
SELECT * FROM r WHERE pos<=2;
Rank / ties ➜ Select rule ➜ Expected rows
WHY THIS WORKS
Engineering returns three employees because two share its second level. Exclude or
handle unassigned/null values as required. For exactly two people, ROW_NUMBER with
salary then employee_id gives deterministic selection.
WATCH OUT
Adding a unique ID to DENSE_RANK changes the salary-level definition.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How many rows should Engineering return?
Engineering has three people across two distinct salary levels: one at 100,000 and two
tied at 80,000.

pages.title: How do you find duplicate business values?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 10   •   COMMON INTERVIEW QUERY CHALLENGES
QUESTION Q048
How do you find duplicate business values?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Group by the business identity columns and retain groups with more than
one row.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT email,COUNT(*) FROM contacts GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*)>1;
Rank / ties ➜ Select rule ➜ Expected rows
WHY THIS WORKS
Define case/space normalization and NULL policy before calling values duplicates. For
removal, first choose a deterministic retained row and review references. Duplicates by
email are not necessarily duplicates by the entire row.
WATCH OUT
DISTINCT only hides duplicates in one result; it does not repair stored data.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which row should survive a cleanup?
Choose a survivor by a documented rule such as earliest verified row, then use
ROW_NUMBER partitioned by the normalized business key, ordered by chosen priority
and ID.

pages.title: How do you solve gaps-and-islands questions?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 10   •   COMMON INTERVIEW QUERY CHALLENGES
QUESTION Q049
How do you solve gaps-and-islands questions?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Derive a stable group key or change marker for consecutive runs, then
aggregate by that group.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
Consecutive integer values: value - ROW_NUMBER() OVER(ORDER BY value)
Equal differences identify one island after deduplication
Rank / ties ➜ Select rule ➜ Expected rows
WHY THIS WORKS
Define consecutive precisely: integer +1, adjacent dates or adjacent events. Deduplicate
input when necessary, handle partitions and use dialect-specific date arithmetic carefully.
A LAG-based start marker is another useful method.
WATCH OUT
Missing weekends are not a gap if the business uses working days.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What interval defines adjacency?
Define whether adjacent means consecutive integers, dates, or gaps no larger than a
threshold; derive groups using that specific definition.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 055

pages.title: How do you find customers who bought every required product?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 10   •   COMMON INTERVIEW QUERY CHALLENGES
QUESTION Q050
How do you find customers who bought every
required product?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use relational division, often expressed as no required product lacking a
corresponding purchase.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (
 SELECT 1 FROM required_products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM purchases x WHERE x.customer_id=c.customer_id
  AND x.product_id=p.product_id));
Rank / ties ➜ Select rule ➜ Expected rows
WHY THIS WORKS
The two NOT EXISTS clauses express universal coverage. Decide whether duplicate
purchases, cancelled orders and an empty required-product set count. Under this
formulation, an empty required set qualifies every customer.
WATCH OUT
Counting raw purchase rows can overcount duplicates.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What should the empty-set case mean for the business?
Mathematically every customer qualifies when the required set is empty, but the product
may choose no result; state the intended business rule explicitly.

SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 11   •   DATA CHANGES, UPSERT AND DEDUPLICATION
QUESTION Q051
How do INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE target
data?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
INSERT adds rows; UPDATE modifies qualifying rows; DELETE removes
qualifying rows.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
UPDATE employees SET salary=salary+1000 WHERE employee_id=5;
Request ➜ Guarded write ➜ Committed state
WHY THIS WORKS
An omitted or incorrect predicate can affect many rows. For practice, use disposable
fixtures and inspect the same predicate with SELECT. Production changes need reviewed
transactions, scope and affected-row evidence.
WATCH OUT
A precheck SELECT does not prevent concurrent changes.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which invariant belongs in the write predicate?
Put the stock or version check in UPDATE ... WHERE, and verify affected rows.
Constraints still enforce the final invariant.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 057

pages.title: What is an upsert?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 11   •   DATA CHANGES, UPSERT AND DEDUPLICATION
QUESTION Q052
What is an upsert?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
It inserts or updates according to a conflict rule, with engine-specific syntax
and semantics.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
-- PostgreSQL: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE ...
-- MySQL: INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE ...
Request ➜ Guarded write ➜ Committed state
WHY THIS WORKS
A unique constraint defines conflict identity. Concurrency, affected-row counts and
chosen update expressions matter. Do not treat upsert as a universal replacement for
domain state-transition checks.
WATCH OUT
PostgreSQL conflict-target behavior differs from MySQL unique-key conflict handling.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which columns define the conflict?
Use the business's unique identifier, for example (tenant_id, external_payment_id), rather
than choosing any convenient column.

CHAPTER 11   •   DATA CHANGES, UPSERT AND DEDUPLICATION
QUESTION Q053
Why is SELECT-then-INSERT unsafe for
uniqueness?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Two transactions can both observe absence and attempt insertion; the
database constraint must arbitrate concurrent writers.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
A: no booking -> insert
B: no booking -> insert
UNIQUE(slot_id) decides whether both can exist
Request ➜ Guarded write ➜ Committed state
WHY THIS WORKS
Handle the conflict as a documented outcome or retry where appropriate. Locking one
nonexistent row is not a universal solution. For a request ID, persist the result/claim
under an appropriate transaction contract.
WATCH OUT
Application prechecks are not a substitute for UNIQUE.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you distinguish duplicate request from conflicting booking?
Use a unique idempotency/slot key; on conflict read the stored request hash and return
its prior result only if the new request matches.

pages.title: How do you remove duplicates deterministically?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 11   •   DATA CHANGES, UPSERT AND DEDUPLICATION
QUESTION Q054
How do you remove duplicates deterministically?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Identify candidates using ROW_NUMBER over the business identity, retain
one chosen key, then perform an engine-specific reviewed delete.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
SELECT contact_id,email,
 ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY email ORDER BY contact_id) AS n
FROM contacts;
-- n>1 are candidates, not automatically safe to delete.
Request ➜ Guarded write ➜ Committed state
WHY THIS WORKS
References, merged fields and audit requirements determine whether deletion is valid.
Use a migration workflow and enforce future uniqueness after cleanup. MySQL/
PostgreSQL delete-from-CTE syntax differs.
WATCH OUT
The minimum ID is not necessarily the best business record.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What if another table references the row being removed?
Update foreign-key references to the chosen survivor inside a safe transaction before
deleting duplicate rows; verify referential integrity.
PORTABLE SQL   •   POSTGRESQL 17   •   MYSQL 8.4 INNODB 060

pages.title: How do you prevent lost updates in a write?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 11   •   DATA CHANGES, UPSERT AND DEDUPLICATION
QUESTION Q055
How do you prevent lost updates in a write?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Use a resource-level atomic expression or an expected-version predicate
instead of blindly writing a stale value.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
UPDATE inventory SET available=available-1
WHERE item_id=:id AND available>0;
Request ➜ Guarded write ➜ Committed state
WHY THIS WORKS
Inspect affected rows: one means the guarded mutation succeeded, zero means
unavailable/missing under the contract. A broader workflow may still require a
transaction and stable request identity. Version checks fit replacing complex stale state.
WATCH OUT
Atomic stock decrement alone does not deduplicate repeated requests.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you handle a timeout after the update committed?
Use a stable request ID, check transaction outcome and read current version/state
before retrying. A timeout does not prove rollback.

pages.title: What is normalization and why use it?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 12   •   NORMALIZATION AND SCHEMA DESIGN
QUESTION Q056
What is normalization and why use it?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
Normalization organizes facts according to dependencies to reduce update,
insert and delete anomalies.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
Store department name once in departments
employees reference department_id
Entity keys ➜ Dependencies ➜ Normalized tables
WHY THIS WORKS
Duplicating department names across employee rows can create conflicting copies.
Normalization improves representation, while constraints and transaction logic enforce
actual integrity. Query needs may justify deliberate derived read models.
WATCH OUT
More tables do not automatically mean a better model.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What update anomaly does the split remove?
The split stops one customer's detail being repeated in many independent rows, so
updating a customer name no longer requires editing each order.

pages.title: What do 1NF, 2NF and 3NF mean?
pages.fullText:
SQL / ZERO TO HERO / PREMIUM INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK
CHAPTER 12   •   NORMALIZATION AND SCHEMA DESIGN
QUESTION Q057
What do 1NF, 2NF and 3NF mean?
SHORT INTERVIEW ANSWER
In the common teaching model, 1NF avoids repeating groups, 2NF removes
partial-key dependencies, and 3NF removes inappropriate transitive
dependencies of non-key facts.
TRACE THE EXAMPLE
Enrollment(student_id,course_id,student_name,grade)
student_name depends on student_id, not the whole composite key
Entity keys ➜ Dependencies ➜ Normalized tables
WHY THIS WORKS
Treat 2NF/3NF definitions through candidate keys and functional dependencies, not
merely the presence of foreign keys. Atomicity of a value depends on the modeled
domain. Decompose carefully and preserve correct joins/constraints.
WATCH OUT
A single-column surrogate key does not cure all business dependency anomalies.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which relation should own student_name?
student_name belongs to Students keyed by student_id, not repeated on each enrollment
relationship.
