pages.title: What is the difference between a tag and a digest?
pages.fullText:
FOUNDATION CHAPTER 04 — Images, tags, digests and registries
What is the difference between a tag and a
digest?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A tag is a mutable name; a digest identifies specific manifest content, including
an image or multi-platform image index.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Mutable name: tag ➜ Content hash: digest ➜ Release identity
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A registry owner can move stable to a new release. Recording a digest identifies the exact published
content that was selected. An index digest can identify multiple platform variants; an individual manifest
digest identifies one variant.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What extra evidence would you require before deploying a pinned image?
A. Require trusted publisher/signature or provenance evidence, a reviewed SBOM and
vulnerability findings, correct platform, license policy, and successful image tests.
⚠ WATCH OUT A digest establishes content identity, not publisher trust, freshness or absence of
vulnerabilities.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 15
Q016
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker pull nginx:stable
docker image inspect nginx:stable \
  --format '{{json .RepoDigests}}'
docker pull REGISTRY/TEAM/APP@sha256:DIGEST_HEX
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 21
pages.shortAnswer:
A tag is a mutable name; a digest identifies specific manifest content, including
an image or multi-platform image index.
pages.visualFlow: Mutable name: tag ➜ Content hash: digest ➜ Release identity

docker image inspect nginx:stable \
  --format '{{json .RepoDigests}}'
docker pull REGISTRY/TEAM/APP@sha256:DIGEST_HEX

content that was selected. An index digest can identify multiple platform variants; an individual manifest
digest identifies one variant.
pages.pitfall:
A digest establishes content identity, not publisher trust, freshness or absence of
vulnerabilities.

A. Require trusted publisher/signature or provenance evidence, a reviewed SBOM and
vulnerability findings, correct platform, license policy, and successful image tests.

pages.title: Does latest mean the newest or safest image?
pages.fullText:
FOUNDATION CHAPTER 04 — Images, tags, digests and registries
Does latest mean the newest or safest
image?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
No. latest is a conventional tag whose meaning is chosen by the publisher; Docker
does not compare all versions to calculate it.
↳ Draw this in the interview
latest = just a tag ➜ Review version & digest ➜ Known rollback target
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
An absent tag commonly selects latest, but that name may lag a release or point to an unsuitable build. A
release tag improves readability; an enforced immutable tag or recorded digest improves reproducibility.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you identify a rollback target reliably?
A. Record the exact working image digest and release configuration in your deployment record.
Roll back to that digest, not whatever a mutable tag means later.
⚠ WATCH OUT A version-looking tag is also mutable unless the registry or workflow prevents
reassignment.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 15
Q017
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker pull TEAM/APP:latest
docker pull TEAM/APP:1.7.0
# Either tag can be moved if registry policy permits.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 22

No. latest is a conventional tag whose meaning is chosen by the publisher; Docker
does not compare all versions to calculate it.

pages.title: What are image layers, and why are they useful?
pages.fullText:
FOUNDATION CHAPTER 04 — Images, tags, digests and registries
What are image layers, and why are they
useful?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Layers represent reusable filesystem changes; images reference those layers
together with configuration metadata.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Base image layers ➜ Reuse unchanged data ➜ Faster build and pull
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Shared layers reduce transfer and storage when builds reuse common content. A later deletion can hide a
file in the resulting filesystem while its bytes remain in an earlier layer. Some instructions alter metadata
rather than add filesystem content.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why should dependency downloads happen before frequently changing source code?
A. Stable dependency files are copied first so Docker can reuse the dependency layer when only
source code changes, avoiding unnecessary package downloads.
⚠ WATCH OUT history is not a complete audit of all file contents or of the supply chain. Never bake a
credential into a layer and expect a later delete to erase it.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 16
Q018
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker image history IMAGE
docker image inspect IMAGE
# Two related images may reuse a common base layer.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 23

Layers represent reusable filesystem changes; images reference those layers
together with configuration metadata.

pages.title: What is the difference between save/load and export/import?
pages.fullText:
FOUNDATION CHAPTER 04 — Images, tags, digests and registries
What is the difference between save/load
and export/import?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
save/load transfers image data and tags; export/import operates on a container
filesystem snapshot with different metadata and history behavior.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Image archive: save/load ➜ Container filesystem: export ➜ Separate database backup
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
An image archive suits an offline image transfer. A container export is not equivalent to its original
layered image and does not include mounted volume contents. Importing a filesystem also does not
automatically restore the original runtime configuration.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you move a service image and its database data separately?
A. Move the image using a registry or `docker save/load`. Back up and restore database data
with database-aware tools and separately verify integrity.
⚠ WATCH OUT Neither path is a substitute for application-consistent database backup. Protect archives that
may contain private code or configuration.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 16
Q019
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker image save -o app-image.tar TEAM/APP:1.7.0
docker image load -i app-image.tar
# Registry push/pull is normally preferable for delivery.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 24
pages.shortAnswer:
save/load transfers image data and tags; export/import operates on a container
filesystem snapshot with different metadata and history behavior.

pages.title: How do you push a local image to a private registry?
pages.fullText:
FOUNDATION CHAPTER 04 — Images, tags, digests and registries
How do you push a local image to a private
registry?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Authenticate to the registry, tag the image under its repository name, push it, and
record the resulting content identity.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Authenticate to registry ➜ Tag and push image ➜ Record pushed digest
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The registry hostname and repository path identify the destination. Authentication and repository write
permission must both be valid. CI should use a protected credential mechanism and capture the digest
produced by publishing.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why should a CI release deploy the pushed digest rather than rebuild from source?
A. A second build might resolve changed base tags, dependencies, or build inputs. Promoting the
tested digest deploys exactly the reviewed artifact.
⚠ WATCH OUT A local image name does not create a remote repository or grant access. Avoid embedding
credentials in command history or image build arguments.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 17
Q020
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker login registry.example.com
docker tag dk-app:local registry.example.com/team/app:1.7.0
docker push registry.example.com/team/app:1.7.0
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 25

record the resulting content identity.

pages.title: What are FROM, WORKDIR, COPY and RUN used for?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 05 — Dockerfile instructions and build context
What are FROM, WORKDIR, COPY and RUN
used for?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
FROM selects a stage base, WORKDIR sets a path, COPY adds files from a source,
and RUN executes a build-time command.
↳ Draw this in the interview
FROM sets base ➜ COPY + RUN build files ➜ ENTRYPOINT runs server
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The Dockerfile assumes target/app.jar exists in the build context. The test runs during image
construction, not whenever a container starts. WORKDIR also creates a missing directory as part of its
defined behavior.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which instruction should launch the server at container startup?
A. Use exec-form `ENTRYPOINT` for the main server command; use `CMD` for optional default
arguments. `RUN` is for image build time.
⚠ WATCH OUT RUN java -jar app.jar starts the server during the build and is usually the wrong lifecycle for
a web application.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 18
Q021
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre
WORKDIR /app
COPY target/app.jar /app/app.jar
RUN test -r /app/app.jar
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 26

and RUN executes a build-time command.

pages.title: What is the build context, and what does .dockerignore do?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 05 — Dockerfile instructions and build context
What is the build context, and what
does .dockerignore do?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
The context is the set of build inputs made available to the builder; .dockerignore
removes matching inputs from that context.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Select build context ➜ Apply .dockerignore ➜ COPY allowed inputs
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A source-build context can exclude old artifacts and private local files. A prebuilt-JAR workflow needs a
different ignore policy. COPY cannot simply reach an arbitrary parent directory outside the selected
context.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why can a working local build fail when CI uses a smaller context?
A. CI may exclude files that a broad local context supplied accidentally. Compare context paths,
`.dockerignore`, COPY sources, and required build artifacts.
⚠ WATCH OUT .gitignore and .dockerignore serve different tools. A .gitignored secret can still enter the
Docker context unless excluded there too.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 18
Q022
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
# .dockerignore
.git
.env
secrets/
target/
# For a Dockerfile that copies a prebuilt JAR, do NOT ignore target/.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 27

The context is the set of build inputs made available to the builder; .dockerignore
removes matching inputs from that context.

pages.title: How are COPY and ADD different?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 05 — Dockerfile instructions and build context
How are COPY and ADD different?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
COPY performs explicit copying; ADD also supports capabilities such as fetching
supported remote sources and extracting local tar archives.
↳ Draw this in the interview
COPY normal file copy ➜ ADD extra features ➜ Verify input trust
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Explicit copying makes application packaging easier to audit. If remote retrieval is required, account for
source identity, validation and cache behavior rather than hiding that decision in a generic instruction.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you verify the bytes of a downloaded dependency?
A. Pin the expected SHA-256 hash or signed release and verify it during the build. Prefer trusted
artifact repositories rather than an unchecked URL.
⚠ WATCH OUT Do not assume a remote archive is extracted like a local tar archive. Features and flags can
depend on the Dockerfile frontend version.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 19
Q023
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
COPY app.jar /app/app.jar
COPY config/ /app/config/
# Choose ADD only when its extra source behavior is intentional.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 28

supported remote sources and extracting local tar archives.

pages.title: Does EXPOSE make a port reachable from the host?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 05 — Dockerfile instructions and build context
Does EXPOSE make a port reachable from
the host?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
No. EXPOSE documents intended container ports; runtime publication or another
network path provides reachability.
↳ Draw this in the interview
EXPOSE = documentation ➜ -p binds host port ➜ Service must listen
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The application must actually listen on port 8080 inside the container. The runtime mapping directs host
port 18080 to it. Same-network containers usually connect directly to the container port without a host
mapping.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Can two containers expose 8080 while one host cannot bind 18080 twice?
A. Yes. Each container has its own port 8080. Host port 18080 is one binding, so use different
host ports or a reverse proxy.
⚠ WATCH OUT Writing EXPOSE 8080 does not change a Spring server configured to listen on 9090.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 19

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
# Dockerfile
EXPOSE 8080
# Runtime on a local development machine
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:18080:8080 TEAM/APP:1.7.0
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 29

No. EXPOSE documents intended container ports; runtime publication or another
network path provides reachability.

pages.title: What is the difference between ARG and ENV?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 05 — Dockerfile instructions and build context
What is the difference between ARG and
ENV?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
ARG is a build-time variable; ENV establishes image environment defaults that
runtime configuration can override.
↳ Draw this in the interview
ARG at build time ➜ ENV default at runtime ➜ Use proper secrets
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
APP_VERSION helps label the build; SERVER_PORT is available to the application at startup. ARG scope
matters across stages and before FROM. Neither instruction is designed to safely hide credentials.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Should a database password be a build input or a runtime dependency?
A. It is a runtime dependency: inject it through an approved secret provider or mounted secret
at startup. Never bake production passwords into images or build args.
⚠ WATCH OUT Build arguments and environment values can surface in image metadata, history, provenance
or process configuration. Use dedicated secret mechanisms.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 20
Q025
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
ARG APP_VERSION=dev
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version=$APP_VERSION
ENV SERVER_PORT=8080
# Runtime override:
docker run -e SERVER_PORT=9090 TEAM/APP:1.7.0
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 30

ARG is a build-time variable; ENV establishes image environment defaults that
runtime configuration can override.

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version=$APP_VERSION
ENV SERVER_PORT=8080
# Runtime override:
docker run -e SERVER_PORT=9090 TEAM/APP:1.7.0
pages.explanation:
APP_VERSION helps label the build; SERVER_PORT is available to the application at startup. ARG scope
matters across stages and before FROM. Neither instruction is designed to safely hide credentials.
pages.pitfall:
Build arguments and environment values can surface in image metadata, history, provenance
or process configuration. Use dedicated secret mechanisms.
pages.followup:
Should a database password be a build input or a runtime dependency?
A. It is a runtime dependency: inject it through an approved secret provider or mounted secret
at startup. Never bake production passwords into images or build args.

pages.title: How do ENTRYPOINT and CMD work together?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 06 — ENTRYPOINT, CMD, PID 1 and signals
How do ENTRYPOINT and CMD work
together?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
ENTRYPOINT supplies the executable; CMD supplies a default command or default
arguments depending on the chosen configuration.
↳ Draw this in the interview
ENTRYPOINT executable ➜ CMD default arguments ➜ docker run overrides CMD
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Arguments after the image replace CMD but keep the exec-form ENTRYPOINT. The application receives
the supplied Spring argument. This makes a fixed executable configurable without a shell wrapper.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What does --entrypoint change, and when is it useful?
A. `--entrypoint` replaces the image's default executable. Use it for an authorized one-off
diagnostic or alternate program, taking care with arguments and privileges.
⚠ WATCH OUT If an image has only CMD, arguments after the image can replace the entire command.
Always inspect the image's actual defaults.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 21

ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]
CMD ["--server.port=8080"]
# docker run IMAGE --server.port=9090
# Starts: java -jar /app/app.jar --server.port=9090
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO

pages.title: Why is exec form often preferred for a server?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 06 — ENTRYPOINT, CMD, PID 1 and signals
Why is exec form often preferred for a
server?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Exec form avoids an implicit shell and makes the configured executable directly
receive container-level signals in the normal setup.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Exec-form Java PID 1 ➜ Receive SIGTERM ➜ Graceful stop
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Direct Java startup removes a common reason that SIGTERM never reaches the JVM. Shell form can have
different argument and signal behavior, especially when a wrapper launches children without replacing
itself.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why can a container stop take exactly its forced-kill timeout?
A. The main process may ignore SIGTERM, a wrapper may not forward it, or shutdown may
exceed the grace period. Docker then sends SIGKILL at the deadline.
⚠ WATCH OUT Exec form does not perform shell expansion: ["echo", "$NAME"] prints a literal argument. Use
application configuration or a deliberate wrapper when needed.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 22
Q027
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]
# Shell form adds a shell layer:
# ENTRYPOINT java -jar /app/app.jar
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 32

receive container-level signals in the normal setup.

pages.title: What is special about PID 1 in a Linux container?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 06 — ENTRYPOINT, CMD, PID 1 and signals
What is special about PID 1 in a Linux
container?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
The main process occupies the container's initial process role and must handle
termination and any child-process lifecycle responsibilities it creates.
↳ Draw this in the interview
PID 1 handles lifecycle ➜ Child processes exit ➜ Reap zombies if present
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
exec replaces the wrapper so Java becomes the main application process. --init inserts a small init process
that can forward signals and reap orphaned children. These solve distinct process-management concerns.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you detect accumulating zombie child processes?
A. Inspect process states with `docker top` or host process tools; zombie children usually appear
with state `Z`. Check whether PID 1 reaps exited children.
⚠ WATCH OUT A Java server that does not spawn unmanaged children may not require an extra init. Adding
one does not repair an application that ignores shutdown.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 22
Q028
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker run --init IMAGE
# If a wrapper is needed:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
exec java -jar /app/app.jar "$@"
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 33

The main process occupies the container's initial process role and must handle
termination and any child-process lifecycle responsibilities it creates.

# If a wrapper is needed:

set -eu
exec java -jar /app/app.jar "$@"

pages.title: How do you pass JVM options without breaking arguments?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 06 — ENTRYPOINT, CMD, PID 1 and signals
How do you pass JVM options without
breaking arguments?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Use Java's supported option environment variables or a wrapper with deliberate
argument handling; do not expect shell expansion inside an exec array.
↳ Draw this in the interview
JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS ➜ JVM parses flags ➜ Verify effective heap
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The JVM consumes JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS when it initializes; the application still receives normal
command arguments. The literal $JAVA_OPTS in an exec array would not be expanded into JVM flags.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you verify the heap size used inside the running container?
A. Inspect `jcmd <pid> VM.flags` or `java -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version` inside a suitable image,
plus container cgroup values and runtime telemetry.
⚠ WATCH OUT Supported option variables have specific parsing and applicability. Avoid secrets in JVM flags
and confirm effective settings on the exact JDK.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 23
Q029
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]
docker run -e JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS='-Xms128m -Xmx384m' IMAGE
# Do not write ["java", "$JAVA_OPTS", "-jar", "app.jar"].
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 34

argument handling; do not expect shell expansion inside an exec array.

pages.title: Why should a Spring Boot container stop gracefully?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 06 — ENTRYPOINT, CMD, PID 1 and signals
Why should a Spring Boot container stop
gracefully?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Graceful shutdown drains accepted work and closes resources before the runtime
forcibly ends the process.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Stop accepting new work ➜ Drain active requests ➜ Close safely before kill
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The JVM must receive the stop signal, and the platform must withdraw traffic while the application drains.
Spring's timeout is per shutdown phase; total shutdown and load-balancer propagation can need
additional time.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What happens to an in-flight database transaction when the process is finally killed?
A. If the process is killed before commit, the database ordinarily rolls back the open transaction
when its connection closes. External effects may still need reconciliation.
⚠ WATCH OUT Graceful HTTP shutdown does not automatically make Kafka processing, scheduled jobs or
external side effects exactly once.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 23
Q030
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
# application.properties - supported Spring Boot baseline
server.shutdown=graceful
spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase=20s
# Docker gives the process a larger total budget:
docker stop --time 45 APP_CONTAINER
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 35

Graceful shutdown drains accepted work and closes resources before the runtime
forcibly ends the process.
pages.visualFlow: Stop accepting new work ➜ Drain active requests ➜ Close safely before kill

spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase=20s

pages.title: How does Docker build caching work?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 07 — BuildKit, caching and build performance
How does Docker build caching work?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
The builder reuses results when relevant instruction inputs match its cache; a
changed dependency can invalidate later dependent steps.
↳ Draw this in the interview
COPY stable POM ➜ Cache dependencies ➜ COPY changing src
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Changing only source can reuse the earlier dependency step, while changing pom.xml invalidates it. A
cache mount preserves downloaded artifacts between builds without copying that cache into the final
image by itself.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you measure whether this change actually speeds up CI?
A. Record cold and warm CI build durations and cache-hit output over repeated representative
changes. Compare medians, total pipeline time, and correctness.
⚠ WATCH OUT dependency:go-offline does not guarantee every project will later build without network access.
Maven extensions and profiles can introduce extra inputs.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 24
Q031
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
COPY pom.xml ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.m2 \
    mvn -B dependency:go-offline
COPY src/ src/
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.m2 mvn -B package
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 36
pages.shortAnswer:
The builder reuses results when relevant instruction inputs match its cache; a
changed dependency can invalidate later dependent steps.
pages.visualFlow: COPY stable POM ➜ Cache dependencies ➜ COPY changing src
pages.codeExample:

RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.m2 \
    mvn -B dependency:go-offline
COPY src/ src/
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.m2 mvn -B package
pages.explanation:
Changing only source can reuse the earlier dependency step, while changing pom.xml invalidates it. A
cache mount preserves downloaded artifacts between builds without copying that cache into the final
image by itself.
pages.pitfall:
dependency:go-offline does not guarantee every project will later build without network access.
Maven extensions and profiles can introduce extra inputs.

changes. Compare medians, total pipeline time, and correctness.

pages.title: Why is COPY . . near the start of a Dockerfile often inefficient?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 07 — BuildKit, caching and build performance
Why is COPY . . near the start of a
Dockerfile often inefficient?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
It makes unrelated context changes inputs to expensive downstream build steps.
↳ Draw this in the interview
COPY all files first ➜ Cache invalidated ➜ Split stable vs changing
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A changed README can cause a rebuild if it is included in the broad copy. Copying the required build
descriptors first and source later narrows invalidation, provided all required project files are included.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which files must a multi-module Maven dependency step receive?
A. Copy the root POM, module POMs, parent descriptors, Maven wrapper/config, and any
version catalogs or files used for dependency resolution.
⚠ WATCH OUT Incorrectly excluding generated sources or parent POMs makes the optimization fail. Correct
inputs matter more than a high cache-hit percentage.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 25
Q032
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
# Less selective:
COPY . .
RUN mvn -B package
# Better structure separates stable build files from changing source.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 37

pages.title: Does a cached RUN automatically refresh remote package versions?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 07 — BuildKit, caching and build performance
Does a cached RUN automatically refresh
remote package versions?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
No. Reusing a cached result does not rerun its network requests just because a
repository changed.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Cached RUN is not rerun ➜ --pull refreshes base ➜ Pin deps for repeatability
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
--pull checks referenced image sources for updates. --no-cache avoids reusing ordinary build-step results.
Neither alone pins application dependencies or makes two builds bit-for-bit reproducible.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How do you combine update automation with reproducible release builds?
A. Use automated dependency/base updates that create reviewed changes; pin dependencies
and digests for release builds, then test and promote one exact image.
⚠ WATCH OUT Persistent cache mounts may still contain downloaded artifacts. Floating package versions
can change during a fresh build.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 25

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker build --pull -t dk-app:fresh-base .
docker build --no-cache --pull -t dk-app:rebuild .
# --pull and --no-cache address different sources of reuse.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 38
pages.shortAnswer:
No. Reusing a cached result does not rerun its network requests just because a
repository changed.

docker build --no-cache --pull -t dk-app:rebuild .

pages.title: How do build secrets differ from copying a secret file?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 07 — BuildKit, caching and build performance
How do build secrets differ from copying a
secret file?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A BuildKit secret mount makes a secret available to a selected build step without
deliberately adding it as ordinary image content.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Temporary secret mount ➜ Maven uses credential ➜ Do not copy secret to image
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The build step reads Maven credentials from its temporary secret mount. The final image should contain
the application artifact, not settings.xml. The command must still avoid writing the secret into logs or
generated files.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you force a credential-sensitive build step to rerun safely?
A. Change a non-secret cache-busting version argument or use `--no-cache` for the relevant
rebuild. Never put the secret content in an ARG or build log.
⚠ WATCH OUT Secret rotation alone does not invalidate a cached step. Secret mounts reduce exposure but
do not make a malicious build trustworthy.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 26

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=maven_settings,required=true \
    mvn -B -s /run/secrets/maven_settings package
docker build --secret id=maven_settings,src=settings.xml .
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 39

deliberately adding it as ordinary image content.

pages.title: How can ephemeral CI workers share build cache?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 07 — BuildKit, caching and build performance
How can ephemeral CI workers share build
cache?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Import and export cache through a supported external backend, while keeping
cache identity and permissions separate from release identity.
↳ Draw this in the interview
CI worker imports cache ➜ Build uses cached steps ➜ Push approved image digest
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A new worker can reuse prior results instead of rebuilding everything. The cache reference is an
optimization artifact; the published application digest remains the release identity. Backend support
depends on builder configuration.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What prevents two concurrent jobs from replacing each other's cache?
A. Use cache keys unique to branch/build, immutable keys where possible, and restricted write
permissions. Promote a selected cache only with controlled updates.
⚠ WATCH OUT Do not grant untrusted pull-request builds permission to overwrite trusted caches or release
tags. Cache misses must not break correctness.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 26

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE

  --cache-from type=registry,ref=REGISTRY/APP:buildcache \
  --cache-to type=registry,ref=REGISTRY/APP:buildcache,mode=max \
  --tag REGISTRY/APP:BUILD_ID --push .

cache identity and permissions separate from release identity.

pages.title: What is a multi-stage build?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 08 — Multi-stage builds and Java packaging
What is a multi-stage build?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
It uses separate build stages and selectively transfers outputs into a final runtime
stage.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Build stage compiles ➜ Copy final JAR only ➜ Small runtime stage
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Maven and source files stay in the build stage unless explicitly copied to the final stage. This example
requires the Maven project to produce target/app.jar and run appropriate tests.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which artifacts would you keep for debugging without shipping them in the runtime
image?
A. Keep test reports, SBOMs, JAR checksums, symbol/debug artifacts, and build logs in
protected CI storage. Ship only the necessary runtime outputs.
⚠ WATCH OUT Multi-stage packaging does not prove that the JAR is valid or that unused secrets never
entered intermediate build output.

WORKDIR /src
COPY pom.xml .
COPY src/ src/
RUN mvn -B package

COPY --from=build /src/target/app.jar /app/app.jar
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 41

It uses separate build stages and selectively transfers outputs into a final runtime
stage.

pages.title: Should a Java runtime image use a JDK, JRE, distroless base or jlink?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 08 — Multi-stage builds and Java packaging
Should a Java runtime image use a JDK,
JRE, distroless base or jlink?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Choose the smallest maintained runtime that satisfies application modules, native
dependencies, observability and operational needs.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Runtime requirements ➜ Select JDK/JRE/jlink ➜ Diagnostic trade-off
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A JRE-based server can run an executable Spring JAR without a compiler. A stripped runtime may need
explicit modules, CA certificates or native libraries. Reduced package count can help, but support and
diagnosis remain design requirements.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you investigate a JVM issue when jcmd is absent?
A. Collect JVM metrics, JFR or thread dumps via supported attach/debug tools or a separate
debug image; temporarily reproduce with a diagnostic JDK image.
⚠ WATCH OUT A shell-free image cannot run a shell-based health check. jlink does not automatically
discover every dynamically loaded dependency.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 28
Q037
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
JDK image:        compiler and diagnostic tools available
JRE image:        runtime-focused packaging
Custom jlink:     selected modules and explicit maintenance
Distroless:       reduced OS tools; inspect by other means
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 42
pages.shortAnswer:
Choose the smallest maintained runtime that satisfies application modules, native
dependencies, observability and operational needs.
pages.visualFlow: Runtime requirements ➜ Select JDK/JRE/jlink ➜ Diagnostic trade-off

JRE image:        runtime-focused packaging
Custom jlink:     selected modules and explicit maintenance

explicit modules, CA certificates or native libraries. Reduced package count can help, but support and

A shell-free image cannot run a shell-based health check. jlink does not automatically
discover every dynamically loaded dependency.
pages.followup:
How would you investigate a JVM issue when jcmd is absent?
A. Collect JVM metrics, JFR or thread dumps via supported attach/debug tools or a separate
debug image; temporarily reproduce with a diagnostic JDK image.

pages.title: How do you run a Java container as a non- root user?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 08 — Multi-stage builds and Java packaging
How do you run a Java container as a non-
root user?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Set a runtime UID and GID, make application files readable, and provide writable
directories only where required.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Set numeric UID / GID ➜ Grant needed file access ➜ Run Java as non-root
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Linux can run this process with a numeric identity even without a named account. The application needs
readable code and a writable temp location. Mounted files are governed by their actual ownership and
mount permissions.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you fix a permission error without making the whole application root?
A. Check numeric UID/GID and actual mount permissions. Grant only the necessary directory
access using ownership, group IDs, or a dedicated writable mount.
⚠ WATCH OUT COPY --chown changes copied image files, not arbitrary host bind mounts. Applications that
look up a named user may need an account entry.

WORKDIR /app
COPY --chown=10001:10001 target/app.jar /app/app.jar
USER 10001:10001
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO

pages.title: Why avoid COPY target/*.jar app.jar without checking the outputs?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 08 — Multi-stage builds and Java packaging
Why avoid COPY target/*.jar app.jar without
checking the outputs?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Builds can produce multiple JARs, and a wildcard can select unintended artifacts
or fail when several sources target a single filename.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Test exact app.jar ➜ COPY named artifact ➜ Verify released bytes
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
An explicit output name makes the Dockerfile contract clear. Spring repackage plugins and project
conventions can produce auxiliary files, so inspect actual build output rather than guessing from a
wildcard.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would CI verify that the copied JAR came from the tested build?
A. CI should test the JAR, compute its SHA-256, and copy that same named artifact into the
image. Check the hash or build attestation after packaging.
⚠ WATCH OUT The example is a POM fragment, not a complete Maven project. Multi-module builds need the
correct module artifact path.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 29

  <finalName>app</finalName>
</build>
# Dockerfile
COPY target/app.jar /app/app.jar

pages.title: How are Spring Boot buildpacks different from a hand-written Dockerfile?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 08 — Multi-stage builds and Java packaging
How are Spring Boot buildpacks different
from a hand-written Dockerfile?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Buildpacks automate supported application detection and runtime image
assembly; a Dockerfile gives direct control over packaging instructions.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Buildpacks automate layers ➜ Dockerfile gives control ➜ Test final image
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Buildpacks can standardize Java runtime selection and image layers across teams. A Dockerfile can handle
specialized native libraries or startup contracts explicitly. Both approaches need maintained bases and a
reproducible delivery policy.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which approach would you standardize for twenty Spring services, and why?
A. For standard Spring services, use approved buildpacks when they fit: simpler shared updates.
Use a reviewed Dockerfile for special native or startup needs.
⚠ WATCH OUT Plugin version, builder and run image affect the result. Neither approach removes the need to
test the produced image and record its digest.

  -Dspring-boot.build-image.imageName=dk-app:local
# Dockerfile alternative:
docker build -t dk-app:local .
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 45

assembly; a Dockerfile gives direct control over packaging instructions.

pages.title: What is the difference between a volume and a bind mount?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 09 — Persistent storage and mount behavior
What is the difference between a volume and
a bind mount?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A volume is managed by Docker; a bind mount exposes a specific path from the
engine host inside the container.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Container writable layer ➜ Named volume = separate life ➜ Bind path = host files
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The named volume outlives the temporary writer container. A bind mount connects directly to an existing
host path, useful for development or managed config files. The storage location belongs to the engine
host.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which mount would you choose for a disposable source checkout versus database data?
A. Use a bind mount for disposable development source files; choose a managed named volume
or dedicated persistent storage for database files, plus backups.
⚠ WATCH OUT Remote engines and Desktop file sharing change how host paths are reached. A bind mount
can allow modification of host files unless restricted.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 30
Q041
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker volume create dk-q-data
docker run --rm --mount type=volume,src=dk-q-data,dst=/data \
  alpine:3.22 sh -c 'echo hello > /data/message'
# Bind example: --mount type=bind,src=HOST_PATH,dst=/config,readonly
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 46
pages.shortAnswer:
A volume is managed by Docker; a bind mount exposes a specific path from the
engine host inside the container.
pages.visualFlow: Container writable layer ➜ Named volume = separate life ➜ Bind path = host files
pages.codeExample:

  alpine:3.22 sh -c 'echo hello > /data/message'

can allow modification of host files unless restricted.

pages.title: What happens when a mount targets a non- empty image directory?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 09 — Persistent storage and mount behavior
What happens when a mount targets a non-
empty image directory?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
The mount obscures the image content at that path; empty named volumes also
have defined initial copy behavior unless disabled.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Image directory has files ➜ Mount covers directory ➜ Visible data may differ
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A missing configuration file can be caused by the mount overlay rather than a broken COPY. Docker can
populate a fresh empty volume from existing container-path content; a bind mount does not perform that
volume initialization.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why might two deployments see different initial directory contents?
A. One deployment might mount a fresh volume that gets initial image content copied in; another
may mount an existing volume or host bind that hides the image files.
⚠ WATCH OUT Do not rely on volume initialization as an application migration system. Existing data and
volume-nocopy alter the outcome.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 31

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE

  --mount type=bind,src=HOST_CONFIG,dst=/app/config,readonly \
  IMAGE
# Files from /app/config in the image are hidden by this mount.

HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 47

have defined initial copy behavior unless disabled.

pages.title: What does tmpfs provide, and when is it appropriate?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 09 — Persistent storage and mount behavior
What does tmpfs provide, and when is it
appropriate?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A Linux tmpfs mount supplies temporary memory-backed filesystem storage
outside the container's writable image layer.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Use tmpfs for temporary data ➜ Files consume memory ➜ Discard when container ends
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The root filesystem is read-only but /tmp accepts temporary files. This suits scratch data that need not
survive a stop. Its capacity still contributes to host and applicable container memory pressure.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would a Java application that creates large temporary files behave with this limit?
A. Large temp files consume tmpfs memory and can hit the tmpfs or container memory limit.
Prefer bounded disk-backed temporary storage when files can be large.
⚠ WATCH OUT tmpfs is not durable storage or a guarantee that data never reaches swap. Availability and
behavior are platform-dependent.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 31
Q043
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker run --rm --read-only \
  --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=64m \
  alpine:3.22 sh -c 'echo scratch > /tmp/note'
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 48

outside the container's writable image layer.

pages.title: Why can a non-root container fail to write to a mounted directory?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 09 — Persistent storage and mount behavior
Why can a non-root container fail to write to
a mounted directory?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
The process UID/GID, mounted file ownership, permissions and security labels
must permit the operation.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Container UID ➜ Host mapped UID / GID ➜ Mount permission check
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
An image directory owned by UID 10001 does not make a replacement bind mount owned by that UID. On
Linux, user namespace mappings and SELinux policy may add further considerations.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How do user namespace mappings change the host UID you should inspect?
A. Container UIDs may map to different host UIDs under user-namespace remapping. Inspect `/
proc/*/uid_map` and effective ownership at the host mount path.
⚠ WATCH OUT chmod 777 or switching to root can mask the underlying mismatch. Avoid recursively
changing ownership of an unrelated host tree.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 32
Q044
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker inspect APP_CONTAINER --format '{{json .Mounts}}'
docker exec APP_CONTAINER id
# On the engine host, inspect the specific mount's ownership.
# Provide the needed directory permissions for UID 10001.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 49

must permit the operation.

pages.title: Does removing a container delete its named volume?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 09 — Persistent storage and mount behavior
Does removing a container delete its named
volume?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Normally no. Named volumes have a separate lifecycle and require explicit
removal when no longer needed.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Remove a container ➜ Volume still exists ➜ Restore test proves backup
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A replacement container can mount the retained volume. That separation enables persistence, but also
leaves data behind after a service is removed. Anonymous volume cleanup and Compose down -v have
additional rules.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you prove that restoring a backup recreates the required application state?
A. Restore the backup into a disposable clean environment, start the service, and verify data
counts, application invariants, permissions, and a known test transaction.
⚠ WATCH OUT Broad prune commands and down -v can remove valuable data. Volume persistence does not
imply backup, replication or disaster recovery.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 32
Q045
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker rm STOPPED_CONTAINER
docker volume inspect NAMED_VOLUME
# Only for disposable, identified data:
docker volume rm NAMED_VOLUME
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 50

removal when no longer needed.

pages.title: Why does localhost fail when one container calls another?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 10 — Networks, DNS and published ports
Why does localhost fail when one container
calls another?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
localhost refers to the calling container's own network namespace in the normal
isolated setup.
↳ Draw this in the interview
localhost = self ➜ DNS service name ➜ Container-to-container call
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The app connects to the service DNS name db and its internal port. It does not use the host's published
database port. A host-side test client instead uses a published endpoint appropriate to the host.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What address should a third container use to call the app?
A. Use the service name and container port, such as `http://api:8080`, when both containers
share a user-defined network. Do not use localhost.
⚠ WATCH OUT Sharing a network does not guarantee the database is accepting connections or that
authentication succeeds.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 33

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE

SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/orders
# Incorrect for a separate db container:
# jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/orders
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 51

localhost refers to the calling container's own network namespace in the normal
isolated setup.

pages.title: What is the difference between the default bridge and a user-defined bridge?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 10 — Networks, DNS and published ports
What is the difference between the default
bridge and a user-defined bridge?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
User-defined bridges provide automatic name-based discovery for connected
containers and a configurable grouping boundary.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Public API network ➜ Private DB network ➜ Restrict DB reachability
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The client resolves dk-q-web through Docker networking and reaches port 80 directly. Default bridge
containers do not receive the same automatic container-name discovery behavior. Compose usually
creates a project network for services.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why would you attach an API to two networks but keep a database on only one?
A. Put the API on both public-facing and private database networks. Keep the database only on
the private network to reduce direct reachability.
⚠ WATCH OUT Network membership is not fine-grained application authorization. Any reachable service
still needs its own access policy.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 34

docker run -d --name dk-q-web --network dk-q-net nginx:stable

  wget -qO- http://dk-q-web
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO

containers and a configurable grouping boundary.

pages.title: How do you interpret -p 127.0.0.1:18080:8080?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 10 — Networks, DNS and published ports
How do you interpret -p
127.0.0.1:18080:8080?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
It maps TCP port 18080 on the engine host's loopback address to port 8080 in
the container.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Host 127.0.0.1:18080 ➜ Container :8080 ➜ Proxy handles external clients
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The application listens inside on 8080, typically on 0.0.0.0. Omitting the host IP commonly publishes on all
host interfaces. For a remote engine, the mapping belongs to the remote host, not the local terminal.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you expose the service through a reverse proxy while restricting direct
access?
A. Bind the backend only on a private/loopback interface and publish the reverse proxy's
intended listener. Apply firewall, routing, and TLS policies at the proxy.
⚠ WATCH OUT Loopback publication had an L2 reachability caveat in Engine releases older than 28.0.0. Use a
maintained engine and verify the actual network boundary.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 34

  -p 127.0.0.1:18080:8080 IMAGE

INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 53

pages.title: Why can a published port still return connection refused?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 10 — Networks, DNS and published ports
Why can a published port still return
connection refused?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Publication cannot make an absent, incorrectly bound or incorrectly addressed
application listener work.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Socket bind and route ➜ Port publication ➜ Test TCP then HTTP
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Follow the path: host mapping, container target port, listener address, process readiness. If the process is
not ready, a correct mapping can still fail temporarily. Authentication or HTTP errors mean a different
layer was reached.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What is the difference between timeout, refused connection and HTTP 503?
A. Refused means a reachable endpoint actively has no listener; timeout suggests a dropped/
unreachable path; HTTP 503 means an HTTP server replied but cannot serve.
⚠ WATCH OUT Do not treat a successful ping as proof of a working HTTP or database connection. Test the
required protocol.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 35
Q049
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE

pages.title: When would you choose bridge, host, none or overlay networking?
pages.fullText:
BUILD / RUNTIME CHAPTER 10 — Networks, DNS and published ports
When would you choose bridge, host, none or
overlay networking?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Choose a driver for the needed isolation and reach: bridge for local groups, host
for intentional host-stack sharing, none for no normal network, overlay for
supported multi-host networking.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Bridge / host / none ➜ Overlay across hosts ➜ Route & secure traffic
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
An offline utility can use none; ordinary local service stacks fit a bridge. Host networking changes port
conflict and isolation behavior. Swarm overlay networking connects services across participating engines.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What additional routing and security decisions arise across multiple hosts?
A. Across hosts you need overlay/routed connectivity, service discovery, ingress, firewall rules,
encrypted traffic, and policies controlling service-to-service access.
⚠ WATCH OUT Desktop host-network support and operating-system behavior require version-specific checking.
Driver choice alone does not provide encryption or a complete network policy.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 35

pages.title: What does Docker Compose do?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 11 — Docker Compose applications
What does Docker Compose do?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Compose describes and manages a related set of services, networks and volumes
using a declarative application configuration.
↳ Draw this in the interview
compose.yaml ➜ Services + networks ➜ Single-host application
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Compose creates the required objects and starts the service. A service definition can also declare a build,
environment and mounts. Current examples use the Compose plugin command with a space.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What operational responsibilities remain on a single-host Compose deployment?
A. You still manage host availability, backups, upgrades, security patches, monitoring, secrets,
capacity, and disaster recovery. Compose is not a full cluster orchestrator.
⚠ WATCH OUT A Compose service definition is not an automatic multi-host scheduler or high-availability plan.
An obsolete top-level version key is not needed in this guide's files.

pages.title: Does depends_on guarantee a database is ready?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 11 — Docker Compose applications
Does depends_on guarantee a database is
ready?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
The basic form orders startup; a health-conditioned dependency can wait for the
configured health check to pass.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Start dependency ➜ DB health status ➜ App schema readiness
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Waiting for PostgreSQL to accept connections reduces an initial race. It does not prove migrations
finished, credentials work for the app, or the database will stay available. A completed migration job can
use a different dependency condition.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you distinguish database readiness from application schema readiness?
A. Database readiness proves the server accepts suitable connections; schema readiness needs
a migration/version check verifying the tables and columns the app requires.
⚠ WATCH OUT Dependency-level restart behavior in Compose is distinct from the container's restart policy.
Check what operation triggers each.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 37

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE

  db:
    condition: service_healthy
# db must define a meaningful healthcheck.
# API connection retry still handles later database outages.

HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 57

configured health check to pass.

pages.title: What is the difference between up, start, restart and down in Compose?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 11 — Docker Compose applications
What is the difference between up, start,
restart and down in Compose?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
up reconciles the application and can recreate services; start starts existing
containers; restart restarts them; down removes the project's runtime objects.
↳ Draw this in the interview
compose up reconciles ➜ restart reuses configuration ➜ down tears down service
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Editing an environment value in YAML and running restart does not recreate the container with the new
configuration. up evaluates the desired definition; --build asks it to build eligible service images.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What command would you use after changing a port mapping?
A. Run `docker compose up -d` so Compose recreates services when configuration changes.
`restart` does not generally apply new port mappings.
⚠ WATCH OUT down normally preserves named volumes; down -v requests volume removal. A restart does
not pull or rebuild a new image by itself.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 37

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE

docker compose ps
docker compose logs --tail=100 web
# After a configuration change, normally use up again.

containers; restart restarts them; down removes the project's runtime objects.

pages.title: interpolation differ from container environment?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 11 — Docker Compose applications
How does Compose configuration
interpolation differ from container
environment?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Compose substitutes variables while reading YAML; service environment and
env_file determine variables passed into the container.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Compose interpolates variable ➜ Service environment mapping ➜ Application receives value
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A project .env file commonly supplies interpolation values, but it does not automatically inject every value
into every container. $$ can defer a dollar sign to a later container shell where appropriate.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why can a variable be visible to Compose but absent from the application?
A. Compose interpolation reads shell/.env values while rendering configuration. A variable
reaches the app only if the service's environment/secrets configuration passes it.
⚠ WATCH OUT config can print resolved sensitive values. Different sources have defined precedence; inspect
the final model in a safe environment.

    environment:

pages.title: Can you scale a Compose service with fixed names and published ports?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 11 — Docker Compose applications
Can you scale a Compose service with fixed
names and published ports?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Scaling works only when the configuration avoids collisions such as a fixed
container_name or one identical host port for every replica.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Replicate API ➜ Resolve host-port collision ➜ Shared state / idempotency
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Replica containers can listen on the same internal port because they have separate network stacks. The
host cannot bind one address/port pair three times. A proxy provides a stable client endpoint and chooses
a replica.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you handle HTTP sessions and scheduled jobs across three API replicas?
A. Use shared session storage or stateless tokens, and protect scheduled jobs with leader
election, partitioned ownership, or idempotent processing.
⚠ WATCH OUT Scaling a database service does not configure database replication. Horizontal capacity also
depends on shared state and downstream limits.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 38
Q055
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker compose up -d --scale api=3
# api must allow replicas: no fixed container_name.
# Put replicas behind a proxy instead of sharing one fixed host bind.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 60

pages.title: Why should one image serve multiple environments?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 12 — Configuration and secrets
Why should one image serve multiple
environments?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Promoting the same tested artifact separates code identity from environment-
specific configuration and reduces rebuild drift.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Build image once ➜ Inject env-specific config ➜ Promote same digest
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The executable content stays fixed while configuration changes. Environment-specific values can include
database endpoints and feature policy. Runtime configuration must still be validated before the service
accepts traffic.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which configuration values should be recorded in release evidence?
A. Record the image digest, env/config version, secret references, resource limits, networks,
mounts, health policy, and migration version for every release.
⚠ WATCH OUT A prod profile name is not an access-control mechanism. Startup overrides can change
behavior dramatically even with an identical digest.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 39

docker run -e SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod APP_IMAGE

specific configuration and reduces rebuild drift.

pages.title: Are environment variables a secure secret store?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 12 — Configuration and secrets
Are environment variables a secure secret
store?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
They are a convenient configuration channel, but authorized inspection, process
tooling and accidental logging can expose their values.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Runtime secret source ➜ Mount or inject at startup ➜ Rotate without rebuild
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Using a file avoids typing every value in the command, but the resulting variables remain part of container
configuration. Threat modeling must include who can inspect the daemon and the process.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you rotate a secret without publishing a new application image?
A. Place the new secret in a runtime secret provider or mounted file, then restart/refresh
affected services safely. The application image need not change.
⚠ WATCH OUT Do not paste docker inspect output containing secrets into support tickets. An env file still
needs access control and must stay out of source and build context.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 39
Q057
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker run --env-file local-settings.env IMAGE
# Appropriate for disposable local values with restricted file access.
# Prefer a platform secret facility for real deployment credentials.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 62

tooling and accidental logging can expose their values.

pages.title: How do Compose secrets reach a service?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 12 — Configuration and secrets
How do Compose secrets reach a service?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A granted secret is typically made available as a mounted file; the application
must explicitly read that file or support a corresponding file-based setting.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Compose secret file ➜ /run/secrets directory ➜ App reads data
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The PostgreSQL image understands its _FILE option and reads the mounted content. That is an image-
specific contract. Compose does not turn every arbitrary secret name into an environment variable
automatically.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How can a Spring application consume a mounted secret directory?
A. Mount the secret directory and configure Spring Boot to read config-tree properties, for
example `spring.config.import=optional:configtree:/run/secrets/`.
⚠ WATCH OUT Local Compose file-backed secrets are not the same as Swarm's managed encrypted secret
distribution. Protect the source file and the engine host.

    file: ./secrets/db_password.txt

pages.title: How can Spring Boot read file-mounted configuration secrets?
pages.fullText:

How can Spring Boot read file-mounted
configuration secrets?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A supported Spring Boot configuration tree import maps files in a directory into
configuration properties.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Mounted config file ➜ Spring config tree ➜ Refresh/restart policy
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The trailing slash marks a directory import. The optional prefix permits a missing directory, which can be
useful locally but may be wrong for mandatory production credentials. Choose file names that map to the
intended properties.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Would file replacement immediately refresh every Spring configuration property?

connection. Use a supported refresh strategy or rolling restart.
⚠ WATCH OUT A missing secret should fail startup when required. Restrict endpoint exposure and logs so
configuration values are not disclosed.

pages.title: How should secrets be rotated in a containerized service?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 12 — Configuration and secrets
How should secrets be rotated in a
containerized service?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Coordinate secret delivery, application reload or recreation, credential overlap and
verification; replacing bytes alone is not a universal reload mechanism.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Install new credential ➜ Shift connections safely ➜ Revoke old credential
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A connection pool may retain old authenticated sessions after a file changes. A staged rotation avoids a
sudden outage and lets you observe whether new connections use the intended credential. The exact
sequence depends on the credential provider.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you test rotation while the database has active traffic?
A. Introduce new credentials with an overlap window, rotate one replica at a time, test reads/
writes and connection recovery, then revoke the old secret.
⚠ WATCH OUT Avoid assuming every bind-mounted file update or Compose secret change is hot-reloaded. Do
not leave both credentials valid indefinitely.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 41

pages.title: What does a Docker HEALTHCHECK do?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 13 — Health checks, restart policies and shutdown
What does a Docker HEALTHCHECK do?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
It executes a probe and records a health status independently of whether the
container's main process is running.
↳ Draw this in the interview
HEALTHCHECK command ➜ healthy/unhealthy status ➜ Router must act on status
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Consecutive probe failures can mark the container unhealthy while its process keeps running. Inspect
probe output to distinguish a failing service from a missing curl executable or incorrect endpoint.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Who routes traffic away from an unhealthy instance in your deployment?
A. Docker records health status but does not automatically remove the instance from an
external load balancer. Compose/orchestrator/proxy must consume readiness or health
appropriately.
⚠ WATCH OUT A Docker health status by itself does not automatically restart an ordinary standalone
container. A controller must act if that behavior is required.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 42
Q061
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
# Only if curl exists in this image:
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/health || exit 1
docker inspect APP_CONTAINER --format '{{json .State.Health}}'
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 66

It executes a probe and records a health status independently of whether the
container's main process is running.

# Only if curl exists in this image:
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/health || exit 1
docker inspect APP_CONTAINER --format '{{json .State.Health}}'

probe output to distinguish a failing service from a missing curl executable or incorrect endpoint.

A Docker health status by itself does not automatically restart an ordinary standalone
container. A controller must act if that behavior is required.
pages.followup:
Who routes traffic away from an unhealthy instance in your deployment?
A. Docker records health status but does not automatically remove the instance from an
external load balancer. Compose/orchestrator/proxy must consume readiness or health
appropriately.

pages.title: How are liveness, readiness and startup checks different?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 13 — Health checks, restart policies and shutdown
How are liveness, readiness and startup
checks different?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Liveness asks whether restart can help; readiness asks whether traffic should be
admitted; startup allows initialization before normal failure decisions.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Startup probe ➜ Readiness probe ➜ Liveness probe
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
An unavailable shared database may make an API unready without making every JVM dead. Restarting all
instances during a dependency outage can worsen recovery. A slow first boot needs a realistic
initialization budget.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What should readiness return during graceful shutdown?
A. Readiness should become false before accepting new work is stopped, so the router drains
traffic while current requests can finish.
⚠ WATCH OUT One Docker HEALTHCHECK cannot express every orchestration policy. Actuator endpoint
availability and access rules must be configured and verified.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 43

Liveness:  is the process making progress?
Readiness: can this instance serve the required traffic?

pages.title: How do no, on-failure, always and unless- stopped restart policies differ?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 13 — Health checks, restart policies and shutdown
How do no, on-failure, always and unless-
stopped restart policies differ?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
They define restart behavior for exits and daemon lifecycle events, with important
handling for intentional stops.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Process exit ➜ Restart policy ➜ Independent health status
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
on-failure targets nonzero exits; always and unless-stopped provide broader restart behavior. Their
treatment of a deliberately stopped container across daemon restarts differs. They operate on exit state
rather than HTTP readiness.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why could a container be unhealthy with a restart count of zero?
A. A failed HEALTHCHECK changes health status, not necessarily process exit. Docker restart
policies react to container stopping, not health status alone.
⚠ WATCH OUT A restart policy is not multi-host failover and is unsuitable for a batch job that must not repeat
side effects. Apply backoff and diagnosis at the right layer.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 43

  --name dk-q-managed IMAGE
docker inspect dk-q-managed \
  --format '{{json .HostConfig.RestartPolicy}}'
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 68

handling for intentional stops.

pages.title: Why do services get stuck in a restart loop?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 13 — Health checks, restart policies and shutdown
Why do services get stuck in a restart loop?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A deterministic startup failure repeats because restart policy changes process
lifecycle, not its invalid inputs or broken dependencies.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Startup fails ➜ Container restarts ➜ Fix root cause, not loop
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A missing JAR, invalid JVM flag or required secret can make each attempt fail identically. Preserve
evidence, repair the configuration or artifact, and recreate with the intended inputs.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What should a migration job do if the schema is already updated?
A. A migration should be idempotent: check its applied version, verify state, and exit
successfully if the required schema change already exists.
⚠ WATCH OUT Repeated restarts can overwrite logs, consume CPU and repeat non-idempotent startup work.
Do not raise retry counts as the only repair.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 44

  --format 'exit={{.State.ExitCode}} restarts={{.RestartCount}}'

pages.title: What makes graceful deployment work end to end?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 13 — Health checks, restart policies and shutdown
What makes graceful deployment work end
to end?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Withdraw new traffic, allow in-flight work to finish within a budget, handle worker
shutdown, then terminate and verify the replacement.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Route new traffic away ➜ Finish in-flight work ➜ SIGTERM + reconciliation
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Correct signal forwarding is necessary but insufficient. Proxy connections, request durations, Kafka
acknowledgments and transaction boundaries all influence the outcome. Deployment verification must
cover user-visible errors and unfinished work.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you test shutdown during an order request that publishes an event?
A. Start an order request, trigger shutdown, and verify the accepted request completes or is
safely retried; inspect outbox records to prevent a lost event.
⚠ WATCH OUT A zero-downtime HTTP rollout cannot promise zero message redelivery or exactly-once
external effects. Design idempotency and recovery explicitly.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 44

Application: drain accepted work and close resources
Runtime: deliver signal; enforce final timeout
Deployment: confirm healthy replacement and observed behavior

shutdown, then terminate and verify the replacement.

pages.title: Why can a container be OOM-killed even when Java has free heap?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 14 — CPU, memory and JVM container behavior
Why can a container be OOM-killed even
when Java has free heap?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
The memory budget includes heap plus native allocations, thread stacks,
metaspace, direct buffers and other charged memory, not just live Java objects.
↳ Draw this in the interview
JVM heap + native memory ➜ Cgroup memory total ➜ Kernel may OOM kill
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The remaining space must cover the actual non-heap workload and any other processes. A process can be
killed by the kernel before Java can produce a heap dump or OutOfMemoryError. Measure peak memory
under representative load.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which evidence separates a Java heap failure from a cgroup memory kill?
A. Compare JVM OOM exceptions/heap dumps with `docker inspect` OOMKilled, cgroup
memory.events, RSS/native memory and host/kernel logs.
⚠ WATCH OUT The example is a budget sketch, not a safe universal ratio. Page cache and runtime
accounting also affect observed numbers.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 45
Q066
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker run --memory=512m \
  -e JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS='-Xms128m -Xmx320m' IMAGE
# Illustrative starting point: leaves 192 MiB outside max heap.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 71

metaspace, direct buffers and other charged memory, not just live Java objects.

pages.title: Do modern JVMs understand container resource limits?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 14 — CPU, memory and JVM container behavior
Do modern JVMs understand container
resource limits?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Supported modern JDKs on Linux detect relevant container CPU and memory
constraints, but exact behavior depends on JDK update, cgroup setup and flags.
↳ Draw this in the interview
JDK container awareness ➜ Read cgroup limits ➜ Set measured JVM options
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Inspect the JVM's reported limits and heap settings inside the constrained container. This is more reliable
than assuming an old Java 8 build behaves like a current Java 21 runtime.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you compare the exact JDK updates used in development and production?
A. Log `java -version` and inspect exact image digests in both places; compare
`UseContainerSupport`, heap defaults, CPU count and patch-level fixes.
⚠ WATCH OUT Host resource detection and container detection can differ across versions. Do not disable
container support without understanding the resulting sizing.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 46
Q067
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker run --rm --memory=512m --cpus=1 \
  eclipse-temurin:21-jre \
  java -XshowSettings:system -XshowSettings:vm -version

HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 72

constraints, but exact behavior depends on JDK update, cgroup setup and flags.

pages.title: How do -Xmx and MaxRAMPercentage differ?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 14 — CPU, memory and JVM container behavior
How do -Xmx and MaxRAMPercentage
differ?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Xmx explicitly caps heap size; MaxRAMPercentage participates in ergonomic heap
sizing from the JVM's detected available memory when an explicit heap maximum
is not supplied.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Heap size ➜ -Xmx or MaxRAMPercentage ➜ Leave native headroom
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A percentage can adapt one image to several memory limits; an explicit cap gives a direct budget. Small-
memory heuristics and other flags can affect the ergonomic result, so verify actual sizing rather than
multiplying blindly.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What changes if a health probe starts a second JVM in the same container?
A. Two JVMs share one container budget. A health JVM adds heap and native memory, so size
the main JVM to leave room for probes and other processes.
⚠ WATCH OUT Neither option caps all process memory. Setting heap near the container limit can leave too
little room for native use.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 46
Q068
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS='-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=60'
# Alternative explicit policy:
JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS='-Xmx320m'
# Inspect effective MaxHeapSize on the selected JDK.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 73

sizing from the JVM's detected available memory when an explicit heap maximum

pages.title: What is the difference between --cpus, -- cpu-shares and --cpuset-cpus?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 14 — CPU, memory and JVM container behavior
What is the difference between --cpus, --
cpu-shares and --cpuset-cpus?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
They represent CPU bandwidth limiting, relative scheduling weight and allowed
CPU placement respectively, subject to platform and cgroup support.
↳ Draw this in the interview
CPU quota / shares / pinning ➜ Runnable Java threads ➜ Latency under throttle
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A 1.5-CPU quota permits a limited amount of scheduled CPU time rather than guaranteeing two dedicated
cores. Placement chooses eligible cores; weight influences competition. Inspect throttling when latency
grows at high load.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why might adding more application threads worsen latency under a small quota?
A. Under CPU quota, too many runnable threads add context switching and throttling; queues
and p99 latency can grow despite more threads.
⚠ WATCH OUT CPU shares are not a hard ceiling. Quotas can affect tail latency and GC even when host-
wide utilization looks modest.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 47

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker run --cpus=1.5 IMAGE
# Separate alternative: --cpuset-cpus=0,1
# Relative weight example: --cpu-shares=512

HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 74

CPU placement respectively, subject to platform and cgroup support.
