pages.title: How should thread pools and connection pools be sized in a container?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 14 — CPU, memory and JVM container behavior
How should thread pools and connection
pools be sized in a container?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Use measured workload, CPU budget, blocking behavior and downstream capacity;
do not size every pool from unconstrained host hardware.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Instance thread pool ➜ DB connection pool ➜ System-wide replica budget
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A modest per-instance pool can collectively overload a database after scaling. Virtual threads improve
waiting-task economics but do not create extra CPU or unlimited database connections. Bound expensive
concurrency separately.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you choose a safe maximum replica count from a database connection limit?
A. Reserve database capacity for admin work and other consumers; divide the safe connection
budget by max pool size per replica, then include headroom.
⚠ WATCH OUT A single benchmark number cannot establish production capacity. Measure throughput, tail
latency, queueing, throttling and dependency saturation.

DB pool per replica: 25
Potential app connections: 4 x 25 = 100

pages.title: Where should a containerized application write logs?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 15 — Logs, inspection and troubleshooting
Where should a containerized application
write logs?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Usually to stdout and stderr, with runtime log collection, retention and external
aggregation configured separately.
↳ Draw this in the interview
stdout and stderr ➜ Central log collection ➜ Trace ID across services
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The logging driver captures supported container output. Central aggregation enables searching across
recreated replicas. The local driver provides rotation behavior; json-file deployments should explicitly
manage rotation and disk use.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you correlate one failed request across several services?
A. Propagate a correlation/trace ID across services, record it in structured logs and tracing
spans, and search all systems using that same identifier.
⚠ WATCH OUT docker logs availability depends on the driver and configuration. File-only application logging is
not automatically collected from an arbitrary image path.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 48

docker run --log-driver=local IMAGE
# Java application logging: console output with request context.

pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 15 — Logs, inspection and troubleshooting
What are inspect, stats, top and events useful
for?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
They expose configuration and state, live resource use, process information and
lifecycle events respectively.
↳ Draw this in the interview
docker inspect ➜ docker stats + top ➜ docker events

Use inspect for actual limits and mounts, stats for a resource snapshot, top for process relationships, and
events for transitions. Combine these with application metrics and timestamps rather than interpreting
one number in isolation.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which additional time-series data would support a CPU-throttling diagnosis?
A. Collect cgroup throttled-period counts/time, container CPU usage, host CPU saturation,
request latency, runnable-thread counts and queue depth over time.

snapshot can miss a short spike.

docker stats --no-stream APP_CONTAINER
docker top APP_CONTAINER
docker events --since 10m --filter container=APP_CONTAINER

lifecycle events respectively.

pages.fullText:

Does exit code 137 always mean an OOM
kill?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
No. 137 commonly corresponds to SIGKILL termination, which can result from
memory enforcement, a forced stop or another kill source.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Exit 137 = SIGKILL ➜ Check OOMKilled flag ➜ Investigate actual cause
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
OOMKilled is a useful clue, but diagnosis needs the relevant time window and memory evidence. A stop
timeout ending in SIGKILL can also produce 137. Java can independently fail with a managed
OutOfMemoryError.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why might an OOM kill produce no Java heap dump?
A. The kernel may kill the JVM abruptly without letting it handle a Java `OutOfMemoryError` or
write a heap dump.
⚠ WATCH OUT A process can deliberately exit with a numeric code, so status alone is not a proof of cause.
Preserve logs and termination context.

# Correlate with runtime events and host/cgroup evidence.

HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 78

memory enforcement, a forced stop or another kill source.

A process can deliberately exit with a numeric code, so status alone is not a proof of cause.

A. The kernel may kill the JVM abruptly without letting it handle a Java `OutOfMemoryError` or
write a heap dump.

OPERATIONS CHAPTER 15 — Logs, inspection and troubleshooting
How do you debug an image that has no
shell or a container that has exited?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Use metadata, logs and copied artifacts; use an approved diagnostic image or
platform tooling when live process inspection is required.
↳ Draw this in the interview
No shell in image ➜ Logs / inspect / debug image ➜ Preserve evidence
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
docker cp can retrieve files from a stopped container, unlike exec. For a shell-free running image,
diagnostics must match access, PID namespace and tool compatibility constraints. A dedicated debug
variant can be useful in test environments.

How would you collect a thread dump without permanently expanding the runtime image?

controlled JVM diagnostic signal/attach method; keep the production image minimal.

personal data or credentials.

pages.title: How do you diagnose Docker disk usage before cleanup?
pages.fullText:
OPERATIONS CHAPTER 15 — Logs, inspection and troubleshooting
How do you diagnose Docker disk usage
before cleanup?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Inspect image, writable-layer, cache, log and volume usage, then remove only
identified disposable objects.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Measure disk consumers ➜ Validate backups ➜ Prune safely and precisely
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A large database volume needs a different response from stale build cache. Reclaimable image sizes
include sharing relationships, so sum carefully. Retention policies prevent recurring exhaustion better
than emergency broad deletion.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which backup and restore evidence is needed before retiring a database volume?

point, credentials, schema compatibility and owner approval.
⚠ WATCH OUT system prune is destructive, has category-specific rules, and is not a database cleanup
strategy. Never assume all unused volumes contain worthless data.

docker ps -a --size
docker volume ls
docker image ls

pages.title: Why should application containers normally avoid root?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 16 — Runtime security and least privilege
Why should application containers normally
avoid root?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A non-root process reduces available authority inside the container and limits
some consequences of an application compromise.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Non-root application ➜ Limit permissions ➜ Prevent unnecessary hostpower
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The application must work with that UID and any required writable directories. Dropping capabilities and
restricting privilege acquisition add separate controls. Test the actual workload under the intended policy.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What explicit privilege would your API need to listen on port 8080?
A. None: port 8080 is unprivileged on normal Linux defaults. Non-root can listen there without
adding privileged-port capabilities.

permissive mounted files. Capabilities and security profiles are distinct.

docker run --user 10001:10001 \
  --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt=no-new-privileges \
  IMAGE

some consequences of an application compromise.

pages.title: rootless Docker and user namespace remapping?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 16 — Runtime security and least privilege
What is the difference between non-root,
rootless Docker and user namespace
remapping?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
They change application identity, daemon authority and host-to-container UID
mapping at different layers.
↳ Draw this in the interview
UID != root ➜ Rootless Docker engine ➜ User namespaces map IDs
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
These controls can overlap but are not interchangeable. Rootless mode changes daemon-level privileges
and can affect supported resource or networking features. Remapping affects how mounted ownership is
interpreted on the host.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would rootless operation affect your bind mount and CPU-limit setup?
A. Rootless changes UID mappings, host path access, network behavior, and availability of
resource controls. Test bind mounts and cgroups on the actual host.
⚠ WATCH OUT Setting USER in a Dockerfile does not make a rootful engine rootless. Inspect runtime
capabilities on the actual supported platform.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 52

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
Non-root USER:    application UID is not zero
Rootless engine:  daemon and containers run without host root
User remapping:   container IDs map to different host IDs
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 82

mapping at different layers.

pages.title: Why is mounting the Docker socket into a container dangerous?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 16 — Runtime security and least privilege
Why is mounting the Docker socket into a
container dangerous?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Engine API access can grant broad control over containers and host resources
within that engine's authority.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Docker socket access ➜ Engine-level privileges ➜ Separate untrusted build
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A job with a rootful engine socket can often create privileged workloads or mount sensitive host paths.
Making the socket bind read-only does not turn the API into a read-only API. Rootless engines still expose
the owning user's authority.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What separate trust boundary would you choose for pull-request image builds?
A. Run untrusted pull-request builds on isolated workers without production registry credentials
or privileged daemon access. Use short-lived scoped tokens only for trusted jobs.
⚠ WATCH OUT A convenient build agent must not receive the production engine socket by default. Isolation
between trusted and untrusted jobs matters.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 52

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
# Review this sensitive mount in CI definitions:
# /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
# Prefer isolated builders and carefully bounded credentials.

within that engine's authority.

pages.title: What do capabilities, seccomp and AppArmor/SELinux control?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 16 — Runtime security and least privilege
What do capabilities, seccomp and
AppArmor/SELinux control?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Capabilities divide privileged operations, seccomp filters system calls, and
mandatory access controls constrain operations through host policy.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Capabilities: privilege ➜ Seccomp: syscalls ➜ LSM: file/process policy
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
These mechanisms address different paths to abuse. If the application fails, identify the required
operation before adding a narrowly justified capability or policy change. Keep host kernel and runtime
patches current.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you investigate a denied syscall without disabling all confinement?
A. Check audit/denial logs, seccomp profiles and effective capabilities. Temporarily reproduce
with a narrowly adjusted policy, then permit only the needed operation.
⚠ WATCH OUT --privileged or an unconfined policy removes important protections and is not a general fix for
permission errors. Host policy can differ across environments.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 53
Q079
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker run --cap-drop=ALL \
  --security-opt=no-new-privileges \
  IMAGE
# Retain the platform's supported default seccomp policy.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 84

mandatory access controls constrain operations through host policy.

  --security-opt=no-new-privileges \
  IMAGE

pages.title: Can a container run with a read-only filesystem?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 16 — Runtime security and least privilege
Can a container run with a read-only
filesystem?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Yes, when the application has explicit writable mounts for its real requirements
and can avoid writing elsewhere.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Read-only root FS ➜ Explicit writable temp mount ➜ Test Spring startup
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The image filesystem cannot be changed through ordinary writes, while /tmp supplies bounded scratch
space. Logs can go to stdout. Persistent uploads or caches require explicitly designed storage rather than
arbitrary writes under /app.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which startup behavior would you test before enforcing this policy on Spring Boot?
A. Test temp-file creation, Java extracted libraries, logs, cache writes and startup scripts.
Provide specific writable tmpfs/volume paths such as `/tmp` if required.
⚠ WATCH OUT A read-only root filesystem does not make every mounted volume read-only. Audit actual write
paths, native-library extraction and JVM temporary files.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 53
Q080
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker run --read-only \
  --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=64m \
  --user 10001:10001 --cap-drop=ALL IMAGE
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 85

and can avoid writing elsewhere.

pages.title: Why should base images be maintained and periodically rebuilt?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 17 — Image maintenance and supply-chain evidence
Why should base images be maintained and
periodically rebuilt?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Application security depends on runtime and OS components too; an unchanged
application can still require an updated base and retesting.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Base image CVE ➜ Rebuild + retest ➜ Promote new pinned digest
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Pinning provides a stable input; an update process prevents that stable input from becoming indefinitely
stale. Rebuild, scan and test the new artifact, then record the new release digest.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you roll out a base-only patch across many Java services?
A. Update the approved base digest, rebuild all dependent services in CI, scan/test images, and
roll out gradually with rollback digests recorded.
⚠ WATCH OUT A smaller image is not automatically supported or vulnerability-free. Deleting package
managers does not patch vulnerable runtime libraries.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 54

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre
# Production policy can pin a reviewed digest.
# An update job proposes the new digest and runs verification.

pages.title: What is an SBOM, and what does it tell you?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 17 — Image maintenance and supply-chain evidence
What is an SBOM, and what does it tell you?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A software bill of materials inventories detected components and versions; it
supports assessment but is not proof that an image is secure.
↳ Draw this in the interview
SBOM lists components ➜ Match CVE to dependency ➜ Fix or mitigate exposure
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
An inventory helps determine whether an affected package may be present. Detection coverage differs for
OS packages, shaded Java dependencies and custom binaries. Pair the inventory with vulnerability
information and actual usage analysis.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you assess a CVE affecting a transitive Java dependency?
A. Check the vulnerable package and exact version in the SBOM, actual runtime reachability,
exploit conditions, fixed version, and transitive upgrade path.
⚠ WATCH OUT An absent finding can reflect scanner limitations. An SBOM does not establish a publisher's
identity or that the application passed tests.

  --tag REGISTRY/APP:BUILD_ID --push .
# Consume the attached inventory with your assessment tools.

pages.title: What is build provenance?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 17 — Image maintenance and supply-chain evidence
What is build provenance?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
It records information about how an artifact was produced, such as builder, inputs
and build parameters, according to the chosen format and mode.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Build provenance record ➜ Verify issuer + subject ➜ Trust approved artifact
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Provenance supports tracing a release back to source and build inputs. Its usefulness depends on a
trusted builder and verifiable binding to the image digest. Richer records can also disclose more build
details.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What makes an attestation trustworthy rather than merely present?
A. Validate a trusted signature and attestation issuer, authorized build identity, subject digest,
source revision and policy. An arbitrary attached JSON file is not enough.
⚠ WATCH OUT Build arguments can appear in provenance. Credentials belong in secret mechanisms, not ARG.
Attestation support also depends on export and storage configuration.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 55

  --tag REGISTRY/APP:BUILD_ID --push .

pages.title: How are image signatures different from digests and vulnerability scans?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 17 — Image maintenance and supply-chain evidence
How are image signatures different from
digests and vulnerability scans?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A digest identifies content, a signature can authenticate an assertion about that
content, and a scan assesses known issues under a specific policy and database.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Digest = identity ➜ Signature = authorization ➜ Scan = vulnerability signal
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Each answers a different question. Signature verification must check the expected identity and trust
policy, not merely find a signature. A legitimate publisher can still publish vulnerable or broken software.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which evidence would you retain when approving a temporary vulnerability exception?
A. Store CVE details, exploitability analysis, mitigation, business risk owner, exception expiry,
evidence links and a planned update date.
⚠ WATCH OUT Signing technology and registry integration vary. A deployment policy must enforce verification
rather than rely on a developer remembering a manual step.

Publisher check: verify signature identity and policy
Risk check:      inspect findings and allowed exceptions
Runtime check:   test application behavior and access policy

pages.title: Why can deleting a secret in a later Dockerfile step still leak it?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 17 — Image maintenance and supply-chain evidence
Why can deleting a secret in a later
Dockerfile step still leak it?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Earlier image layers or build output may retain the original bytes even when the
final filesystem view hides the file.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Secret added to early layer ➜ Later deletion hides only ➜ Credential still exposed
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Layered storage means a later deletion does not rewrite all prior content. The response to a real exposure
includes revoking the secret and correcting the build pipeline, not just removing the final visible file.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you investigate where the exposed image and credential were distributed?
A. List affected image digests, registries, tags, build logs and deployed clusters; revoke the
leaked credential, rotate it, and search for unauthorized access.
⚠ WATCH OUT Private registries do not make embedded long-lived credentials an acceptable design.
Intermediate caches and logs also need review.

pages.title: What should a container CI pipeline verify?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 18 — CI/CD and release delivery
What should a container CI pipeline verify?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Source tests, build inputs, the produced image's startup and behavior, security
policy and release identity all need appropriate checks.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Source and tests ➜ Build + image smoke test ➜ Publish approved digest
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A JAR passing unit tests can still fail because the runtime lacks a library, uses the wrong UID or receives
the wrong arguments. Image tests should exercise the packaging and runtime contract, not only repeat
compilation.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What smoke test catches a wrong container port or missing certificate bundle?
A. Boot the exact built image under test settings, call the expected HTTP health endpoint, and
confirm SSL/TLS connections or CA trust to a test dependency.

codes and readiness deadlines.

Image candidate -> runtime smoke test -> assessment
Published digest -> deployment -> observed verification

pages.title: Why deploy the same digest that passed image testing?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 18 — CI/CD and release delivery
Why deploy the same digest that passed
image testing?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
It ties production deployment to the verified artifact and avoids rebuild
differences between stages.
↳ Draw this in the interview
CI-tested image digest ➜ Promotion record ➜ Production runs same bytes
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Source, dependencies, timestamped output or a base tag can change when rebuilding. Digest promotion
removes that specific drift while preserving environment-specific values. Record which platform image or
index was approved.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you prove which digest an incident-affected replica actually ran?
A. Inspect orchestrator-reported image IDs/digests and `docker inspect` for each replica, then
compare them with the signed release manifest.
⚠ WATCH OUT Production behavior can still differ because configuration, architecture, data and dependencies
differ. Test the relevant variant and environment contract.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 58

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
Test:   registry.example.com/team/app@sha256:APP_DIGEST
Stage:  same digest + stage configuration
Prod:   same digest + production configuration

pages.title: How should image-build credentials be handled in CI?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 18 — CI/CD and release delivery
How should image-build credentials be
handled in CI?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Provide short-lived or narrowly scoped credentials through protected CI channels,
with separate permissions for reading, building and release publication.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Untrusted pull request ➜ Isolated build without secrets ➜ Trusted publish later
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The source of a build can execute code during dependency resolution and compilation. An external pull
request must not inherit a trusted release job's secrets or engine access. Limit credentials by destination
and purpose.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you test contributions from forks while protecting a private registry?
A. Build fork contributions without secrets or write permissions. Run trusted publishing only
after review on protected branches/workflows.
⚠ WATCH OUT Hiding a secret in logs does not stop malicious code from transmitting it elsewhere. Trust
separation must occur before executing the job.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 58
Q088
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
Untrusted PR: read-only dependencies; no production secrets
Trusted release: authorized publish identity
Deployment: permission to deploy an approved digest
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 93

with separate permissions for reading, building and release publication.

Trusted release: authorized publish identity

after review on protected branches/workflows.

pages.title: What is the difference between rolling, blue- green and canary deployment?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 18 — CI/CD and release delivery
What is the difference between rolling, blue-
green and canary deployment?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Rolling replaces instances incrementally; blue-green switches between complete
environments; canary admits limited traffic to a candidate before expansion.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Rolling update ➜ Blue-green environment ➜ Canary traffic slice
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
All need readiness, capacity, version compatibility and a rollback decision. Blue-green may require more
temporary resources. Canary decisions need meaningful traffic and user-impact signals, not only an alive
process.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What metrics would stop a canary before most users are affected?
A. Stop rollout if error rates, p95/p99 latency, saturation, business failures or health checks
breach preset thresholds relative to baseline.
⚠ WATCH OUT Container tooling alone does not provide every traffic strategy. Shared database changes can
prevent a simple application rollback.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 59
Q089
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
Rolling:    old and new replicas overlap
Blue-green: two deployment groups; controlled traffic switch
Canary:     measured small candidate share, then promotion
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 94

environments; canary admits limited traffic to a candidate before expansion.

pages.title: Why do database migrations complicate container rollback?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 18 — CI/CD and release delivery
Why do database migrations complicate
container rollback?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Rolling back an image does not automatically restore the schema, data or
external effects changed by the newer release.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Schema migration ➜ New code rollout ➜ Backward-compatible rollback
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
An expand-contract strategy gives overlapping application versions a compatible period. A migration job
needs ownership, retries and a clear completion result. Destructive transformations require a separate
recovery plan.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you roll back code after a non-reversible data transformation?
A. Roll code forward with a compatibility adapter or restore transformed data from a validated
backup. A simple old-image rollback cannot reverse changed data.
⚠ WATCH OUT A container restart is not a migration lock. Running every replica's startup migration
concurrently can create contention or failure.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 59
Q090
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
Expand: add compatible schema without removing old fields
Deploy: allow old and new code to coexist safely
Migrate: backfill and verify
Contract: remove old paths after the rollback window closes
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 95

external effects changed by the newer release.

pages.title: What is a multi-platform image?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 19 — Multi-platform images and native compatibility
What is a multi-platform image?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
It uses an image index or manifest list to reference distinct image variants for
supported operating-system and CPU combinations.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Multi-platform index ➜ linux/amd64 image ➜ linux/arm64 image
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The same readable tag can lead an AMD64 host and an ARM64 host to different manifests. The variants
should provide equivalent application behavior but their binary layers need not be identical.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What exactly does pinning the index digest fix?
A. Pinning the index digest locks the manifest list and which platform variants it references, but
different hosts still select their respective platform-specific manifests.
⚠ WATCH OUT Attestation descriptors can also appear in an index. Do not mistake every descriptor for a
runnable platform variant.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 60
Q091
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker buildx imagetools inspect REGISTRY/APP:TAG
# Example variants: linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
# A pull normally selects a compatible variant for the target.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 96

It uses an image index or manifest list to reference distinct image variants for
supported operating-system and CPU combinations.

pages.title: How do you build and publish AMD64 and ARM64 variants?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 19 — Multi-platform images and native compatibility
How do you build and publish AMD64 and
ARM64 variants?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Use a builder configured for the platforms through native workers, supported
emulation or a deliberate cross-compilation approach.
↳ Draw this in the interview
buildx multiplatform ➜ Native/emu builders ➜ Push image index
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The resulting registry reference can contain both variants. The Java runtime base must support the
platforms, and native dependencies must be compatible. Exporting directly to a registry avoids assuming
the local image store supports every multi-platform output.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
When is a native ARM worker preferable to emulation?
A. Native ARM workers avoid emulation overhead and can test native libraries on real ARM
behavior, especially for expensive builds and platform-specific tests.
⚠ WATCH OUT The command does not provision missing builders or emulators. Test each target variant; a
successful build is not a compatibility test.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 60
Q092
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  --tag REGISTRY/APP:BUILD_ID --push .
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 97

Use a builder configured for the platforms through native workers, supported
emulation or a deliberate cross-compilation approach.

  --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  --tag REGISTRY/APP:BUILD_ID --push .

A. Native ARM workers avoid emulation overhead and can test native libraries on real ARM

pages.title: Why does exec format error happen?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 19 — Multi-platform images and native compatibility
Why does exec format error happen?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
An executable can have an incompatible architecture or format, or a script can
lack a valid interpreter contract.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Wrong binary architecture ➜ exec format error ➜ Build for correct target
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Compare the image's declared platform with the host and the file being launched. A manually copied
AMD64 binary can still be wrong inside an ARM64 image. Script failures can also stem from CRLF or a
missing interpreter.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you prevent a developer's native build output entering a cross-platform image?
A. Build dependencies inside the selected target architecture or cross-compile with verified
target flags. Never blindly COPY a developer's host-built native executable.
⚠ WATCH OUT A platform label does not validate every copied file. permission denied is a related but different
failure that needs permission and mount checks.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 61
Q093
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker image inspect IMAGE \
  --format '{{.Os}}/{{.Architecture}}'
# Check copied native binaries, script shebang and line endings.
# Also confirm the interpreter actually exists in the image.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 98

lack a valid interpreter contract.

  --format '{{.Os}}/{{.Architecture}}'

pages.title: Can Java bytecode portability hide OS-library incompatibility?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 19 — Multi-platform images and native compatibility
Can Java bytecode portability hide OS-library
incompatibility?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Yes. JNI, native agents, TLS providers and other libraries can depend on
architecture, libc and available system components.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Portable bytecode ➜ JNI / OS native dependency ➜ Test target platform
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A smaller Alpine-based image uses a different libc family from many conventional Linux bases. Pure Java
code can run while a native transport or agent fails at load time. Exercise the actual features under the
target image.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which integration test would detect a failing native compression library?
A. Run a container integration test on each target architecture that loads the compression
library and performs actual compress/decompress with checked output.
⚠ WATCH OUT Do not claim Alpine is always wrong or always better. Choose from supported dependencies
and operational needs, then measure size and performance.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 61
Q094
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
Java class: portable within its supported Java runtime contract
Native .so: requires matching architecture and ABI
Base choice: verify glibc/musl and required library support
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 99

Yes. JNI, native agents, TLS providers and other libraries can depend on
architecture, libc and available system components.

pages.title: TARGETPLATFORM help cross-platform builds?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 19 — Multi-platform images and native compatibility
How do BUILDPLATFORM and
TARGETPLATFORM help cross-platform
builds?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
They identify the builder's execution platform and requested output platform,
enabling explicit control of stages and compiler targets.
↳ Draw this in the interview
BUILDPLATFORM builds tools ➜ TARGETPLATFORM runsoutput ➜ Validate compiled architecture
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A native build stage can run on the builder while producing an artifact for the target, if the toolchain
actually supports that cross-compilation. Automatic platform arguments must be declared where their
values are used in stage instructions.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why can a Dockerfile run quickly but produce the wrong native artifact?
A. A fast build might accidentally compile for BUILDPLATFORM and copy that output into a
TARGETPLATFORM image. Confirm target architecture and run it in a target test.
⚠ WATCH OUT Merely printing TARGETPLATFORM does not cross-compile a binary. Java-native packaging
and generated libraries still need a target-aware workflow.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 62
Q095
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
# Dockerfile sketch, not a complete cross compiler:
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM TOOLCHAIN_IMAGE AS build
ARG TARGETPLATFORM
# Build the target artifact using a toolchain that supports it.
FROM RUNTIME_IMAGE
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 100

enabling explicit control of stages and compiler targets.

pages.title: Can you run a database in Docker safely?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 20 — Databases, Kafka and stateful workloads
Can you run a database in Docker safely?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Yes, with a supported image, correctly mounted durable storage, resource
planning, backup/restore verification and an operational recovery policy.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Persist DB data ➜ Verified backup + restore ➜ Recovery after host loss
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Separating data from the container lets you recreate the process without discarding the database.
Database upgrades still require compatible data handling. Single-host storage remains dependent on that
host's reliability.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you recover after losing both the container and its host disk?
A. Restore a tested off-host backup and transaction logs onto replacement storage, recreate the
database container, verify integrity, then bring clients back carefully.
⚠ WATCH OUT A volume is not a replica or an off-host backup. PostgreSQL 18+ image layout differs, so do
not blindly reuse a 17 mount recipe.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 63
Q096
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
# PostgreSQL 17 image-specific data path:
--mount type=volume,src=orders-db,dst=/var/lib/postgresql/data
# Do not publish its port unless a host client needs access.
# Review data path and upgrade guidance for the chosen major version.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 101

planning, backup/restore verification and an operational recovery policy.

pages.title: Why are raw volume copies risky for a running database?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 20 — Databases, Kafka and stateful workloads
Why are raw volume copies risky for a
running database?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A filesystem copy can capture an inconsistent point unless the database and
storage snapshot procedure provide the required consistency.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Copy live data? inconsistent ➜ Database-aware snapshot ➜ WAL for PITR
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A logical backup tool understands database consistency better than copying arbitrary live files. The
example covers one database; roles, global objects and point-in-time recovery require additional planning.
Avoid a TTY for streamed backup bytes.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
When would physical backup plus transaction-log archival be preferable?
A. Use physical backups plus WAL/archive logs for large databases, low RPO and point-in-time
recovery, when the database's tooling supports it.
⚠ WATCH OUT A successful dump command is not a tested restore. Preserve encryption, retention, integrity
and recovery-time requirements.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 63

  pg_dump -U app -d orders > orders.sql

# Validate by restoring into a separate disposable database.

storage snapshot procedure provide the required consistency.

pages.title: Why do database initialization environment variables seem to stop working?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 20 — Databases, Kafka and stateful workloads
Why do database initialization environment
variables seem to stop working?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Many official database images use initialization settings only when creating an
empty data directory, not to alter an existing database on every start.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Existing initialized volume ➜ Initialization env ignored ➜ Change DB state safely
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Retained volume data changes the startup path. Recreating the container with a new password value does
not imply the existing PostgreSQL role password has changed. Inspect the image contract and the actual
database state.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you diagnose a password mismatch without deleting any data?
A. Check whether a data directory was initialized earlier, inspect effective env/secret inputs and
logs, then use supported SQL/password rotation without deleting the volume.
⚠ WATCH OUT Deleting the volume to make settings take effect is destructive. Treat credential rotation and
database migrations as explicit operations.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 64
Q098
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
# First initialization: POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE is consumed.
# Later start with the same volume: existing database remains.
# Change real roles/credentials using the database's own procedure.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 103

Many official database images use initialization settings only when creating an
empty data directory, not to alter an existing database on every start.

not imply the existing PostgreSQL role password has changed. Inspect the image contract and the actual
database state.

Deleting the volume to make settings take effect is destructive. Treat credential rotation and
database migrations as explicit operations.

How would you diagnose a password mismatch without deleting any data?
A. Check whether a data directory was initialized earlier, inspect effective env/secret inputs and
logs, then use supported SQL/password rotation without deleting the volume.

pages.title: Why does Kafka connect initially and then fail from a container?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 20 — Databases, Kafka and stateful workloads
Why does Kafka connect initially and then
fail from a container?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
The bootstrap endpoint may be reachable while broker metadata advertises
addresses that the client cannot resolve or reach.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Bootstrap broker ➜ Advertised broker address ➜ Client must reach each broker
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Kafka clients discover broker endpoints after bootstrapping. Each client network needs usable advertised
addresses. A successful TCP connection to the initial bootstrap address therefore proves only the first
step.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you support both host tools and same-network Spring clients?
A. Configure Kafka advertised listeners separately for host clients and Docker-network clients;
each client must receive broker endpoints reachable from its own network.
⚠ WATCH OUT listener configuration, TLS identity and advertised endpoint design must agree. Docker port
mapping does not rewrite arbitrary broker metadata for every client network.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 64

Advertised internal listener: kafka:9092
Host client listener: a separately reachable host endpoint

addresses that the client cannot resolve or reach.

pages.title: Can docker compose scale turn one database into a database cluster?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 20 — Databases, Kafka and stateful workloads
Can docker compose scale turn one
database into a database cluster?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
No. Starting replicas of a container does not configure application replication,
membership, leader election or data ownership.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Compose replicas != cluster ➜ Database ownership & quorum ➜ Use real HA design
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Each database process must have the correct identity and storage. Pointing unrelated replicas at the
same data directory can corrupt data or violate the database's supported usage. Managed stateful
services may simplify the responsibility.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which workload would you keep outside a first single-host Compose deployment?
A. Keep a critical production database, distributed Kafka cluster, or other stateful service
needing multi-host failover outside an initial single-host setup.
⚠ WATCH OUT Likewise, several Kafka or Redis containers do not automatically form a correctly configured
fault-tolerant cluster. Test failure and recovery semantics.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 65

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker compose up -d --scale api=3
# Appropriate only if the API's state and jobs permit it.
# Database replication requires its own explicit cluster design.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 105

membership, leader election or data ownership.

needing multi-host failover outside an initial single-host setup.

pages.title: How do Engine, Compose, Swarm and Kubernetes differ?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 21 — Orchestration, scaling and operational boundaries
How do Engine, Compose, Swarm and
Kubernetes differ?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Engine runs container objects; Compose manages an application definition;
Swarm and Kubernetes add cluster-level service or workload orchestration.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Docker Engine ➜ Compose single app ➜ Kubernetes orchestration
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A cluster controller can replace failed workloads on eligible nodes, subject to capacity and storage
constraints. Compose can be useful for development and suitable single-host services without becoming a
cluster scheduler.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What requirement would make you move beyond a single host?
A. Multi-node recovery, rolling rescheduling after host failure, stronger deployment controls, or
independent autoscaling can justify adopting an orchestrator.
⚠ WATCH OUT Product selection should follow requirements and team operations capacity. A cluster is not
automatically simpler or highly available in every component.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 66

Single engine: container lifecycle on its selected host
Compose:      related services, config, networks and volumes
Cluster:      scheduling, desired replicas and platform recovery

HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 106

pages.title: Does Kubernetes require Docker Engine or dockershim?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 21 — Orchestration, scaling and operational boundaries
Does Kubernetes require Docker Engine or
dockershim?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Current Kubernetes uses CRI-compatible runtimes; Docker Engine needs an
adapter if selected as the runtime, while Docker-built compatible images remain
usable.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Kubernetes controller spec ➜ CRI container runtime ➜ Reconciled Pods
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Image format and node runtime integration are separate contracts. Removing dockershim did not make
Dockerfiles unusable. Docker Engine itself does not implement the Kubernetes CRI contract directly.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Why might editing a managed container directly be undone by its controller?
A. A Deployment controller continuously reconciles desired state. A manual change to one Pod/
container can disappear when it is replaced from the declared template.
⚠ WATCH OUT Do not treat Docker CLI commands as the workload-control interface for a Kubernetes-
managed service. Use the orchestrator's ownership model.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 67

Docker build -> compatible image in registry
Kubernetes -> CRI runtime such as containerd -> workload
# The old in-tree dockershim was removed in Kubernetes 1.24.

pages.title: Why should a scalable API avoid local durable state?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 21 — Orchestration, scaling and operational boundaries
Why should a scalable API avoid local
durable state?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Replacement or rescheduling can lose container-local data, and independent
replicas cannot safely assume the same local files or memory.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Stateless API replicas ➜ Shared durable business state ➜ Idempotent side effects
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Keeping durable state behind explicit services allows replicas to come and go. Local caches may still be
useful when invalidation and loss are acceptable. Background jobs need coordination and idempotency
rather than one in-memory singleton per replica.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you prevent three replicas from charging the same order twice?
A. Use a shared durable idempotency store with a unique order/payment key and an atomic
business transaction; each replica follows the same contract.
⚠ WATCH OUT Stateless HTTP handlers can still create stateful external effects. The architecture must
define retry and concurrency behavior.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 67

from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
Durable orders -> database
Shared uploads -> appropriate object/file storage
Session policy -> external state or suitable signed tokens
Local /tmp -> disposable scratch data

replicas cannot safely assume the same local files or memory.

pages.title: Do resource limits guarantee a workload gets scheduled or has reserved capacity?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 21 — Orchestration, scaling and operational boundaries
Do resource limits guarantee a workload
gets scheduled or has reserved capacity?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
No. Runtime ceilings, scheduling requests or reservations, available capacity and
failure headroom solve different resource questions.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Request limits ➜ Scheduled capacity ➜ N-1 failure headroom
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A memory limit can protect against growth while insufficient cluster capacity prevents replacement
elsewhere. An orchestrator's requests or reservations guide placement according to its own policy. Load
testing determines whether the admitted workload meets latency goals.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What capacity would remain if your largest node failed?
A. Plan N-1 capacity: after the largest node fails, remaining nodes must still fit critical requests
plus headroom or degrade according to an explicit policy.
⚠ WATCH OUT A nominal replica count does not prove survivability during node loss. Storage location and
network dependencies can constrain failover too.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 68
Q104
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
Runtime ceiling: prevent unrestricted per-workload consumption
Placement budget: determine whether the node can accept work
Failure headroom: permit recovery after a node is lost
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO
HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 109

failure headroom solve different resource questions.

pages.title: What are the limits of container-level high availability?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 21 — Orchestration, scaling and operational boundaries
What are the limits of container-level high
availability?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
A restarted or replaced process restores only part of service availability; traffic,
durable data, dependency health and recovery time still matter.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Restart container ➜ Recover storage and traffic ➜ Verify measured RTO
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Choose acceptable outage and data-loss objectives first, then prove them with failure exercises. A replica
may start correctly but be unable to reach data or receive user traffic. Observe both infrastructure and
user-visible behavior.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you demonstrate the service's recovery time instead of merely describing it?
A. Perform a timed failure rehearsal: kill a node/container, measure alert-to-recovery and
request success, then compare observed RTO/RPO to targets.
⚠ WATCH OUT Three containers on one host share a host failure domain. Replication without independent
failure domains can provide less resilience than expected.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 68
Q105
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
API replica loss: admit traffic to another ready instance
Host loss:        schedule elsewhere with accessible inputs
Data loss:        restore or fail over under a database policy
Dependency loss:  timeouts, degraded behavior and recovery

HANDWRITTEN-STYLE STUDY EDITION • JAVA + SPRING 110

durable data, dependency health and recovery time still matter.

pages.title: A Spring API cannot reach PostgreSQL in Compose. What do you check first?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 22 — Senior interview scenarios
A Spring API cannot reach PostgreSQL in
Compose. What do you check first?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Check caller-relative addressing, shared network membership, actual database
readiness, credentials and schema compatibility before changing unrelated flags.
↳ Draw this in the interview
API -> db DNS ➜ DB accepts connection ➜ Credentials & schema
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
localhost in the API points to that API, not db. If db resolves but rejects authentication, DNS is already
working. If SQL fails because a table is missing, the network may be fine and migration state is the
problem.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
Which error message would move your investigation from network to database state?
A. Errors such as `relation does not exist`, missing table/column or failed migration shift focus
from DNS to schema state; authentication failures shift to credentials.
⚠ WATCH OUT config and logs can include sensitive values. Preserve the current data volume; rebuilding or
deleting it is not an initial network diagnosis.

docker compose config

pages.title: MiB production limit. What is your approach?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 22 — Senior interview scenarios
The API works locally but dies under a 512
MiB production limit. What is your
approach?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Compare exact image and configuration, verify termination cause, inspect total
memory and workload concurrency, then tune from measured evidence.
↳ Draw this in the interview
512 MiB cap ➜ Measure heap + nativememory ➜ Tune limit or application
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A laptop without limits can hide native or thread-related memory growth. Increasing the limit may be a
valid immediate mitigation, but it does not identify the growth source. Separate heap retention from
native buffers, thread stacks and cache behavior.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What evidence would justify a larger limit rather than a code or pool-sizing change?
A. Show a stable measured peak including heap, native/thread memory and headroom, with
legitimate throughput exceeding the old budget; rule out leaks and oversized pools.
⚠ WATCH OUT Exit 137 alone is not enough evidence. Do not set Xmx equal to the full container budget as
a blanket fix.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 69
Q107
from original guide COMMAND OR MINI EXAMPLE 
docker inspect API_CONTAINER \
  --format 'oom={{.State.OOMKilled}} memory={{.HostConfig.Memory}}'
docker stats --no-stream API_CONTAINER
# Compare effective JVM settings and peak-load telemetry.
INTERVIEW NOTEBOOK / DOCKER ZERO TO HERO

memory and workload concurrency, then tune from measured evidence.

pages.title: Production runs different code from the image tested in CI. How do you investigate?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 22 — Senior interview scenarios
Production runs different code from the
image tested in CI. How do you investigate?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Trace source, built artifact, published digest, platform selection and deployed
runtime identity; then inspect mounts and configuration that can override
packaged behavior.
↳ Draw this in the interview
CI tested digest ➜ Deployment manifest drift ➜ Lock promotion to digest
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
A mutable tag, rebuild or bind mount over /app can change what executes. A stale replica may still use a
previous artifact. Resolve each identity step before concluding that the container runtime is inconsistent.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you prevent this mismatch in the release process?
A. Allow only tested immutable digests into deployment manifests, promote a signed release
record, and reject build/rebuild operations during promotion.
⚠ WATCH OUT Digest agreement does not prove identical environment configuration or external
dependencies. Check both artifact and runtime inputs.
ORIGINAL QUESTION PRESERVED Source guide p. 70

Runtime:   selected image identity and mounted paths
Registry:  tag history or immutable release record

pages.title: A security policy blocks a previously working Java image. How do you repair it?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 22 — Senior interview scenarios
A security policy blocks a previously working
Java image. How do you repair it?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Identify the precise denied operation and required path, then adapt the
application or grant the narrowest justified allowance.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Security policy denies action ➜ Find exact denial ➜ Grant narrow exception
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
The application may only need a writable scratch directory rather than root privileges. Verify the repaired
image with the intended security profile and representative startup and runtime features. Preserve denial
evidence for the policy owner.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
How would you prove no unexpected persistent write paths remain?
A. Run the app with a read-only root filesystem, trace filesystem write attempts during startup
and representative traffic, and whitelist only required writable mounts.
⚠ WATCH OUT Disabling all controls trades a diagnosis problem for a larger authority boundary. Do not use
--privileged as a standard production repair.

pages.title: How would you design container delivery for a Spring order service?
pages.fullText:
PRODUCTION / SENIOR CHAPTER 22 — Senior interview scenarios
How would you design container delivery for
a Spring order service?
THE 20-SECOND ANSWER
Define the artifact, configuration, resource, data, traffic and recovery contracts,
then test their interactions rather than stopping at a Dockerfile.
↳ Draw this in the interview
Tested image + config ➜ Deploy + observe traffic ➜ Failure rehearsal + recovery
WHY / HOW IT WORKS
Start from traffic and durability requirements. Keep database credentials outside the image, persistent
data outside the writable layer, and asynchronous effects retryable and idempotent. Choose single-host or
cluster operations from the required failure tolerance.
THE INTERVIEWER MAY ASK…
What would you demonstrate in a deployment and failure rehearsal for this design?
A. Deploy a tested immutable image, demonstrate canary metrics and graceful shutdown, kill a
replica mid-order, retry the request and verify one order/payment and durable event; restore
data from backup.
⚠ WATCH OUT Docker does not create business correctness or exactly-once external behavior. The service
contract must cover duplicates, partial failures and data recovery.

pages.title: One container-ready Java HTTP service
pages.fullText:
04 / PRACTICAL JAVA MINI PROJECT
One container-ready Java HTTP service
Build a tiny Java HTTP server, give it a Java-based health probe, and package it with a
multi-stage Dockerfile. This is a source-derived example; it is not a full Spring Boot
application.
Build and runtime contract

pages.title: Docker commands without confusion
pages.fullText:
06 / QUICK REVISION
Docker commands without confusion
docker build -t app:local . Build an image from the current context
docker run --rm image Create + start; auto-remove when exited
docker ps -a Show both running and stopped containers
docker logs --tail=100 name Read recorded stdout/stderr
docker inspect name Inspect effective runtime configuration/state
docker exec -it name sh New shell only if container is running and contains sh
docker stop --time 45 name Give process time to shut down
docker compose up -d Reconcile multi-service app
docker compose down Remove Compose services/networks; not named volumes by default
docker volume ls List managed volumes
docker stats --no-stream Snapshot of resource use
docker context show Check which engine receives commands
Read-only observation first. Commands such as rm -f, volume rm, or compose down -v can remove
state; use only with explicit understanding.

pages.title: Six distinctions to say clearly
pages.fullText:
06 / QUICK REVISION
Six distinctions to say clearly
Image vs container Image is the packaged template; container is the created instance with
process and writable state.
EXPOSE vs -p EXPOSE declares intent; -p publishes a host port. Neither makes a dead
application listen.
Volumes vs backups Volume persists locally; backup must be restorable, ideally after losing the
original host.
Health vs restart Unhealthy status does not itself guarantee a restart under Docker's restart
policy.
Tags vs digests Tag is a movable name; digest is content identity. Identity alone does not
prove trust.
Heap vs container
memory
Heap is only part of JVM memory; thread stacks, metaspace and native buffers
count too.
A safe production checklist
Tested image digest · non-root process · least-privilege policy · bound CPU/memory ·
health endpoints · graceful shutdown · protected secrets · volume backups · observability
· rollback plan.

pages.title: What is Kubernetes?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Kubernetes foundations FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q001. What is Kubernetes?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Kubernetes keeps the requested number of containers running and helps
them talk to each other.
Interview precision: Kubernetes is a platform for declaring and reconciling containerized
workloads, including placement, service discovery and operational lifecycle.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
kubectl get deployments,pods,services -n interview
# The manifest declares desired state; controllers work toward it.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · A Deployment requesting three replicas causes controllers to
maintain matching Pods. This is a continuing reconciliation process, not a one-time shell
script.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which responsibility belongs to the application rather than the orchestrator?
Answer: The app must still handle business rules, failed payments, safe retries
and data correctness.
Watch out: Kubernetes does not automatically create correct retries, secure application
code or database backups.
Original guide: page 6 · K01, K02, K47, K39 (source directory).

pages.title: How is Kubernetes different from Docker?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Kubernetes foundations FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q002. How is Kubernetes different from Docker?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Docker builds and runs containers. Kubernetes manages those
containers across a cluster.
Interview precision: Docker tools package and run containers; Kubernetes coordinates
workloads across cluster resources through compatible runtimes.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Source -> image build -> registry
Kubernetes manifest -> node runtime -> running Pod
# Docker-built images remain usable with a compatible runtime.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Image format and node runtime integration are separate contracts.
Kubernetes uses CRI-compatible runtime integration; it does not require Docker Engine on
every node.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What changes when you move a single-host service into a cluster?
Answer: Add scheduling, Services, shared configuration, health checks, security,
storage and safe rollout rules.
Watch out: A Docker Compose file is not automatically a Kubernetes deployment
specification.
Original guide: page 7 · K01, K02, K47, K39 (source directory).

pages.title: What does declarative configuration mean?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Kubernetes foundations FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q003. What does declarative configuration mean?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Write what the cluster should look like; controllers keep trying to reach
that state.
Interview precision: You describe the desired object state; the platform compares it with
observed state and attempts reconciliation.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
spec:
  replicas: 3
# Deleting one owned Pod does not change this desired replica count.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · The controller can replace an owned Pod to restore the declared
count. Changing the Deployment specification changes the goal. Actual state may
temporarily differ during scheduling or failures.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How do you distinguish an accepted manifest from a healthy application?
Answer: A successful apply only proves the API accepted the object. Check Pod
readiness and real requests too.
Watch out: A declaration can be impossible to satisfy because of capacity, policy or
missing dependencies.
Original guide: page 7 · K01, K02, K47, K39 (source directory).

pages.title: What are labels, selectors and annotations?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Kubernetes foundations FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q004. What are labels, selectors and annotations?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Labels identify objects, selectors choose them, and annotations carry
extra notes.
Interview precision: Labels identify and group objects, selectors match label sets, and
annotations carry metadata not used as ordinary selector criteria.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
metadata:
  labels:
    app: orders
    tier: api
  annotations:
    example.com/source-commit: abc123
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · A Service can select app=orders, while a deployment system records
source identity in an annotation. Stable selector design matters because traffic and
controller ownership depend on it.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why should release-version labels be separate from a Service's stable
selector?
Answer: Keep Service selectors stable so a new release label does not remove
every Pod from service traffic.
Watch out: A label is not an authorization rule. Mislabeling can route traffic to an
unintended workload.
Original guide: page 8 · K01, K02, K47, K39 (source directory).

pages.title: What does a namespace isolate?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Kubernetes foundations FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q005. What does a namespace isolate?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
A namespace groups Kubernetes resources, but is not a complete
security wall.
Interview precision: A namespace scopes many API objects and supports separate policy
boundaries; it does not by itself isolate all networking, nodes or privileges.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl get pods -n orders
kubectl get namespaces
kubectl get nodes
# Nodes and PersistentVolumes are cluster-scoped.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Two namespaces can each contain a Service named api.
Namespaces help organize ownership, quotas and RoleBindings. NetworkPolicy and runtime
controls add other boundaries.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What additional controls would you use for two independent teams?
Answer: Add RBAC, network rules, quotas, Pod Security policies and isolated
credentials for each team.
Watch out: Namespace separation alone is insufficient for hostile multi-tenancy. Cluster-
scoped resources and administrator authority remain shared.
Original guide: page 8 · K01, K02, K47, K39 (source directory).

pages.title: What are the main control-plane components?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · Control plane and node architecture FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q006. What are the main control-plane
components?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
The API server receives requests, etcd stores state, the scheduler picks
nodes, and controllers repair differences.
Interview precision: The API server exposes cluster operations, etcd stores cluster state, the
scheduler selects nodes, and controllers reconcile objects.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl -> API server -> stored desired state
Scheduler -> node assignment
Controller -> reconcile owned workloads
Kubelet -> execute assigned Pod through runtime integration
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · These responsibilities are cooperative. A scheduler does not start the
Java process, and etcd does not contain the application's database.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which component would you investigate for a Pod with no node assignment?
Answer: Inspect the scheduler and Pod Events; verify node resources, selector
rules, taints and PVC topology.
Watch out: Distribution-specific packaging can differ. Managed services hide some
components but do not remove their architectural roles.
Original guide: page 9 · K01, K41, K51, K52 (source directory).

pages.title: What do kubelet, the runtime, CNI and service networking do?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · Control plane and node architecture FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q007. What do kubelet, the runtime, CNI and
service networking do?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Kubelet manages a node's Pods, the runtime starts containers, and
networking connects them.
Interview precision: Kubelet manages node-side Pod execution, the runtime runs containers,
CNI integration supplies Pod networking, and service networking implements Service
reachability.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl describe node NODE
kubectl get pods -n kube-system
# Service forwarding may use kube-proxy or a supported replacement.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · A running container with broken Pod networking is a different
failure from a container creation error. Network implementations can use different
mechanisms, including eBPF-based service handling.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you separate a runtime startup failure from a network failure?
Answer: Check waiting reason, events and container ID first; if running, inspect
Pod IP, DNS, CNI and connectivity.
Watch out: Do not assume every cluster has an identical kube-proxy datapath or CNI
policy capability.
Original guide: page 10 · K01, K41, K51, K52 (source directory).

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · Control plane and node architecture FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q008. Why is etcd important, and what needs
backing up?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
etcd stores the cluster's desired and observed API state, not your
application's database.
Interview precision: etcd retains Kubernetes control-plane state; recovery requires a supported
backup and restoration procedure appropriate to the cluster distribution.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Cluster objects and control-plane state -> etcd recovery plan
Business database and volume data -> separate data recovery plan
# Test both recovery procedures independently.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Restoring cluster objects is not the same as restoring orders,
uploaded files or database transaction logs. A managed platform may own etcd operations,
but the application team still owns its data guarantees.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which secrets and encryption configuration must a control-plane restore
account for?
Answer: Preserve etcd snapshots, encryption keys/configuration, certificate
material and secrets-restoration procedures.
Watch out: A backup without a tested restore does not establish recovery time or
consistency.

pages.title: What happens if the API server is temporarily unavailable?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · Control plane and node architecture FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q009. What happens if the API server is
temporarily unavailable?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Existing Pods might keep serving, but new deployments and many
cluster repairs may stop.
Interview precision: Existing workloads can often continue running, but API-driven changes
and reconciliation that require the unavailable control plane are impaired.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Existing node process: may continue serving
New Deployment update: cannot rely on API acceptance
Failed-node replacement: may be delayed
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · The impact depends on local node state, network implementation
and the specific failure. Availability of existing traffic does not imply the cluster can scale,
reschedule or accept deployments.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you monitor control-plane health separately from application
availability?
Answer: Track API availability and request errors separately from real application
success and user-facing latency.
Watch out: Do not promise every application keeps working; control-plane-dependent
operations and credentials may have their own requirements.
Original guide: page 11 · K01, K41, K51, K52 (source directory).

pages.title: How does a Pod get scheduled and started?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · Control plane and node architecture FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q010. How does a Pod get scheduled and started?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Admission checks a Pod, the scheduler selects a node, and kubelet starts
its containers.
Interview precision: Admission accepts or rejects the object, scheduling assigns an eligible
node, and the node prepares networking, storage and containers.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl get pod POD -n interview -o wide
kubectl describe pod POD -n interview
# Look at node assignment, conditions and Events.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Pending with no assigned node points toward placement constraints.
A node-assigned Pod can still wait for image pulls or volume attachment. Event evidence
helps locate the failing step.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why can a Pod be assigned to a node yet never become Ready?
Answer: Image pull errors, volume mounts, crashing processes or failing probes
can block readiness after assignment.
Watch out: Admission, scheduling and application readiness are distinct gates.

kubectl get pod POD -n interview -o wide
kubectl describe pod POD -n interview
# Look at node assignment, conditions and Events.

Pending with no assigned node points toward placement constraints.
A node-assigned Pod can still wait for image pulls or volume attachment. Event evidence
helps locate the failing step.
pages.pitfall: Admission, scheduling and application readiness are distinct gates.
pages.followup:
Why can a Pod be assigned to a node yet never become Ready?
Answer: Image pull errors, volume mounts, crashing processes or failing probes
can block readiness after assignment.

pages.title: What is a Pod?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · Pods, containers and lifecycle FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q011. What is a Pod?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
A Pod is the smallest scheduled unit: its containers share one network
identity and selected volumes.
Interview precision: A Pod groups one or more containers scheduled together, sharing a
network identity and declared volumes.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
spec:
  containers:
    - name: api
      image: TEAM/APP:TAG
    - name: helper
      image: TEAM/HELPER:TAG
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · The two containers share the Pod network namespace and can
reach each other through localhost. They do not automatically share every filesystem path;
a declared volume can be mounted into both.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why should an API and its separately scalable database usually be different
workloads?
Answer: A database needs different scaling, upgrades, storage and recovery rules
from an API, so separate them.
Watch out: A Pod should represent tightly coupled execution, not every service in the
system.

pages.title: What is the difference between restarting a container and replacing a Pod?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · Pods, containers and lifecycle FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q012. What is the difference between restarting a
container and replacing a Pod?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Restarting a container keeps its Pod; replacing the Pod creates a new
Pod identity.
Interview precision: A container restart stays within the same Pod identity; replacement creates
a new Pod object, normally with a new UID and potentially a different IP or node.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl get pod POD -n interview -o wide
kubectl get pod POD -n interview -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}'
kubectl logs POD -n interview -c api --previous
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · A kubelet restart can retain Pod-level context such as an emptyDir
volume. A controller replacement does not preserve emptyDir data or promise the same
network address. Use stable discovery and durable storage for those needs.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which data survives a container crash but not a Pod replacement?
Answer: An emptyDir survives a container restart in the same Pod, but is lost
when that Pod is replaced.
Watch out: A Pod's restart count is not a count of every historical replacement.
Original guide: page 13 · K02, K22, K34 (source directory).
Container restart Same Pod emptyDir stays

pages.title: What are init containers used for?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · Pods, containers and lifecycle FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q013. What are init containers used for?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Init containers prepare something before the main application begins.
Interview precision: Ordinary init containers complete sequentially before application
containers start, allowing preparation with a separate runtime contract.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
initContainers:
  - name: prepare
    image: busybox:1.37
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo prepared > /work/state"]
    volumeMounts:
      - {name: work, mountPath: /work}
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · The app can read a prepared file if it mounts the same declared
volume. Init work should have bounded retries and observable failure. A cluster-wide
migration needs stronger ownership than one init container per replica.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When would a separate Job be better than an init container?
Answer: Use a Job for one shared migration or task that must finish once per
planned workflow, not once per replica.
Watch out: This is a fragment requiring a work volume. A forever-waiting init step can
leave every replica unavailable.
Original guide: page 13 · K02, K22, K34 (source directory).

work

pages.title: What is a sidecar, and how is it different from an ordinary init container?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · Pods, containers and lifecycle FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q014. What is a sidecar, and how is it different
from an ordinary init container?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
A sidecar is a helper that runs alongside the main application.
Interview precision: A sidecar supports the app while it runs; Kubernetes also supports
restartable init-container sidecars under the relevant feature/version contract.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
# Native sidecar sketch:
initContainers:
  - name: support
    image: TEAM/SUPPORT:TAG
    restartPolicy: Always
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · The support process can remain active while application containers
execute. Legacy sidecar patterns also use regular app containers. Lifecycle and ordering
behavior differ, so select a supported pattern deliberately.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would a helper affect readiness, resource totals and shutdown order?
Answer: Count its memory/CPU, decide whether failure affects readiness, and test
process termination order.
Watch out: Do not put restartPolicy: Always on an ordinary init container without
understanding native-sidecar support. Job completion behavior also matters.
Original guide: page 14 · K02, K22, K34 (source directory).
App container Helper process Shared Pod budget

pages.title: What are Pod phases and CrashLoopBackOff?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · Pods, containers and lifecycle FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q015. What are Pod phases and
CrashLoopBackOff?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Pod phases are broad states. CrashLoopBackOff means a container
keeps failing and restarting.
Interview precision: Phases summarize lifecycle broadly; CrashLoopBackOff is a container
waiting reason for repeated restarts, not a Pod phase.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl get pod POD -n interview -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'
kubectl describe pod POD -n interview
kubectl logs POD -n interview -c api --previous
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · A Pod can be in Running phase while one container repeatedly
crashes or the Pod is not Ready. Inspect per-container state, exit cause, restart count and
previous logs.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What evidence distinguishes an application exception from a failed liveness
probe?
Answer: Read prior logs and exit reasons; a probe failure appears in events, while
an exception appears in app logs.
Watch out: The STATUS column from kubectl is not always the literal phase field.
Original guide: page 14 · K02, K22, K34 (source directory).

pages.title: How do Deployment, ReplicaSet and Pod relate?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 · Deployments, ReplicaSets and rollouts FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q016. How do Deployment, ReplicaSet and Pod
relate?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Deployment manages ReplicaSets; each ReplicaSet creates and replaces
matching Pods.
Interview precision: A Deployment manages ReplicaSets for updates; a ReplicaSet maintains
matching Pods; Pods run the containers.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl get deploy,rs,pods -n interview
kubectl rollout status deployment/orders -n interview
kubectl rollout history deployment/orders -n interview
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · A template update creates or reuses an appropriate ReplicaSet and
moves replica ownership through a rollout. You normally manage the Deployment rather
than hand-editing its ReplicaSets.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which object should you edit to change the image for every future replica?
Answer: Edit the Deployment's Pod template, not a running Pod or generated
ReplicaSet.
Watch out: Direct Pod edits can be replaced by the controller and may not change the
desired template.
Original guide: page 15 · K03 (source directory).
