pages.title: How do Helm and Kustomize differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Helm, Kustomize, apply and GitOps FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q081. How do Helm and Kustomize differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Helm templates and packages app resources; Kustomize patches/
combines YAML without its own templates.
Interview precision: Helm packages and templates releases with values; Kustomize composes
and transforms Kubernetes configuration through bases and overlays without a general
template language.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
helm template orders ./chart -f values-prod.yaml
kubectl kustomize overlays/prod
# Review rendered objects before applying them.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Both can create environment-specific manifests. Helm also tracks
release operations; Kustomize is integrated into kubectl workflows. Choose conventions your
team can audit and maintain.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What should CI check after rendering a production overlay?
Answer: Run rendering, schema checks, policy validation, secrets scans and
intended-diff checks in CI.
Watch out: Rendering success does not prove API admission, policy compliance or
application health.

pages.title: Why use bases and overlays instead of copying whole manifests?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Helm, Kustomize, apply and GitOps FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q082. Why use bases and overlays instead of
copying whole manifests?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Shared bases avoid duplicating manifests; overlays add differences for
each environment.
Interview precision: A shared base preserves common configuration while focused overlays
describe environment-specific differences with less accidental drift.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
# kustomization.yaml sketch
resources: [../../base]
namespace: orders-prod
replicas:
  - {name: orders, count: 3}
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · The overlay can adjust the desired replica count and namespace
while inheriting common labels and runtime settings. Inspect the output to ensure patches
target the intended resources.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you verify that a patch changed only the intended container
image?
Answer: Render both old and new manifests and inspect container image,
selectors and resource diffs.
Watch out: Overly clever patches can be harder to review than explicit configuration. Keep
secret material outside plain committed files.

pages.title: What does server-side apply field ownership mean?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Helm, Kustomize, apply and GitOps FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q083. What does server-side apply field ownership
mean?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Server-side apply tracks which manager owns fields so controllers can
share object updates safely.
Interview precision: The API records managers for managed fields and can report conflicts
when an apply tries to take over another manager's field.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=delivery \
  -f rendered.yaml
kubectl get deployment orders -n interview -o yaml
# Inspect managedFields when ownership conflicts occur.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Ownership helps multiple controllers or tools coexist intentionally.
Resolve the intended owner rather than blindly forcing every conflict. An autoscaler and a
delivery tool can disagree over replica management.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How should a GitOps definition handle replicas managed by HPA?
Answer: Let HPA own replica count; avoid GitOps repeatedly enforcing conflicting
spec.replicas.
Watch out: --force-conflicts changes ownership and can override another actor's intent. It
is not a universal deployment fix.

pages.title: What is GitOps reconciliation?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Helm, Kustomize, apply and GitOps FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q084. What is GitOps reconciliation?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
GitOps controllers compare the cluster with reviewed Git configuration
and reconcile drift.
Interview precision: A delivery controller compares declared version-controlled desired state
with live state and reconciles according to its configured sync policy.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Git change -> review -> rendered desired objects
Delivery controller -> compare -> authorized synchronization
Live health and drift -> observable status
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Version history can explain a deployment change and support
reproducible rollback decisions. Automatic synchronization, pruning and self-healing are
policy choices, not identical defaults across products.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you make an emergency change persistent and reviewable?
Answer: Commit the approved emergency change into Git, or it may be reverted
by reconciliation.
Watch out: A manual production edit may be reverted by reconciliation. A healthy sync
status alone does not prove business behavior.

pages.title: Does helm rollback or a Git revert undo every release effect?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Helm, Kustomize, apply and GitOps FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q085. Does helm rollback or a Git revert undo
every release effect?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Helm rollback or Git revert changes manifests; it cannot undo every
changed database row or side effect.
Interview precision: No. It changes declared release state under the tool's contract; migrations,
external effects, volumes and runtime configuration may need separate recovery.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Artifact rollback -> reviewed earlier image/template
Schema rollback  -> separate compatibility/recovery decision
External effects -> durable compensation or reconciliation
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Use backward-compatible migration sequencing where possible.
Check hooks, retained revisions, secret versions and data compatibility before treating
rollback as safe. Observe restored user behavior after the change.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What would block a rollback after a data transformation?
Answer: Backward-incompatible transformed data may need a forward fix,
compatible reader or restored data.
Watch out: Pruning or reverting a storage object can be destructive. A packaging tool is
not an application-consistent backup system.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Spring Boot and Java workload design FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q086. What should a production Spring Boot
Deployment define?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
A production Java Deployment needs secure identity, resources, probes,
traffic, config and graceful shutdown.
Interview precision: An explicit artifact, runtime identity, resources, probes, configuration,
writable paths and termination policy should match the application's verified requirements.
→ →

Image: approved registry digest
HTTP: main listener 8080 with /livez and /readyz

application teams. Test the image under the same settings rather than adding them only in
production. Record supported Spring and JDK versions.

and business smoke tests.

behavior can prevent startup.

pages.title: Why should database pool size account for replica count?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Spring Boot and Java workload design FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q087. Why should database pool size account for
replica count?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Every new API Pod opens database connections, so total pool size must
fit database capacity.
Interview precision: Each replica can open its own connections; scaling and rollout overlap
multiply the possible total load on the database.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Steady replicas: 6
Pool maximum per replica: 20
Surge allowance: 1 replica
Possible API pool connections during rollout: 7 x 20 = 140
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Add jobs, administration and other services before comparing with
the database's budget. A small per-instance pool can collectively exceed the safe capacity.
Tie HPA bounds to downstream limits.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you choose a safe replica maximum for the order service?
Answer: Compute max replicas x per-Pod maximum connections, include surge
and other apps, then leave headroom.
Watch out: Virtual threads do not make database connections or CPU unlimited. Idle
connections and active query capacity are different concerns.

pages.title: How should a Kafka consumer shut down during Pod replacement?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Spring Boot and Java workload design FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q088. How should a Kafka consumer shut down
during Pod replacement?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Stop new consumption, finish or cancel safely, and close Kafka clients
during graceful shutdown.
Interview precision: Stop admitting new work, finish or safely abandon bounded processing,
coordinate acknowledgment and commit behavior, then close the consumer within the grace
budget.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Pod terminating -> consumer drain policy
Successful durable processing -> corresponding offset policy
Interrupted processing -> safe redelivery and deduplication
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Kafka group rebalancing and a forced termination can lead to
redelivery. Application transactions and external side effects must be designed for that
possibility. Measure worst-case processing and use idempotent business operations.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What happens if the database commits but the offset is not committed?
Answer: The message may be processed again; dedupe the effect using a stable
event ID or database transaction.
Watch out: Kubernetes does not make external payments exactly once. More consumer
replicas are useful only within partition and downstream constraints.

pages.title: Why can a Java image fail only on some cluster nodes?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Spring Boot and Java workload design FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q089. Why can a Java image fail only on some
cluster nodes?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
The chosen CPU architecture, kernel and native dependencies may vary
by node.
Interview precision: Image platform selection, native dependencies, permissions, node features
and runtime configuration can differ across eligible nodes.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl get nodes -L kubernetes.io/arch
kubectl get pod POD -n interview -o wide
kubectl describe pod POD -n interview
# Verify image index variants and any JNI/native-agent requirements.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Portable bytecode does not make an AMD64 native library work on
ARM64. Select appropriate image variants or constrain placement when a supported
runtime requirement demands it. Compare the actual admitted inputs.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you test the ARM variant before allowing ARM node placement?
Answer: Build/test the ARM64 image on an ARM-capable runner, verify digest
and JNI dependencies, then permit ARM nodes.
Watch out: Architecture labels are not a substitute for testing each published variant.
Kernel and storage behavior can also matter.

pages.title: How should business readiness differ from an alive JVM?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Spring Boot and Java workload design FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q090. How should business readiness differ from
an alive JVM?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Being alive means the JVM responds; being ready means this instance
can serve its assigned work.
Interview precision: Readiness must match the traffic the instance can safely accept, while
liveness should target local failures where restart is an appropriate repair.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Alive JVM -> process and local progress
Ready API -> required initialization and traffic contract
Correct order flow -> transaction, authorization and event behavior
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Warm-up, schema compatibility or intentional drain can make an
alive instance unready. A synthetic business check can verify more than health groups, but
it needs safe test data and side-effect policy.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which readiness condition would you use after loading a required reference-
data cache?
Answer: Mark ready only when essential reference data has loaded and required
local startup steps finished.
Watch out: Putting a slow full transaction in a frequent liveness probe can create load
and restart storms.

pages.title: What does a PodDisruptionBudget protect?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 · Availability, disruption and rollout strategy FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q091. What does a PodDisruptionBudget protect?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
PDB limits eligible voluntary evictions that would reduce available
replicas below its rule.
Interview precision: A PDB limits eligible voluntary disruptions through the eviction mechanism
based on workload availability; it does not prevent all failures or direct deletions.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata: {name: orders}
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: orders}}
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · With three healthy matching Pods, one voluntary eviction may be
allowed. With only two healthy Pods, maintenance can be blocked. Rollout strategy has its
own availability controls.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why can a safe drain be blocked while an application rollout still replaces
Pods?
Answer: Draining uses the eviction API and honors the PDB; rollout replacement
can follow separate controller rules.
Watch out: PDB does not stop a node crash, every direct Pod delete or Deployment-
controlled rolling-update deletion.
Original guide: page 61 · K03, K23, K28, K06, S02 (source directory).

pages.title: Why are three replicas on one node not sufficient high availability?
pages.fullText:

Q092. Why are three replicas on one node not
sufficient high availability?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Three copies on one node all fail together if that node fails.
Interview precision: They share the same node failure domain and can fail together; topology
and independent dependency resilience determine the actual protection.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Replicas -> spread across eligible nodes
Availability requirement -> consider zone placement
Shared database -> independent failure and recovery design
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Use supported spread or anti-affinity policy with sufficient capacity.
Node diversity is only one layer: shared storage, network and database failures can still
affect every API replica.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What would happen if the largest node or one zone disappeared?
Answer: Spread across nodes/zones and test losing one node or zone while
preserving minimum capacity.
Watch out: Strict placement without enough eligible domains can reduce running
capacity. Design and test the capacity tradeoff.

pages.title: How do rolling, blue-green and canary deployment differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 · Availability, disruption and rollout strategy FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q093. How do rolling, blue-green and canary
deployment differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Rolling swaps Pods gradually, blue-green switches environments, and
canary shifts small traffic fractions.
Interview precision: They replace instances incrementally, switch traffic between deployment
groups, or expose a limited candidate share before promotion.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Rolling:    old/new versions overlap during replacement
Blue-green: switch traffic between prepared groups
Canary:     measure limited candidate traffic before expansion
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Controllers and routing integrations implement the chosen strategy.
Standard Deployment rolling updates do not alone provide every precise traffic-weight
policy. Database compatibility must cover coexistence and rollback.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which metric would stop promotion despite healthy Pods?
Answer: Stop promotion if customer error rate, latency or business success
worsens, even if Pods are Ready.
Watch out: A Service selector switch may not instantly end all old connections. Canary
evidence needs representative traffic and user-impact signals.

dropped connections and duplicate effects.

CHAPTER 20 · Cluster operations and recovery boundaries FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q096. What is the difference between cordon,
drain and uncordon?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Cordon blocks new scheduling, drain evicts supported workloads, and
uncordon reopens scheduling.
Interview precision: Cordon marks a node unschedulable for normal placement; drain
attempts supported workload eviction; uncordon restores normal scheduling eligibility.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl cordon NODE
# Review workload and data impact before an authorized drain.
kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets
kubectl uncordon NODE
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Cordon alone does not move existing Pods. Drain respects
applicable eviction constraints and has special handling for DaemonSets, local data and
unmanaged workloads. Review failed preconditions rather than adding force blindly.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How could a PDB or node-local volume block maintenance?
Answer: PDB minAvailable or node-local storage may prevent eviction; inspect
and plan maintenance accordingly.
Watch out: These are operator commands, not exercises against an unknown cluster. Do
not add delete-emptydir-data without understanding disposable-data loss.

pages.title: What happens when a node becomes unavailable?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 · Cluster operations and recovery boundaries FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q097. What happens when a node becomes
unavailable?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
A lost node may trigger Pod replacement elsewhere after control-plane
detection and timeouts.
Interview precision: Node conditions, controller detection and configured eviction/replacement
behavior guide recovery, while storage and capacity determine where replacements can run.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl get nodes
kubectl describe node NODE

pages.title: Why is disk or ephemeral-storage pressure different from application heap pressure?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 · Cluster operations and recovery boundaries FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q098. Why is disk or ephemeral-storage pressure
different from application heap pressure?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Disk pressure is node-storage exhaustion, not necessarily JVM heap
failure.
Interview precision: Node storage pressure concerns local logs, writable layers and temporary
data; it can cause eviction even without Java heap exhaustion.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl describe node NODE
kubectl describe pod POD -n interview
# Inspect node disk, container logs and ephemeral-storage policy.

Volume-backed data has a separate backend capacity contract. Apply rotation and bounded
scratch storage, then verify retention and incident evidence.

Which application write paths can consume node-local storage?
Answer: Container logs, emptyDir, writable layers, temp uploads, heap dumps and
image layers can fill node storage.
Watch out: More heap is not a repair for a full node disk. An Evicted Pod and OOMKilled
container describe different paths.

pages.title: How should Kubernetes upgrades be planned?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 · Cluster operations and recovery boundaries FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q099. How should Kubernetes upgrades be
planned?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Upgrade control plane and nodes using compatibility checks, staged
node pools and safe workload drains.
Interview precision: Follow the distribution's supported sequence and version-skew policy,
check API compatibility and add-on support, then stage and verify recovery.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Inventory: control plane, nodes, CNI, CSI, controllers and CRDs
Review: supported skew and removed/deprecated APIs
Rehearse: backup/restore plus workload and traffic checks
Upgrade: approved staged sequence with observation
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Version compatibility covers more than kubectl and the API server.
Webhooks, operators, storage drivers and network controllers can affect admission or
workload operation. Use the official policy for the exact versions.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which application tests should gate a node-pool upgrade?
Answer: Gate on API compatibility, CNI/CSI checks, Java smoke tests, disruption
budget and user SLIs.
Watch out: Do not invent a universal safe upgrade order for every managed or self-
hosted product. A downgrade may not be a supported rollback.

pages.title: What should a disaster-recovery plan include?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 · Cluster operations and recovery boundaries FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q100. What should a disaster-recovery plan
include?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Disaster recovery must restore cluster configuration and business data
within tested goals.
Interview precision: Define acceptable downtime and data loss, then test infrastructure,
configuration, credentials, persistent data and application recovery together.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
Control plane: supported state recovery
Application:   reproducible images and manifests
Data:          consistent backups/replication and restore
Traffic:       routing, identity and observed business checks
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · A restored Deployment can still fail because its secret, storage class
or database is missing. Recovery evidence should include elapsed time and data
correctness. Keep backups in an appropriate independent failure domain.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you prove that a recovered order service preserves committed
orders?
Answer: Restore a backup into isolation, replay required logs and compare
committed order IDs and totals.
Watch out: Replica count and retained PVCs are not substitutes for a recovery rehearsal.

cluster?

pages.title: Why is a locally built Docker image unavailable to a Pod?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 21 · Minikube, image loading and Windows/WSL access FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q102. Why is a locally built Docker image
unavailable to a Pod?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
A Pod uses the image store on its Kubernetes node, not necessarily the
laptop's Docker images.
Interview precision: The cluster's node runtime can use a different image store from the
developer's Docker client or daemon.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
docker build -t orders-api:local .
minikube image load orders-api:local -p interview-lab
minikube image ls -p interview-lab
# Alternative: minikube image build -t orders-api:local . -p interview-lab
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Load or build into the intended profile and verify node-side
availability. Then use the exact tag and a compatible pull policy. With multiple nodes,
confirm the required image distribution.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What would ImagePullBackOff tell you after loading the image?
Answer: If pull still fails, inspect tag/policy, node image cache, registry access and
Pod events.
Watch out: A successful host docker build does not prove Kubernetes can fetch or find
the image. Native architecture still matters.

pages.title: How do Always, IfNotPresent and Never image pull policies differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 21 · Minikube, image loading and Windows/WSL access FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q103. How do Always, IfNotPresent and Never
image pull policies differ?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Always requests the image each start; IfNotPresent pulls only if missing;
Never uses local only.
Interview precision: They control registry resolution or local-image reliance according to the
runtime contract; tags and defaults must be considered deliberately.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
image: orders-api:local
imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
# Use an explicitly loaded image for this local exercise.
# Never requires the needed image to be present on the target node.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · Always can still reuse cached content after resolving the required
image identity. IfNotPresent can reuse a node's local tag, so mutable tag updates can
produce confusing results. Prefer new tags or digests for repeatable delivery.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why can two nodes run different bytes behind one reused local tag?
Answer: Different nodes may keep different bytes under one mutable tag; use
immutable tags or digests.
Watch out: Pull-policy defaulting occurs when the object is created; changing the image
tag does not automatically imply a new default policy.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 21 · Minikube, image loading and Windows/WSL access FOUNDATION → ARCHITECT
Q104. Why does NodePort access sometimes fail
on Windows/WSL or Docker Desktop?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Desktop/WSL node addresses or routing may be hidden behind a VM/
NAT layer.
Interview precision: The local driver's node network may not be directly reachable from the
chosen host, so a supported proxy or tunnel route may be required.
→ →

minikube service orders --url -p interview-lab -n interview
# Or a stable local development endpoint:
kubectl port-forward -n interview svc/orders 18080:80
# Keep the port-forward process running; test localhost:18080.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS · minikube may print a temporary proxy URL depending on the driver
and platform. Service port-forward uses a local listener while selecting a backend Pod
through the Kubernetes path; it is a development diagnostic route.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you compare host access with a same-namespace Pod client?
Answer: Test through host port-forward and through a same-namespace Pod;
differences localize the broken route.
Watch out: The generated proxy URL can change and may require its process to stay
alive. Port-forward success does not test the normal Service datapath or Ingress.

Q106. A Spring API is Running but Ingress returns
503. How do you investigate?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
A Running Pod can be unready or have a wrong Service/Ingress route.
Interview precision: Locate the response source and trace route ownership, Service selector,
ready EndpointSlices, target port, listener and policy in that order.
→ →
YAML / COMMAND EXAMPLE
kubectl get ingress,svc,pods -n orders
kubectl get endpointslices -n orders \
  -l kubernetes.io/service-name=orders
kubectl logs API_POD -n orders --tail=100

many failures before proxy tuning. If a direct backend test works, compare the controller
route and logs. A backend-generated 503 needs application diagnosis.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What observation would shift attention from readiness to path rewriting?
Answer: If direct Service access succeeds and returns 404 only on ingress,
inspect path rewrite and Host rules.
Watch out: Preserve the exact request host/path and release identity. Deleting all Pods
can worsen availability without repairing selection.

pages.fullText:

Q107. A rollout stalls when readiness is enabled.
What is your approach?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
Check exact probe path, port, startup time, dependencies and events
without removing protection.
Interview precision: Check probe response, startup timing, endpoint access and dependencies,
then inspect capacity and the Deployment's progress conditions.
→ →

kubectl describe deployment orders -n orders
kubectl describe pod NEW_POD -n orders
kubectl logs NEW_POD -n orders
# Verify /readyz on the configured port and security policy.

fixes. With maxUnavailable=0, an unready new Pod can deliberately preserve old capacity

before readiness/liveness checks.

rather than hiding the gate.

pages.fullText:

Q108. HPA adds API replicas, but latency gets
worse. What could cause it?
20-SECOND ANSWER • IN SIMPLE WORDS
More API Pods can overload a shared database or connection pool,
making latency worse.
Interview precision: Scaling can increase downstream contention, connection demand,
rebalances, warm-up work or scheduling pressure when the shared bottleneck does not scale.
→ →

Compare: replicas, pool totals, DB latency, queue depth
Inspect: CPU throttling, request rate, GC and readiness
Check:   scale timing and deployment overlap

saturated database may need bounded API concurrency and query repair rather than
more consumers. Verify metric meaning and prevent oscillation.
INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What safe mitigation would you choose while investigating the shared
bottleneck?
Answer: Cap replicas/pools and apply admission or backpressure while
measuring and fixing the shared limit.
Watch out: A correlation alone is not proof; compare workload changes and controlled
test evidence.

detach before attachment.

pages.title: HANDS-ON LAB 01 / 12
pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON LAB 01 / 12
L01 · Declare and scale a Deployment
Goal: The controller maintains Pods for its updated replica goal. Scaling changes the
replica count without requiring a different image template.
SOURCE LAB · RUN ONLY ON A DISPOSABLE LOCAL CLUSTER
set -eu
test -z "$(ls -A)"
kubectl config current-context
K_NS="k8s-l01-$$"
! kubectl get namespace "$K_NS" >/dev/null 2>&1
kubectl create namespace "$K_NS"
trap 'kubectl delete namespace "$K_NS" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
cat > web.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: web}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: web}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: web}}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:stable
          ports: [{name: http, containerPort: 80}]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 2
YAML
kubectl apply -n "$K_NS" -f web.yaml
kubectl rollout status deployment/web -n "$K_NS" --timeout=120s
kubectl scale deployment/web -n "$K_NS" --replicas=3
kubectl rollout status deployment/web -n "$K_NS" --timeout=120s
test "$(kubectl get deploy web -n "$K_NS" -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')" = 3
test "$(kubectl get deploy web -n "$K_NS" -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}')" = 3
printf 'PASS: Deployment desired and ready replicas are three\n'
Watch for: Needs capacity for three small nginx Pods. Image-pull access and namespace admission must
work.

pages.title: HANDS-ON LAB 04 / 12
pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON LAB 04 / 12
L04 · ConfigMap environment snapshot versus file
update
Goal: Projected configuration can refresh eventually; the container environment remains
the startup snapshot. No subPath mount is used.
SOURCE LAB · RUN ONLY ON A DISPOSABLE LOCAL CLUSTER
set -eu
test -z "$(ls -A)"
kubectl config current-context
K_NS="k8s-l04-$$"
! kubectl get namespace "$K_NS" >/dev/null 2>&1
kubectl create namespace "$K_NS"
trap 'kubectl delete namespace "$K_NS" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
cat > config.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata: {name: settings}
data: {MODE: old}
YAML
cat > pod.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: worker}
spec:
  containers:
    - name: worker
      image: busybox:1.37
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 600"]
      env:
        - name: MODE
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef: {name: settings, key: MODE}
      volumeMounts:
        - {name: settings, mountPath: /config}
  volumes:
    - name: settings
      configMap: {name: settings}
YAML
kubectl apply -n "$K_NS" -f config.yaml -f pod.yaml
kubectl wait pod/worker -n "$K_NS" --for=condition=Ready --timeout=120s
test "$(kubectl exec -n "$K_NS" worker -- printenv MODE)" = old
kubectl patch configmap settings -n "$K_NS" --type=merge \
  -p '{"data":{"MODE":"new"}}'
K_UPDATED=0
for K_N in $(seq 1 36); do
  if test "$(kubectl exec -n "$K_NS" worker -- cat /config/MODE)" = new; then
    K_UPDATED=1; break
  fi
  sleep 5
done
test "$K_UPDATED" = 1
test "$(kubectl exec -n "$K_NS" worker -- printenv MODE)" = old
printf 'PASS: projected file updated; environment remained old\n'
Watch for: Propagation timing is cluster-dependent. The bounded wait can fail on unusually slow settings.
This does not test application hot reload.

pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON LAB 05 / 12
L05 · Narrow RBAC scope for a ServiceAccount
Goal: The Role contains only selected ConfigMap read verbs, and the namespaced
binding grants that scope to the lab account.
SOURCE LAB · RUN ONLY ON A DISPOSABLE LOCAL CLUSTER
set -eu

kubectl create rolebinding reader -n "$K_NS" --role=config-reader \
  --serviceaccount="$K_NS:reader"

printf 'PASS: account can read ConfigMaps but not Secrets\n'

pages.title: HANDS-ON LAB 06 / 12
pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON LAB 06 / 12
L06 · Bounded Job completion
Goal: The Job records successful completion rather than maintaining a permanent server.
The command is harmless and deterministic.
SOURCE LAB · RUN ONLY ON A DISPOSABLE LOCAL CLUSTER

cat > job.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: task}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 120
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: task
          image: busybox:1.37
          command: ["sh", "-c", "printf 'complete\n'"]
YAML
kubectl apply -n "$K_NS" -f job.yaml
kubectl wait job/task -n "$K_NS" --for=condition=Complete --timeout=150s

test "$(kubectl get job task -n "$K_NS" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}')" = 1
printf 'PASS: Job completed once with the expected output\n'

pages.title: HANDS-ON LAB 09 / 12
pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON LAB 09 / 12
L09 · Diagnose an unsatisfiable node selector
Goal: The lab first confirms that no node has the requested label. The scheduler cannot
satisfy the selector, independent of current CPU utilization.
SOURCE LAB · RUN ONLY ON A DISPOSABLE LOCAL CLUSTER
set -eu
test -z "$(ls -A)"
kubectl config current-context
K_NS="k8s-l09-$$"
! kubectl get namespace "$K_NS" >/dev/null 2>&1
kubectl create namespace "$K_NS"
trap 'kubectl delete namespace "$K_NS" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
cat > pod.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: worker}
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    interview.example.com/eligible: never-match
  containers:
    - name: worker
      image: busybox:1.37
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 600"]
YAML
test -z "$(kubectl get nodes -l interview.example.com/eligible=never-match -o name)"
kubectl apply -n "$K_NS" -f pod.yaml
kubectl wait pod/worker -n "$K_NS" --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Pending --timeout=30s
test -z "$(kubectl get pod worker -n "$K_NS" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')"
kubectl describe pod worker -n "$K_NS"
# Verify scheduler evidence rather than changing shared node labels.
printf 'PASS: Pod is Pending and has no assigned node\n'
Watch for: Pending alone does not prove the cause. Read Events for the actual scheduling message;
admission or cluster failure can produce other symptoms.

HANDS-ON LAB 10 / 12
L10 · Observe a stalled rollout and explicit undo
Goal: A missing nginx path makes new replicas unready while the previous template can
still provide capacity. The exercise chooses an explicit undo after observing the failure.
SOURCE LAB · RUN ONLY ON A DISPOSABLE LOCAL CLUSTER
set -eu
test -z "$(ls -A)"
kubectl config current-context
K_NS="k8s-l10-$$"
! kubectl get namespace "$K_NS" >/dev/null 2>&1
kubectl create namespace "$K_NS"
trap 'kubectl delete namespace "$K_NS" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
cat > web.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: web}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: web}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: web}}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:stable
          ports: [{name: http, containerPort: 80}]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 2
YAML
kubectl apply -n "$K_NS" -f web.yaml
kubectl rollout status deployment/web -n "$K_NS" --timeout=120s
K_PATCH='{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[
  {"name":"web","readinessProbe":{
    "httpGet":{"path":"/missing-lab-path","port":"http"}}}
]}}}}'
kubectl patch deployment web -n "$K_NS" --type=strategic -p "$K_PATCH"
if kubectl rollout status deployment/web -n "$K_NS" --timeout=30s; then
  printf 'FAIL: broken readiness unexpectedly passed\n' >&2; exit 1
fi
kubectl describe deployment web -n "$K_NS"
kubectl rollout undo deployment/web -n "$K_NS"
kubectl rollout status deployment/web -n "$K_NS" --timeout=120s
test "$(kubectl get deploy web -n "$K_NS" -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}')" = 2
printf 'PASS: rollout stalled; explicit undo restored ready replicas\n'
Watch for: The 30-second client timeout is not an automatic rollback or necessarily the Deployment
progress deadline. Real rollbacks require schema/config compatibility review.

pages.title: HANDS-ON LAB 12 / 12
pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON LAB 12 / 12
L12 · Temporary host access with port-forward
Goal: An omitted local port requests an available one. The script discovers the reported
loopback port and tests HTTP while the forwarding process is alive.
SOURCE LAB · RUN ONLY ON A DISPOSABLE LOCAL CLUSTER
set -eu
test -z "$(ls -A)"
kubectl config current-context
K_NS="k8s-l12-$$"
! kubectl get namespace "$K_NS" >/dev/null 2>&1
kubectl create namespace "$K_NS"
trap 'kubectl delete namespace "$K_NS" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
cat > web.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: web}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: web}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: web}}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:stable
          ports: [{name: http, containerPort: 80}]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 2
YAML
cat > service.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: web}
spec:
  selector: {app: web}
  ports: [{name: http, port: 80, targetPort: http}]
YAML
kubectl apply -n "$K_NS" -f web.yaml -f service.yaml
kubectl rollout status deployment/web -n "$K_NS" --timeout=120s
kubectl port-forward -n "$K_NS" svc/web :80 > forward.log 2>&1 &
K_FORWARD_PID=$!
trap 'kill "$K_FORWARD_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true;
      kubectl delete namespace "$K_NS" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
K_PORT=""
for K_N in $(seq 1 30); do
  K_PORT=$(sed -n 's/.*127.0.0.1:\([0-9]*\) -> 80.*/\1/p' forward.log | head -n 1)
  if test -n "$K_PORT"; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
test -n "$K_PORT"
curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:$K_PORT" -o page.html
grep -q 'Welcome to nginx' page.html
printf 'PASS: temporary local port reached the selected backend\n'
Watch for: Requires host curl and standard sed/head. Port-forward uses a Kubernetes diagnostic
connection, not the ordinary Service virtual-IP or external-ingress path.

pages.title: What is AWS and what does cloud computing change?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Cloud foundations and interview thinking INTERVIEW NOTE 001/100
Q001. What is AWS and what does cloud computing
change?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
AWS lets teams rent computing, storage, and managed services when
needed instead of buying all the hardware first.
Precise interview detail: AWS supplies on-demand infrastructure and managed services. You
trade some infrastructure ownership for service contracts, usage-based costs and API-driven
operations. Your application correctness, access controls and architecture still need deliberate
engineering.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Traditional: buy server -> install OS -> deploy app
AWS option: provision capacity -> deploy -> measure
Managed option: use service API -> manage data and access
WHAT HAPPENS · A Spring service can run on a VM, a managed container platform or a
function. The programming model and operating responsibilities differ.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which responsibilities would you keep when moving a Java API from EC2 to
ECS?
Answer: You still own Java code, application configuration, IAM access, data
protection, monitoring, deployments, and recovery. ECS manages container
scheduling, not business correctness.
Common mistake: Calling every managed service serverless hides meaningful capacity and
billing differences.
Source guide p. 6   ·   Further reading: A01, A02, A41, A42

pages.title: What is the shared responsibility model?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Cloud foundations and interview thinking INTERVIEW NOTE 002/100
Q002. What is the shared responsibility model?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
AWS secures the cloud infrastructure. You secure the way your application
uses cloud services and customer data.
Precise interview detail: AWS protects the underlying cloud infrastructure. Customers protect
their use of it, including identities, data and configuration. The boundary moves by service: an
EC2 guest OS needs your patching, while a managed database removes much of that host
administration.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
EC2: customer patches guest OS and application
RDS: customer controls DB access, schema and queries
S3: customer controls object access and retention
WHAT HAPPENS · Using a managed service changes the boundary rather than eliminating your
duties.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you explain this boundary for Lambda?
Answer: For Lambda, AWS manages the hosts and runtime infrastructure; you still
control function code, dependencies, IAM role, secrets, input checks, data, and
observability.
Common mistake: An encrypted bucket can still expose data through an overly broad policy.
Source guide p. 7   ·   Further reading: A01, A02, A41, A42

their use of it, including identities, data and configuration. The boundary moves by service: an
EC2 guest OS needs your patching, while a managed database removes much of that host
administration.
pages.pitfall: An encrypted bucket can still expose data through an overly broad policy.
pages.followup:
How would you explain this boundary for Lambda?
Answer: For Lambda, AWS manages the hosts and runtime infrastructure; you still
control function code, dependencies, IAM role, secrets, input checks, data, and
observability.

pages.title: What is the difference between a Region, Availability Zone and edge location?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Cloud foundations and interview thinking INTERVIEW NOTE 003/100
Q003. What is the difference between a Region,
Availability Zone and edge location?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A Region is a geographic area, an AZ is an isolated location inside a
Region, and an edge location brings selected content closer to users.
Precise interview detail: A Region is a geographic AWS service area. An Availability Zone is an
isolated infrastructure location within a Region, built from one or more data centers. Edge
locations serve functions such as content delivery close to users; they are not interchangeable
with application AZs.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Region: application and primary data location
AZ A + AZ B: independent deployment failure domains
Edge: cache selected HTTP responses near users
WHAT HAPPENS · Choose Regions for latency, residency, service availability and disaster
recovery. Choose AZs for in-Region resilience.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When would two Regions be justified instead of two AZs?
Answer: Choose two Regions when a whole-Region outage, residency rule, or global
latency target demands it. Multi-AZ is usually simpler for routine failure recovery
within one Region.
Common mistake: Two instances in one AZ do not protect against that AZ failing.
Source guide p. 7   ·   Further reading: A01, A02, A41, A42
Region Several AZs Independent recovery
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 7

pages.title: Is high availability the same as disaster recovery?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Cloud foundations and interview thinking INTERVIEW NOTE 004/100
Q004. Is high availability the same as disaster
recovery?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
High availability reduces ordinary outages. Disaster recovery gets the
business running again after a major incident or data loss.
Precise interview detail: High availability limits interruption from expected component failures.
Disaster recovery restores business capability after a larger disruption. Both require explicit
failure assumptions; DR additionally depends on recovery procedures, independent copies and
tested recovery objectives.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
HA scenario: one task or AZ fails
DR scenario: Region unavailable or data corrupted
RTO: time to recover service
RPO: acceptable amount of lost data, expressed as time
WHAT HAPPENS · A multi-AZ database can keep serving through a host failure while
propagating accidental deletion to its replicas.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How do you test recovery from a destructive schema migration?
Answer: Rehearse restoring a backup to a separate environment, apply or reverse
migration steps, confirm key records and application compatibility, then measure RTO
and RPO. Never test only backup creation.
Common mistake: Replica availability is not an independent recoverable backup.
Source guide p. 8   ·   Further reading: A01, A02, A41, A42
Backup Isolated restore Validate data
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 8

business running again after a major incident or data loss.

pages.title: How should a senior candidate approach an AWS design question?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 · Cloud foundations and interview thinking INTERVIEW NOTE 005/100
Q005. How should a senior candidate approach an
AWS design question?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Start with requirements and risks, then pick AWS services. Tell the
interviewer how you would test the design.
Precise interview detail: Clarify users, traffic, data, consistency, security and recovery objectives
before choosing services. Explain an initial architecture, identify its bottleneck and failure
boundary, and show how measurements would justify changes.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Given: 500 requests/s, 200 ms target p95
Ask: peak factor, payload, transactions, residency
Design: ingress -> compute -> durable data
Validate: load, failure, restore, cost per request
WHAT HAPPENS · An interviewer learns more from your assumptions and tradeoffs than from a
long service list.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What new requirement would force you to change your first design?
Answer: A stricter recovery target, greater peak traffic, new data residency law, or
critical cross-Region availability need can change the network, storage, or compute
design. Say which assumption changed.
Common mistake: Treating illustrative traffic numbers as measured capacity leads to
unsupported promises.
Source guide p. 8   ·   Further reading: A01, A02, A41, A42
Requirements Minimal design Failure test
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 9

interviewer how you would test the design.

pages.title: What are IAM users, roles and policies?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · IAM, STS and authorization INTERVIEW NOTE 006/100
Q006. What are IAM users, roles and policies?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
IAM users represent identities, roles offer assumable temporary identity,
and policies say which API actions are allowed or denied.
Precise interview detail: A user is an identity that can have long-lived credentials. A role is an
assumable identity normally used with temporary credentials. Policies describe permitted or
denied actions. Prefer federation for people and workload roles for applications over distributing
static access keys.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Human -> identity provider -> temporary role session
ECS task -> task role -> S3 API
Policy -> Action + Resource + optional Condition
WHAT HAPPENS · The application uses a credential provider to obtain and refresh temporary
credentials.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why are static keys especially risky inside a container image?
Answer: A leaked image or registry layer can expose a static key to anyone who can
read it; rotation is hard once images are copied. Give containers short-lived workload-
role credentials.
Common mistake: A role's existence does not grant every caller permission to assume it.
Source guide p. 9   ·   Further reading: A03-A06
Image leak Static key copied Account exposure
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 11

pages.title: How does IAM evaluate access?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · IAM, STS and authorization INTERVIEW NOTE 007/100
Q007. How does IAM evaluate access?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
IAM considers the caller, requested action, resource, and all applicable
policies. An applicable explicit deny wins.
Precise interview detail: Authorization considers applicable identity and resource policies and
relevant limiting controls. An applicable explicit deny takes precedence. Boundaries and
organization policies limit authority rather than grant it. Evaluation details vary with the principal,
account relationship and service.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Identity Allow: s3:GetObject on reports/*
Boundary: permits the same action
Applicable explicit Deny: blocks the request
No relevant permission: implicit deny
WHAT HAPPENS · For diagnosis, identify the actual principal, API action, resource ARN and
request context, then inspect every applicable control.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What changes for a cross-account request?
Answer: Cross-account calls generally require permission on the caller side and trust
or resource authorization on the target side, with SCPs and other controls also
applied. Check both accounts and the actual role session.
Common mistake: Same-account resource grants to users, roles and sessions have different
implicit-deny interactions; avoid a universal 'all policies intersect' rule.
Source guide p. 10   ·   Further reading: A03-A06
Caller policy Target trust Final authorization
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 12

IAM considers the caller, requested action, resource, and all applicable
policies. An applicable explicit deny wins.

No relevant permission: implicit deny

pages.title: What is the difference between a trust policy and a permissions policy?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · IAM, STS and authorization INTERVIEW NOTE 008/100
Q008. What is the difference between a trust policy
and a permissions policy?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A trust policy decides who can assume a role. A permissions policy decides
what that role may do afterward.
Precise interview detail: A role trust policy controls who may assume the role and under what
conditions. Its permissions policies control what the resulting role session may do. Cross-
account access generally needs authorization in the caller account and trust or resource
authorization in the target account.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Trust: allow ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com to assume role
Permission: allow s3:GetObject on one object prefix
AssumeRole: returns temporary session credentials
WHAT HAPPENS · A trusted caller gets only the permissions of the session, subject to applicable
restrictions.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Where would you enforce an external ID for a third-party integration?
Answer: Put the external ID as an sts:ExternalId condition in the target role's trust
policy for the third party. Also restrict the trusted principal and grant only the needed
operations.
Common mistake: Adding S3 permissions does not fix a role's missing trust relationship.
Source guide p. 10   ·   Further reading: A03-A06
Trusted caller Assume role Scoped actions
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 13

what that role may do afterward.

pages.title: What do SCPs and permissions boundaries do?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · IAM, STS and authorization INTERVIEW NOTE 009/100
Q009. What do SCPs and permissions boundaries
do?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
SCPs and permissions boundaries cap possible permissions; they do not
grant access by themselves.
Precise interview detail: A service control policy restricts the permissions available to affected
principals in organization member accounts. A permissions boundary sets a maximum for an
IAM user or role. Neither is an independent permission grant. SCP scope and exceptions,
including management-account behavior, matter.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Role policy: allow a deployment action
Boundary: exclude IAM privilege escalation
SCP: restrict allowed Regions for member accounts
Effective access: evaluate grants and restrictions
WHAT HAPPENS · Use organization controls for guardrails and role policies for operational
permissions.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you safely delegate role creation to a deployment team?
Answer: Let deployment teams create only roles with a required permissions
boundary. Limit iam:PassRole, role paths, and policy changes; test that created roles
cannot escape the guardrails.
Common mistake: 'AdministratorAccess' does not bypass an applicable organizational
explicit deny.
Source guide p. 11   ·   Further reading: A03-A06
Role permission Boundary + SCP Limited authority
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 14

SCPs and permissions boundaries cap possible permissions; they do not
grant access by themselves.

pages.title: What is least privilege for an application?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 · IAM, STS and authorization INTERVIEW NOTE 010/100
Q010. What is least privilege for an application?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Least privilege means giving an application only the actions and resource
paths it actually needs.
Precise interview detail: Grant the smallest practical actions and resource scope that satisfy
observed business operations. Use conditions where supported and separate unrelated
workloads. Review real access, test denied paths and revise policies when the workload changes.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
{
 "Effect":"Allow", "Action":"s3:GetObject",
 "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::EXAMPLE_BUCKET/reports/*"
}
WHAT HAPPENS · This statement covers object reads under one prefix, not bucket listing or KMS
decryption.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you add prefix-restricted ListBucket access?
Answer: Add a separate s3:ListBucket statement against the bucket ARN and restrict
s3:prefix with a condition such as reports/*. Object reads still need a separate object
ARN statement.
Common mistake: An action can require a bucket ARN, object ARN, other service permission
or a resource policy; ARN shape is not interchangeable.
Source guide p. 11   ·   Further reading: A03-A06
Bucket ARN + prefix List keys Object permissions
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 15

paths it actually needs.

pages.title: What are a VPC, subnet and route table?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · VPC and network controls INTERVIEW NOTE 011/100
Q011. What are a VPC, subnet and route table?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A VPC is your AWS network, subnets are AZ-specific IP ranges, and route
tables decide where packets should go.
Precise interview detail: A VPC is an isolated network boundary. A subnet occupies one AZ and
defines an address range. A route table chooses destinations for traffic leaving the subnet. Route
reachability and security rules are separate concerns.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
VPC: 10.20.0.0/16
AZ A app subnet: 10.20.10.0/24
AZ B app subnet: 10.20.20.0/24
Route: destination CIDR -> target
WHAT HAPPENS · A multi-AZ service uses subnets in multiple AZs within the intended network.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why must subnet address ranges avoid overlap?
Answer: Overlapping addresses make routing ambiguous and complicate VPC peering,
Transit Gateway, VPN, or on-prem connectivity. Plan CIDR ranges before connecting
networks.
Common mistake: A route allowing reachability does not authorize an application
connection.
Source guide p. 12   ·   Further reading: A07-A10, A53, A54
VPC CIDR Non-overlap subnets Clear routes
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 17

pages.title: What makes a subnet public or private?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · VPC and network controls INTERVIEW NOTE 012/100
Q012. What makes a subnet public or private?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A public subnet routes toward an internet gateway. A private subnet does
not provide that direct route and can use NAT for outbound IPv4.
Precise interview detail: A public subnet has a route to an internet gateway. Direct IPv4 internet
communication also requires an appropriate public address and permissive controls. A private
subnet lacks that direct internet-gateway route; it may use a NAT gateway for outbound IPv4
access.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Public route: 0.0.0.0/0 -> internet gateway
Private route: 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT gateway
Private task: private IP, no public IP
Database: private subnet, bounded inbound rule
WHAT HAPPENS · A task in a private subnet can call public APIs through an established
outbound path without accepting unsolicited inbound connections through that NAT.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you handle IPv6 egress differently?
Answer: For private IPv6 outbound traffic, evaluate an egress-only internet gateway
and correct IPv6 routes and security controls. NAT Gateway is primarily an IPv4
solution; verify the specific setup.
Common mistake: Assigning a public IP alone does not create a working internet route.
Source guide p. 13   ·   Further reading: A07-A10, A53, A54
Private IPv6 subnet Egress-only IGW Internet
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 18

pages.title: How do security groups differ from network ACLs?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · VPC and network controls INTERVIEW NOTE 013/100
Q013. How do security groups differ from network
ACLs?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Security groups are stateful allow rules around resources. Network ACLs
are stateless ordered subnet rules that can also deny traffic.
Precise interview detail: Security groups are stateful allow-rule controls on supported resources
or network interfaces. Network ACLs are stateless subnet controls with ordered allow and deny
rules. Stateless controls need explicit allowance for both directions, including return traffic ports.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
ALB SG: inbound HTTPS from intended clients
Task SG: inbound 8080 from ALB SG
DB SG: inbound 5432 from task SG
NACL: evaluate inbound and outbound separately
WHAT HAPPENS · Referencing another security group expresses the permitted traffic source for
supported networking arrangements.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why can an allowed inbound connection still fail with a restrictive NACL?
Answer: The inbound NACL rule may permit the request while an outbound rule
blocks the response's ephemeral port, or vice versa. Inspect both directions and rule
order.
Common mistake: A security-group reference does not copy the referenced group's rules.
Source guide p. 13   ·   Further reading: A07-A10, A53, A54
Inbound accepted Return port blocked Timeout
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 19

pages.title: When should you use VPC endpoints instead of NAT?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · VPC and network controls INTERVIEW NOTE 014/100
Q014. When should you use VPC endpoints instead
of NAT?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Use VPC endpoints for private access to supported AWS services. NAT
supports general outbound internet access.
Precise interview detail: Use endpoints when private access to a supported service meets the
routing, security and cost requirements. Gateway endpoints are available for S3 and DynamoDB;
interface endpoints use private network interfaces for supported services. NAT supports broader
outbound destinations.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
S3 traffic -> gateway endpoint route
Secrets Manager -> supported interface endpoint
External payment API -> outbound internet path
Endpoint policy + IAM + resource policy -> evaluate
WHAT HAPPENS · An endpoint reduces reliance on public service paths but does not
automatically grant service access.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you compare endpoint and NAT costs for your traffic?
Answer: Estimate traffic volume, number of AZs, endpoint hourly charges, data-
processing charges, NAT transfer charges, and operational needs. Gateway endpoints
for S3/DynamoDB may have different pricing from interface endpoints.
Common mistake: Interface endpoint security groups, DNS settings and endpoint policies
can still block requests.
Source guide p. 14   ·   Further reading: A07-A10, A53, A54
AWS API traffic Endpoint or NAT Cost check
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 20

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 · VPC and network controls INTERVIEW NOTE 015/100
Q015. What are VPC peering, Transit Gateway, VPN
and Direct Connect?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH

encrypted tunnels, and Direct Connect gives dedicated connectivity.

managed hub for multiple networks. Site-to-Site VPN uses encrypted tunnels over network paths.

Many VPCs + on premises: evaluate a routing hub
VPN: encrypted tunnel

needs.

What redundancy would you add to hybrid connectivity?

separate locations, diverse devices and paths, monitored BGP failover, and a tested

pages.title: What is EC2 and how do you choose an instance?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 · EC2, Auto Scaling and instance operations INTERVIEW NOTE 016/100
Q016. What is EC2 and how do you choose an
instance?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
EC2 rents virtual machines. Choose the CPU, memory, networking, storage,
and processor type that match your measured Java workload.
Precise interview detail: EC2 provides virtual compute instances. Select an instance family and
size using CPU, memory, network, storage and architecture needs, then measure the workload.
Java heap alone is not the whole memory budget.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Task memory estimate:
heap + metaspace + thread stacks + native buffers
Measure: CPU, allocation rate, GC, RSS, throughput
Check: x86_64 or arm64 dependencies
WHAT HAPPENS · A larger machine may postpone a bottleneck without fixing database
contention or poor queries.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you benchmark a memory-heavy Java service?

pauses, native memory, thread count, p95/p99 latency, CPU, and throughput. Check
behavior near the memory ceiling.
Common mistake: Assuming equal vCPU counts produce identical performance ignores
generation and workload differences.

pages.title: What happens when an EC2 instance stops or terminates?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 · EC2, Auto Scaling and instance operations INTERVIEW NOTE 017/100
Q017. What happens when an EC2 instance stops or
terminates?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Stopping EC2 ends compute but can keep EBS volumes. Termination may
remove volumes depending on their settings; instance-store files are
temporary.
Precise interview detail: Stopping a supported EBS-backed instance stops its compute execution
while preserving attached EBS data. Termination ends the instance and removes volumes
configured for deletion. Instance-store data has a temporary lifecycle and should not be treated
as durable application storage.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Instance stopped: process gone, EBS retained
Instance terminated: inspect DeleteOnTermination
Instance store: do not depend on persistent recovery
External data: database or object storage
WHAT HAPPENS · Storage retention depends on the storage type and attachment configuration.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you recover a replacement service without local mutable state?
Answer: Build replacement machines from versioned images and infrastructure code.
Keep configuration and secrets external and business state in RDS, S3, or durable
services; run a failover test.
Common mistake: Stopped instances can still incur charges for retained storage and other
resources.
Source guide p. 15   ·   Further reading: A11-A13, A62

AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 24

pages.title: What is an Auto Scaling group?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 · EC2, Auto Scaling and instance operations INTERVIEW NOTE 018/100
Q018. What is an Auto Scaling group?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
An Auto Scaling group keeps the requested number of EC2 instances and
can raise or lower capacity using policies.
Precise interview detail: An Auto Scaling group maintains desired instance capacity across
configured locations and can adjust it using policies. Launch templates define instance
configuration. Health assessment and replacement help restore compute capacity but do not
prove that application dependencies are healthy.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Minimum: 2 instances
Desired: 3 instances
Maximum: 8 instances
Metric: suitable demand per serving instance
WHAT HAPPENS · Scaling policies need capacity headroom, initialization time and sensible
signals.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you scale a queue worker using backlog per instance?
Answer: Estimate acceptable queue wait and processing time, then scale from backlog
per healthy worker or oldest-message age. Add limits for worker startup and database
capacity.
Common mistake: Scaling CPU-bound workers using request count alone may miss uneven
processing cost.

Queue backlog Worker target Capacity cap
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 25

pages.title: What is the difference between On-Demand, Spot and commitment discounts?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 · EC2, Auto Scaling and instance operations INTERVIEW NOTE 019/100
Q019. What is the difference between On-Demand,
Spot and commitment discounts?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
On-Demand gives flexible capacity, Spot is cheaper but interruptible, and
commitments discount eligible long-term usage.
Precise interview detail: On-Demand suits flexible capacity without a long-term usage
commitment. Spot uses spare capacity with interruption risk. Savings Plans and Reserved
Instances are discount mechanisms with specific terms and coverage. Capacity reservations are
a separate concern and must be evaluated explicitly.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
API baseline: availability-sensitive capacity
Batch overflow: interruption-tolerant Spot workers
Stable measured usage: evaluate commitment coverage
Every option: compare utilization and constraints
WHAT HAPPENS · Design Spot workloads to checkpoint, retry and move work when interrupted.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which parts of a payment service would you place on Spot?
Answer: Put no irreplaceable payment decision on Spot alone. Spot can host
replayable, idempotent reconciliation or analytics workers with checkpoints and
durable queues.
Common mistake: A discount commitment should not be described as universally
guaranteeing capacity.
Source guide p. 16   ·   Further reading: A11-A13, A62
Payment authority Durable store Optional Spot worker

EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 26

pages.title: How do you operate EC2 securely without exposing SSH?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 · EC2, Auto Scaling and instance operations INTERVIEW NOTE 020/100
Q020. How do you operate EC2 securely without
exposing SSH?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Use controlled management access, instance roles, patching, logs, and
IMDSv2 rather than keeping SSH open to the world.
Precise interview detail: Use Systems Manager Session Manager where its prerequisites and
policies are satisfied, restrict administrative access, use instance roles and protect metadata
access. Maintain patching and auditability. Enforce IMDSv2 for compatible workloads and avoid
passing instance credentials to unrelated processes.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Operator -> authorized management session
Instance role -> required service actions
Metadata access -> controlled and IMDSv2-aware
Logs -> centralized audit and diagnostics
WHAT HAPPENS · Removing inbound SSH simplifies one access path, but management agents,
service reachability and operator permissions still need configuration.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you investigate an instance that cannot establish its management
connection?
Answer: Check instance SSM agent status, IAM instance profile, Systems Manager
permissions, VPC endpoints or internet path, DNS, proxy, and regional agent support.
Inspect managed-node connection status.
Common mistake: IMDSv2 does not replace IAM least privilege or workload isolation.
Source guide p. 17   ·   Further reading: A11-A13, A62
Instance agent IAM + network SSM control
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 27

pages.title: What is the difference between S3, EBS and EFS?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 · S3 and storage choices INTERVIEW NOTE 021/100
Q021. What is the difference between S3, EBS and
EFS?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
S3 is object storage, EBS is a disk-like block volume, and EFS is a shared
network filesystem.
Precise interview detail: S3 stores objects accessed through APIs. EBS supplies block storage
associated with EC2 availability-zone placement. EFS provides shared file storage using NFS with
deployment options and mount targets. Choose from access semantics, sharing, latency and
failure requirements.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Reports and images -> S3 objects
Database disk on EC2 -> EBS blocks
Shared POSIX-style files -> evaluate EFS
Durability requirement -> include backup and restore
WHAT HAPPENS · Replacing a filesystem with S3 normally changes the application interface.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which choice would you make for uploaded documents in a replicated API?
Answer: Store uploaded documents in S3 and put ownership, upload status, and object
keys in a database. Let multiple API replicas read through scoped permissions or
presigned URLs.
Common mistake: S3 key prefixes resemble directories but are not general filesystem
directories.
Source guide p. 18   ·   Further reading: A14-A16, A37

EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 29

pages.title: Is S3 strongly consistent?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 · S3 and storage choices INTERVIEW NOTE 022/100
Q022. Is S3 strongly consistent?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
S3 has strong consistency for supported object reads and listings after
writes, but it does not provide a database transaction across objects.
Precise interview detail: S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for object writes,
overwrites and deletes, including listings. This does not create multi-object transactions or
eliminate independent caches, replication delays and application races.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
PUT invoice-42.json succeeds
GET same key sees the successful write
Two writers overwrite one key: app needs coordination
CDN copy: governed by its separate cache behavior
WHAT HAPPENS · A client can observe a completed object write without using an old eventual-
consistency workaround.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would conditional requests protect an update from a lost write?
Answer: Use an ETag-based condition such as If-Match when updating an object so a
stale writer fails instead of overwriting a newer version. Handle conflicts explicitly.
Common mistake: Strong object consistency does not make a read-modify-write sequence
atomic.
Source guide p. 19   ·   Further reading: A14-A16, A37
Read ETag Conditional write Detect conflict
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 30

pages.title: What do S3 versioning and lifecycle rules provide?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 · S3 and storage choices INTERVIEW NOTE 023/100
Q023. What do S3 versioning and lifecycle rules
provide?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
S3 versioning saves separate object versions; lifecycle rules control when
objects or versions move or expire.
Precise interview detail: Versioning preserves distinct versions and changes deletion behavior.
Lifecycle rules transition or expire eligible objects and versions according to a policy. Together
they support retention management, but protection from deletion needs explicit permissions and
possibly Object Lock controls.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Version 1: original invoice
Version 2: corrected invoice
Delete marker: current key appears deleted
Recovery: choose a retained prior version
WHAT HAPPENS · Version history helps recover overwritten data when the prior version remains
available.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you test a retention policy before enabling it broadly?
Answer: Apply the rule to a test bucket with test versions, preview the selected objects,
verify Object Lock and retention expectations, and confirm restore before changing
production rules.
Common mistake: Expiring noncurrent versions or broad delete permissions can defeat
your recovery plan.
Source guide p. 19   ·   Further reading: A14-A16, A37
Version history Retention rule Recovery test
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 31

pages.title: How do presigned URLs work?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 · S3 and storage choices INTERVIEW NOTE 024/100
Q024. How do presigned URLs work?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A presigned URL grants temporary permission for a specific S3 operation;
anyone holding it can use it while valid.
Precise interview detail: A presigned URL authorizes a specific supported operation using the
signer's credentials and signature conditions for a limited validity period. It acts as a bearer
capability. Actual usability can end sooner if credentials expire or applicable permissions
change.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
API validates customer ownership
API presigns PUT for uploads/customer-42/object-id
Client uploads directly to S3
API verifies the completed object before publishing
WHAT HAPPENS · Direct upload can reduce traffic through your Java application.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you constrain upload size, type and downstream trust?
Answer: Authorize the caller first, use a narrow key, short expiry and signed conditions
where supported. Verify the stored object's actual size and magic bytes, scan it, and
publish only after validation.
Common mistake: A presigned URL can be reused during its usable period; it is not
inherently a one-time token.
Source guide p. 20   ·   Further reading: A14-A16, A37
Authorize Upload directly Verify + scan
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 32

pages.title: How do you secure an S3 bucket?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 · S3 and storage choices INTERVIEW NOTE 025/100
Q025. How do you secure an S3 bucket?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Keep buckets private, scope IAM access, encrypt objects, log sensitive
operations, and plan retention and recovery.
Precise interview detail: Use bounded IAM and bucket policies, appropriate Block Public Access
settings, encryption, audit signals and retention controls. Prefer explicit ownership and access
policies over unnecessary ACLs. Validate both intended access and unintended public or cross-
account paths.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Private bucket -> no public grants
Object prefix -> tenant-aware authorization
SSE-KMS -> evaluate S3 and KMS permissions
Audit -> record relevant data access events as needed
WHAT HAPPENS · Encryption at rest protects one threat surface; authorization decides who may
retrieve plaintext.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What would you inspect after an unexpected AccessDenied on an encrypted
object?
Answer: Check the real principal, bucket and object ARN, bucket policy, SCP, VPC
endpoint policy, key ownership, and KMS key policy or grants. SSE-KMS often needs
kms:Decrypt too.
Common mistake: Blocking public access is not a complete defense against an
overprivileged internal principal.
Source guide p. 20   ·   Further reading: A14-A16, A37
GetObject S3 checks KMS decrypt

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 · Load balancing, DNS and edge delivery INTERVIEW NOTE 026/100
Q026. What is the difference between ALB and
NLB?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
ALB understands HTTP paths and hosts. NLB routes lower-level TCP/UDP/
TLS traffic.
Precise interview detail: An Application Load Balancer routes HTTP and HTTPS traffic using
application-level rules such as paths and hosts. A Network Load Balancer handles transport-level
traffic such as TCP and UDP and TLS listeners. Choose from protocol behavior, addressing,
traffic scale and target needs.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
ALB: /orders -> order target group
ALB: /catalog -> catalog target group
NLB: TCP traffic -> transport-level targets
TLS termination: choose listener and trust boundary
WHAT HAPPENS · For a typical Spring REST API, ALB routing and health checks are often a
useful fit.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When would a non-HTTP protocol push you toward NLB?
Answer: Choose NLB for supported raw TCP or UDP protocols, certain fixed-address
needs, or applications where HTTP-aware routing is not appropriate. Check protocol
and target requirements.
Common mistake: A load balancer does not repair an unhealthy application or add
database capacity.

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 · Load balancing, DNS and edge delivery INTERVIEW NOTE 027/100
Q027. What do load-balancer health checks prove?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A health check tests a configured endpoint, not every user action or
database invariant.
Precise interview detail: They determine target health according to configured requests,
thresholds and timings. Design a fast endpoint that reflects traffic readiness. Separate startup
and readiness from deep diagnostics so a dependency incident does not cause harmful
replacement or admission behavior.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
GET /actuator/health/readiness -> serving readiness
Startup incomplete -> return non-ready status
Dependency incident -> controlled degradation policy
Shutdown -> stop new traffic, drain existing work
WHAT HAPPENS · Probe design affects routing and recovery. ALB can fail open when all
registered targets are unhealthy, so health status alone is not a hard security or traffic-
isolation boundary.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What should readiness return during a brief database failover?
Answer: Choose readiness based on whether the instance can serve useful requests.
During brief failover it may temporarily return unavailable; avoid restarting healthy
instances and test the load balancer's all-unhealthy behavior.
Common mistake: A health check that merely reports process existence misses deadlocked
request handling.

pages.title: What does Route 53 do?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 · Load balancing, DNS and edge delivery INTERVIEW NOTE 028/100
Q028. What does Route 53 do?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Route 53 turns names into addresses and supports different routing
policies. DNS caches can delay failover.
Precise interview detail: Route 53 provides DNS functionality and routing policies, with associated
health-check capabilities. DNS resolves names; clients and resolvers cache responses. DNS
failover therefore depends on health detection, TTLs, caches and client behavior rather than an
instantaneous global switch.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
api.example.com -> intended service endpoint
Policy -> simple, weighted, latency or failover design
TTL -> cache guidance for recursive resolvers
Client pool -> may retain existing connections
WHAT HAPPENS · Plan failover for new resolution and existing connections.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you verify a regional failover from multiple client networks?
Answer: Test from different networks and Regions, resolve the name repeatedly,
compare actual endpoint IPs, send application requests, and check recovery time for
both new and existing connections.
Common mistake: Lower TTL does not force every client to reconnect immediately.
Source guide p. 22   ·   Further reading: A17, A18, A55, A56, A64, A65
Health event DNS routing Client verification
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
