pages.title: What is CloudFront and what can be cached?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 · Load balancing, DNS and edge delivery INTERVIEW NOTE 029/100
Q029. What is CloudFront and what can be
cached?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
CloudFront caches eligible content near users. Cache keys and privacy
settings decide which response can be reused.
Precise interview detail: CloudFront delivers content through edge locations and can cache
eligible responses from origins. Configure cache keys and policies around the response's true
variation: path, selected headers, query parameters and cookies. Authenticated personalized
content needs particular care.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Static /assets/app-HASH.js -> long immutable cache
Product page -> bounded TTL and correct key
Personal invoice -> explicit protected delivery policy
Invalidation or new object key -> update strategy
WHAT HAPPENS · A cache hit avoids some origin work but may serve an older permitted
representation.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When would versioned object names be preferable to invalidation?
Answer: Use content-hashed file names for static JavaScript, images, and assets so old
and new releases can coexist and long cache lifetimes are safe. Invalidate when
names cannot change.
Common mistake: Omitting a tenant-dependent header from a shared cache key can
expose one tenant's response to another.
Source guide p. 22   ·   Further reading: A17, A18, A55, A56, A64, A65
Versioned URL Edge cache Safe release
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 38

pages.title: How do WAF, Shield and TLS differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 · Load balancing, DNS and edge delivery INTERVIEW NOTE 030/100
Q030. How do WAF, Shield and TLS differ?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
TLS encrypts transport, WAF filters selected web traffic, and Shield helps
defend against DDoS.
Precise interview detail: TLS protects data in transit and authenticates endpoints according to
certificate validation. AWS WAF evaluates web requests against rules on supported integrations.
AWS Shield addresses DDoS protection with different service tiers. These solve overlapping
operational concerns but do not replace application authorization.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
TLS -> secure connection to intended endpoint
WAF -> reject selected suspicious HTTP patterns
App -> authenticate user and authorize invoice access
Rate policy -> protect bounded backend capacity
WHAT HAPPENS · Layer edge controls with correct identity and resource ownership checks.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you distinguish credential stuffing from a large legitimate sale?
Answer: Compare account-level failed logins, IP/device patterns, bot indicators,
conversion rates, and authenticated activity. Apply user-aware limits without blocking
legitimate demand only because traffic is high.
Common mistake: A WAF rule cannot guarantee that every request is safe or that business-
level abuse is prevented.
Source guide p. 23   ·   Further reading: A17, A18, A55, A56, A64, A65
Traffic WAF + auth data Risk decision
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 39

pages.title: How do ECS, EKS and Fargate differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 · ECS, EKS and Java containers INTERVIEW NOTE 031/100
Q031. How do ECS, EKS and Fargate differ?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
ECS runs AWS-managed container workloads. EKS runs Kubernetes
workloads. Fargate is a compute choice available for supported workloads.
Precise interview detail: ECS is AWS container orchestration. EKS provides managed Kubernetes
control-plane capabilities. Fargate supplies a managed compute option for supported ECS and
EKS workloads. Orchestration choice and compute choice are separate decisions.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
ECS + Fargate -> managed task scheduling and compute
ECS + EC2 -> customer-managed container host capacity
EKS -> Kubernetes APIs and ecosystem
Choose -> skills, platform needs, operations and cost
WHAT HAPPENS · Fargate removes much host administration while leaving task configuration,
permissions and application operation with you.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What would justify EKS for a team already productive on ECS?
Answer: Choose EKS when standard Kubernetes APIs, operators, custom scheduling,
or an established K8s platform justify its extra operational work; not just because it
sounds more advanced.
Common mistake: Describing Fargate as a replacement for every Kubernetes capability
misses workload restrictions.
Source guide p. 24   ·   Further reading: A19-A21, A43, A49, A50
Team needs ECS or EKS EC2 or Fargate

pages.title: What are ECS task definitions, tasks and services?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 · ECS, EKS and Java containers INTERVIEW NOTE 032/100
Q032. What are ECS task definitions, tasks and
services?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
An ECS task definition is a blueprint, a task is one running copy, and a
service maintains desired tasks.
Precise interview detail: A task definition describes a workload configuration, including
containers and resources. A task is a running instance of that definition. A service maintains
desired task count and manages deployment and optional load-balancer integration.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Task definition revision: orders:17
Task: one launched instance of orders:17
Service desired count: 3
New revision: deployment replaces eligible old tasks
WHAT HAPPENS · The service is responsible for ongoing reconciliation rather than a single task
launch.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you roll back a failed service deployment?
Answer: Deploy a known-good task-definition revision or enable an appropriate
deployment circuit breaker and rollback. Validate database compatibility and user-
facing metrics after restoration.
Common mistake: Registering a task definition does not start a service or move production
traffic.
Source guide p. 25   ·   Further reading: A19-A21, A43, A49, A50
Revision Service deployment Verified rollback
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 42

pages.title: How do the ECS task role and execution role differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 · ECS, EKS and Java containers INTERVIEW NOTE 033/100
Q033. How do the ECS task role and execution role
differ?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
The ECS task role is for application AWS calls. The execution role is for
supported ECS startup actions such as image pulls and logs.
Precise interview detail: The task role supplies application permissions to AWS APIs. The
execution role supplies permissions used by ECS or Fargate agents for supported startup and
execution activities, such as pulling images, sending logs and resolving configured secrets. Keep
these identities separate.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
taskRoleArn -> application reads reports and sends SQS
executionRoleArn -> image pull and log delivery
secrets injection -> execution-role permission path
SDK secret fetch -> application task-role path
WHAT HAPPENS · Who retrieves a value determines which principal needs permission.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which role needs KMS access for a secret retrieved by Java at runtime?
Answer: If Java itself calls Secrets Manager and then KMS is needed, the task role
and relevant key policy must allow that action. Execution-role access applies to ECS-
managed secret injection.
Common mistake: Adding an S3 permission only to the execution role does not grant the
application's SDK that permission.
Source guide p. 25   ·   Further reading: A19-A21, A43, A49, A50
Task startup role Java task role KMS access

pages.title: How do you make Spring Boot ready for container deployment?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 · ECS, EKS and Java containers INTERVIEW NOTE 034/100
Q034. How do you make Spring Boot ready for
container deployment?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Use an immutable Java image, external configuration, limited JVM memory,
readiness checks, graceful shutdown, and workload credentials.
Precise interview detail: Build an immutable reviewed image, externalize configuration, budget
total JVM memory, expose bounded health endpoints and implement graceful shutdown. Tune
startup, request timeouts and connection pools for platform limits. Use workload credentials
through the SDK provider chain.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
server.shutdown=graceful
spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase=20s
management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true
# Select exposure and access controls deliberately.
WHAT HAPPENS · The platform and application must agree on admission and shutdown timing.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you detect memory pressure before task replacement?
Answer: Watch container RSS and memory utilization, GC activity, native memory and
thread count, JVM heap usage, and OOM kills. Alert before approaching task memory
limits.
Common mistake: Heap size equal to the container memory limit leaves no room for native
allocations and threads.

pages.title: Who is responsible for security in EKS?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 · ECS, EKS and Java containers INTERVIEW NOTE 035/100
Q035. Who is responsible for security in EKS?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
AWS operates the managed EKS control plane, while your team must
secure workloads, identities, data, and supported node configuration.
Precise interview detail: AWS manages the EKS control-plane responsibilities defined by the
service. Customers manage application code, workload identity and access, policies and data.
Responsibilities for nodes and OS maintenance depend on the selected compute option and EKS
mode.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Cluster -> control-plane service boundary
Workloads -> image, RBAC, secrets, network policy
Compute -> EC2 nodes or supported managed option
AWS access -> workload identity, bounded IAM role
WHAT HAPPENS · The managed control plane does not make every pod trustworthy or every
network policy effective.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you keep one namespace from reading another application's AWS
data?
Answer: Give each workload a dedicated service account and scoped IAM role, plus
namespace RBAC and network policies. Enforce tenant ownership in the application's
data layer.
Common mistake: Giving all pods the node's broad IAM authority destroys workload
separation.

pages.title: What is Lambda and when is it a good fit?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 · Lambda and API Gateway INTERVIEW NOTE 036/100
Q036. What is Lambda and when is it a good fit?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Lambda runs short-lived event or API logic without operating servers
directly. Compare its execution limits with your workload.
Precise interview detail: Lambda runs functions on managed compute in response to supported
invocations. It suits event-driven work and APIs that fit its execution constraints. Compare
startup behavior, duration, resource needs, concurrency and integration costs against containers
or other compute.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
S3 event -> thumbnail function
Scheduled event -> bounded cleanup job
HTTP integration -> short API operation
Long continuous process -> evaluate other compute
WHAT HAPPENS · There is no application server fleet for you to operate, but functions still need
resource budgets and deployment discipline.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What makes a streaming socket service a poor fit for a simple function model?
Answer: A continuously connected socket needs long-lived state, session routing, and
connections. Simple Lambda invocation is usually a poor match without an additional
managed connection service and state layer.
Common mistake: 'Serverless' does not mean unlimited duration or zero operations.
Source guide p. 27   ·   Further reading: A22-A24, A56
Persistent sockets Session ownership Suitable compute
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 47

pages.title: What is a cold start and how do you reduce its effect for Java?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 · Lambda and API Gateway INTERVIEW NOTE 037/100
Q037. What is a cold start and how do you reduce
its effect for Java?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A cold start is the extra startup work before Lambda handles a request.
Keep Java initialization lean and measure it.
Precise interview detail: A cold start includes creating and initializing an execution environment
before useful handling. Reduce avoidable initialization, use suitable packaging and evaluate
provisioned concurrency or supported SnapStart configurations. Measure end-to-end latency
under actual traffic and deployment patterns.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Initialization: load classes, construct clients
Invocation: validate input, perform business operation
Warm reuse: retain safe reusable clients
Restore-aware features: validate initialization state
WHAT HAPPENS · Sharing SDK clients across invocations can avoid repeated setup. SnapStart
needs special care with uniqueness, credentials and restore-safe connections.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you measure cold and warm p99 separately?
Answer: Tag invocation metrics by cold versus warm path using init indicators and
tracing, then compare separate p99 distributions under representative traffic. Do not
average different p99 values.
Common mistake: Cached mutable request data can leak between invocations in a reused
environment.
Source guide p. 28   ·   Further reading: A22-A24, A56
Cold or warm Timing samples Separate p99
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 48

pages.title: How does Lambda concurrency affect downstream services?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 · Lambda and API Gateway INTERVIEW NOTE 038/100
Q038. How does Lambda concurrency affect
downstream services?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Lambda can rapidly run many copies, but each copy may put pressure on a
limited database or API.
Precise interview detail: Concurrency is the number of simultaneous executions. Reserved
concurrency can bound a function's use and reserve part of account capacity; provisioned
concurrency prepares execution environments. Downstream connection and rate budgets must
fit the admitted concurrency.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Example: 100 executions x 1 DB connection = 100
Database safe application budget: 60 connections
Controls: cap concurrency, pool/proxy, queue work
Measure: throttles, duration, backlog and DB saturation
WHAT HAPPENS · A highly elastic function tier can overwhelm a comparatively fixed database.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you choose a safe concurrency limit during a traffic spike?
Answer: Measure maximum safe database connections and execution time; reserve
downstream capacity, set concurrency limits, use queues or RDS Proxy where suitable,
then load-test expected bursts.
Common mistake: Provisioned concurrency and reserved concurrency solve different
problems.
Source guide p. 28   ·   Further reading: A22-A24, A56
Lambda concurrency DB capacity Safe cap
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 49

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 · Lambda and API Gateway INTERVIEW NOTE 039/100
Q039. How are Lambda failures retried?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Lambda retry rules depend on whether calls are synchronous,
asynchronous, or read from an event source such as SQS.
Precise interview detail: Retry behavior depends on the invocation path. Synchronous callers
own their retry decisions. Asynchronous invocation has service-managed retry and failure-
handling settings. Event-source mappings such as SQS have their own processing and retry
contracts.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
HTTP caller timeout -> caller decides next action
Async event -> inspect retry and destination settings
SQS mapping -> message visibility and batch handling
Every path -> business operation must tolerate replay
WHAT HAPPENS · Configure retry duration and failure destinations for the selected path.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would partial batch failure reporting change SQS processing?
Answer: Report only failed item IDs in the batch response when supported, allowing
successful items to stay complete. Keep each item's effect idempotent because retries
still happen.
Common mistake: One universal 'Lambda retries twice' claim is incorrect across invocation
modes.

pages.title: What do RDS and Aurora manage?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 · RDS, Aurora and relational reliability INTERVIEW NOTE 041/100
Q041. What do RDS and Aurora manage?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
RDS manages supported relational database infrastructure; Aurora is a
managed relational family with its own storage architecture.
Precise interview detail: RDS provides managed relational database offerings with engine-
specific capabilities. Aurora is a compatible managed database family with its own distributed
storage and topology. AWS manages service infrastructure; you still own schema design, SQL
performance, access and application transaction behavior.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Java service -> JDBC -> relational endpoint
Customer: indexes, transactions, migrations, access
Service: managed infrastructure within its contract
Design: availability, backup, read/write requirements
WHAT HAPPENS · Choose from engine compatibility, operational requirements, topology and
measured workload rather than branding.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which parts of a PostgreSQL migration would you verify before choosing
Aurora?
Answer: Test PostgreSQL extensions, SQL behavior, version support, transaction
isolation, parameter settings, replication, networking, failover, and query plans with
production-like data.
Common mistake: Managed databases do not automatically fix inefficient queries or lock
contention.

pages.title: How do Multi-AZ and read replicas differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 · RDS, Aurora and relational reliability INTERVIEW NOTE 042/100
Q042. How do Multi-AZ and read replicas differ?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Multi-AZ is mainly for availability; read replicas primarily add read
capacity. Exact RDS topologies have different rules.
Precise interview detail: Multi-AZ deployment options support availability, while read replicas
support read scaling and other workflows. A traditional RDS Multi-AZ DB instance uses a
standby that does not serve reads. Multi-AZ DB clusters have readable instances; Aurora has its
own cluster architecture.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Traditional Multi-AZ instance -> primary + standby
Read replica -> async read copy, lag may exist
Multi-AZ DB cluster -> different readable topology
Application -> choose writer and reader endpoints
WHAT HAPPENS · Always identify the exact RDS deployment type before describing behavior.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Where should a read immediately after a critical write go?
Answer: Send a critical read-after-write to the writer or another path with a proven
fresh-read guarantee. An asynchronous read replica may still contain the old value.
Common mistake: 'Every Multi-AZ standby serves reads' and 'no Multi-AZ instance can ever
serve reads' both hide topology distinctions.
Source guide p. 31   ·   Further reading: A25-A27, A42
Critical write Writer read Current data
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 54

pages.title: What happens to a Java application during database failover?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 · RDS, Aurora and relational reliability INTERVIEW NOTE 043/100
Q043. What happens to a Java application during
database failover?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
During DB failover, old connections can break and an in-flight commit may
have an unknown outcome.
Precise interview detail: Connections may fail, transactions may abort or outcomes may become
uncertain. Clients must resolve the appropriate endpoint, refresh invalid connections and retry
only operations whose semantics permit it. Failover completion at the service level is not
identical to application recovery.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Connection lost before commit -> likely retryable path
Connection lost during commit -> outcome may be unknown
Client request key -> resolve previous outcome
Connection pool -> evict broken connections
WHAT HAPPENS · Use bounded reconnects and idempotency for operations that might have
committed.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you determine whether the first transaction committed?
Answer: Query a durable request ID or unique transaction record at the new writer to
see if the effect exists. Only retry with the same idempotency identity after checking
the outcome.
Common mistake: Retrying a payment after any connection exception can charge twice.
Source guide p. 31   ·   Further reading: A25-A27, A42
Connection failure Query request key Resume safely
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 55

have an unknown outcome.

pages.title: How do you size connection pools and use RDS Proxy?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 · RDS, Aurora and relational reliability INTERVIEW NOTE 044/100
Q044. How do you size connection pools and use
RDS Proxy?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
The total database connection demand is the sum across all tasks and jobs,
not just one HikariCP pool.
Precise interview detail: Budget connections across all replicas and jobs, leaving operational
headroom. RDS Proxy can pool and manage connections for supported engines, but session
state, pinning and transaction behavior affect benefits. Query optimization and concurrency
control remain necessary.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
20 tasks x pool max 15 = up to 300 connections
Database budget for app: 220
Adjust: task count, pool, proxy and query duration
Measure: wait time, active sessions, pinned sessions
WHAT HAPPENS · A local pool configuration multiplies across the deployment.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What happens when autoscaling doubles the number of Java tasks?
Answer: Doubling 20 tasks with pool 15 raises possible connections from 300 to 600.
Limit task scaling, reduce pool sizes, and reserve capacity for maintenance; RDS Proxy
is not infinite capacity.
Common mistake: A proxy does not increase the database's ability to execute unlimited
concurrent work.
Source guide p. 32   ·   Further reading: A25-A27, A42
Task count x pool max DB budget Admission
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 56

pages.title: How do you handle backups and schema migrations?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 09 · RDS, Aurora and relational reliability INTERVIEW NOTE 045/100
Q045. How do you handle backups and schema
migrations?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Backups protect recoverable data; expand-and-contract schema changes
let old and new app versions coexist during rollout.
Precise interview detail: Use recovery mechanisms appropriate to the database, retention and
independence requirements. Test restores into an isolated environment. Deploy backward-
compatible expand-and-contract migrations so old and new application versions can coexist
during rollout.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Expand: add nullable column and compatible readers
Migrate: backfill and verify
Switch: use new column after compatibility checks
Contract: remove old column in a later release
WHAT HAPPENS · Rollback must account for data changes, not just application images.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you roll back an application after a destructive migration?
Answer: A destructive migration may make code rollback unsafe. Restore a tested
snapshot or use a compatible forward correction and reconciled data plan; define the
rollback boundary before deploying.
Common mistake: A successful backup job without a restore test does not demonstrate a
usable recovery path.
Source guide p. 32   ·   Further reading: A25-A27, A42
Schema change Data compatibility Recovery path
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 57

pages.title: How does DynamoDB differ from a relational database?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 10 · DynamoDB data modeling INTERVIEW NOTE 046/100
Q046. How does DynamoDB differ from a relational
database?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
DynamoDB uses keys and access patterns for fast lookups; relational
databases are better for many joined queries and constraints.
Precise interview detail: DynamoDB is a managed key-value and document database built
around explicit keys and access patterns. Model efficient queries and distribution before writing
application code. It supports conditional operations and transactions, but general joins and
arbitrary relational querying are not its core model.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Access pattern: get one order by customer and ID
PK = CUSTOMER#42
SK = ORDER#2026-10-09#123
Query -> bounded key range, not whole-table scan
WHAT HAPPENS · Key design makes the requested operation predictable and bounded.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you list a customer's last 20 orders?
Answer: Partition by customer and sort by order time plus a unique tie-breaker; Query
the customer's key in descending order with Limit 20, avoiding a full table scan.
Common mistake: Translating every SQL table directly into a DynamoDB table can miss the
workload's actual query needs.
Source guide p. 33   ·   Further reading: A28-A30, A59, A67
Customer key Descending query 20 orders
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 59

pages.title: What causes a hot partition or hot key?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 10 · DynamoDB data modeling INTERVIEW NOTE 047/100
Q047. What causes a hot partition or hot key?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A hot DynamoDB key receives much more traffic than others, even if
overall capacity looks fine.
Precise interview detail: Skewed access concentrates work on a limited key space even when
aggregate capacity appears sufficient. Choose keys and access patterns that distribute demand.
Caching, sharding or write aggregation may help, but each changes application behavior.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Poor key: PK = STATUS#OPEN for every new order
Better starting point: tenant/customer-based keys
High-volume tenant: evaluate controlled sharding
Query fan-out: account for the new read cost
WHAT HAPPENS · Distribution must match real traffic, including a single unusually large
customer.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you detect and relieve a single celebrity-item hot key?
Answer: Use per-key metrics and throttling patterns, cache popular reads, and split
safe write counters or workloads when business semantics permit. Do not shard exact
stock decisions without coordination.
Common mistake: High cardinality alone does not guarantee evenly distributed requests.
Source guide p. 33   ·   Further reading: A28-A30, A59, A67
Hot key Observe skew Cache or split safely
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 60

pages.title: Which DynamoDB reads can be strongly consistent?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 10 · DynamoDB data modeling INTERVIEW NOTE 048/100
Q048. Which DynamoDB reads can be strongly
consistent?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Some DynamoDB table and LSI reads may be strongly consistent; GSI
reads are eventually consistent.
Precise interview detail: Tables and local secondary indexes support strongly consistent reads
where applicable. Global secondary indexes support eventually consistent reads. Global tables
have consistency modes and Region constraints that must be selected and verified; do not
assume all multi-Region configurations behave alike.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Table GetItem: request ConsistentRead where supported
GSI query: eventual consistency
Critical write result: return known committed data
Projection query: tolerate or detect freshness lag
WHAT HAPPENS · Select consistency per operation and index, and consider its capacity
consequences.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you prevent a stale projection from authorizing an action?
Answer: Do not authorize a sensitive action using a possibly stale GSI alone. Recheck
the item or permission against the authoritative table or dedicated trusted store at
decision time.
Common mistake: Reading a GSI immediately after writing the base table can return a stale
projection.
Source guide p. 34   ·   Further reading: A28-A30, A59, A67
Stale GSI Authoritative read Authorization
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 61

pages.title: How do conditional writes support idempotency?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 10 · DynamoDB data modeling INTERVIEW NOTE 049/100
Q049. How do conditional writes support
idempotency?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A conditional write accepts a change only if the stored condition is true;
this can guard a durable request key.
Precise interview detail: A conditional write applies only when its condition is satisfied. Use a
durable request key and a state model to distinguish a first attempt, an in-progress attempt and
a completed result. Keep related effects inside an appropriate transaction where supported.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Key: REQUEST#client-key
Condition: attribute_not_exists(PK)
State: IN_PROGRESS -> COMPLETED with result
Duplicate: read state and return resolved outcome
WHAT HAPPENS · The conditional claim must be combined with a recovery policy for
abandoned processing.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you recover after a crash between the charge and saving the result?
Answer: Treat charge outcome as unknown, then query the payment provider using
the same stable idempotency key or reconcile transaction ID. Store the result durably
before responding and never issue an unrelated second charge.
Common mistake: Claiming a key and then charging an external payment provider is not
one atomic transaction.
Source guide p. 34   ·   Further reading: A28-A30, A59, A67
Charge sent Unknown result Query provider key
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 62

pages.title: What do DynamoDB TTL and Streams provide?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 10 · DynamoDB data modeling INTERVIEW NOTE 050/100
Q050. What do DynamoDB TTL and Streams
provide?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
DynamoDB TTL expires eligible items asynchronously. Streams exposes
ordered item changes within defined scopes and retention limits.
Precise interview detail: TTL enables eventual removal of eligible expired items; it is not a
precise deletion timer. Streams capture item-change records for consumers, with defined
retention and processing behavior. Consumers need replay tolerance and monitoring for lag or
failures.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
expiresAt: epoch seconds in configured TTL attribute
Read path: exclude logically expired data immediately
Stream event: update projection or publish workflow
Consumer: deduplicate and handle failed batches
WHAT HAPPENS · Application validity checks can take effect before physical deletion.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What recovery plan do you need if a stream consumer falls behind retention?
Answer: Track checkpoint age and alarm before retention expiry. If events are lost,
rebuild state using source-of-truth records, exports/backups, or a re-scan and
reconcile before resuming.
Common mistake: TTL is unsuitable as an exact-time security revocation mechanism by
itself.
Source guide p. 35   ·   Further reading: A28-A30, A59, A67
Stream lag Retention limit Rebuild state
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 63

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 11 · Caching and ElastiCache INTERVIEW NOTE 051/100
Q051. When would you add ElastiCache to a Java
service?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
ElastiCache stores useful temporary data in memory to reduce latency or
database reads; the database usually remains the source of truth.
Precise interview detail: Add a compatible managed cache when repeated reads or expensive
calculations dominate latency or load and the application can define acceptable freshness.
ElastiCache offers engine and deployment choices; verify the selected engine's API, persistence
and availability features.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Request -> look up product key
Cache hit -> return permitted cached representation
Cache miss -> load durable source and populate
Source remains authority for product data
WHAT HAPPENS · A cache can reduce database work but introduces stale data and new failure
paths.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which data in a payment application should you avoid treating as cache-
authoritative?
Answer: Do not make cached balances, confirmed payment states, or scarce inventory
authoritative. Read and update those with a durable transactional owner; cache only
safe views.
Common mistake: Adding a cache before measuring query and index performance may
complicate a solvable database issue.
Source guide p. 36   ·   Further reading: A51, A41
API read Cache hit or miss Durable owner
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 65

pages.title: What is cache-aside and how do you invalidate entries?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 11 · Caching and ElastiCache INTERVIEW NOTE 052/100
Q052. What is cache-aside and how do you
invalidate entries?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Cache-aside first checks a cache and loads from the database on a miss;
writes need a safe invalidation plan.
Precise interview detail: In cache-aside, the application loads missing data from the source and
populates the cache. After updates, invalidate or refresh affected entries. Define a freshness
budget and handle races between readers and writers; TTL bounds some staleness but is not
instant coherence.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Read miss -> DB read -> cache value with TTL
Write -> DB commit -> invalidate affected key
Race -> old reader may repopulate an old value
Mitigation -> versioning or stronger coordination
WHAT HAPPENS · Invalidation must consider all derived keys, including lists and aggregates.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you cache customer-specific prices safely?
Answer: Key the cache by tenant and customer context, authorize before returning a
price, and include pricing rules or version in the key. Never reuse a shared key for
private quotes.
Common mistake: Deleting a key after a commit is not automatically a proof of zero stale
reads.
Source guide p. 37   ·   Further reading: A51, A41
Tenant + customer Cache key Authorized price
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 66

pages.title: What is a cache stampede?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 11 · Caching and ElastiCache INTERVIEW NOTE 053/100
Q053. What is a cache stampede?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A cache stampede happens when many users miss the same hot key
together and overload the source database.
Precise interview detail: A stampede occurs when many requests simultaneously rebuild a
missing or expired value and overwhelm the source. Use request coalescing, TTL jitter, controlled
refresh or bounded stale serving according to the business contract.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
1,000 callers -> same expired product key
Without coordination -> 1,000 DB loads
With coalescing -> one loader, bounded waiters
Add jitter -> spread unrelated expirations
WHAT HAPPENS · Protect both loader concurrency and waiting request resources.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When would stale-while-revalidate be unacceptable?
Answer: Do not serve stale values for a one-time password, permission revocation,
payment authorization, or final inventory decision. Those need current authoritative
checks.
Common mistake: A distributed lock without a timeout or correct ownership release can turn
a stampede into an outage.
Source guide p. 37   ·   Further reading: A51, A41
Hot key expires Many loaders Single flight
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 67

pages.title: What happens when the cache fails?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 11 · Caching and ElastiCache INTERVIEW NOTE 054/100
Q054. What happens when the cache fails?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A cache outage should not create unlimited new database requests; use
bounded fallback and protect essential operations.
Precise interview detail: Choose a deliberate degraded mode: fall back within a bounded
database budget, serve allowed stale data, shed load or fail selected operations. Circuit breakers
and timeouts prevent the cache failure from holding all application threads.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Cache timeout budget: small part of request deadline
Fallback: concurrency-limited DB query
Over budget: reject or degrade selected endpoints
Recovery: avoid synchronized cache refill
WHAT HAPPENS · A healthy cache can hide how little database capacity remains for an all-miss
event.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What failure test would verify your fallback budget?
Answer: Disable or simulate Redis failure under representative peak load. Verify
database CPU, connection pools, fallback rate limits, p99 latency and error behavior
stay within stated budgets.
Common mistake: Unlimited fallback can transform a cache outage into a database outage.
Source guide p. 38   ·   Further reading: A51, A41
Cache down Limited fallback DB survives
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 68

pages.title: Can Redis-based locks guarantee exactly- once work?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 11 · Caching and ElastiCache INTERVIEW NOTE 055/100
Q055. Can Redis-based locks guarantee exactly-
once work?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Redis locks coordinate work but do not alone prove an external effect
happens exactly once.
Precise interview detail: A lease-style lock can coordinate attempts under stated assumptions,
but expiration, pauses and network failures can allow an old holder to continue. Use durable
invariants, idempotency and fencing where necessary. The underlying resource must enforce the
correctness boundary.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Worker A holds lease, then pauses
Lease expires; worker B starts
Worker A resumes with stale authority
Fencing or durable invariant rejects stale effect
WHAT HAPPENS · Mutual exclusion during normal conditions is weaker than a durable business
guarantee.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Where would you validate a fencing token?
Answer: The protected database or resource must store the highest accepted fencing
token and reject stale tokens in the write path. An unchecked token offers no safety.
Common mistake: A lock is not a substitute for a database uniqueness constraint or
payment idempotency key.
Source guide p. 38   ·   Further reading: A51, A41
Lease owner Monotonic token Resource rejects stale
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 69

happens exactly once.

pages.title: How do SQS, SNS and EventBridge differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 · SQS, SNS and EventBridge INTERVIEW NOTE 056/100
Q056. How do SQS, SNS and EventBridge differ?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
SQS holds tasks for workers, SNS fans out published messages, and
EventBridge routes matching events by rules.
Precise interview detail: SQS buffers messages for consumers that poll and acknowledge them.
SNS publishes to subscribers for fan-out. EventBridge routes events using rules and supported
integrations. They can be combined; choose based on buffering, routing, subscriber ownership
and failure handling.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Order service -> event routing or notification
Subscriber A queue -> email worker
Subscriber B queue -> analytics worker
Independent queues -> independent retry and lag
WHAT HAPPENS · A queue decouples consumer availability from producer timing.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why might every subscriber need its own queue?
Answer: Give each independent subscriber its own queue so one slow consumer
cannot block another and each group gets independent retries, retention, dead-letter
handling, and scaling.
Common mistake: A topic by itself does not define the same consumer-controlled
acknowledgement workflow as an SQS queue.
Source guide p. 39   ·   Further reading: A31-A35, A52
Event Fan-out Separate queues
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 71

pages.title: What guarantees do SQS Standard and FIFO queues provide?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 · SQS, SNS and EventBridge INTERVIEW NOTE 057/100
Q057. What guarantees do SQS Standard and FIFO
queues provide?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
SQS Standard can deliver duplicates and has best-effort ordering. FIFO
offers scoped ordering and deduplication rules, not universally once-only
business effects.
Precise interview detail: Standard queues support at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering.
FIFO queues provide ordering within message groups and producer deduplication under the
documented rules. Neither makes an external business side effect exactly once without
application coordination.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Standard: tolerate duplicate and out-of-order events
FIFO group: order-42 -> sequence for that group
Deduplication ID: stable ID for a producer retry
Consumer: durable business-key deduplication
WHAT HAPPENS · A FIFO message can become visible again after an unacknowledged
processing attempt.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What grouping key gives useful parallelism without breaking required ordering?
Answer: Group by an entity requiring order, such as orderId, so independent orders
can run in parallel. A single global group would create a processing bottleneck.
Common mistake: Service-level deduplication does not atomically combine 'charge card' and
'delete message'.
Source guide p. 40   ·   Further reading: A31-A35, A52
Order ID FIFO group Ordered handling
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 72

pages.title: What is the SQS visibility timeout?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 · SQS, SNS and EventBridge INTERVIEW NOTE 058/100
Q058. What is the SQS visibility timeout?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Visibility timeout temporarily hides a received SQS message while a worker
processes it; failure to delete can lead to redelivery.
Precise interview detail: After receipt, visibility timeout temporarily hides a message from other
consumers. It does not delete the message. Successful processing must be followed by deletion
using the receipt handle. Extend visibility for longer work within service constraints and tolerate
redelivery.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Receive -> receipt handle H1 -> hidden interval
Process and commit durable effect
DeleteMessage(H1) after successful commit
Crash before delete -> message can return
WHAT HAPPENS · Size the timeout for realistic processing and retries rather than only average
duration.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What is a safe heartbeat strategy for variable-length jobs?
Answer: Extend visibility periodically only while the worker holds valid ownership, with
a maximum run time, progress checks, and a recovery policy. Set timeout above
normal work with margin.
Common mistake: A short visibility timeout can create concurrent processing; a very long
one can delay recovery after a crash.
Source guide p. 40   ·   Further reading: A31-A35, A52
Receive message Extend while working Delete on success
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 73

pages.title: What are DLQs and redrive policies?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 · SQS, SNS and EventBridge INTERVIEW NOTE 059/100
Q059. What are DLQs and redrive policies?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A dead-letter queue keeps messages that repeatedly fail, giving operators a
way to investigate and replay.
Precise interview detail: A dead-letter queue captures eligible messages that exceeded
configured processing attempts. It supports diagnosis and controlled recovery. Decide retention,
alerting and redrive procedures so failed work is neither silently lost nor endlessly replayed.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Main queue -> repeated processing failure
Redrive threshold -> dead-letter queue
Operator -> classify cause and repair
Controlled replay -> verify duplicate tolerance
WHAT HAPPENS · A DLQ is an operational backlog with ownership and an SLA. For FIFO
workflows, removing a failed message can affect the intended business sequence.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you distinguish transient failure from invalid business input?
Answer: Retry network timeouts with bounded backoff; reject schema-invalid or
impossible business messages without endless retries. Record event ID, reason,
attempts, and repair owner.
Common mistake: Automatically replaying every poison message can recreate the incident.
Source guide p. 41   ·   Further reading: A31-A35, A52
Message failure Classify cause Retry or DLQ
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 74

way to investigate and replay.

Redrive threshold -> dead-letter queue

pages.title: How do you publish an event reliably after a database commit?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 12 · SQS, SNS and EventBridge INTERVIEW NOTE 060/100
Q060. How do you publish an event reliably after a
database commit?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Write the business update and an outbox event in the same database
transaction, then publish events asynchronously.
Precise interview detail: Use a transactional outbox: write the business row and an outbox
record in one local transaction, then publish asynchronously. The publisher may repeat delivery,
so consumers use idempotent processing. Monitor outbox age and replay safely.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
BEGIN
  insert order row
  insert outbox(order_id, event_id, payload)
COMMIT
Publisher -> send -> mark published with recovery
WHAT HAPPENS · The outbox closes the gap between a committed business change and a
missing publish attempt.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What happens if sending succeeds but marking the outbox row fails?
Answer: The event may be sent again after restart because the row still looks pending.
Consumers must deduplicate the business effect using a durable event ID.
Common mistake: It does not create one distributed transaction spanning the database and
queue.
Source guide p. 41   ·   Further reading: A31-A35, A52
DB + outbox commit Publish Safe replay
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 75

Write the business update and an outbox event in the same database
transaction, then publish events asynchronously.

pages.title: When would you choose Kinesis or MSK instead of SQS?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 · Streaming and workflow orchestration INTERVIEW NOTE 061/100
Q061. When would you choose Kinesis or MSK
instead of SQS?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
SQS is great for task distribution; Kinesis or MSK fits streaming workloads
needing retained ordered records and independent readers.
Precise interview detail: Choose a stream or Kafka-based log when partitioned ordering, replay
and multiple independent readers are core needs. SQS fits work distribution with message
acknowledgements. Kinesis and MSK have different operational and capacity models; evaluate
ecosystem and access patterns.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Work item completed -> queue acknowledgement
Event history -> stream offsets/checkpoints
Kafka ecosystem requirement -> evaluate MSK
AWS-native stream pipeline -> evaluate Kinesis
WHAT HAPPENS · The unit of ordering and consumer progress differs between a queue and a
partitioned log.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you replay historical events without repeating external side effects?
Answer: Replay with an event ID and an idempotent consumer effect stored
transactionally. For external payments/emails use provider keys, result tracking, or
controlled replay filters.
Common mistake: Managed Kafka does not remove partition planning, client configuration
or data-retention decisions.
Source guide p. 42   ·   Further reading: A36, A57, A58
Retained event Consumer replay Dedup effect
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 77

pages.title: What is partition-key design in streaming?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 · Streaming and workflow orchestration INTERVIEW NOTE 062/100
Q062. What is partition-key design in streaming?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Partition keys decide both event ordering scope and how streaming load
spreads across partitions.
Precise interview detail: A partition key groups related events onto an ordering boundary and
distributes traffic. Balance required order against hot partitions and consumer parallelism.
Within-partition order does not establish a global order across all producers and partitions.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Key = orderId -> per-order ordering
Key = constant -> severe concentration risk
Key = random -> distributes but loses entity grouping
Consumers -> checkpoint after safe processing
WHAT HAPPENS · Choose the smallest business entity that needs sequential processing.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you preserve customer ordering while scaling a very large customer?
Answer: Keep per-customer sequence numbers at the owner, partition a large
customer's independent substreams, and coordinate or reorder when those streams
must later become one ordered view.
Common mistake: Increasing consumer count cannot always overcome a single hot
partition's serial workload.
Source guide p. 43   ·   Further reading: A36, A57, A58
Customer sequence Multiple partitions Merge safely
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 78

Key = constant -> severe concentration risk

pages.title: What does Step Functions add to a workflow?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 · Streaming and workflow orchestration INTERVIEW NOTE 063/100
Q063. What does Step Functions add to a
workflow?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Step Functions tracks workflow state and transitions across multiple service
calls and retries.
Precise interview detail: Step Functions models workflow state, branching, retries and service
integrations. Workflow types have different execution and delivery semantics. Keep activities
idempotent, use bounded retries and represent compensation explicitly for multi-service
business operations.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Reserve inventory -> authorize payment -> confirm order
On payment rejection -> release inventory
On timeout -> inspect outcome before compensation
Workflow state -> correlate business operation ID
WHAT HAPPENS · An explicit workflow improves visibility into progress and recovery.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
When would you choose a Standard workflow over an Express workflow?
Answer: Use Standard for durable long-running workflows with their required audit
and execution semantics; use Express for suitable high-volume shorter workflows after
checking limits and delivery behavior.
Common mistake: State-machine execution semantics do not make each external API effect
magically transactional.
Source guide p. 43   ·   Further reading: A36, A57, A58
Event Workflow state Task outcomes
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 79
pages.shortAnswer:
Step Functions tracks workflow state and transitions across multiple service
calls and retries.
pages.codeExample:
Reserve inventory -> authorize payment -> confirm order
On payment rejection -> release inventory
On timeout -> inspect outcome before compensation
Workflow state -> correlate business operation ID
pages.explanation:
Step Functions models workflow state, branching, retries and service
integrations. Workflow types have different execution and delivery semantics. Keep activities
idempotent, use bounded retries and represent compensation explicitly for multi-service
business operations.
pages.pitfall:
State-machine execution semantics do not make each external API effect
magically transactional.
pages.followup:
When would you choose a Standard workflow over an Express workflow?
Answer: Use Standard for durable long-running workflows with their required audit
and execution semantics; use Express for suitable high-volume shorter workflows after
checking limits and delivery behavior.

pages.title: What is a saga and how does it differ from a transaction?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 · Streaming and workflow orchestration INTERVIEW NOTE 064/100
Q064. What is a saga and how does it differ from a
transaction?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A saga coordinates several local transactions with recovery or
compensation. A single ACID transaction cannot cover arbitrary remote
services.
Precise interview detail: A saga coordinates local transactions and compensating actions across
services. It exposes intermediate states and compensation failures. A local ACID transaction
protects one database boundary; a saga handles a wider business process with weaker atomicity.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Inventory reservation -> local commit
Payment authorization -> local commit
Failure -> release or refund where appropriate
Customer view -> show pending, completed or failed
WHAT HAPPENS · Compensation is a business action, not always a perfect reversal.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you reconcile a payment that succeeded after the workflow timed
out?
Answer: Query the provider by stable payment key, match it to order/reservation state,
then settle, refund, or compensate according to a documented state machine. Never
assume timeout means failure.
Common mistake: Sending an email cannot generally be undone by rolling back another
database.
Source guide p. 44   ·   Further reading: A36, A57, A58
Order pending Payment unknown Reconcile
AWS / ZERO TO HERO

pages.title: How do you evolve event schemas safely?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 13 · Streaming and workflow orchestration INTERVIEW NOTE 065/100
Q065. How do you evolve event schemas safely?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Keep event changes backward-compatible during a rolling migration, and
test old consumers against new producers.
Precise interview detail: Use explicit versioning, compatible additions and consumer-tolerant
parsing. Validate contracts in tests and keep replay requirements in mind. Deprecate fields only
after proving that live and recovery consumers no longer depend on them.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Event: type=OrderCreated, schemaVersion=2
Add: optional deliveryPreference
Do not reuse: existing field with changed meaning
Replay: old events remain interpretable
WHAT HAPPENS · Event retention makes compatibility a historical concern, not just a rollout
concern.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you migrate an enum value that older consumers cannot parse?
Answer: Add a compatible fallback or new field/version, teach consumers to handle
the new value before producers emit it, and retire legacy behavior after measured
adoption.
Common mistake: Updating every live consumer does not guarantee an old event can still
be replayed correctly.
Source guide p. 44   ·   Further reading: A36, A57, A58
Old consumer Compatible schema New producer
AWS / ZERO TO HERO

pages.title: How do CloudWatch, CloudTrail and AWS Config differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 · Observability and incident diagnosis INTERVIEW NOTE 066/100
Q066. How do CloudWatch, CloudTrail and AWS
Config differ?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
CloudWatch tracks operations and metrics, CloudTrail records supported
AWS API activity, and AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes.
Precise interview detail: CloudWatch supports operational telemetry such as metrics, logs and
alarms. CloudTrail records supported account activity and API events. AWS Config records
supported resource configuration history and evaluates rules. These answer different questions
and require appropriate configuration.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
CloudWatch: did API latency increase?
CloudTrail: who changed the security group?
Config: how did the resource configuration evolve?
Trace: where did one request spend its time?
WHAT HAPPENS · Combine signals to connect a change with its operational consequences.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which signal would investigate unexpected S3 object reads?
Answer: Check CloudTrail S3 data events if enabled for object access, plus relevant
CloudWatch logs and access telemetry. Management events alone may not show every
GetObject.
Common mistake: CloudTrail data events and other detailed coverage are not all enabled
simply because a default event history exists.
Source guide p. 45   ·   Further reading: A39-A41
Unexpected read S3 data events Principal
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 83

pages.title: Which metrics matter for a Spring Boot API?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 · Observability and incident diagnosis INTERVIEW NOTE 067/100
Q067. Which metrics matter for a Spring Boot API?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Track real API success, p95/p99 latency, throughput, saturation, JVM
pressure, and downstream delays.
Precise interview detail: Measure customer-facing request rate, errors and latency along with
saturation and dependency signals. Track JVM, pool and queue behavior to explain symptoms.
Use percentiles and realistic traffic segmentation rather than averages alone.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
API: rate, p95/p99, error ratio
JVM: allocation, GC pause, threads, memory
DB: pool wait, query latency, active sessions
Queue: age, backlog, processing failures
WHAT HAPPENS · A rising p99 with normal average latency can indicate a subset of stalled
requests.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which metric separates database execution time from pool acquisition wait?
Answer: Measure HikariCP connection acquisition wait separately from query
execution timer or database traces. A long checkout wait with short SQL means the
pool may be exhausted.
Common mistake: A CPU alarm alone may miss thread starvation or a saturated connection
pool.
Source guide p. 45   ·   Further reading: A39-A41
Request time Pool wait SQL time
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 84

pages.title: How should you design alerts and SLOs?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 · Observability and incident diagnosis INTERVIEW NOTE 068/100
Q068. How should you design alerts and SLOs?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
An SLI measures user-visible service behavior; an SLO is its target. Alert on
rapid error-budget loss rather than arbitrary noise.
Precise interview detail: Define a service-level objective around customer outcomes and use
alerts that demand an actionable response. Monitor error-budget consumption and relevant
dependencies. Distinguish immediate paging from lower-urgency capacity or configuration
investigation.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
SLO example: 99.9% eligible requests succeed
Window: chosen business measurement period
Alert: excessive error-budget burn
Runbook: diagnosis, mitigation and escalation
WHAT HAPPENS · An SLO includes explicit eligibility and measurement definitions.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Would an expected validation error count against your availability objective?
Answer: An expected 400 validation response normally should not count as
unavailable when it is correct behavior. Define eligibility and failures clearly; 500s or
overload errors usually do count.
Common mistake: A high dashboard uptime can hide broken critical business operations.
Source guide p. 46   ·   Further reading: A39-A41
Eligible request Success rule Error budget
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 85

pages.title: How do correlation IDs and distributed tracing help?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 · Observability and incident diagnosis INTERVIEW NOTE 069/100
Q069. How do correlation IDs and distributed
tracing help?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Correlation IDs connect an API call with downstream logs and traces so
one user journey is easier to debug.
Precise interview detail: They connect work across service boundaries and asynchronous stages.
Propagate trace context through supported mechanisms and carry business operation
identifiers for durable diagnosis. Keep sensitive data out of logs and control metric label
cardinality.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
HTTP request -> trace context
Outbox event -> eventId and business operation ID
Worker -> linked trace or propagated context
Logs -> timestamp, service, operation, outcome
WHAT HAPPENS · A trace identifies timing relationships; a business ID connects retries and
delayed workflow work.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you correlate a queue retry with the original API request?
Answer: Include the original trace/correlation ID in event metadata, preserve message
ID and attempt count, and start a linked consumer span on each retry. Do not use the
trace ID as an idempotency key.
Common mistake: Customer IDs as unbounded metric labels can create high cardinality and
cost.
Source guide p. 46   ·   Further reading: A39-A41
API trace Event metadata Retry trace
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 86

pages.title: How would you investigate a sudden production latency increase?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 14 · Observability and incident diagnosis INTERVIEW NOTE 070/100
Q070. How would you investigate a sudden
production latency increase?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Diagnose latency by finding where time grew: network, load balancer, JVM,
database, or external APIs.
Precise interview detail: Establish the impact and time window, compare recent changes, then
localize delay using ingress, application and dependency evidence. Apply a bounded mitigation
and verify customer recovery before deeper optimization.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
1. Check error ratio and latency by endpoint
2. Compare deploy, config and traffic changes
3. Inspect traces, pools, GC and DB waits
4. Mitigate; validate; preserve evidence
WHAT HAPPENS · Evidence distinguishes a capacity issue from a regression or dependency
failure.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What would you do if rollback does not reduce the latency?
Answer: If rollback has no effect, look for shared dependency saturation, regional
incidents, queueing, a hot DB query, DNS issues, and network changes. Use traces and
time-series evidence before scaling.
Common mistake: Restarting every task before collecting diagnostics can erase the
information needed to prevent recurrence.
Source guide p. 47   ·   Further reading: A39-A41
Latency alert Stage breakdown Root cause
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 87

pages.title: What is KMS and what is envelope encryption?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 15 · KMS, secrets and application security INTERVIEW NOTE 071/100
Q071. What is KMS and what is envelope
encryption?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
KMS manages cryptographic keys. Envelope encryption encrypts data with
a data key and protects that key using a KMS key.
Precise interview detail: KMS manages keys and cryptographic operations under policy controls.
Envelope encryption encrypts data with a data key, then protects that key with a higher-level key.
Service integrations can manage this workflow, while authorization controls who can use the key.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Plain data -> encrypt with data key
Data key -> encrypt under KMS key
Store ciphertext + encrypted data key
Read -> authorized key access -> decrypt data
WHAT HAPPENS · Protecting encrypted data requires both secure key use and secure data
access.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What happens if an application's S3 access works but KMS decrypt is denied?
Answer: S3 permission may succeed but downloading a KMS-encrypted object can fail
because the caller lacks effective kms:Decrypt rights or the key policy/conditions
reject it.
Common mistake: Key rotation is not the same as rewriting every old object with a new data
key.
Source guide p. 48   ·   Further reading: A37, A38, A48, A60, A66
S3 GetObject KMS permission Plaintext
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 89

pages.title: How do Secrets Manager and Parameter Store differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 15 · KMS, secrets and application security INTERVIEW NOTE 072/100
Q072. How do Secrets Manager and Parameter
Store differ?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Secrets Manager specializes in managed secrets and rotation; Parameter
Store stores configuration and can hold protected values.
Precise interview detail: Secrets Manager provides secret management features including
supported rotation workflows. Systems Manager Parameter Store stores hierarchical
configuration with supported encrypted SecureString values. Compare rotation, integration,
throughput, size and cost requirements rather than treating them as identical products.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Nonsecret feature setting -> configuration parameter
Database password -> managed secret workflow
Application retrieval -> IAM + KMS where applicable
Cache -> controlled refresh and failure behavior
WHAT HAPPENS · Choose a lifecycle that matches how the value changes and how applications
consume it.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you keep a connection pool working during rotation?
Answer: Allow old and new credentials to overlap, update the secret, reconnect or
refresh existing pool connections, verify success, then revoke old credentials after all
replicas transition.
Common mistake: A stored encrypted password does not automatically rotate the database
credential.
Source guide p. 48   ·   Further reading: A37, A38, A48, A60, A66
New credential Pool refresh Revoke old
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 90

pages.title: Should secrets be injected at startup or retrieved at runtime?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 15 · KMS, secrets and application security INTERVIEW NOTE 073/100
Q073. Should secrets be injected at startup or
retrieved at runtime?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Startup secret injection is simple but needs restart for changes. Runtime
retrieval permits refresh but adds an API and caching contract.
Precise interview detail: Startup injection is simple but normally requires a new workload
deployment to consume a changed value. Runtime retrieval can support refresh but adds
dependency, cache and authorization behavior. Select the strategy from rotation timing and
failure requirements.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
ECS configured secret -> resolved for task startup
Java SDK retrieval -> application fetches and caches
Rotation -> update consumer at defined time
Fallback -> use only a still-valid allowed value
WHAT HAPPENS · The consumer must know when a retrieved secret stops being valid.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you prevent credentials from appearing in startup logs?
Answer: Never print environment dumps, command-line credentials, connection URLs
with passwords, or exception values containing secrets. Redact known keys and test
logs during startup failures.
Common mistake: Rotating the source does not automatically update an already injected
environment value.
Source guide p. 49   ·   Further reading: A37, A38, A48, A60, A66
Secret delivery Redaction Safe logs
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 91

pages.title: How do Cognito and IAM differ for a web application?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 15 · KMS, secrets and application security INTERVIEW NOTE 074/100
Q074. How do Cognito and IAM differ for a web
application?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Cognito can authenticate application users; IAM secures AWS API actions
by principals. Neither automatically applies your business ownership rules.
Precise interview detail: Cognito can provide application user authentication and token-related
capabilities. IAM governs access to AWS resources. For a Spring resource server, validate the
intended token type, issuer, signature, expiry and audience or client-related constraints
appropriate to the token contract.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
User login -> identity provider -> access token
Spring API -> validate token -> authorize resource
Java workload -> IAM role -> S3 or SQS
User identity != workload service credentials
WHAT HAPPENS · An authenticated user still needs ownership or role checks for each business
operation.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you ensure customer A cannot read customer B's invoice?
Answer: Validate the user token and then check invoice owner or tenant ID in your
database before issuing a scoped S3 download. A valid token alone does not authorize
another person's invoice.
Common mistake: Accepting an ID token as an API access token can confuse
authentication purpose and authorization.
Source guide p. 49   ·   Further reading: A37, A38, A48, A60, A66
JWT identity Invoice ownership Signed GET
AWS / ZERO TO HERO

pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 15 · KMS, secrets and application security INTERVIEW NOTE 075/100
Q075. How do you secure a multi-tenant AWS
application?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Secure tenants at the API, identity, data query, storage, and observability
layers.
Precise interview detail: Enforce tenant identity at trusted boundaries and in data access. Scope
object keys, queries and credentials appropriately, and verify negative tests. Choose shared or
isolated infrastructure based on compliance, noisy-neighbor, operational and cost requirements.
→ →

SQL -> predicate includes tenant_id
S3 -> bounded tenant prefix access design
Audit -> tenant, actor, operation, result
WHAT HAPPENS · Infrastructure boundaries complement application-level ownership checks.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What requirement would justify a separate account per tenant?
Answer: Use separate accounts when isolation, regulatory boundaries, independent
keys, audit ownership, quota separation, or customer contracts require stronger blast-
radius boundaries than pooled tenancy.
Common mistake: A tenant ID supplied only in a request body must not override the
authenticated authorization context.

pages.title: What is infrastructure as code?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 · Infrastructure as code and CI/CD INTERVIEW NOTE 076/100
Q076. What is infrastructure as code?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Infrastructure as code stores reviewed cloud configuration in versioned
files instead of unmanaged console clicks.
Precise interview detail: Infrastructure as code describes resources and changes in versioned
definitions. CloudFormation, CDK and other tools offer different authoring and state models.
Review generated plans, validate security and detect drift; declarative definitions do not remove
deployment risk.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Commit -> review -> validation -> change preview
Apply -> service deployment -> verification
Record -> resource identity and artifact digest
Drift -> compare actual state with intended state
WHAT HAPPENS · Repeatability depends on parameters, permissions, external dependencies and
tool behavior.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which changes would you prevent from being automatically applied?
Answer: Require manual approval for destructive data changes, broad IAM permission
increases, production network exposure, key deletion, and other high-impact changes.
Preview the proposed change set.
Common mistake: A template that parses is not proof that deployment will succeed or be
safe.

pages.title: How do CloudFormation and CDK differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 · Infrastructure as code and CI/CD INTERVIEW NOTE 077/100
Q077. How do CloudFormation and CDK differ?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
CloudFormation runs declarative resource templates; CDK generates those
templates from general-purpose code.
Precise interview detail: CloudFormation deploys AWS resource templates through stacks and
managed lifecycle operations. CDK lets you author infrastructure using programming languages
and synthesizes CloudFormation templates for its common deployment model. Both require
reviewing the actual resource changes.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
CDK source -> synthesize template
CloudFormation template -> change set -> stack update
Parameters and context -> deployment-specific inputs
Application image -> separate immutable artifact
WHAT HAPPENS · Higher-level constructs can accelerate authoring while producing resources
that still need inspection.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Why should a reviewer inspect synthesized IAM policies?
Answer: Synthesized templates show the actual IAM actions, resources, wildcards, and
trust conditions. Reviewers should not trust friendly source-code constructs without
inspecting the effective policy.
Common mistake: A short CDK construct can create many resources and permissions.
Source guide p. 52   ·   Further reading: A43, A47, A48
CDK code Synthesized template IAM review
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 96

pages.title: How should a Java container pipeline work?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 · Infrastructure as code and CI/CD INTERVIEW NOTE 078/100
Q078. How should a Java container pipeline work?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A delivery pipeline should test Java, build once, scan and sign the image as
needed, publish its digest, and deploy that exact artifact.
Precise interview detail: Build and test one immutable candidate, scan and verify it, publish its
digest, deploy that digest and run health and business smoke checks. Keep environment
configuration separate from the binary and capture the identity needed for rollback.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Source -> unit/integration tests -> image candidate
Candidate -> security and runtime checks -> registry
Digest -> stage -> approval policy -> production
Observe -> compare error, latency and business result
WHAT HAPPENS · Promoting the same digest reduces accidental differences between stages.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What should a production smoke test verify beyond HTTP 200?
Answer: Smoke-test representative authenticated business paths, database connectivity,
permission boundaries, real writes with safe fixtures, telemetry, and failure handling—
not just a health URL.
Common mistake: Rebuilding separately for production can change dependencies while
keeping the same source commit.
Source guide p. 52   ·   Further reading: A43, A47, A48
Commit Test + image digest Business smoke test
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 97

pages.title: How do rolling, blue-green and canary deployments differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 · Infrastructure as code and CI/CD INTERVIEW NOTE 079/100
Q079. How do rolling, blue-green and canary
deployments differ?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Rolling replaces instances gradually, blue-green swaps between separate
fleets, and canary exposes a small share to the new version.
Precise interview detail: Rolling replaces portions of existing capacity. Blue-green prepares a
separate environment or target set and switches traffic. Canary exposes a small share of traffic
to the new version before expansion. Each needs spare capacity, compatibility and a measurable
rollback decision.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Rolling -> mixed old/new versions
Blue-green -> switch target set
Canary -> limited traffic -> evaluate -> expand
Every approach -> compatible schema and events
WHAT HAPPENS · Traffic switching alone cannot reverse incompatible database writes.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which signals would stop an automated rollout?
Answer: Stop rollout if customer-visible error rate, p99, dependency pressure, or
critical business invariant alerts breach guardrails. Consider a minimum sample size
and observation period.
Common mistake: A canary without enough representative requests may miss a critical
regression.
Source guide p. 53   ·   Further reading: A43, A47, A48
New release Small exposure Stop or expand
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 98

fleets, and canary exposes a small share to the new version.

pages.title: How should CI authenticate to AWS?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 16 · Infrastructure as code and CI/CD INTERVIEW NOTE 080/100
Q080. How should CI authenticate to AWS?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
CI should obtain temporary workload credentials using an approved
federation or role assumption flow, not store permanent AWS keys.
Precise interview detail: Use a supported identity federation mechanism to obtain temporary
deployment-role credentials. Restrict role trust to the expected repository, workflow, environment
or equivalent claims, and bound deployment permissions. Keep build and production roles
separate where practical.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
CI identity token -> STS federation -> deploy role
Trust conditions -> intended workflow identity
Role policy -> required deployment operations
Session -> temporary credentials and audit trail
WHAT HAPPENS · Trust claims protect who can obtain the role, while permissions restrict what it
can do.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you separate pull-request builds from production deployment
authority?
Answer: Do not give untrusted pull requests production-role trust. Separate build
identity from release identity and require reviewed branch, protected environment and
tightly scoped deploy role.
Common mistake: A wildcard trust condition can let an unintended workflow deploy even
with no stored access key.
Source guide p. 53   ·   Further reading: A43, A47, A48
PR build role Reviewed release Deploy role
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 99

pages.title: How do timeouts, retries and circuit breakers work together?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Resilience, retries and disaster recovery INTERVIEW NOTE 081/100
Q081. How do timeouts, retries and circuit breakers
work together?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Timeouts bound waiting; retries address likely temporary failures; circuit
breakers reject calls when a dependency is unhealthy.
Precise interview detail: A timeout bounds waiting. A retry starts another attempt where
semantics allow it. A circuit breaker temporarily avoids a failing dependency based on a policy.
Combine an end-to-end deadline, limited attempts, jitter and concurrency bounds.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Total request deadline: 1,000 ms
Attempts: at most 2 with bounded backoff
Per-attempt timeout: fit remaining budget
Retry eligibility: transient + idempotent or resolvable
WHAT HAPPENS · Multiple layers of retry can multiply attempts and overload a recovering
service.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you prevent SDK retries and service retries from exceeding the
caller's deadline?
Answer: Set one end-to-end deadline and pass remaining time to each layer. Limit
total retries, use jitter, and align SDK settings with the caller's budget to avoid retry
storms.
Common mistake: A timeout does not prove that the downstream operation did not
complete.
Source guide p. 54   ·   Further reading: A35, A41, A42
Caller deadline Retry budget Fail fast
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 101

pages.title: What is idempotency in an AWS application?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Resilience, retries and disaster recovery INTERVIEW NOTE 082/100
Q082. What is idempotency in an AWS application?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Idempotency means repeating a request has one intended business effect
when the caller reuses the same durable key.
Precise interview detail: Idempotency means repeating a logical operation has the same
intended effect as one successful execution. Implement it with a stable operation key, durable
state and recovery for uncertain outcomes. Include result replay and key-retention policy.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Client key -> unique durable operation row
First request -> execute and record outcome
Repeat -> return outcome or in-progress status
Different payload with same key -> reject conflict
WHAT HAPPENS · The request key must cover the business operation rather than one network
attempt.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How long should payment idempotency records remain available?
Answer: Retain payment keys longer than your maximum realistic client and provider
retry/reconciliation window, considering delayed messages and business records.
Document scope and expiry explicitly.
Common mistake: A randomly generated key on every retry removes the deduplication
benefit.
Source guide p. 55   ·   Further reading: A35, A41, A42
Same request key Durable result Safe retry
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 102
