pages.title: What are common AWS disaster recovery strategies?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Resilience, retries and disaster recovery INTERVIEW NOTE 083/100
Q083. What are common AWS disaster recovery
strategies?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Disaster recovery choices range from backup-and-restore to warm standby
and active-active, with different RTO, RPO, and cost.
Precise interview detail: Common patterns include backup-and-restore, pilot light, warm standby
and multi-site designs. They trade operational cost and complexity against achievable recovery
objectives. Verify data replication, infrastructure readiness, dependencies and traffic cutover
through rehearsals.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Backup/restore -> rebuild and recover copies
Pilot light -> essential foundations retained
Warm standby -> reduced running environment
Multi-site -> coordinated serving and data design
WHAT HAPPENS · Architecture labels do not guarantee a recovery time; measured drills establish
evidence.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which dependencies belong in your DR checklist?
Answer: Include DNS, IAM/KMS keys, secrets, certificates, ECR images, app config,
VPC, database, S3 data, event queues, client integrations, and runbooks in the DR
inventory.
Common mistake: An active application in another Region is not useful if its critical secrets
or data cannot be recovered.
Source guide p. 55   ·   Further reading: A35, A41, A42
Primary outage Recover dependencies Test restore
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 103

pages.title: Why is multi-Region active-active difficult?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Resilience, retries and disaster recovery INTERVIEW NOTE 084/100
Q084. Why is multi-Region active-active difficult?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Active-active across Regions is hard because state, ordering, failover,
identity, and conflicts become distributed problems.
Precise interview detail: Serving from multiple Regions adds data-conflict handling, routing,
identity, capacity and operational coordination. Decide which operations can be independent
and which require a single authority or a suitable consistency mechanism. Higher availability
can come with harder correctness tradeoffs.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Catalog reads -> distributed copies may be sufficient
Inventory decrement -> bounded global invariant
Payment -> external authority and idempotent outcome
Failover -> prevent unintended competing writers
WHAT HAPPENS · Business invariants determine whether stale or conflicting writes are
acceptable.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you prevent overselling a scarce product across Regions?
Answer: Assign scarce stock to one authority or divide stock into region-specific
allocations whose sum never exceeds real stock. A stale global cache must not decide
the last item.
Common mistake: 'Use global tables' is not a complete answer to global stock correctness.
Source guide p. 56   ·   Further reading: A35, A41, A42
Global demand Stock authority No oversell
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 104

pages.title: What failure experiments would you run before production?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 17 · Resilience, retries and disaster recovery INTERVIEW NOTE 085/100
Q085. What failure experiments would you run
before production?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Failure tests prove whether timeouts, queues, recovery, and rate limits
behave as designed rather than only on paper.
Precise interview detail: Test the stated failure model with bounded experiments and recovery
assertions. Include task loss, dependency slowdown, cache loss, database failover, duplicate
events and restore. Measure customer impact, backlog recovery and operational response.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Kill one task -> target recovery without lost invariant
Duplicate message -> one business effect
DB failover -> bounded errors and eventual recovery
Restore -> validated data and working application
WHAT HAPPENS · A good experiment includes a stop condition, observations and cleanup of
only its own test resources.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which experiment would expose an unlimited fallback from cache to database?
Answer: Cut the cache during peak replay traffic and watch DB connections,
admission limits, rejection rate, pool wait and latency. The test fails if fallback traffic
overwhelms the database.
Common mistake: Testing only happy-path load provides no evidence of recovery behavior.
Source guide p. 56   ·   Further reading: A35, A41, A42
Cache failure Fallback surge Capacity test
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 105

pages.title: How should you estimate AWS cost?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Cost, quotas and performance INTERVIEW NOTE 086/100
Q086. How should you estimate AWS cost?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Estimate AWS cost from realistic usage, including data transfer, requests,
runtime, retention, and management overhead.
Precise interview detail: Model measured usage and architecture-specific cost components.
Include compute, storage, requests, data transfer, logs, backup, networking and managed-service
charges. Use current regional pricing and forecast ranges rather than memorized totals.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Monthly model = baseline + variable usage + resilience
Example drivers: task hours, DB hours, S3 bytes
Often missed: NAT processing, cross-AZ traffic, logs
Compare: cost per successful business operation
WHAT HAPPENS · A low compute bill can hide expensive transfer and telemetry paths.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which component could become the dominant cost for large uploads?
Answer: Large uploads can be dominated by data transfer, S3 storage and requests,
replication, image processing, or outbound CDN traffic depending on direction and
scale. Measure bytes by path.
Common mistake: Free-tier assumptions and old prices should not drive production budgets.
Source guide p. 57   ·   Further reading: A41, A51, A61
Upload bytes Storage + processing Egress
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 107

pages.title: What is the difference between vertical and horizontal scaling?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Cost, quotas and performance INTERVIEW NOTE 087/100
Q087. What is the difference between vertical and
horizontal scaling?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Vertical scaling makes one machine bigger. Horizontal scaling runs more
machines while shared resources may remain fixed.
Precise interview detail: Vertical scaling increases resources of a unit; horizontal scaling adds
units. Horizontal compute scaling needs shared or externalized state and bounded downstream
capacity. Neither strategy fixes an invariant that serializes every request.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Vertical: larger database or task
Horizontal: more API tasks behind load balancer
Constraint: DB connections and write contention
Measure: throughput gain versus extra cost
WHAT HAPPENS · Stateless application replicas are easier to add and replace than stateful
singleton workloads.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you recognize that the database is now the limiting tier?
Answer: Watch database CPU, active sessions, connection waits, lock time, query
latency, and flat throughput as API replicas grow. More servers may amplify a
database bottleneck.
Common mistake: Doubling replicas does not guarantee doubled end-to-end capacity.
Source guide p. 57   ·   Further reading: A41, A51, A61
More API tasks Same DB Saturation
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 108

pages.title: What are service quotas and why do they matter?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Cost, quotas and performance INTERVIEW NOTE 088/100
Q088. What are service quotas and why do they
matter?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
AWS services have regional and account quotas that can block a scale-out
or recovery plan.
Precise interview detail: Quotas limit supported resources or request rates and vary by service,
account and Region. Some can be adjusted, others are fixed. Include quota review and capacity
validation in planning, especially for traffic spikes and recovery into another Region.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Review: compute, IP addresses, concurrency and APIs
Request increases early where supported
Load test: throttling and backpressure behavior
DR: target Region needs sufficient headroom too
WHAT HAPPENS · Operational capacity includes the ability to create replacement resources
under stress.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which quota could prevent a failover from launching enough tasks?

pages.title: How do you reduce observability and storage cost safely?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Cost, quotas and performance INTERVIEW NOTE 089/100
Q089. How do you reduce observability and storage
cost safely?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Keep enough logs and metrics to investigate incidents without paying to
retain everything forever.
Precise interview detail: Control log volume and retention, sample traces appropriately, avoid
high-cardinality metrics and apply storage lifecycle policies consistent with recovery
requirements. Keep the audit and diagnostic evidence that the business actually needs.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Keep: security and critical business audit evidence
Reduce: noisy debug logs and repeated payload dumps
Retain: defined time windows by data purpose
Verify: incident diagnosis and restore still work
WHAT HAPPENS · Cost reduction should preserve required visibility and recoverability.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you choose a log-retention period for incident investigation?
Answer: Start from incident detection lag, regulatory needs and forensic lookback. Use
different retention for hot logs, archives, traces and sensitive audit events; test that
evidence remains searchable.
Common mistake: Deleting all old backups to save money can destroy a recovery objective.
Source guide p. 58   ·   Further reading: A41, A51, A61
Incident window Retention tier Cost control
AWS / ZERO TO HERO

pages.title: When is serverless more expensive or less suitable?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 18 · Cost, quotas and performance INTERVIEW NOTE 090/100
Q090. When is serverless more expensive or less
suitable?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Serverless can cost more for high steady traffic, high concurrency, long
runtimes, or unsuitable runtime behavior.
Precise interview detail: Serverless value depends on workload shape, latency, duration,
concurrency and integrations. Bursty or intermittent workloads can benefit from reduced idle
capacity. Sustained compute, expensive invocation patterns or special runtime needs may favor
another model.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Low idle usage + bursts -> evaluate functions
Steady CPU-heavy processing -> compare containers
Heavy DB access -> include connection and proxy cost
Decision -> measured workload and full cost model
WHAT HAPPENS · Compare the whole system, including queue, gateway, networking and
monitoring.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What measurements would you gather before migrating a busy Java API to
Lambda?
Answer: Measure real request rate, duration, cold/warm latency, memory,
concurrency, existing container utilization, API Gateway fees, network costs, and
required operations.
Common mistake: Invocation price alone is not the total architecture cost.
Source guide p. 59   ·   Further reading: A41, A51, A61
Current API metrics Lambda cost test Decide
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 111

pages.title: Design a resilient Spring Boot order API on AWS.
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 · Senior architecture scenarios INTERVIEW NOTE 091/100
Q091. Design a resilient Spring Boot order API on
AWS.
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
For an order system, route requests through managed ingress to multi-AZ
Java tasks; save orders and outbox events in one transaction; process side
effects asynchronously.
Precise interview detail: Use managed ingress, multi-AZ stateless compute, a durable relational
store for transactional invariants, and an outbox-driven asynchronous path. Add least-privilege
identities, controlled secrets, telemetry and tested recovery. Choose service variants based on
explicit traffic and recovery targets.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Route 53 -> ALB -> ECS Fargate tasks in two AZs
Tasks -> RDS writer -> order + outbox transaction
Publisher -> SQS -> idempotent fulfilment workers
S3 -> private invoices, authorized downloads
WHAT HAPPENS · The synchronous response acknowledges the database outcome;
asynchronous fulfilment has separate state and latency.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What do you return if the client times out after the order committed?
Answer: Use a client-supplied request key: when the retry arrives, find the already-
committed order and return its stored status or resource. A timeout does not prove
rollback.
Common mistake: Do not claim that this topology alone guarantees zero downtime or zero
lost orders.
Source guide p. 60   ·   Further reading: A19, A25, A33, A35, A42
Client request key Order commit Same result
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 113

pages.title: Design a secure file-upload and processing workflow.
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 · Senior architecture scenarios INTERVIEW NOTE 092/100
Q092. Design a secure file-upload and processing
workflow.
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Issue a narrow S3 upload URL, store upload intent, validate the object, then
process it asynchronously and publish a safe result.
Precise interview detail: Authorize the uploader, allocate a scoped object key, issue a suitable
presigned upload capability and validate the resulting object before use. Trigger bounded
processing through a replay-tolerant event path and publish a result only after validation
succeeds.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
API -> upload intent and scoped key
Client -> S3 upload
Event -> queue -> scan and transform worker
Status -> pending, accepted, rejected or failed
WHAT HAPPENS · The object should remain untrusted until validation, size/type checks and
business ownership are confirmed.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you avoid reprocessing the same uploaded object version twice?
Answer: Deduplicate on bucket, object key, and immutable version ID or verified
content identity, committing that marker with the processing result. Redeliveries then
return the stored outcome.
Common mistake: Treating Content-Type from a client as proof of file content is unsafe.
Source guide p. 60   ·   Further reading: A19, A25, A33, A35, A42
S3 object version Dedup record Processing
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 114

process it asynchronously and publish a safe result.

pages.title: Design a flash-sale inventory system.
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 · Senior architecture scenarios INTERVIEW NOTE 093/100
Q093. Design a flash-sale inventory system.
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Reserve scarce stock with an atomic database update, put payment in a
recoverable state, and use durable request IDs.
Precise interview detail: Make inventory reservation a durable conditional operation or
transaction at the chosen authority. Queue bounded downstream work, use stable request IDs
and release expired reservations safely. Cache product views while keeping scarce-stock
invariants out of ordinary stale caches.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Attempt reserve -> atomic invariant check
Reservation -> pending with expiry and ownership
Payment outcome -> confirm or release
Duplicate request -> resolve stored outcome
WHAT HAPPENS · Admission control keeps backend work within tested capacity even when
public demand is much larger.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you reconcile a late successful payment after a reservation expired?
Answer: Check provider outcome and reservation history. If stock was released and
cannot safely be reallocated, refund or fulfill through a documented exception
workflow; never quietly oversell.
Common mistake: A cache count followed by a database decrement can oversell under
concurrent requests.
Source guide p. 61   ·   Further reading: A19, A25, A33, A35, A42
Reservation expiry Late payment Refund or resolve
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 115

recoverable state, and use durable request IDs.

pages.title: Design a multi-tenant reporting service.
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 · Senior architecture scenarios INTERVIEW NOTE 094/100
Q094. Design a multi-tenant reporting service.
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Queue authorized report jobs, isolate tenant data, and cap workers so a
large tenant cannot starve others.
Precise interview detail: Separate authorization from execution scheduling, store input/output
under tenant-scoped identities or enforced paths, queue jobs and isolate noisy workloads.
Decide fairness, retention, audit and cancellation behavior. Use durable job state so retries do
not publish conflicting reports.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
API -> tenant-authorized job record
Queue -> bounded worker concurrency
Worker -> scoped data read -> S3 report object
Download -> verify job ownership -> presigned GET
WHAT HAPPENS · Job identity and tenant identity must travel through the asynchronous
boundary.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you enforce per-tenant fairness without a queue for every customer?
Answer: Use tenant-aware scheduling with per-tenant active-job limits or weighted fair
queues over a shared worker pool. Persist tenant identity with each job and apply
global safety limits.
Common mistake: One giant tenant should not consume all workers and starve every other
tenant.
Source guide p. 61   ·   Further reading: A19, A25, A33, A35, A42
Tenant jobs Fair scheduler Shared workers
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 116

large tenant cannot starve others.

pages.title: How would you lead an AWS migration from an on-premises Java monolith?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 19 · Senior architecture scenarios INTERVIEW NOTE 095/100
Q095. How would you lead an AWS migration from
an on-premises Java monolith?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Migrate a monolith in measured steps: inventory dependencies, establish
networking and identity, pilot a small workload, rehearse data cutover, then
stabilize.
Precise interview detail: Inventory dependencies, data and operational requirements, establish a
secure network and identity foundation, then migrate a bounded workload with measurable
parity. Choose rehosting, replatforming or redesign per component. Plan data cutover, rollback
and operational ownership before execution.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Assess -> baseline performance and dependency map
Pilot -> bounded environment and rehearsed data move
Cutover -> controlled writes, verification, rollback rule
Optimize -> measured improvements after stabilization
WHAT HAPPENS · A migration is complete only when the team can operate, recover and control
cost in the new environment.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What evidence would allow the business to approve the data cutover?
Answer: Require tested reconciliation totals, business transaction parity, performance
metrics, cutover rehearsal, rollback checkpoints, security sign-off, and a clear owner
for go/no-go.
Common mistake: Rewriting every component during the migration can combine too many
unproven changes.
Source guide p. 62   ·   Further reading: A19, A25, A33, A35, A42
Old system Parallel validation Approved cutover
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 117

networking and identity, pilot a small workload, rehearse data cutover, then
stabilize.

pages.title: An ECS task cannot pull its image. What do you check?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 · Troubleshooting and interview traps INTERVIEW NOTE 096/100
Q096. An ECS task cannot pull its image. What do
you check?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
For failed ECS image pulls, check task stop reasons, execution role, image
digest, registry path, CPU architecture, and network route.
Precise interview detail: Inspect the task stopped reason, image reference, execution-role
permissions, registry availability and network paths to required endpoints. Check platform
architecture and credentials where applicable. Application task-role permissions are a different
path.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Evidence: stopped reason and container reason
Identity: execution role for supported ECR pull
Network: routes, DNS, security and endpoints/NAT
Artifact: repository, digest, architecture
WHAT HAPPENS · The failure occurs before your application starts, so application logs may be
absent.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Which endpoints might a private-subnet ECR pull depend on?
Answer: A private-subnet pull from ECR commonly needs connectivity to ECR API and
Docker registry endpoints and the S3 layer-storage path, through endpoints or NAT as
designed. Verify DNS and security groups.
Common mistake: Debugging JDBC settings will not repair a missing image-pull route.
Source guide p. 63   ·   Further reading: A03, A17, A20, A33, A43

pages.title: SQS queue age rises while CPU stays low. What might be wrong?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 · Troubleshooting and interview traps INTERVIEW NOTE 097/100
Q097. SQS queue age rises while CPU stays low.
What might be wrong?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Growing SQS message age with low CPU often means workers are waiting
on downstream resources, not doing useful work.
Precise interview detail: Inspect consumer concurrency, blocked dependency calls, visibility
churn, poison messages and polling configuration. Low CPU can indicate waiting rather than
spare useful capacity. Compare processing rate with incoming rate and examine downstream
saturation.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Incoming: 200 messages/s
Processed: 100 messages/s
CPU: 20%, DB pool wait: high
Action: fix waiting bottleneck before more workers
WHAT HAPPENS · Scaling consumers can worsen the database queue if every consumer waits
on the same constrained resource.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you detect repeated processing of the same message?
Answer: Track message ID, receive count, processing attempts, idempotency-store hits
and DLQ events. Compare these with age and throughput to spot visibility churn or
repeats.
Common mistake: Backlog size alone cannot explain processing progress without message
age and throughput.
Source guide p. 63   ·   Further reading: A03, A17, A20, A33, A43
SQS receive Same message ID Repeat counter
AWS / ZERO TO HERO

pages.title: An S3 request returns AccessDenied. What is your diagnosis?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 · Troubleshooting and interview traps INTERVIEW NOTE 098/100
Q098. An S3 request returns AccessDenied. What is
your diagnosis?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
For S3 AccessDenied, check exactly which caller, operation, key, bucket,
endpoint policy, SCP and KMS key are involved.
Precise interview detail: Capture the actual caller, operation, bucket/key and encryption context
without exposing credentials. Check applicable IAM, bucket, endpoint and organization policies,
relevant ownership settings and KMS permissions. Verify the ARN type and request conditions.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Who: workload role session
What: GetObject, not ListBucket
Where: object ARN and intended prefix
Extra: KMS decrypt and endpoint policy if applicable
WHAT HAPPENS · An error can come from several authorization layers; repair the specific
missing or denied permission.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
How would you prove the repair still denies another tenant's prefix?
Answer: Test the intended prefix with a least-privileged role and a neighboring
tenant's prefix using the same operation. The first should work; the cross-tenant test
must remain denied.
Common mistake: Replacing policies with Action:* and Resource:* masks the cause and
grants unnecessary authority.
Source guide p. 64   ·   Further reading: A03, A17, A20, A33, A43
Authorized prefix Allow Other tenant denied
AWS / ZERO TO HERO

pages.title: A deployment is healthy but customers get errors. Why?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 · Troubleshooting and interview traps INTERVIEW NOTE 099/100
Q099. A deployment is healthy but customers get
errors. Why?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
A healthy load balancer target may still fail real orders due to auth,
database, routing, or schema problems.
Precise interview detail: Health probes may cover only a narrow endpoint or traffic path. Check
real business requests, authentication, schema compatibility, dependency access and routing.
Compare new and old versions using customer-facing metrics and representative smoke tests.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND

Business request: order insert fails schema check
Routing: only one path points to the wrong target
Evidence: per-route errors and deployed revision
WHAT HAPPENS · Infrastructure health and application correctness are separate observations.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
What should trigger rollback versus a forward fix?
Answer: Rollback when a new version causes widespread user-visible failures and old
code remains data-compatible. Forward-fix a small isolated defect only if risk and
time are lower and rollback cannot solve it.
Common mistake: A green deployment dashboard is not sufficient release evidence.

pages.title: Which AWS interview claims should you avoid?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 20 · Troubleshooting and interview traps INTERVIEW NOTE 100/100
Q100. Which AWS interview claims should you
avoid?
SAY THIS FIRST · SIMPLE ENGLISH
Avoid oversimplified statements such as 'managed means secure' or 'FIFO
means exactly once.' Always state the actual scope and failure case.
Precise interview detail: Avoid guarantees broader than the service contract or your validation.
State scope, topology and failure assumptions. Distinguish deployment configuration from
observed production behavior and measured recovery.
→ →
ORIGINAL AWS SCENARIO / COMMAND
Avoid: 'FIFO makes payment exactly once'
Avoid: 'all Multi-AZ standbys are identical'
Avoid: 'a private subnet has no outbound access'
Avoid: 'managed means no customer responsibility'
WHAT HAPPENS · Replace slogans with one precise statement and a failure example.
ORIGINAL INTERVIEWER FOLLOW-UP
Pick one claim and defend a correct replacement in 60 seconds.
Answer: For example: SQS FIFO can constrain message order and deduplication
within its contract, but a payment consumer still needs an idempotency key because a
message or external effect may be retried.
Common mistake: Memorizing service names without explaining their limits weakens senior-
level answers.
Source guide p. 65   ·   Further reading: A03, A17, A20, A33, A43
Claim Contract boundary Failure example

pages.shortAnswer:
Avoid oversimplified statements such as 'managed means secure' or 'FIFO
means exactly once.' Always state the actual scope and failure case.
pages.codeExample:
Avoid: 'FIFO makes payment exactly once'
Avoid: 'all Multi-AZ standbys are identical'
Avoid: 'a private subnet has no outbound access'
Avoid: 'managed means no customer responsibility'
pages.explanation:
Avoid guarantees broader than the service contract or your validation.
State scope, topology and failure assumptions. Distinguish deployment configuration from
observed production behavior and measured recovery.

Memorizing service names without explaining their limits weakens senior-
level answers.

Answer: For example: SQS FIFO can constrain message order and deduplication
within its contract, but a payment consumer still needs an idempotency key because a
message or external effect may be retried.

pages.title: Spring Boot Orders
pages.fullText:
Spring Boot Orders
on AWS
A durable order, a recoverable event, and an
idempotent worker.
→ →
Normal path: A client submits a stable request ID. The Java service checks stock
and writes the order plus outbox event in one database transaction. A publisher
sends the event to SQS. A worker applies an idempotent fulfilment effect.
Failure path: If the client loses a successful response, the retry returns the
stored order instead of creating another. If the publisher resends, the consumer
detects the duplicate.
Example only. Replace accounts, Regions, IAM roles, image digests, secrets, networks and
database settings. The example has not been deployed to AWS here.
WORKED ARCHITECTURE
Client / Route53 /
ALB ECS Fargate API RDS order + outbox
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 124

pages.title: ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS
pages.fullText:
ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS
Separate the boundaries
Ingress: ALB terminates HTTPS and forwards to healthy targets; WAF only where
needed.
Network: ALB uses intended public placement; API tasks and DB use approved
private placements and scoped security groups.
Identity: Execution role handles image pull/logs/injected secrets; task role handles
app SDK calls; worker has separate rights.
Durable order: One RDS transaction commits order and outbox so event intent
cannot disappear after an acknowledged order.
Messages: SQS can redeliver. Worker saves a durable event key before committing
local effect.
Observability: Monitor p99, target health, pool waits, outbox age, queue age, rejected
operations and restore tests.

pages.title: HANDS-ON EXERCISE 01 / 08
pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON EXERCISE 01 / 08
L01. Confirm the identity and Region before
diagnosis
This identifies a caller; it does not prove the caller may read S3 or deploy ECS. No
resources are created or deleted.
BASH SCRIPT FROM THE ATTACHED GUIDE
set -euo pipefail
export AWS_PAGER=""
PROFILE=YOUR_PROFILE
REGION=YOUR_REGION
aws --profile "$PROFILE" --region "$REGION" \
  sts get-caller-identity --output json
aws --profile "$PROFILE" configure get region
Expected: The identity response contains Account, Arn and UserId. Confirm they match
the intended environment. The configured Region can be empty or differ from the
explicit REGION, which overrides it for the first command.
Verification: Syntax verified; requires AWS account. AWS account permissions, API behavior and
production readiness were not checked.

pages.title: HANDS-ON EXERCISE 02 / 08
pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON EXERCISE 02 / 08
L02. Inspect an existing S3 bucket without reading
object contents
ETag is not a universal object-content MD5. Account-level public-access controls and
bucket policies also matter. The script stops on the first API failure so inspect that failure
before continuing.
BASH SCRIPT FROM THE ATTACHED GUIDE
set -euo pipefail
export AWS_PAGER=""
PROFILE=YOUR_PROFILE
REGION=YOUR_REGION
BUCKET=YOUR_BUCKET
KEY=YOUR_EXISTING_OBJECT_KEY
aws --profile "$PROFILE" --region "$REGION" \
  s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket "$BUCKET"
aws --profile "$PROFILE" --region "$REGION" \
  s3api get-public-access-block --bucket "$BUCKET"
aws --profile "$PROFILE" --region "$REGION" \
  s3api head-object --bucket "$BUCKET" --key "$KEY" \
  --query '{Size:ContentLength,ETag:ETag,Version:VersionId}'
Expected: Record the versioning state, public-access settings and object metadata. An
absent versioning Status differs from Enabled or Suspended. A missing public-access-
block configuration can produce an API error; do not infer public exposure from that
error alone.
Verification: Syntax verified; requires AWS account. AWS account permissions, API behavior and
production readiness were not checked.

pages.title: HANDS-ON EXERCISE 06 / 08
pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON EXERCISE 06 / 08
L06. Calculate a deployment-wide JDBC
connection budget
A connection budget is not a throughput estimate. Query time, locks, proxy pinning and
other sessions can reduce safe concurrency.
BASH SCRIPT FROM THE ATTACHED GUIDE
python3 - <<'PY'
db_limit = 300
reserved_for_ops = 30
other_apps = 50
max_tasks = 20
pool_per_task = 15
budget = db_limit - reserved_for_ops - other_apps
worst_case = max_tasks * pool_per_task
safe_pool = budget // max_tasks
assert budget == 220
assert worst_case == 300
assert safe_pool == 11
print("Application budget:", budget)
print("Requested worst case:", worst_case)
print("Upper bound per task:", safe_pool)
assert worst_case > budget
print("PASS: proposed pool exceeds budget")
PY
Expected: The application budget is 220, requested worst-case connections are 300 and
the arithmetic upper bound is 11 per task. This bound still requires workload and failover
headroom validation.
Verification: Syntax verified; offline executed. AWS account permissions, API behavior and
production readiness were not checked.
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 138

pages.title: HANDS-ON EXERCISE 07 / 08
pages.fullText:
HANDS-ON EXERCISE 07 / 08
L07. Simulate duplicate delivery with a durable
invariant
This models a local database effect only. It does not prove exactly-once payment, queue
delivery or cross-service atomicity. An external effect needs its own idempotency/
reconciliation contract.
BASH SCRIPT FROM THE ATTACHED GUIDE
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
c = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
c.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE orders(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY);
CREATE TABLE outbox(event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    order_id TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE effects(event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                     order_id TEXT NOT NULL);
""")
with c:
 c.execute("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?)", ("O42",))
 c.execute("INSERT INTO outbox VALUES (?, ?)",
           ("E42", "O42"))
event = c.execute("SELECT * FROM outbox").fetchone()
for delivery in range(2):
 with c:
  c.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO effects VALUES (?, ?)",
            event)
count = c.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM effects").fetchone()[0]
assert count == 1
assert c.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM orders").fetchone()[0] == 1
print("PASS: two deliveries, one durable local effect")
PY
Expected: Two deliveries yield one effects row because event_id is unique. The initial
order and outbox records are committed together. Explain how a real publisher can
resend after a send-success/mark-failure window.
Verification: Syntax verified; offline executed. AWS account permissions, API behavior and
production readiness were not checked.
AWS / ZERO TO HERO
EXPLAIN · SKETCH · TEST · DEFEND 139

pages.title: INVESTIGATE SYMPTOMS
pages.fullText:
INVESTIGATE SYMPTOMS
Signal → first evidence
ECS image cannot pull
Stopped reason, execution role, ECR/S3 endpoint path, image platform.
ECS task starts but API fails
Task logs, ALB target health, Spring listener, secrets and JDBC.
SQS backlog age grows
Arrival/processing rate, DB pool waits, redeliveries and oldest age.
Sudden p99 latency
Distributed trace, pool wait, query duration, throttling and deploy history.
S3 AccessDenied
Actual caller, GetObject versus ListBucket, bucket and KMS policy.
RDS writer fails over
Connection refresh, commit uncertainty, request idempotency.
Cache outage causes DB spike
Cache miss rate, fallback concurrency caps and DB load.
Rollout healthy but orders fail
Smoke tests, schema compatibility, business outcome metrics.
High AWS bill
Cost Explorer dimensions, transfer, NAT, logs, storage and usage spikes.

pages.title: How to use these notes
pages.fullText:
How to use these notes
Every original interview question is reproduced in the same order and wording as the
source PDF. The answer is kept short and precise; the practical command example,
real behavior and danger signs help you understand why it works.
① Say the answer in your own words (30 seconds).
② Read the command and predict whether it changes HEAD, index, files or a
remote reference.
③ Answer the follow-up before reading its purple answer box.
④ Sketch the concept on paper and explain one failure.
⑤ Run the labs only in separate empty practice folders.
The mini concept maps are learning aids, not exhaustive Git object graphs. Sample
commands may use placeholders such as BAD_COMMIT; replace them with the
correct IDs, and do not run alternatives in sequence unless the exercise explicitly says
to do so.
Safety: Hard reset, clean, force-push and history rewrite can permanently affect
work or collaborators. Always inspect status, create backups where appropriate,
and follow your team's branch protections.

pages.title: What is Git and why is it called distributed?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Git fundamentals and the right mental model Q 001 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q001
What is Git and why is it called distributed?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Git is a version-control system. Each normal full clone has local history and can
create commits without contacting a central server; sharing happens through
explicit network operations.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git log --oneline
   git add src/OrderService.java
   git commit -m "Validate positive order quantity"
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✎
Most Git work is offline; sharing uses push.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The commit is local. A later push publishes reachable objects and updates a remote reference
if permitted. Shallow and partial clones intentionally omit some history or objects, so do not
assume every clone contains everything.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which Git operations can you perform without internet access?
You can edit files, stage, commit, branch, switch, inspect history, diff, merge and rebase
using objects already available locally. Fetch and push normally need a reachable remote.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Committing does not automatically publish your work to teammates.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 5. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: What is the difference between Git and GitHub?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Git fundamentals and the right mental model Q 002 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q002
What is the difference between Git and GitHub?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Git is the version-control tool and data model. GitHub is one hosting and
collaboration platform that can store Git repositories and provide reviews,
permissions and automation.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Git: commit, branch, merge, fetch.
   Hosting platform: pull request, review, protected branch.
   Remote name: origin; it may point to any supported server.
✎ REMEMBER Git: commit, branch, merge, fetch.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
A repository can be hosted locally or by another provider. A pull request is a collaboration
request defined by the platform, not a Git object type. Server policy can reject a push even
when the local history is valid.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Can a Git repository exist without any hosting account?
Yes. `git init` creates a local repository. GitHub, GitLab or another server is optional for
hosting and collaboration.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Git pull and a pull request are different concepts.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 5. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: Does Git store changes or snapshots?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Git fundamentals and the right mental model Q 003 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q003
Does Git store changes or snapshots?
THE SHORT ANSWER
The logical model is a snapshot for each commit, with unchanged content
reused by identity. Storage may use compression and deltas internally, but those
are implementation details.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Commit A: Order.java version 1; Customer.java version 1.
   Commit B: Order.java version 2; Customer.java version 1.
   The unchanged Customer content can be shared.
✎ REMEMBER Commit A: Order.java version 1; Customer.java version 1.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
A commit points to a root tree describing tracked paths. Diff computes a comparison between
snapshots. This explains why Git can inspect an old state without replaying a sequence of edits
from the beginning.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What object connects a commit to its file hierarchy?
A tree object. Each commit names a root tree, which links directory entries to blobs and
nested trees.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A commit is not simply a text patch file stored by Git.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 6. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: What is a commit and what does its identifier mean?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Git fundamentals and the right mental model Q 004 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q004
What is a commit and what does its identifier
mean?
THE SHORT ANSWER
A commit is an immutable object containing a tree, parent references and
metadata. Its object ID is derived from its encoded contents, so changing those
contents changes the ID.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git show --no-patch --format=fuller HEAD
   git rev-parse HEAD
   git cat-file -p HEAD
✎ REMEMBER git show --no-patch --format=fuller HEAD
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The parent relationship is part of the object. Rebase or amend can create a new ID even
when a file snapshot stays the same. ID length depends on repository object format, and
abbreviated IDs must be unambiguous within the repository.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Why does changing only a commit message create a new commit ID?
The message is part of the commit object's contents. Changing it changes the object's
hash, even when the file tree is identical.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A short hash is an abbreviation, not a sequential commit number.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 6. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: What are HEAD, a branch and a tag?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 01 / Git fundamentals and the right mental model Q 005 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q005
What are HEAD, a branch and a tag?
THE SHORT ANSWER
HEAD identifies the checked-out position, usually through a branch reference. A
branch names a movable tip. A tag names a chosen object, commonly a release
commit.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git symbolic-ref --short HEAD
   git branch --show-current
   git tag v1.0.0
✎ REMEMBER git symbolic-ref --short HEAD
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
On a branch, committing creates a child of the current tip and moves that branch to the new
commit. In detached HEAD, HEAD points directly to a commit instead. Tags do not advance
with normal commits.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What reference moves when you commit on feature/orders?
`refs/heads/feature/orders` moves to the new commit. `main` stays where it was.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A branch is a reference, not a copied directory of files.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 6. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: What are the working tree, index and repository?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Working tree, index and staging Q 006 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q006
What are the working tree, index and repository?
THE SHORT ANSWER
The working tree contains checked-out files. The index records the proposed
next commit snapshot. The repository stores objects and references representing
history.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Edit file -> working tree changes.
   git add file -> copy its current content into the index.
   git commit -> create a commit from the index.
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✎
Commit reads the index, not unstaged edits.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Staging does not freeze the working file. If you edit it again, the staged version and working
version differ. This lets one file have both staged and unstaged changes at the same time.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which version is committed if you edit again after git add?
The version captured by the last `git add` is committed. The edit made afterward remains
unstaged in your working file.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A normal commit includes staged content, not every current file edit.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 7. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: How do you read git status --short?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Working tree, index and staging Q 007 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q007
How do you read git status --short?
THE SHORT ANSWER
The first status column compares the index with HEAD; the second compares
the working tree with the index. Untracked paths appear with question marks.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git status --short
   M  src/Order.java   # staged modification
    M src/Customer.java  # unstaged modification
   MM src/Price.java   # staged, then edited again
✎ REMEMBER git status --short
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Unmerged statuses describe conflict stages and need separate attention. The long status view
gives operation guidance. Read status before applying an undo command because the correct
action depends on which area contains the work.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you inspect the two changes represented by MM?
Run `git diff --staged -- FILE` for HEAD-to-index changes and `git diff -- FILE` for index-
to-working-file changes.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Treating both M columns as identical can cause you to discard the wrong
version.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 7. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: How do git diff, git diff --staged and git diff HEAD differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Working tree, index and staging Q 008 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q008
How do git diff, git diff --staged and git diff HEAD
differ?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Plain diff compares working files to the index; staged diff compares the index to
HEAD; diff HEAD compares tracked working content to HEAD.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git diff -- src/Order.java
   git diff --staged -- src/Order.java
   git diff HEAD -- src/Order.java
✎ REMEMBER git diff -- src/Order.java
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The third comparison can include both staged and unstaged effects, but ordinary diff does not
display an untracked file as a normal tracked change. Use the comparison that answers your
actual question: what remains unstaged, or what the next commit would contain.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which command reviews the proposed commit before committing?
`git diff --staged` shows the exact tracked changes currently proposed for the next commit.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Plain git diff can be empty even when staged changes exist.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 8. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: How can you stage only part of a file?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Working tree, index and staging Q 009 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q009
How can you stage only part of a file?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Use interactive patch staging to select relevant hunks, then review the staged diff.
Split hunks or edit the patch when the changes need finer separation.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git add -p -- src/OrderService.java
   git diff --staged
   git diff
✎ REMEMBER git add -p -- src/OrderService.java
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The index may now contain a different version from both HEAD and the working file. Test the
intended staged snapshot or separate changes carefully so the commit is coherent. New files
may need intent-to-add before patch selection.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you keep a formatting change out of a bug-fix commit?
Stage only the bug-fix hunks with `git add -p`, review with `git diff --staged`, and commit
formatting separately.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Staging one hunk does not guarantee the resulting commit compiles
independently.

pages.title: How do you unstage a file without deleting the edit?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 02 / Working tree, index and staging Q 010 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q010
How do you unstage a file without deleting the
edit?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Restore the index entry from HEAD while leaving the working tree alone. This
changes what the next commit contains, not the edited file itself.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git restore --staged -- src/Order.java
   git diff --staged
   git diff -- src/Order.java
✎ REMEMBER git restore --staged -- src/Order.java
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
This assumes the repository already has a HEAD commit. Older workflows use path-form reset
for the same index operation. Verify the remaining working diff afterward.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How does unstaging differ from restoring the working file?
Unstaging changes the index but keeps the edited file. `git restore -- FILE` replaces the
unstaged tracked file content and can lose edits.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Adding --worktree as well changes the files and can discard edits.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 8. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: How do git init and git clone differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Setup, configuration and cloning Q 011 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q011
How do git init and git clone differ?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Init creates a repository in a chosen directory. Clone creates a repository from
another one, normally configuring a remote and checking out an initial branch.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git init -b main interview-demo
   git clone REPOSITORY_URL order-service
   git -C order-service remote -v
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✎
Identity settings and network authentication differ.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
An existing folder can be initialized, but its files are not committed automatically. A normal
clone creates local and remote-tracking references according to the remote configuration. A
bare clone is different because it has no ordinary checked-out working tree.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which remote is normally configured by clone?
Normally `origin`. Confirm with `git remote -v`; it is only a conventional name.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A folder containing source files is not versioned until those files are tracked
and committed.

pages.title: What is the difference between local, global and system Git configuration?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Setup, configuration and cloning Q 012 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q012
What is the difference between local, global and
system Git configuration?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Local configuration applies to one repository, global to a user, and system to a
machine installation. Higher-precedence sources can override earlier settings;
inspect the origin when behavior is surprising.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git config --local user.name "Interview Learner"
   git config --local user.email "learner@example.test"
   git config --show-origin --get-all user.email
✎ REMEMBER git config --local user.name "Interview Learner"
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Command-line settings and environment variables can also affect behavior. Repository-local
identity is useful when work and personal projects differ. Avoid assuming that the global value
is the effective value in every repository.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you find where pull.rebase was configured?
Use `git config --show-origin --show-scope --get-all pull.rebase` to see the effective values
and their configuration sources.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Changing a global setting can alter unrelated repositories for that user.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 9. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: Does user.name or user.email authenticate a push?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Setup, configuration and cloning Q 013 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q013
Does user.name or user.email authenticate a push?
THE SHORT ANSWER
No. They normally populate commit identity metadata. Network authentication
uses the transport and credential mechanism, such as an SSH key or an HTTPS
credential helper.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git config user.email "developer@example.test"
   git remote get-url origin
   git config --get credential.helper
✎ REMEMBER git config user.email "developer@example.test"
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
An author email can be configured locally without proving control of that address. Hosting
platforms may associate verified emails or signatures with accounts, but authorization to
update a repository is separate. Commit signing also differs from transport authentication.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Why can committing work while pushing returns permission denied?
Local commits need no remote permission. Pushing requires network access and valid
authentication plus permission to update the target reference.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A successful local commit does not show that you can push to the server.

CHAPTER 03 / Setup, configuration and cloning Q 014 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q014
Why should you explicitly select the initial branch
name in examples?

The initial name can depend on Git configuration or hosting conventions.

user's global defaults.

deployment scripts, docs and developer clones/upstreams.

pages.title: What is a bare repository used for?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 03 / Setup, configuration and cloning Q 015 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q015
What is a bare repository used for?
THE SHORT ANSWER
A bare repository stores Git data without an ordinary working tree. It is
commonly used as a remote endpoint because branches can be updated without
overwriting a checked-out application folder.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git init --bare demo-remote.git
   git clone demo-remote.git developer-a
   git -C developer-a remote -v
✎ REMEMBER git init --bare demo-remote.git
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The labs use local bare repositories to demonstrate sharing without contacting a hosting
service. A bare repository is not automatically secured, backed up or configured with review
policy; those concerns belong to its deployment.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Why is pushing to a checked-out non-bare branch restricted by default?
The push could change the branch's files without updating the remote working tree/index.
Bare repositories avoid that mismatch.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A bare remote does not provide a pull-request interface by itself.

pages.title: What makes a good commit?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Commits, inspection and useful history queries Q 016 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q016
What makes a good commit?
THE SHORT ANSWER
A good commit captures one understandable purpose, includes necessary tests
or configuration and has a message explaining the behavior change. Keep
unrelated formatting and fixes separate when practical.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git diff --staged
   git commit -m "Reject negative checkout quantity"
   git show --stat HEAD
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✎
Parents define history; display order is a view.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The commit should be reviewable and useful for later debugging or revert. A small commit is
not necessarily coherent if it relies on an uncommitted dependency. Explain why the change
is needed in the message body when the diff alone is insufficient.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Can this commit be reverted without removing an unrelated feature?
Usually yes if the commit contains only one coherent change. `git revert OID` then test;
unrelated later commits remain in history.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: git commit -a includes tracked changes, but does not automatically add
untracked files.

pages.title: How do you inspect one commit and its changed files?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Commits, inspection and useful history queries Q 017 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q017
How do you inspect one commit and its changed
files?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Use show to inspect the commit patch and metadata, or request summary forms
when only paths and sizes matter.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git show HEAD
   git show --name-status HEAD
   git show --stat HEAD
   git show HEAD:src/Order.java
✎ REMEMBER git show HEAD
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The last command reads a path from the selected commit without switching branches. Merge
commits have multiple-parent comparison semantics, so choose the desired parent
comparison when investigating a merge.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How can you inspect yesterday's version without changing your files?
Use `git show COMMIT:path/to/File.java` or `git show HEAD@{yesterday}:path` if that reflog
date exists. These commands do not change your files.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A file path must exist in the selected snapshot, not just in today's working tree.

pages.title: How do you view branches and merges in history?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Commits, inspection and useful history queries Q 018 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q018
How do you view branches and merges in history?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Use a graph-oriented log with reference decoration and a bounded scope. Read
parent relationships rather than treating screen order as a universal
chronological sequence.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git log --graph --oneline --decorate --all
   git log --first-parent --oneline main
✎ REMEMBER git log --graph --oneline --decorate --all
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The first view shows reachable history across selected references. First-parent follows the
main line through merges and can help understand integration history. Author timestamps
and topology can disagree, so a log is not a simple numbered timeline.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Why might a side-branch commit appear below a newer main commit?
Git graphs follow parent relationships, not just timestamps; branch topology and display
ordering can place commits in surprising rows.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A commit missing from a limited log view may still exist elsewhere in the
repository.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 12. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.

pages.title: What do A..B and A...B mean in git log?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Commits, inspection and useful history queries Q 019 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q019
What do A..B and A...B mean in git log?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Two-dot selects commits reachable from B but not A. Three-dot selects commits
reachable from either side but not both: the symmetric difference.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git log main..feature
   git log --left-right main...feature
   git rev-list --left-right --count main...feature
✎ REMEMBER git log main..feature
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
These are set operations over commit ancestry. The notation has different comparison
meaning in git diff: three-dot diff compares the merge base to the second endpoint. Name the
command when explaining the range.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which range shows feature commits not reachable from main?
`git log main..feature` lists commits reachable from `feature` but not from `main`.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Log three-dot and diff three-dot are not interchangeable definitions.
Original question & example: uploaded Git guide, source page 12. Follow-up answer: added for this edition.
GIT / PREMIUM NOTEBOOK ZERO TO HERO • JAVA TEAM WORKFLOWS
Understand • Practice • Explain 22

   git rev-list --left-right --count main...feature
✎ REMEMBER git log main..feature

pages.title: How do you compare a feature's changes with main?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 04 / Commits, inspection and useful history queries Q 020 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q020
How do you compare a feature's changes with
main?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Use a merge-base comparison to inspect what the feature changed since its
shared ancestor, and an endpoint comparison when you want final snapshot
differences.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git diff main...feature
   git diff main feature
   git merge-base main feature
✎ REMEMBER git diff main...feature
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The first comparison is useful for many review workflows because it excludes independent
main changes from the starting snapshot. The second answers how the two tips differ now.
Neither view alone proves that the feature integrates cleanly with current main.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What changes if main advanced after the feature branch was created?
The two branch tips may now differ in more ways, and merging may conflict. `git diff
main...feature` still starts from their merge base.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A clean-looking feature diff can still conflict during integration.

pages.title: How do you create and switch to a branch?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Branches, switching and detached HEAD Q 021 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q021
How do you create and switch to a branch?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Use switch -c to create a branch at the current commit and check it out. Use
switch with an existing name to change the checked-out branch.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git switch -c feature/order-validation
   git branch --show-current
   git switch main
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✎
A branch is a movable reference, not a copied folder.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Creating the branch does not create a new commit. Both branch names can initially point to
the same commit. Subsequent commits on the feature move only that branch. Switching may
be refused if local edits would be overwritten.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What happens to main when you commit on the new feature?
Nothing moves on `main`. Your newly created commit advances only the currently
checked-out feature branch.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A successful switch can carry compatible uncommitted edits into the new
branch.

pages.title: How do git switch and git checkout differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Branches, switching and detached HEAD Q 022 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q022
How do git switch and git checkout differ?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Switch focuses on selecting branches or detached commits. Checkout is an older
multipurpose command that can also replace paths. Restore separates file-
restoration operations from branch switching.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git switch main
   git switch --detach v1.0.0
   git restore --source=HEAD -- src/Order.java
✎ REMEMBER git switch main
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Explicit commands reduce ambiguity between a branch name and a path. Switch and restore
are available in modern Git; this guide's labs run on Git 2.51.1. Older installations may require
the corresponding checkout forms.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Why is git checkout ambiguous when a path and branch share a name?
Git cannot always tell if that word names a file or a branch. Use `git switch branch` or `git
restore -- file` to make intent clear.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Checkout of a path changes file content; it is not a branch switch.

pages.title: What is detached HEAD and is it always a problem?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Branches, switching and detached HEAD Q 023 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q023
What is detached HEAD and is it always a
problem?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Detached HEAD points directly to a commit instead of a branch. It is useful for
inspecting or testing an old version, but new work needs a reference if you want
to keep it reachable.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git switch --detach v1.0.0
   # after creating an experimental commit:
   git switch -c experiment/fix
✎ REMEMBER git switch --detach v1.0.0
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Creating a branch at the detached tip preserves the new commits. If you already switched
away, inspect the reflog and create a branch at the intended commit. CI often checks out a
detached commit intentionally for reproducible builds.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you keep an experiment before returning to main?
Before leaving detached HEAD, run `git switch -c experiment/name` at the experiment tip.
That branch keeps the commit reachable.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Detached commits are not immediately deleted, but unreferenced history can
eventually be collected.

pages.title: How do you rename or delete a branch?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Branches, switching and detached HEAD Q 024 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q024
How do you rename or delete a branch?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Rename updates the local branch name. Delete removes a local branch
reference, with a checked deletion policy or a forced form. Remote references
require separate operations.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git branch -m feature/old-name feature/new-name
   git branch -d feature/done
   git push origin --delete feature/done
✎ REMEMBER git branch -m feature/old-name feature/new-name
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The remote delete line changes the server and needs the team's authorization. Local -d
checks merge reachability using its documented rules, not whether a squash-merged patch
looks equivalent. Renaming may require updating upstream and hosting settings.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Why might -d reject a feature that was squash-merged?
Squash creates a different commit on main, without preserving original feature commits as
ancestors. `-d` checks reachability, not patch similarity.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Branch deletion removes a name, not necessarily all reachable commit objects.

pages.title: Why can uncommitted changes follow you when switching branches?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 05 / Branches, switching and detached HEAD Q 025 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q025
Why can uncommitted changes follow you when
switching branches?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Edits live in the working tree and index, not in an immutable branch snapshot.
Git may carry them when the switch can preserve them without overwriting
incompatible content.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git status --short
   git switch feature/another-task
   git status --short
✎ REMEMBER git status --short
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Do not rely on accidental carry-over when changing tasks. Commit coherent work, stash it
with the needed file categories, or use another worktree. If a switch is refused, inspect rather
than forcing away useful edits.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you move an unfinished edit to a separate task safely?
Commit it on a dedicated WIP branch, or `git stash push -u` then create/switch to the
other branch and apply the stash deliberately.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Forcing a checkout or switch can discard local changes.

pages.title: What is a fast-forward merge?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Merging and resolving conflicts Q 026 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q026
What is a fast-forward merge?
THE SHORT ANSWER
When the current tip is an ancestor of the target tip, integration can move the
current branch reference forward without creating a merge commit.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git switch main
   git merge --ff-only feature/orders
   git log --oneline --decorate -3
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✎
Conflicts need a correct final result and tests.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The existing feature commits become reachable from main. No new two-parent commit is
required. The --ff-only policy refuses integration if histories have diverged, making the allowed
outcome explicit.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What happens if main already contains an independent commit?
`--ff-only` fails because neither tip is the ancestor of the other. Use an agreed merge or
rebase after inspecting the diverged history.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Fast-forward does not mean changes were tested or reviewed.

pages.title: What is a three-way merge and a merge commit?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Merging and resolving conflicts Q 027 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q027
What is a three-way merge and a merge commit?
THE SHORT ANSWER
A three-way merge uses a common ancestor and both tips to combine changes.
When divergent histories are integrated normally, a merge commit records both
parents.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git switch main
   git merge feature/orders
   git show --no-patch --format=%P HEAD
✎ REMEMBER git switch main
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Two parents preserve ancestry from both lines of work. The first parent is normally the
branch that was checked out when merging. A merge can be conflict-free when both sides
change different files, yet still require integration testing.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Why does preserving both parents matter for future merges?
Git remembers both lines as ancestors, so future merges can identify common commits
and avoid re-merging already integrated history.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A merge commit can include a hand-written resolution beyond either parent.

pages.title: How do you resolve a merge conflict correctly?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Merging and resolving conflicts Q 028 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q028
How do you resolve a merge conflict correctly?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Inspect the conflicting intent, edit the final desired content, stage the resolution,
verify it and continue the merge. Do not choose a side solely to remove markers.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git status
   git diff --cc
   # edit file and remove conflict markers after deciding the result
   git add -- src/Order.java
   git merge --continue
✎ REMEMBER git status
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Staging records the chosen resolved version. Run relevant tests because a syntactically valid
combination may violate behavior. Deleted/modified or renamed paths need a decision about
the path as well as the content.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which test demonstrates that both branches' intended behavior survives?
Run unit and integration tests for the feature introduced by each branch, plus one test of
the combined workflow after conflict resolution.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Conflict markers left in Java files can become compile errors or accidental text.

pages.title: How do --no-ff, --ff-only and --squash differ?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Merging and resolving conflicts Q 029 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q029
How do --no-ff, --ff-only and --squash differ?
THE SHORT ANSWER
No-ff creates a merge commit even when a fast-forward is possible. Ff-only
allows only a fast-forward. Squash prepares combined changes for a later
ordinary commit without recording merge ancestry.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git merge --no-ff feature
   git merge --ff-only feature
   git merge --squash feature
   git commit -m "Add order validation"  # after squash
✎ REMEMBER git merge --no-ff feature
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
These are alternatives, not commands to run consecutively for the same integration. Squash is
useful for one reviewable result but changes how later Git operations recognize ancestry.
Choose the repository's integration policy rather than using a flag mechanically.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Why can later merging the same long-lived branch become surprising after squash?
The squash patch is present, but the old feature commits are not ancestors. A later merge
may replay changes or produce unexpected conflicts.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Squash merge does not mark all original feature commits as ancestors of
main.

pages.title: How do you abort a merge, and what are the limits?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 06 / Merging and resolving conflicts Q 030 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q030
How do you abort a merge, and what are the
limits?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Merge --abort attempts to restore the pre-merge state. Start with a clean
working tree or preserve existing edits because reconstructing them after a
complex interrupted merge is not always guaranteed.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git status
   git merge --abort
   git status
✎ REMEMBER git status
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Abort is for an in-progress merge, not for removing an already committed merge. After a
committed shared merge, a revert may be appropriate. Verify that your original edits are
present instead of assuming every cancellation has identical behavior.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What should you do if the merge already became a public commit?
Do not reset the shared branch to erase history. Consider `git revert -m` for a public
merge, confirm the right mainline parent, and review/test the result.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Mixing unrelated local edits with conflict resolution makes recovery harder.

pages.title: What does git rebase do?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Rebase and rewriting a private branch Q 031 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q031
What does git rebase do?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Rebase takes selected commits from one line of development and replays their
changes onto another base, normally producing new commit identities and
moving the rebased branch tip.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git switch feature/orders
   git branch backup/feature-before-rebase
   git rebase main
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✎
Rewrite only with clear collaboration rules.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Use the backup reference to preserve the original tip while learning or doing a risky rewrite.
Main is not moved by rebasing the feature onto it. Replay can omit commits already
represented upstream according to Git's rules.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
Which branch moves when you rebase feature onto main?
The checked-out `feature` branch tip moves to new replayed commits. The `main` branch
tip does not move.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Rebase is not simply moving unchanged commit objects to a different parent.

pages.title: When should you merge and when should you rebase?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Rebase and rewriting a private branch Q 032 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q032
When should you merge and when should you
rebase?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Merge preserves the existing ancestry and integrates it. Rebase can simplify a
private branch before integration, but rewriting shared commits requires
coordination with people depending on them.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
Shared integration branch: preserve accepted history.
   Private feature: fetch, then rebase onto selected base if policy permits.
   Release hotfix: choose explicit backport or merge strategy.
✎ REMEMBER Shared integration branch: preserve accepted history.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
There is no universally superior history shape. Merge records integration events; a linear
history can make some navigation easier. Focus on audit, review and collaboration
requirements rather than visual neatness alone.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What team agreement would make a shared rebase acceptable?
Agree who may rewrite, when teammates must stop working, how backups/notifications
work, and how to synchronize; protect the remote update with an explicit lease.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Rebasing a published branch can leave coworkers based on commits you
replaced.

pages.title: How do you resolve a rebase conflict?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Rebase and rewriting a private branch Q 033 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q033
How do you resolve a rebase conflict?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Resolve the current replayed change, stage the desired files and continue. Abort
returns to the original branch state; skip drops the current replayed commit's
contribution and needs careful review.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git status
   # edit conflicting file
   git add -- src/Order.java
   git rebase --continue
   # alternative cancellation: git rebase --abort
✎ REMEMBER git status
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Several commits can conflict in sequence, so resolving the first does not necessarily finish the
operation. Rebase --skip is not a generic fix for a difficult conflict. Check the final diff and
tests against the intended feature.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How do you determine whether a skipped change is actually redundant?
Compare the original patch with upstream using `git show`/`git range-diff`; skip only after
confirming the intended behavior already exists, then run tests.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Skipping a commit can silently remove behavior if its change was not already
present.

pages.title: Why can ours and theirs feel reversed during rebase?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Rebase and rewriting a private branch Q 034 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q034
Why can ours and theirs feel reversed during
rebase?
THE SHORT ANSWER
During a rebase merge-backend conflict, ours is the already-rebased side
including the new base, while theirs is the commit being replayed from your old
branch.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git ls-files -u
   git show :2:src/Order.java  # stage 2: ours
   git show :3:src/Order.java  # stage 3: theirs
✎ REMEMBER git ls-files -u
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
These labels describe the current operation, not permanently your work versus a colleague's.
In a normal merge they refer to the checked-out side and the other side. Inspect the content
and intent before selecting a side.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
What does stage 1 represent in a conflicted index?
Stage 1 stores the common base version of a conflicted path; stages 2 and 3 store the two
competing versions.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Blindly using --ours to keep your feature during rebase can select the opposite
content.

pages.title: How do you review a branch after rebase?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 07 / Rebase and rewriting a private branch Q 035 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q035
How do you review a branch after rebase?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Compare the rewritten patch series with the preserved old series, inspect the
final base-relative diff and run relevant tests. New IDs alone are expected and
do not indicate changed behavior.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git range-diff main..backup/feature-before-rebase main..feature/orders
   git diff main...feature/orders
   git log --graph --oneline --decorate -10
✎ REMEMBER git range-diff main..backup/feature-before-rebase main..feature/orders
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
Choose the old and new base ranges accurately; the first line is a convenient sketch when
main is a suitable boundary for both. Range-diff highlights patch-series changes but is not a
correctness proof. Check conflict resolutions particularly closely.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you distinguish expected ID changes from unexpected patch changes?
Use `git range-diff` between original and rebased series. New hashes are expected;
unexpected added, removed or changed patches need review.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: A conflict resolution can unintentionally delete part of the old feature.

pages.title: What does cherry-pick do?
pages.fullText:
CHAPTER 08 / Cherry-pick, amend and interactive cleanup Q 036 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q036
What does cherry-pick do?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Cherry-pick applies the change introduced by a selected commit to the current
branch, usually creating a new commit there. It does not merge the entire
source branch's ancestry.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git switch release/1.4
   git cherry-pick -x FIX_COMMIT
   git show --stat HEAD
DRAW IT TO REMEMBER ✎
Transferred changes need not share ancestry.
WHAT REALLY HAPPENS
The -x trailer records the source commit for a backport. The fix may depend on earlier
source-branch changes, so inspect prerequisites and test the release version. Identical
patches can have different IDs because parent and metadata differ.
FOLLOW-UP QUESTION + ANSWER
How would you backport a fix that depends on a renamed method?
Backport any necessary rename first, or adapt the patch to the old method name on the
release branch; compile and test against that release API.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Selecting one commit does not automatically select its semantic dependencies.

How do you handle a cherry-pick conflict?

abandons the in-progress sequence; skip deliberately omits the current selected
commit.

When picking multiple commits, several may need resolution. A conflict-free backport can still
compile incorrectly against older dependencies.

Which release-specific tests should you run after the backport?
Run the release's own build/tests, regression tests for the defect, and compatibility tests for
its Java version, dependencies and schema.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Choosing the whole source version may bring unrelated newer behavior into
the release.

pages.title: What does git commit --amend change?

CHAPTER 08 / Cherry-pick, amend and interactive cleanup Q 038 of 110
INTERVIEW QUESTION / Q038
What does git commit --amend change?
THE SHORT ANSWER
Amend creates a replacement for the current tip using the selected staged
content and message options. The old commit is not edited in place, and its ID
usually changes.
COMMAND EXAMPLE / SCENARIO
git add -- src/OrderTest.java
   git commit --amend --no-edit
   git show --stat HEAD

No-edit keeps the message; it does not mean keeping the original content. For a message-
only amendment, ensure no unintended staged changes are present. The default author
handling differs from the updated committer metadata.

How would you change only the message without adding staged edits?
First check `git diff --staged` and unstage anything unintended. Then `git commit --amend
-m "New message"` on a private commit.
⚠ INTERVIEW TRAP: Amending a shared tip is a history rewrite, not an ordinary new follow-up
commit.
